```
constexpr uint32_t OFF_MAIN_FULL      =      0;   // 8 x 8 B ClusterTransactionBarrier, count 1
constexpr uint32_t OFF_MAIN_EMPTY     =     64;   // 8 x 8 B ClusterBarrier, count 2
constexpr uint32_t OFF_EPI_LOAD_FULL  =    128;   // 4 x 8 B (beta != 0 only; reserved, not initialised: E.10 item 6)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_EPI_LOAD_EMPTY =    160;   // 4 x 8 B (idem)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_LOAD_ORDER     =    192;   // 2 x 8 B (idem)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_CLC_FULL       =    208;   // 2 x 8 B, count 1 (+16 tx bytes)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_CLC_EMPTY      =    224;   // 2 x 8 B, count 800 (only CTA 0's are used)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_ACC_FULL       =    240;   // 4 x 8 B, count 1
constexpr uint32_t OFF_ACC_EMPTY      =    272;   // 4 x 8 B, count 256
constexpr uint32_t OFF_THROTTLE_FULL  =    304;   // 2 x 8 B, count 32
constexpr uint32_t OFF_THROTTLE_EMPTY =    320;   // 2 x 8 B, count 32
constexpr uint32_t OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC   =    336;   // 1 x 8 B, count 32
constexpr uint32_t OFF_CLC_RESPONSE   =    352;   // 2 x 16 B, alignas(16)
constexpr uint32_t OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR  =    384;   // 4 B, written by tcgen05.alloc
constexpr uint32_t OFF_SMEM_CD        =    512;   // 4 x 8192 B, Swizzle<2,5,2>, 512-byte aligned
constexpr uint32_t OFF_SMEM_A         =  33792;   // 8 x 16384 B, Swizzle<3,4,3>, 1024-byte aligned
constexpr uint32_t OFF_SMEM_B         = 164864;   // 8 x  8192 B, idem
constexpr uint32_t kSmemBaseLow24     =  0x400;   // measured base (D.1 D5): 0x400 + (rank << 24); computed at run time, never assumed

static_assert(OFF_SMEM_A == OFF_SMEM_CD + kEpiStages * kEpiStageBytes + 512, "Section 6.2 (FusionStorage pad to 512)");
static_assert(OFF_SMEM_B == OFF_SMEM_A + kStages * kStageBytesA, "Section 6.2");
static_assert(kSmemBytes == OFF_SMEM_B + kStages * kStageBytesB, "Section 6.2: SharedStorageSize 230400");
static_assert(kStageBytesAHalf == 64u * 64u * 2u, "one CTA's 64x64 fp16 half of the 128x64 A stage (B.4): TMA box (64, 64, 1)");
static_assert(OFF_SMEM_A % 1024 == 0 && OFF_SMEM_B % 1024 == 0, "SW128 stage bases need 1 KiB alignment (Section 7.5)");
static_assert(OFF_SMEM_CD % 512 == 0, "SW128_32B epilogue stages need 512 B alignment (Section 7.7)");
static_assert(OFF_CLC_RESPONSE % 16 == 0 && OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR % 4 == 0, "b128 response slots");
static_assert(kSmemBaseLow24 + kSmemBytes < (1u << 18), "14-bit UMMA start-address field spans 256 KiB (B.3.2 step 4)");
static_assert(kThreads == 256 && kMmaM == 256 && kMmaN == 128 && kKBlocks == 4, "Section 4");
```

### 5.7.1 The byte map

The offsets are the CUTLASS `SharedStorage` of `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:182-212` flattened: a `PipelineStorage` (`aligned_struct<16>`) of all barrier arrays in declaration order, the CLC response slots, the TMEM base word, then `TensorStorage` (epilogue storage first, mainloop storage second). Every barrier is one 8-byte `mbarrier` object (`ClusterBarrier`/`ClusterTransactionBarrier`, `barrier.h`). The map, with every barrier (counts are Section 5.9's; init warps are the prologue's, Chapter 11):

```
offset   size   region / object                            count or alignment           initialised by
------   -----  -----------------------------------------  ---------------------------  --------------------
     0     64   OFF_MAIN_FULL    full[s], s = 0..7, 8 B    1 (+ 49152 tx bytes)         warp 0 (elected lane)
    64     64   OFF_MAIN_EMPTY   empty[s], s = 0..7        2                            warp 0
   128     32   OFF_EPI_LOAD_FULL  [0..3]                  (C-load pipeline, beta != 0)  not initialised
   160     32   OFF_EPI_LOAD_EMPTY [0..3]                  (idem)                       not initialised
   192     16   OFF_LOAD_ORDER   [0..1]                    (idem)                       not initialised
   208     16   OFF_CLC_FULL     full[0..1]                1 (+ 16 tx bytes)            warp 4
   224     16   OFF_CLC_EMPTY    empty[0..1]               800                          warp 4  (only CTA 0's are arrived on)
   240     32   OFF_ACC_FULL     full[st], st = 0..3       1                            warp 5
   272     32   OFF_ACC_EMPTY    empty[st], st = 0..3      256                          warp 5  (only the leader's are arrived on)
   304     16   OFF_THROTTLE_FULL  [0..1]                  32                           warp 3  (rank 0 uses them)
   320     16   OFF_THROTTLE_EMPTY [0..1]                  32                           warp 3
   336      8   OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC                           32                           warp 0 (lane_pred lane)
   344      8   padding                                    PipelineStorage is aligned_struct<16> -> sizeof 352
   352     32   OFF_CLC_RESPONSE  response[0..1], 16 B     alignas(16); read by ld.shared.b128
   384      4   OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR                          written by tcgen05.alloc, read by warps 0 and 4-7
   388    124   padding                                    tensors.epilogue is alignas(512)
   512  32768   OFF_SMEM_CD   C/D stage (e % 4), 4 x 8192  Swizzle<2,5,2>; 512 % 512 == 0
 33280    512   FusionStorage (an empty tuple, 1 B) + pad  the epilogue TensorStorage is padded to its own 512-B alignment
 33792 131072   OFF_SMEM_A    A stage s, 8 x 16384         Swizzle<3,4,3>; 33792 = 33 x 1024
164864  65536   OFF_SMEM_B    B stage s, 8 x 8192          Swizzle<3,4,3>; 164864 = 161 x 1024
230400          end = kSmemBytes                           2048 B below the 232448-B opt-in maximum
```

Two remarks on the totals. First, the stage count. The builder's formula (5.5, `kStages`) left `198464 - 8 x 24592 = 1728` B, far short of the 24592 B a ninth stage costs in that formula (24576 B of tensors + 16 B of barriers). The *physical* slack is `232448 - 230400 = 2048` B, 320 B more, because the builder's estimate `192 + 33792 + 8 x 24592 = 230720` overstates the real `SharedStorage` by 320 B. It budgets the epilogue as its full `SharedStorage` of 33792 B (the 33280-byte `TensorStorage` plus a 64-byte load pipeline, rounded to 512; note, Section 6.1), whereas the kernel embeds only the 33280-byte `TensorStorage`: 512 B too many. In the other direction, its 192-byte kernel carveout plus the 8 x 16 B of mainloop barriers inside the stages under-budget the real 512-byte pre-tensor area by 192 B; net 512 - 192 = 320 B. Either way a ninth stage is out of reach.

Second, where the two pads come from. `tensors.epilogue` starts at 512 and not at 388 because the epilogue's `CollectiveStorageReuseC` declares its `smem_C`/`smem_D` union members `alignas(MaxSmemAlignment)`, with `SmemAlignmentD = cutlass::detail::alignment_for_swizzle(SmemLayoutD{}) = 1 << (B + M + |S|) = 1 << (2 + 5 + 2) = 512` for `Swizzle<2,5,2>` (`sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:170-172`, `:190-193`; `cutlass/detail/layout.hpp:420-426`). The kernel's `TensorStorage : cute::aligned_struct<128, _1>` (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:203`) inherits alignment 512 from its first member, so the compiler rounds 388 up to 512. The 512 bytes at 33280 are the `sizeof` rounding of the epilogue `TensorStorage { CollectiveStorage collective; FusionStorage thread; }` (`sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:208-215`): 32768 B of stages plus the 1-byte empty `FusionStorage` of the linear-combination tree = 32769, rounded to the struct's own 512-byte alignment = 33280. The mainloop storage therefore starts at 512 + 33280 = 33792. The mainloop `TensorStorage` declares only `aligned_struct<128>` (`sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:224`). The 1024-byte alignment that `Swizzle<3,4,3>` needs (`alignment_for_swizzle = 1 << (3 + 4 + 3) = 1024`) is *declared nowhere*; it holds only because 33792 = 33 x 1024 happens to be a multiple (note, Section 6.2). That is why the explicit kernel's `static_assert` at `:162` exists: it turns a coincidence into a checked invariant. Measured confirmation: `alignof 512`, `PipelineStorage 352`, `EpilogueSharedStorage 33792`, `off_epilogue_thread 33280`, `off_smem_A 33792` (note D.1 D2).

Three facts about the base make this map usable (facts 1 and 2 measured, note D.1 D5; fact 3 read from the kernel's source; restated at `explicit.cu:138` and `:156`, the peer-bit rule at `:187`):

1. The dynamic shared memory of rank `r` starts at the 32-bit `shared::cta` address `0x400 + (r << 24)`. The low kilobyte is the system-reserved shared memory (`SHARED:1024` in the resource line of every kernel in the binary, note G.3). The SASS shows what lives there (note D.2, `tcgen05.alloc` row, and D.6 item 7): ptxas lowers the `cta_group::2` TMEM allocation into an atomic in the leader's elected lane, followed by a handshake with the peer. The handshake stores the result locally (`IMAD.SHL.U32 R8, R9, 0x20, RZ; STS [UR29+0x180], R8`, the atomic's result rescaled from 32-column units to columns), forwards it with `st.async`, and completes a barrier in the peer's reserved kilobyte at `(rank << 24) + 0x48`, with bookkeeping words at `+0x50/+0x54/+0x58`. The kernel declares no static `__shared__` (`sharedSizeBytes 0`, note D.1 D4), so `extern __shared__ char smem[]` is the first user byte, at `0x400`. Hence `kSmemBaseLow24 = 0x400`. Adding any static `__shared__` variable could move the dynamic base: where static storage sits relative to the dynamic array is not a source-level contract (NVIDIA internal). That would invalidate the compile-time cross-checks that use `kSmemBaseLow24`, though not the kernel itself, which computes the base at run time (fact 3). The rank sits in address byte 3 (bits [24,32)); only bits 24-25 are set for a 4-CTA cluster.
2. Therefore `smem_base + OFF_*` is the shared address of anything, and clearing bit 24 of such an address names the same object in the *pair leader* (the even rank): `0xFEFFFFFF` (Section 5.9).
3. The kernel *computes* `smem_base = smem_u32(smem)` (the `:258` wrapper around `__cvta_generic_to_shared`) at run time (`explicit.cu:1098`) and never assumes `0x400`; `kSmemBaseLow24` exists only for the compile-time cross-checks at `:165` and `:177`.

The address-space rule that follows (stated at `explicit.cu:22-23`): every `asm` operand naming shared memory is the 32-bit `smem_base + OFF_*`; every C++ dereference uses the generic pointer `smem + OFF_*`. The two classic mistakes have different symptoms. Passing a bare `OFF_*` as a `shared::cta` operand, without `smem_base`, is off by exactly `0x400` = 1 KiB in rank 0; an offset below `0x400` (the control region and `OFF_SMEM_CD`) lands in the reserved kilobyte; `OFF_SMEM_A` and `OFF_SMEM_B` land 1 KiB too low, in the last C/D stage and the last A stage. In ranks 1-3 it is off by `0x1000400` / `0x2000400` / `0x3000400` (16 / 32 / 48 MiB + 1 KiB) and carries rank 0's rank bits instead of this CTA's (a `shared::cluster` operand would name rank 0's window; for a `shared::cta` operand outside the executing CTA's window the PTX ISA, 5.1.7, specifies nothing). Passing the 64-bit generic pointer where a 32-bit shared operand is expected is not an offset error at all: the generic address is truncated to 32 bits and becomes an arbitrary shared address or a fault.

### 5.7.2 What each `static_assert` protects

| Line | Assert | Protects | What breaks without it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 158 | `OFF_SMEM_A == 512 + 4 * 8192 + 512` | the 512-byte pad after the C/D stages (the empty `FusionStorage` padded to the epilogue storage's 512-byte alignment) | an A stage base off by 512 breaks the 1024-byte swizzle alignment and every A address |
| 159 | `OFF_SMEM_B == OFF_SMEM_A + 8 * 16384` | A and B stages are contiguous | B addresses and the B descriptor base |
| 160 | `kSmemBytes == OFF_SMEM_B + 8 * 8192` | the requested dynamic size equals the laid-out size | too small: the last B stages overrun; too large: wasted smem, fewer resident CTAs only if it crossed a boundary (here still 1 CTA/SM) |
| 161 | `kStageBytesAHalf == 64 * 64 * 2` | the multicast half equals one A box | the `+ 8192 y` destination and the 49152 transaction count |
| 162 | `OFF_SMEM_A % 1024 == 0`, `OFF_SMEM_B % 1024 == 0` | SW128 swizzle period | TMA writes and UMMA reads XOR with absolute address bits [7,10); a base not 1024-aligned shifts the pattern between writer and reader -> garbage operands |
| 163 | `OFF_SMEM_CD % 512 == 0` | SW128_32B period | same for the epilogue: the kernel's `st.shared` XOR and TMA's un-swizzle would disagree |
| 164 | `OFF_CLC_RESPONSE % 16 == 0`, `OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR % 4 == 0` | `ld.shared.b128` of the response needs a 16-byte aligned address; the b32 store of `tcgen05.alloc` needs 4 | undefined behaviour (PTX ISA 9.4, 6.4.1: the access may silently mask off low-order address bits, or the instruction may fault) |
| 165 | `0x400 + 230400 < 2^18` | the UMMA start-address field holds `(addr & 0x3FFFF) >> 4`: the encode mask spans `2^18` B = 256 KiB of `shared::cta` space (5.8.1) | nothing launchable on a B200 can violate it: the largest window is `0x400 + 232448 = 233472 < 262144`, and a kernel with `230400 + 30720 = 261120` B of shared memory could not be launched at all. The assert documents the 256 KiB span. It would fire only if `kSmemBaseLow24` or the offset table were changed to assume a base high enough to wrap; an address at or above 256 KiB would wrap silently inside the descriptor, and the MMA would read the wrong stage |
| 166 | `kThreads == 256`, `kMmaM == 256`, `kMmaN == 128`, `kKBlocks == 4` | the Section 4 configuration the rest of the file hard-codes | every loop bound and every descriptor increment |

## 5.8 `explicit.cu` Section 1, group 3: the UMMA descriptors

```
$ sed -n 168,177p explicit.cu
// tcgen05 LAYOUT  UMMA shared-memory descriptors (Section 7.6, D.7): 64-bit = {hi word constant, lo word = LBO (1 = 16 B) | (start_address >> 4)
// in a 14-bit field}. Per stage s and k-block kb the low word is lo_a = 0x10880 + 1024 s + 2 kb, lo_b = 0x12880 + 512 s + 2 kb (units of 16 B:
// 1024 = 16384 B, 512 = 8192 B, 2 = 32 B = 16 fp16 k values). Example, rank 0, s = 3, kb = 2: desc_a = 0x4000404000011484, desc_b = 0x4000404000012E84.
constexpr uint32_t kSmemDescHi  = 0x40004040u;   // SBO = 64 (1024 B) at [32,46), version = 1 at [46,48), layout_type = 2 (SWIZZLE_128B) at [61,64)
constexpr uint32_t kSmemDescLo0 = 0x00010000u;   // LBO = 1 (16 B) at [16,30); start address (addr >> 4) & 0x3FFF is OR'ed in at run time
constexpr uint32_t kInstrDesc   = kInstrDescConst;   // 0x10200010: c_format F32 (bit 4), n_dim 128 >> 3 = 16 at [17,23), m_dim 256 >> 4 = 16 at [24,29)
static_assert(((uint64_t(kSmemDescHi) << 32) | kSmemDescLo0) == kSmemDescConst, "D.7 descriptor constant 0x4000404000010000");
static_assert((64u | (1u << 14) | (2u << 29)) == kSmemDescHi, "SmemDescriptor high word (mma_sm100_desc.hpp:101-127)");
static_assert(((1u << 4) | (16u << 17) | (16u << 24)) == kInstrDesc, "InstrDescriptor bit map (mma_sm100_desc.hpp:416-443)");
static_assert(((kSmemBaseLow24 + OFF_SMEM_A) >> 4) == 0x880 && ((kSmemBaseLow24 + OFF_SMEM_B) >> 4) == 0x2880, "D.7: desc_a low word 0x10880, desc_b 0x12880 for the measured base");
```

`tcgen05.mma` does not take pointers to A and B. It takes two 64-bit *shared-memory descriptors*, which encode where an operand starts in shared memory and how its 8-row swizzle atoms are laid out, plus a 32-bit *instruction descriptor*, which encodes types, shapes and major-ness. The MMA unit walks the operand from the descriptor alone; the kernel's only job is to form the right bits. The table below reproduces the `SmemDescriptor` union of `mma_sm100_desc.hpp:101-127` (CUTLASS's bitfield names and ranges). The authoritative definition is PTX ISA Table 49, "Shared memory descriptor layout" (9.7.18.4.1), which draws some field boundaries differently. The two agree on every bit the kernel sets; the differences and the ISA's extra rules follow the table.

### 5.8.1 The 64-bit shared-memory descriptor

| Bits | Field (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp`) | Value here | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| [0,14) | `start_address_` = (shared address >> 4) | A: `(smem_base + 33792 + 16384 s + 32 kb) >> 4`, masked to 14 bits; B: `(smem_base + 164864 + 8192 s + 32 kb) >> 4` | 16-byte units (the 4 LSBs are "not included", so operands must be 16-byte aligned). The 14 encoded bits, the ISA's `(x & 0x3FFFF) >> 4`, span 256 KiB (5.7.2, `:165`). The mask `& 0x3FFF` drops the rank bits [24,26) of `smem_base`, so the descriptor is rank-independent: the leader's MMA reads the *same CTA-relative offset* in both CTAs of the pair (note B.6) |
| [14,16) | unused | 0 | |
| [16,30) | `leading_byte_offset_` (LBO) >> 4 | 1 (= 16 B) | `make_umma_desc` sets `leading_byte_offset_ = stride_10 = 1` for a swizzled K-major canonical layout (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp:831-832`, with `expected_stride_10 = 1` asserted a few lines above); for K-major SW128 the K extent of one MMA (16 fp16 = 32 B) lies inside one 128-byte row, so the field carries the canonical placeholder rather than a real stride (my analysis of the canonical-layout comment at `:801-809`) |
| [30,32) | unused | 0 | |
| [32,46) | `stride_byte_offset_` (SBO) >> 4 | 64 (= 1024 B) | the byte distance between consecutive 8-row swizzle atoms along M/N: 8 rows x 128 B = 1024 B (`Layout_K_SW128_Atom_Bits`: `Shape<_8,_1024>`, `mma_traits_sm90_gmma.hpp:84`); the MMA's 128 (A) or 64 (B) rows are 16 or 8 such atoms |
| [46,48) | `version_` | 1 | "Set the version for blackwell" (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp:746`); Hopper's wgmma descriptor had 0 here |
| [48,49) | unused | 0 | |
| [49,52) | `base_offset_` | 0 | the swizzle phase of the repeating pattern's start address (9.7.18.4.1); 0 is valid because every stage base is 1024-byte aligned (`:757-758`, `constexpr uint8_t base_offset = 0`), and advancing the start address by 32/64/96 B for `kb` does not touch address bits [7,10) |
| [52,53) | `lbo_mode_` | 0 | "legacy mode by default" (`:747`) |
| [53,61) | unused | 0 | |
| [61,64) | `layout_type_` | 2 = `SWIZZLE_128B` | `enum class LayoutType { SWIZZLE_NONE = 0, SWIZZLE_128B_BASE32B = 1, SWIZZLE_128B = 2, SWIZZLE_64B = 4, SWIZZLE_32B = 6 }` (`:82-88`); it tells the MMA unit to apply the same 16-byte-chunk XOR that TMA applied on write |

**What PTX ISA Table 49 says, where it differs from the union, and the rules you need for other layouts.** The ISA defines bits 0-14 (15 bits) as "matrix-descriptor-encode (Matrix start address)", bit 15 "Reserved - Must be 0", and bits 16-30 (15 bits) as the encoded leading-dimension byte offset (relative) *or* byte address (absolute), with bit 31 reserved. Bits 32-45 hold the encoded SBO; bits 46-48 (3 bits) a "Fixed constant value of 0b001"; bits 49-51 the "Matrix base offset"; bit 52 the leading-dimension stride mode (0 relative offset, 1 absolute address); bit 53 the `lut::b` "Matrix B K_Segment start offset" (decompression only, 0 here); bits 54-60 fixed 0; bits 61-63 the swizzle mode ("0. No swizzling 1. 128-Byte with 32B atomic swizzling 2. 128-Byte swizzling 4. 64-Byte swizzling 6. 32-Byte swizzling"; 3, 5, 7 invalid), "where matrix-descriptor-encode(x) = (x & 0x3FFFF) >> 4". CUTLASS's 14-bit `start_address_` plus 2 unused bits, and its 14-bit LBO plus 2 unused bits, are the same bits under a narrower name; its `version_ = 1` at [46,48) is bit 46 of the ISA's fixed `0b001`. So the 256 KiB span of the start address is a property of the encode mask `0x3FFFF`, not of a "14-bit field" as such; the assert at `:165` is written against the span. The ISA adds three rules. The kernel satisfies them by construction, but you must check them when you encode a different layout. (1) "The following must be 16-byte aligned: Matrix start address, Leading dimension byte offset, Stride dimension byte offset", hence the `>> 4`. (2) The base offset "is 0 when the repeating pattern of the specified swizzling mode starts" on a 1024-byte boundary for 128-byte swizzle, 512-byte for 64-byte swizzle, 256-byte for 32-byte swizzle (Table 50); "Otherwise, the base offset must be a non-zero value, computed using the following formula: base offset = (pattern start addr >> 0x7) & 0x7". The 1024-byte alignment of every A/B stage base (5.7.2, line 162) is what lets CUTLASS hard-code `base_offset = 0`. (3) "The byte address mode for the leading dimension stride is supported on sm_103a", so on the B200 the LBO is always a relative offset (`lbo_mode_ = 0`).

Assembling the constant high word: SBO `64 = 0x40` at hi bits [0,14); version `1 << 14 = 0x4000`; layout type `2` in the 3-bit field [61,64) is `0b010`, i.e. global bit 62 = hi bit 30 = `0x40000000`. Sum: `0x40004040`, which is the second `static_assert` (`64u | (1u << 14) | (2u << 29)`: `2 << 29 = 1 << 30`). The constant low word is LBO `1 << 16 = 0x10000`. Together `0x4000404000010000 = kSmemDescConst` (first assert).

The run-time part is the start address. For the measured base `0x400`: `(0x400 + 33792) >> 4 = 0x8800 >> 4 = 0x880` and `(0x400 + 164864) >> 4 = 0x28800 >> 4 = 0x2880` (fourth assert), so the stage-0, k-block-0 low words are `0x10880` and `0x12880`, and

```
lo_a(s, kb) = 0x10880 + 1024 s + 2 kb        (16384 B per stage = 1024 units; 32 B per k-block = 2 units)
lo_b(s, kb) = 0x12880 +  512 s + 2 kb        ( 8192 B per stage =  512 units)
```

**Worked example, recomputed (rank 0, `s = 3`, `kb = 2`).** A: shared address `0x400 + 33792 + 3 x 16384 + 2 x 32 = 0x400 + 0x8400 + 0xC000 + 0x40 = 0x14840`; `>> 4 = 0x1484`; `& 0x3FFF = 0x1484` (fits); `lo = 0x10000 | 0x1484 = 0x11484`; `desc_a = 0x40004040_00011484`. Check with the increment form: `0x10880 + 3 x 1024 + 4 = 0x10880 + 0xC00 + 0x4 = 0x11484`. B: `0x400 + 164864 + 3 x 8192 + 64 = 0x400 + 0x28400 + 0x6000 + 0x40 = 0x2E840`; `>> 4 = 0x2E84`; `lo = 0x12E84`; `desc_b = 0x40004040_00012E84`; increment form `0x12880 + 3 x 512 + 4 = 0x12880 + 0x600 + 0x4 = 0x12E84`. Both match the comment and the measured K3 records (`desc_a = 0x4000404000010880` at `s = 0, kb = 0`, `+2` per k-block, `+0x400` A / `+0x200` B per stage; note D.1 D7).

How the kernel builds them (`explicit.cu:896-897`, `:928-929`, `:933-934`): once per role entry, `desc_lo_a = kSmemDescLo0 | (((smem_base + OFF_SMEM_A) >> 4) & 0x3FFFu)`; per k-tile, `uint32_t const lo_a = desc_lo_a + 1024u * rs;` (`rs` the read stage); per k-block, `desc64(kSmemDescHi, lo_a + 2u * uint32_t(kb))`. The addition is on the 32-bit low word, not the 64-bit value, exactly as CUTLASS's `DescriptorIterator::operator+` does for nvcc <= 13.3 (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp:843-875`, the add at `:870`, commented at `:868`: "Use 32-bit calculation rather than 64-bit calculation as we only update part of desc"). In SASS this is one `ULEA` per operand per k-tile (`ULEA UR10, UR8, UR30, 0xa` for A, x1024; `ULEA UR12, UR8, UR31, 0x9` for B, x512), a `UIADD3 +2/+4/+6` per operand for k-blocks 1-3 (k-block 0 uses the `ULEA` result directly), and a `UMOV 0x40004040` high word per descriptor, eight per k-tile (measured, `sass_explicit.txt` `0x5270-0x5470`, note G.3; the baseline shows the same pattern, note D.2). Why the start address advances by 32 B per k-block inside a swizzled row: the descriptor's address is the *unswizzled* position of element (row 0, k = 16 kb). The hardware derives every other element's physical chunk by XORing with the row index, so stepping the base through the four 32-byte slices of the 128-byte row is the canonical way to iterate K; it is what `UMMA::smem_desc` iterators do.

### 5.8.2 The 32-bit instruction descriptor

PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.18.4.2, Table 51 ("Instruction descriptor format for .kind::tf32, .kind::f16, .kind::f8f6f4, .kind::i8 and .kind::ti16") defines the 32-bit word with the ISA's row names: `dtype (Matrix D type)` at bits 4-5 ("F16 = 0, F32 = 1"), `atype (Matrix A type)` at bits 7-9 ("F16 = 0, BF16 = 1" for `.kind::f16`), and so on. The table below uses the field names of CuTe's mirror `InstrDescriptor` (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp:416-443`), the vocabulary of the kernel's own comment (explicit.cu:173); the value is `0x10200010` (decimal 270532624, the `mov.b32` operand in the PTX, note Section 7.2):

| Bits | Field | Value | Meaning here |
|---|---|---|---|
| [0,2) | `sparse_id2_` | 0 | no sparsity metadata |
| [2,3) | `sparse_flag_` | 0 | dense |
| [3,4) | `saturate_` | 0 | no saturation (S8 only anyway) |
| [4,6) | `c_format_` | 1 = F32 | fp32 accumulator in TMEM (`0x10` = bit 4); "0 = F16. 1 = F32, 2 = S32" |
| [6,7) | unused | 0 | |
| [7,10) | `a_format_` | 0 = F16 | `F32F16Format`: "0 = F16, 1 = BF16, 2 = TF32" |
| [10,13) | `b_format_` | 0 = F16 | |
| [13,14) | `a_negate_` | 0 | |
| [14,15) | `b_negate_` | 0 | |
| [15,16) | `a_major_` | 0 = K-major | A is M x K row-major (K contiguous); "0 = K-major. 1 = MN-major" |
| [16,17) | `b_major_` | 0 = K-major | B is N x K with K contiguous (the harness's `ColumnMajor` B) |
| [17,23) | `n_dim_` = N >> 3 | 16 -> N = 128 | `0x200000` = 16 << 17; "3 LSBs not included. Valid values range from 1 (N=8) to 32 (N=256)" |
| [23,24) | unused | 0 | |
| [24,29) | `m_dim_` = M >> 4 | 16 -> M = 256 | `0x10000000` = 16 << 24; "4 LSBs not included. Valid values are: 4 (M=64), 8 (M=128), 16 (M=256)" |
| [29,30) | K dimension (an anonymous `: 1` in the union, `:436`) | 0 | PTX ISA Table 51 names bit 29 "K Dimension": for `.kind::f16` its value is "(Dense K=16 / Sparse K=32) = 0", and it is likewise 0 for `.kind::tf32` ("(Dense K=8 / Sparse K=16) = 0"); the `.kind::f8f6f4` cell lists two options, "(Dense K=32 / Sparse K=64) = 0" and "(Dense K=64) = 1" (the dense K = 64 shapes that Table 48 allows for `.e4m3`/`.e5m2` only), and the merged `.kind::i8`/`.kind::ti16` cell reads "NA"; the 9.7.18.4.2.1 Target ISA Note restricts bit 29 to "sm_107f or higher in the same family", so the K = 64 option does not exist on the B200 (sm_100a). CUTLASS leaves the bit unnamed; `make_instr_desc` (`:482-506`) never sets it, and every MMA built with this union (the f16/bf16, tf32, i8 and f8f6f4 traits of `mma_traits_sm100.hpp`: dense K of 256 bits, sparse K of 512 bits per instruction) has a K extent whose Table 51 entry is "= 0" or "NA", so the bit is 0 for all of them (my analysis). K is therefore encoded as the fixed value 0, not as a free parameter |
| [30,32) | `max_shift_` | 0 | weight-stationary shift, unused |

`0x10000000 + 0x200000 + 0x10 = 0x10200010`, the third assert (`(1u << 4) | (16u << 17) | (16u << 24)`). Bit 29 fixes K at 16 elements per instruction for `kind::f16` (the atom's `Shape_MNK (256,128,16)`), which is why four instructions cover a 64-wide k-tile. The descriptor is identical for all 512 MMAs of a tile and for every tile; apart from the operand descriptors and the TMEM address, the only per-instruction variation is the `scale_c` predicate (0 for the first MMA of a tile, 1 afterwards; Chapter 9).

## 5.9 `explicit.cu` Section 1, group 4: protocol constants

```
$ sed -n 179,192p explicit.cu
// mbarrier  Protocol constants (Section 7.2): arrive counts and transaction bytes of every barrier, and the multicast masks
constexpr uint32_t kMainloopTxBytes  = 2 * (kStageBytesA + kStageBytesB);   // 49152: six 8192-byte boxes per stage credit the leader
constexpr uint32_t kClcTxBytes       = 16;
constexpr uint32_t kMainFullCount    = 1, kMainEmptyCount = 2;      // 2/2 + 2/1 - 1
constexpr uint32_t kClcFullCount     = 1, kClcEmptyCount  = 800;    // 32 + 4 * (32 + 128 + 32); beta = 0
constexpr uint32_t kAccFullCount     = 1, kAccEmptyCount  = 256;    // 2 x 128 epilogue threads
constexpr uint32_t kThrottleCount    = 32, kTmemDeallocCount = 32;
constexpr uint16_t kMainloopReleaseMask = 0xF;                       // calculate_multicast_mask<kRowCol> (sm100_pipeline.hpp:57-91)
constexpr uint32_t kPeerBitMask      = 0xFEFFFFFFu;                  // cute::Sm100MmaPeerBitMask (copy_sm100_tma.hpp:45); nvcc folds it to 0xFEFFFFF8
constexpr uint64_t kCacheHintEvictNormal = 0x1000000000000000ull;    // TMA::CacheHintSm100::EVICT_NORMAL = Sm100MemDescDefault
constexpr uint32_t kWaitTicks        = 0x989680u;                    // ClusterBarrier::wait suspend-time hint (barrier.h:415)
constexpr uint32_t kBarEpilogue      = 1, kBarTmemAlloc = 6;         // ReservedNamedBarriers (barrier.h:169-178)
constexpr uint32_t kEpilogueThreads  = 128, kTmemAllocBarThreads = 160;
static_assert(kMainloopTxBytes == 49152 && kClcEmptyCount == 32 + 4 * (32 + 128 + 32), "Section 7.2 counts");
```

Chapter 4 explains the protocol these numbers implement; the rows below keep what Chapter 4 does not already derive (all derived from the sources named, matching note Section 7.2):

| Constant | Value | Derivation |
|---|---|---|
| `kClcTxBytes` | 16 | one CLC response is a 16-byte `b128` (`struct CLCResponse { uint32_t data[4] = {0}; };`, `sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:74`) |
| `kMainloopReleaseMask` | `0xF` | `calculate_multicast_mask<kRowCol>` (`sm100_pipeline.hpp:57-91`): every CTA in the same MMA row *or* column; with a 2 x 2 cluster and a 2 x 1 atom that is all four ranks, so each leader's commit releases the stage in every CTA. 16-bit because `tcgen05.commit ... multicast::cluster` takes a `.b16` CTA mask (`"h"` operand) |
| `kPeerBitMask` | `0xFEFFFFFF` | `cute::Sm100MmaPeerBitMask` (`copy_sm100_tma.hpp:45`): clears bit 24, the rank's bit 0, of a `shared::cta` address, turning "my barrier" into "the pair leader's barrier" (ranks `2y+1 -> 2y`; a no-op on even ranks). nvcc folds the known-zero low bits of the barrier address into the constant where it can. In the explicit kernel the literal `0xFEFFFFF8` (`and.b32 ..., -16777224`, the three alignment bits of an 8-byte-aligned barrier address folded in) survives only at the epilogue's accumulator release (SASS `0x44c0`). In the producer warp the mask was folded onto the hoisted 1024-byte-aligned barrier base as `& 0xFEFFFFF0` (PTX `-16777232`, SASS `ULOP3 ... 0xfefffff0` at `0x0c00`), equivalent for all `s <= 7` because the base's low four bits are zero and `8 s <= 56` cannot carry into bit 24 (fold measured, note G.3). The `-16777224` of note D.6 item 2 describes the CUTLASS baseline, which carries the `and` per k-tile. The `0xFEFFFFFF` and `0xFEFFFFF8` forms are semantically identical for every 8-byte-aligned barrier address; the `0xFEFFFFF0` form is not, and is correct here only on the hoisted base, as above (Chapter 2, Section 2.9.3) |
| `kCacheHintEvictNormal` | `0x1000000000000000` | `TMA::CacheHintSm100::EVICT_NORMAL` (`copy_sm90_desc.hpp:193-197`) = `cute::Sm100MemDescDefault` (`copy_sm100_tma.hpp:46`), the 64-bit L2 cache-policy operand of every `cp.async.bulk.tensor ... .L2::cache_hint` load; "normal" priority, the value CUTLASS passes by default for the mainloop loads. In SASS it is the register pair `{0x0, 0x10000000}` (note D.2) |
| `kWaitTicks` | `0x989680` = 10,000,000 | the suspend-time hint operand of `mbarrier.try_wait.parity` (`timeHint` in the PTX ISA; CUTLASS's local variable is `ticks`): a time limit in **nanoseconds** after which a suspended thread resumes even if the phase is incomplete, so the loop around it re-tests. PTX ISA, `mbarrier.test_wait`/`mbarrier.try_wait`: "Suspended thread resumes execution when the specified phase completes OR before the phase completes following a system-dependent time limit. The optional 32-bit unsigned integer operand timeHint specifies the time limit, in nanoseconds, that may be used for the time limit instead of the system-dependent limit". 10 ms is CUTLASS's "arbitrarily large" value (`barrier.h:414-415`). It is a hint, so a shorter system limit may wake the thread earlier. In SASS it becomes `NANOSLEEP.SYNCS 0x989680` in the retry loop (note D.2) |

The `static_assert` at `:192` re-derives the two counts that are easiest to get wrong (the transaction bytes and the 800).

## 5.10 `explicit.cu` Section 1, group 5: the CuTe swizzle cross-check

```
$ sed -n 194,204p explicit.cu
// [CHECK] LAYOUT  CuTe cross-check (compile time only, the only use of CuTe in this TU): the epilogue smem byte formula uses
// Swizzle<2,5,2> on byte offsets, bits [5,7) ^= bits [7,9) (Layout_MN_SW128_32B_Atom<float>, Section 4; B.3.3 step 17).
// Example: byte offset 0x1E4 (fp32 element 121 = row 25 of column 3 of a 32 x 4 fp32 atom column block) -> 0x1E4 ^ ((0x1E4 & 0x180) >> 2) = 0x1E4 ^ 0x60 = 0x184.
__host__ __device__ constexpr uint32_t epi_swz(uint32_t o) { return o ^ ((o & 0x180u) >> 2); }
using EpiSwizzle = cute::Swizzle<2, 5, 2>;
static_assert(EpiSwizzle::num_bits == 2 && EpiSwizzle::num_base == 5 && EpiSwizzle::num_shft == 2, "Swizzle<2,5,2>");
static_assert(EpiSwizzle::yyy_msk::value == 0x180 && EpiSwizzle::zzz_msk::value == 0x60, "Swizzle<2,5,2> masks: bits [7,9) fold into bits [5,7)");
static_assert(epi_swz(0x080u) == EpiSwizzle{}(0x080u) && epi_swz(0x1E4u) == EpiSwizzle{}(0x1E4u) && epi_swz(0x7FFCu) == EpiSwizzle{}(0x7FFCu),
              "epi_swz matches cute::Swizzle<2,5,2> (E.6.1) [confirm at first build: apply() is constexpr]");
// Swizzle<3,4,3> (A/B stages) is applied by the TMA unit on write and by the UMMA unit on read (SWIZZLE_128B); the kernel never computes it.
static_assert(cute::Swizzle<3, 4, 3>::yyy_msk::value == 0x380 && cute::Swizzle<3, 4, 3>::num_shft == 3, "Swizzle<3,4,3>: 16-byte chunk ^= row mod 8");
```

The `:196` comment's element 121 is `0x1E4 = 484 = 4 x 121 = 3 x 128 + 25 x 4`: row 25 of column 3 of the 32 x 4 atom (Section 5.10.2 works the example).

### 5.10.1 `cute::Swizzle<B, M, S>` in one picture

`cute/swizzle.hpp:42-96` defines the functor on an integer offset:

```
      0bxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxYYYxxxxxxxZZZxxxx          (the header's own picture, swizzle.hpp:43-47)
                                    ^--^  M = num_base : the M least-significant bits are left alone
                       ^-^       ^-^      B = num_bits : the width of the two masks
                         ^---------^      S = num_shft : the distance from the YYY mask down to the ZZZ mask

      bit_msk = (1 << B) - 1
      yyy_msk = bit_msk << (M + max(0, S))          the source bits
      zzz_msk = bit_msk << (M - min(0, S))          the target bits (for S > 0 this is bit_msk << M)
      apply(o) = o ^ ((o & yyy_msk) >> S)           ZZZ ^= YYY   (swizzle.hpp:78: offset ^ shiftr(offset & yyy_msk{}, msk_sft{}))
```

So a swizzle XORs a B-bit field at bit position `M + S` into the B-bit field at bit position `M`, and leaves everything else alone. Why it is written this way for GPU shared memory: the low `M` bits address bytes inside one access unit (a 16- or 32-byte chunk), the `ZZZ` bits select the chunk within a line, and the `YYY` bits are the line (row) index. XORing the chunk index with the row index changes, from one row to the next, the bank a given logical chunk lands in, so a column of chunks does not pile onto one bank group. CUTLASS names each swizzle by its `(B, M, S)`:

| Swizzle | `bit_msk` | `yyy_msk` (source bits) | `zzz_msk` (target bits) | Plain English | TMA enumerator |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Swizzle<3,4,3>` | 7 | `7 << 7 = 0x380`, bits [7,10) | `7 << 4 = 0x70`, bits [4,7) | the 16-byte chunk index (3 bits, 8 chunks of a 128-byte line) ^= line index mod 8 | `SWIZZLE_128B` |
| `Swizzle<2,5,2>` | 3 | `3 << 7 = 0x180`, bits [7,9) | `3 << 5 = 0x60`, bits [5,7) | the 32-byte chunk index (2 bits, 4 chunks of a 128-byte line) ^= line index mod 4 | `SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B` |

Both have the line index at bit 7 because both have 128-byte lines; they differ in the chunk size (16 B vs 32 B), hence `M = 4` vs `M = 5` and `B = 3` vs `B = 2`. `S = B` in both, which is what makes the two fields adjacent.

Why the hardware keys the XOR on *absolute* shared-address bits and not on a buffer-relative row index: the TMA unit and the UMMA unit see only addresses, a destination or start address plus a swizzle mode, never a CuTe layout or a buffer base. Both compute the physical chunk from bits [7,10) (SW128) or [7,9) (SW128_32B) of the address they are handed. Three facts stated separately in this chapter follow from this one rule. The A/B stage bases must be 1024-byte aligned and the C/D bases 512-byte aligned (`explicit.cu:162-163`; 5.4.3 (2), 5.7.2), so that the address bits the hardware XORs with are the row index the layout means; the same alignment is what lets the UMMA descriptor's `base_offset` be 0 (5.8.1) instead of `(pattern start >> 7) & 7`. The epilogue's `st.shared` must apply the same XOR to the same address bits (`epi_swz`, `:197`), so that TMA's un-swizzle on the way out recovers the logical row order within each column (5.10.2).

### 5.10.2 The asserts, by hand

- `:199` pins the three template parameters.
- `:200` checks the masks: for `<2,5,2>`, `bit_msk = 3`, `yyy_msk = 3 << (5 + 2) = 3 << 7 = 0x180`, `zzz_msk = 3 << (5 - 0) = 0x60`. Correct.
- `:197` is the hand-written formula `epi_swz(o) = o ^ ((o & 0x180) >> 2)`, i.e. `apply` with these masks and `S = 2`. `:201` checks it against the real `cute::Swizzle` at three points (this works because `Swizzle::apply` is `constexpr`, `swizzle.hpp:73-79`):
  - `0x080`: `0x080 & 0x180 = 0x080`; `>> 2 = 0x20`; `0x080 ^ 0x20 = 0x0A0`. (Line 1, chunk 0 -> chunk 1.)
  - `0x1E4` (the comment's example): `0x1E4 = 0b1_1110_0100`; `& 0x180 = 0x180` (bits 7 and 8 set: line 3 of the 4-line period); `>> 2 = 0x60`; `0x1E4 ^ 0x60 = 0b1_1000_0100 = 0x184`. In atom terms `0x1E4 = 484 = 4 x 121`: element 121 of a 32 x 4 fp32 atom block, i.e. line `n = 3` (bytes 384..511), byte 100 within the line, chunk `100 >> 5 = 3`, offset 4 inside the chunk; swizzled chunk `3 ^ 3 = 0`, so the physical byte is `384 + 0 + 4 = 388 = 0x184`.
  - `0x7FFC`: `& 0x180 = 0x180`; `^ 0x60` -> `0x7F9C`. (The last word of the whole 32768-byte four-stage C/D region, `OFF_SMEM_CD`-relative: `4 x 8192 - 4 = 32764 = 0x7FFC`; the last word of a single 8192-byte stage would be `0x1FFC`.)
- `:204` checks `Swizzle<3,4,3>`: `yyy_msk = 7 << (4 + 3) = 0x380` and `S = 3`, which is the "16-byte chunk ^= row mod 8" statement of Sections 5.4.3 and 5.6.

Why the kernel needs `Swizzle<2,5,2>` in software but not `Swizzle<3,4,3>`: TMA writes the A/B stages and the MMA unit reads them, two hardware agents that both know `SWIZZLE_128B`, so no thread ever touches those bytes. *Threads* write the C/D stage (`st.shared.b32` in the epilogue) and TMA reads it with `SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B`. TMA un-permutes the 32-byte chunks on the way out, so the threads must store each value at the permuted position; otherwise, within output column `j` (one 128-byte line of the stage), box row `m` would receive the data of row `m ^ (8 (j & 3))`: the eight-row chunks of a line are permuted, never the columns. Apart from `cute::get` in the host-only header bridge (`explicit.hpp:107-110`, a template the kernel TU never instantiates), this is the only piece of CuTe the TU uses, and only at compile time (`explicit.cu:17-18`): the device code evaluates the integer formula, never a `cute::Layout`.

## 5.11 Section 2 in brief: the trace-only types

```
$ sed -n 206,240p explicit.cu
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
// 2. [TRACE]  Trace-only diagnostics (E.7.2 B1/B2, E.7.3): hang records in a host-mapped pinned buffer, heartbeats, K_TAIL.
//    With the toggle off this section reduces to the two #else lines: EXPLICIT_WAIT is the plain blocking wait and the CLC
//    record kinds are 0 (clc_consume then emits nothing).
///////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)   // [TRACE]
...   // [TRACE] branch elided (compiled out in the performance binary)
#else
// [PROD] with the toggle off: the baseline's mbarrier.try_wait.parity loop with the 0x989680 suspend hint (W6); site/tile/q vanish
#define EXPLICIT_WAIT(addr, parity, site, tile, q) mbar_wait((addr), (parity))
constexpr uint32_t K_CLC_SCHED_KIND = 0u;             // no records with the toggle off
constexpr uint32_t K_CLC_MMA_KIND   = 0u;
#endif
```

What matters for the production kernel: with the toggle off, `EXPLICIT_WAIT(addr, parity, site, tile, q)` *is* `mbar_wait(addr, parity)`, the W6 wrapper that copies `ClusterBarrier::wait` (`barrier.h:410-430`). `site`, `tile`, `q` vanish in the preprocessor, and `K_CLC_SCHED_KIND = K_CLC_MMA_KIND = 0` make the two traced call sites (`:853`, `:913`) the same `clc_consume<0>` as the untraced ones (`:793`, `:1028`); the recording block inside `clc_consume` (`:695-704`) is under the same toggle `#if`, so no instantiation emits a record (7.4.1). The SASS of two toggle-off builds is byte-identical (measured, note G.3 D6). The `__device__` variable `g_explicit_hang_buf` is absent from the production cubin: it is declared only under `#if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)` (`explicit.cu:211`, `:229`; derived from the source; the note names the variable only once, in F.2 item 2, not in G.3's inventory). Consistent with that, G.3's resource line reports `GLOBAL:10`, ten one-byte libcu++ tag objects that no instruction of the kernel references. Nothing in Section 2 costs an instruction or a byte of global memory in the binary you time.

# Chapter 6. The Vocabulary: PTX Wrappers W1-W37, Character by Character

Chapter 4 explained the protocol these wrappers implement. Chapter 5 defined the constants they consume (`OFF_*`, `kPeerBitMask`, the counts and masks). Chapters 7-11 show the call sites in their roles. This chapter is the dictionary between those levels.

---

## 6.0 Why a vocabulary layer, and how to read an inline-asm statement

### 6.0.1 The design rule of Section 3

The banner at explicit.cu:243-254 states the contract:

```
// 3. [PROD]  E.6.2 PTX wrappers (W1-W37); each asm string is copied verbatim from the CUTLASS source named in its comment,
//    so the emitted PTX is identical to the CUTLASS kernel's (verified row by row in G.3). Grouped by hardware family:
//      warp/cluster identity  W1 (shfl), W2 (elect.sync), W3/W4 (%cluster_ctarank, %cluster_ctaid)
//      mbarrier               W5 init, W6 blocking wait, W7 peek, W8 test_wait, W9 local arrive, W10 remote arrive (mapa),
//                             W11 pair-leader arrive (peer bit), W12 local arrive.expect_tx, W13 remote arrive.expect_tx
//      fences                 W14 fence.mbarrier_init, W15 fence.proxy.async (generic-proxy writes -> async proxy)
//      cluster / named bars   W16/W17 barrier.cluster arrive/wait, W18/W19 bar.sync / bar.arrive
//      TMA                    W20 prefetch.tensormap, W21 2SM multicast load, W22 2SM load, W23 store, W24 commit_group, W25 wait_group.read
//      tcgen05                W26-W28 alloc/dealloc/relinquish, W29 mma, W30 commit (multicast), W31 ld 32x32b.x16, W32 wait::ld
//      CLC                    W33 try_cancel (the query), W34 decode (is_canceled, get_first_ctaid)
//      GDC                    W35 griddepcontrol.wait, W36 launch_dependents; W37 = __syncwarp()
//    A wrapper does exactly one thing; the protocol (who calls it, on which barrier, with which count/parity) lives in sections 5-10.
```

Three consequences shape everything below.

1. **One asm string per wrapper (W1 and W37 are intrinsics), copied from CUTLASS.** The explicit kernel's claim is the same PTX with no abstraction layer. Where the CUTLASS function does more than emit one instruction (an election, an `if (pred)`, a fence, an address mask), that extra work moves to the call site in C++ and the wrapper stays a single instruction. Four relocations occur.
   - W10: the `if (pred)` of `ClusterBarrier::arrive(ptr, cta_id, pred)` (barrier.h:489).
   - W21/W22: the `& Sm100MmaPeerBitMask` that `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_3D::copy` and `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_MULTICAST_3D::copy` apply to the barrier address (copy_sm100_tma.hpp:115 and :292), hoisted by the kernel to `full_masked_base` (explicit.cu:770).
   - W29/W30: the `elect_one_sync()` of `fma` and of `umma_arrive_multicast_2x1SM` (mma_sm100_umma.hpp:570 and barrier.h:851).
   - W34: the `fence_view_async_shared()` of `work_tile_info_from_clc_response` (sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:430).

   W11 alone keeps a non-asm step inside: `umma_arrive_2x1SM_sm0` applies `& cute::Sm100MmaPeerBitMask` (barrier.h:909), which W11 writes as `& kPeerBitMask` (explicit.cu:371), and W11's call site is a single per-thread arrive with nothing to hoist.

2. **The address-space rule.** Every asm operand that names shared memory is a 32-bit `shared::cta` address `smem_base + OFF_*`; every C++ dereference uses the generic pointer `smem + OFF_*` (explicit.cu:22-23). The wrappers therefore take `uint32_t` addresses for shared memory, never pointers to it (the only pointer arguments, the `desc_ptr` of W20-W23, are generic addresses of the tensor maps in parameter space, Section 6.6.1). `smem_u32` (Section 6.1) is the only bridge.

3. **Convergence is the caller's problem.** Several instructions (`elect.sync`, every `.sync.aligned`, `barrier.cluster.*.aligned`, `bar.sync`) require the whole warp to execute them together. The wrappers do not check this. The role functions keep every branch around a wrapper warp-uniform (`is_leader`, `is_cta0`, `warp_idx == k`, `e == 7`). The only lane-divergent predicates are election results (a fresh `elect_one_sync()`, or the prologue's `lane_pred` reused as `is_leader_lane` around W12 at explicit.cu:736 and around the prefetches at :1113-1119) and the `lane < 4` that W13 turns into a PTX predicate inside its asm.

### 6.0.2 Anatomy of an `asm volatile` statement

Every wrapper has the GCC/nvcc form

```
asm volatile("template string" : output operands : input operands : clobbers);
```

- **Template string.** PTX text. `%0`, `%1`, ... are operand placeholders, numbered in order of appearance in the operand lists, outputs first. A literal `%` (needed for PTX special registers such as `%cluster_ctarank` and for PTX register names such as `%rx`) is written `%%`. `\n\t` separates PTX statements. The compiler concatenates adjacent string literals (translation phase 6 of C/C++, after preprocessing), which is why a PTX template can be split across source lines.
- **`{ ... }`.** A PTX statement block. Register declarations (`.reg .pred P1;`) and labels (`LAB_WAIT:`) inside the braces are local to the block, so W6 can be inlined at a dozen call sites without ptxas complaining about duplicate symbols (note E.6.2: "write the blocking wait and the election with PTX labels/registers inside `{ }` so they can be inlined many times"). Braces are *required* only where the template declares local registers or labels: W2, W6, W7, W8, W10, W13, W29, W34. W3/W4, W16-W26, W28, W31 and W35/W36 have no braces (W1 and W37 are intrinsics, not asm). W5, W9, W11, W12, W14, W15, W27, W30, W32 and W33 carry harmless braces around a single instruction with no local name, because the CUTLASS source does.
- **Constraint letters** (note E.6.2, matching the nvcc inline-PTX documentation):

| Constraint | PTX type | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `"r"` | 32-bit `.b32`/`.u32`/`.s32` register | addresses, counts, parities, coordinates, idesc, TMEM address |
| `"l"` | 64-bit `.b64` register | tensor-map generic addresses, UMMA descriptors, cache hint |
| `"h"` | 16-bit `.b16` register | the three multicast masks (W21, W30): the ISA's default `ctaMask` width is 16 bits (`::16b`; a `::32b` form exists, Section 6.6.3) |
| `"n"` | integer immediate | `cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read N` (W25): the ISA wants a constant |
| `"=r"` | write-only output | W3/W4, W7, W8, W31, W34: values the asm always writes (W34's `x0/y0/z0` are the one exception, Section 6.8.3) |
| `"+r"` | read-write output | W2 only (Section 6.2.2 explains why) |

In the emitted PTX (measured, `trace_out_v2/ptx_explicit.txt`, note G.3) the kernel declares four register classes, `.reg .pred %p<92>; .reg .b16 %rs<7>; .reg .b32 %r<1014>; .reg .b64 %rd<29>;` (ptx_explicit.txt:7-10). `"r"` operands become `%r` (`.b32`), `"l"` operands `%rd` (`.b64`), `"h"` operands `%rs` (`.b16`), and `"n"` is pasted into the instruction text as a literal (`cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read 1`). The `.b16` class is tiny and fully accounted for: `%rs6` is `a_mcast_mask` at both A-load sites (:556, :658); `%rs3` is the constant 15 = `kMainloopReleaseMask` (`mov.b16 %rs3, 15;` at :1384, used by the mainloop commit at :1387); `%rs4` is `acc_commit_mask` (the accumulator commit at :1415); `%rs1`, `%rs2`, `%rs5` are rank bookkeeping narrowed to 16 bits: `%rs2` is the rank, `%rs1 = %rs2 & 1` (`rank & 1`, the negation of `is_leader`) and `%rs5 = %rs1 & 255`; `setp.ne.b16` tests `%rs1` or `%rs5` against 0 (:34-35, :406-407, :1112, :1430, :1516). The baseline declares `%rs<16>` for the same reason plus its C path.

- **`volatile`.** Tells the compiler the statement has side effects it cannot see. The compiler must not delete the statement when its outputs are unused, must not merge it with an identical statement (two consecutive `elect.sync` stay two instructions), and must not hoist it out of a loop. For a wait (`mbarrier.try_wait`) this is essential: without `volatile` the compiler could evaluate the "pure" asm once and spin on a stale token. Every wrapper in Section 3 is `volatile`, as are the CUTLASS originals.
- **`"memory"` clobber.** Tells the compiler the asm may read or write any memory: pending C++ stores must be issued before it, and values loaded before it must be reloaded after it. It is a *compiler* fence, not a hardware one. Section 3 follows the CUTLASS origin exactly (note E.6.2):

| Has `"memory"` | Lacks `"memory"` |
|---|---|
| W5-W15 (all mbarrier operations and both fences), W18/W19 (`bar.sync`/`bar.arrive`), W20 (prefetch), W21-W23 (TMA load/store), W25 (`wait_group.read`), W30 (`tcgen05.commit`), W32 (`tcgen05.wait::ld`), W34 (CLC decode), W35 (`griddepcontrol.wait`) | W2 (`elect.sync`), W3/W4 (special registers), W16/W17 (`barrier.cluster.*`), W24 (`commit_group`), W26-W28 (TMEM alloc/dealloc/relinquish), W29 (`tcgen05.mma`), W31 (`tcgen05.ld`), W33 (`try_cancel`), W36 (`launch_dependents`) |

The right column is safe for the following reasons (my analysis, following the CUTLASS authors' choices). W2-W4 only produce register values. W29, W31 and W33 have register-only operands (W31's sixteen `"=r"` outputs included); the shared memory (W29, W33) or tensor memory (W31) they touch is accessed asynchronously and is synchronised by mbarrier waits (W29, W33) or by W32's `tcgen05.wait::ld` (W31), which do carry the clobber. W24 merely groups prior bulk operations whose issuing asm (W23) already has the clobber. W36 is a scheduling hint. W16/W17 provide the cluster rendezvous, but the memory ordering of the preceding `mbarrier.init`s is carried by W14, which has the clobber and follows each of the four init groups before W16 (the exception is the `tmem_dealloc` init at explicit.cu:1165-1167, after the fourth W14 with no fence of its own, as in kernel :562-580; Section 11.5.4). The one subtle case is W26: `tcgen05.alloc` writes the TMEM base address into shared memory, and the kernel then reads it with a plain C++ load (explicit.cu:888). The ordering holds because W19 (`bar.arrive`, with the clobber) sits between the alloc and the load. That is the argument of note E.6.4 (`mma_role` paragraph: the load "is guaranteed by the `"memory"` clobber of the intervening `bar.arrive 6,160` (W19, barrier.h:308), which W19 must keep per E.6.2"); W37 (`__syncwarp()`, also a compiler barrier) sits there too and would suffice on its own (my addition to the note's argument). In the left column, the clobber matters most for W25: after `wait_group.read 1` the epilogue overwrites a stage released by an earlier `wait_group.read` (subtile `e + 1` writes stage `(e + 1) % 4`, last read by group `e - 3`, Section 3.5.4) with ordinary `st.shared` through a C++ pointer (explicit.cu:1047), and without the clobber nothing in W25 itself would stop the compiler from hoisting those stores above the wait (in this kernel the clobber-carrying `bar.sync 1, 128` of W18 at explicit.cu:1071 also separates the wait from the next subtile's stores, and only warp 4 executes the wait).

### 6.0.3 The family map and the dynamic counts you will see

The per-tile counts quoted below are for one CTA on the executed path of the fixed run (beta = 0, 128 k-tiles per tile). They are derived from the role code (Chapters 7-10) and match the note's inventory (note B.5, 7.5-7.7). "Pair leader" means the even rank, which alone issues MMAs and `expect_tx`; "rank 0" means the single CTA of each cluster that runs the scheduler warp. Measured quantities (SASS mnemonics, instruction counts) come from note D.2 and G.3.

---

## 6.1 Family 0: the address bridge, `smem_u32`

```
// cute::cast_smem_ptr_to_uint (cute/arch/util.hpp:93-108): the 32-bit shared::cta address of a generic pointer
__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t smem_u32(void const* p) { return static_cast<uint32_t>(__cvta_generic_to_shared(p)); }
```
(explicit.cu:257-258)

**Purpose.** Convert the generic pointer of the dynamic shared buffer into the 32-bit address that every `shared::cta` / `shared::cluster` asm operand of this kernel takes (PTX also accepts 64-bit shared addresses, ISA 6.4.1).

**Decomposition.** `__cvta_generic_to_shared` is the CUDA intrinsic for the PTX `cvta.to.shared` conversion: it subtracts the shared window base from the generic address and returns the offset inside the CTA's shared window. The cast to `uint32_t` drops the upper half, which is zero for a `shared::cta` address. There is no `asm` here: nvcc knows the intrinsic and, in this kernel, folds it into `mov.b32 %r, smem` plus the constant offset (`trace_out_v2/ptx_explicit.txt` has no `cvta.to.shared`, only four `cvta.param` for the tensor-map addresses; note B.6 observed the same of the CUTLASS kernel: "no `cvta.to.shared` instruction occurs in the compiled kernel").

**Caller.** explicit.cu:1098, once per thread: `uint32_t const smem_base = smem_u32(smem);`. Every other shared address in the kernel is derived from it: `smem_base + OFF_*`, or that address with bit 24 cleared to name the pair leader's barrier (`& kPeerBitMask`, explicit.cu:371, 770).

**What the value is.** Measured (note D.1 item D5): `0x400 + (rank << 24)`. The low 24 bits are the same in every CTA (the 1 KiB of system-reserved shared memory precedes the dynamic buffer); the cluster rank sits in byte 3. The kernel never assumes this (the comment at explicit.cu:1098 says "computed, never assumed"), but its *structure* is relied upon in two ways: the peer-bit mask clears bit 24 (W11, Section 6.3.7, and the producer's `full_masked_base`), and ptxas lowers `mapa` (W10, W13) to a byte-3 insert (note D.2: `PRMT ..., 0x654`).

**Pitfall.** A generic pointer passed where a 32-bit address is expected compiles (both are integers after a cast) and faults or silently addresses garbage at run time. The address-space rule of Section 6.0.1 is the defence: wrappers take `uint32_t` for shared memory, C++ dereferences take `char*`.

---

## 6.2 Family 1: warp and cluster identity, W1-W4

These four wrappers answer "who am I?" at warp and cluster granularity. W1, W3 and W4 run once per thread in the prologue (explicit.cu:1101, 1104, 1173-1174) and nowhere in the tile loop; W2 runs there too (1103) and at every election site in the `mbarrier.init` groups and in the producer, scheduler and MMA loops (the Callers table of Section 6.2.2).

### 6.2.1 W1 `warp_idx_sync`: a warp-uniform warp index

```
// W1 [warp]  cutlass::canonical_warp_idx_sync (cutlass.h:127-133)
__device__ __forceinline__ int warp_idx_sync() { return __shfl_sync(0xffffffff, static_cast<int>(threadIdx.x / 32), 0); }
```
(explicit.cu:260-261)

**Purpose.** Produce the warp index 0..7 in a form the compiler can prove is identical in all 32 lanes.

**Decomposition.** `threadIdx.x / 32` is already the same in every lane, but the compiler does not know that: each lane computed it from its own `threadIdx.x`. `__shfl_sync(0xffffffff, v, 0)` broadcasts lane 0's value to all lanes with the full mask (all 32 lanes must participate, so the warp must be converged, which it is at kernel entry). ptxas can prove the result warp-uniform (PTX carries no such mark; the SASS moves it into `UR20` with `R2UR` right after the `SHFL.IDX`), so every plain `if (warp_idx == k)` below becomes a uniform branch (the guards that also test `lane_pred` stay per-lane, 11.3.1) and the value lives in a uniform register. In the SASS it is one `SHFL.IDX`, and the role dispatch became a three-entry jump table (`BRXU`) that executes once per thread (note G.3).

The wrapper adds the `static_cast<int>`, writes `NumThreadsPerWarp` (= 32, cutlass.h:96) as the literal `32`, and drops the host-side `#else return 0;` branch; the shuffle itself is unchanged.

**Caller.** explicit.cu:1101 `int const warp_idx = warp_idx_sync();`. Count: once per thread.

### 6.2.2 W2 `elect_one_sync`: one lane, deterministically

```
// W2 [warp]  cute::elect_one_sync (cluster_sm90.hpp:180-197): pred is 1 in exactly one lane of the converged warp, 0 elsewhere
__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t elect_one_sync() {
  uint32_t pred = 0;
  uint32_t laneid = 0;
  asm volatile(
    "{\n"
    ".reg .b32 %%rx;\n"
    ".reg .pred %%px;\n"
    "     elect.sync %%rx|%%px, %2;\n"
    "@%%px mov.s32 %1, 1;\n"
    "     mov.s32 %0, %%rx;\n"
    "}\n"
    : "+r"(laneid), "+r"(pred)
    : "r"(0xFFFFFFFF));
  return pred;
}
```
(explicit.cu:263-278)

**Purpose.** Return 1 in exactly one lane of the warp and 0 in the other 31, so that a warp-wide instruction stream can issue a single TMA, MMA, commit or CLC query.

**Decomposition.**

| Text | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `.reg .b32 %%rx; .reg .pred %%px;` | block-local PTX registers; `%%` escapes the `%` of a PTX register name |
| `elect.sync %%rx\|%%px, %2;` | `elect.sync d\|p, membermask`: among the lanes named in `membermask` that execute the instruction, exactly one is elected; `d` receives its lane id in every lane, `p` is true in the elected lane only. `.sync` is mandatory: the instruction waits until all lanes in the mask have reached it, so the warp must be converged and every executing lane must be in the mask. The ISA guarantees determinism: "Election of a leader thread happens deterministically, i.e. the same leader thread is elected for the same membermask every time", and "The behavior is undefined if the executing thread is not in membermask" (PTX ISA 9.4, section 9.7.15.15). It does not say *which* lane wins, so the kernel must not assume lane 0. It may rely on every W2 call with mask `0xFFFFFFFF` in a given warp electing the same lane, which is what makes the re-election before `tcgen05.commit` safe (Section 6.7.3). |
| `%2` = `"r"(0xFFFFFFFF)` | the full warp mask, passed as a register: the ISA wants a 32-bit operand and CUTLASS writes it as a register, hence the PTX `mov.b32 %r, -1` the note observed (note 7.2, "Operand form") |
| `@%%px mov.s32 %1, 1;` | predicated: only the elected lane writes 1 into `pred` |
| `mov.s32 %0, %%rx;` | every lane copies the winner's lane id into `laneid` (unused by the kernel; kept for PTX parity) |

**Why `"+r"` with zero-initialised locals.** `pred` is written only in the elected lane. With a write-only `"=r"` constraint the compiler would assume the asm always writes the register and could drop the `pred = 0` initialisation as dead, leaving the 31 non-elected lanes with an indeterminate value. `"+r"` declares the register as read *and* written, so the initial 0 is materialised and survives in every lane the asm does not touch (note E.6.2: "the `+r` plus the zero init is what returns 0 in the non-elected lanes; `"=r"` would leave them indeterminate"). `laneid` gets the same treatment for symmetry with the source.

**`volatile`, no `"memory"`.** `volatile` keeps every election distinct: the kernel calls W2 four times in a row inside the k-tile loop of the MMA warp (one per `tcgen05.mma`, explicit.cu:932), and without `volatile` the compiler could reuse one result for all four. No memory is touched, so no clobber (CUTLASS has none either).

**Callers** (explicit.cu, grep of `elect_one_sync`):

| Line | Who | What the election guards |
|---|---|---|
| 1103 | every thread, prologue | `lane_pred`, reused for the tensormap prefetches (1113-1119), the producer's `is_leader_lane` (1192) and the `tmem_dealloc` init (1165) |
| 1125, 1136, 1146, 1156 | warps 0, 4, 5, 3 | one fresh election per `mbarrier.init` group (mirrors `initialize_barrier_array*_aligned`, barrier.h:123/134/146, each of which calls `elect_one_sync()` itself) |
| 740 | warp 2, per k-tile | the A + B TMA pair (one election for both loads, as `sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:619-622`) |
| 843 | rank-0 warp 1, per tile | the `clusterlaunchcontrol.try_cancel` |
| 932 | leader warp 0, per k-block | each `tcgen05.mma` |
| 942 | leader warp 0, per k-tile | the mainloop `tcgen05.commit` |
| 944 | leader warp 0, per tile | the accumulator `tcgen05.commit` |

**Count per tile per CTA.** Warp 2: 128. Pair leader's warp 0: 4 x 128 + 128 + 1 = 641 (note B.3.2 counts the same 641). Rank-0 warp 1: 1. Peer warp 0 and the epilogue warps: 0.

**What ptxas made of it (measured).** The PTX has 14 `elect.sync` sites in the explicit kernel. The SASS keeps 4 `ELECT` (prologue, two inside the `tcgen05.alloc` lowering, one near the exit sequence (0x55d0), origin unresolved; not the relinquish, which is warp-collective (NVIDIA internal, Section 6.7.1)) and none in the producer, MMA or scheduler loops: `UTMALDG`, `UTCHMMA`, `UTCBAR` and `UGETNEXTWORKID` are uniform-datapath instructions that issue once per warp whatever the lane count, so the election is folded away (note D.6 item 6, G.3). The PTX form remains the contract you write; the hardware makes it free.

**Pitfalls.** (1) Never call W2 under a lane-divergent branch. The ISA's `.sync` rule is that the executing thread waits "until all threads in the membermask execute the elect instruction". Lanes that are in the mask but skip the instruction therefore leave the others waiting (a hang), and a lane that executes it while *not* in the mask is undefined behaviour (both sentences in 9.7.15.15). In this kernel every W2 sits under warp-uniform conditions only. (2) Do not merge elections "to save instructions": the SASS shows they are already free, and merging changes the PTX contract (note E.6.7: "one per TMA A+B pair, per MMA, per commit, per CLC query"; E.6.2's W2 row: "one fresh call per TMA pair, per MMA, per commit, per CLC query"). (3) Conversely, do not "fix" the re-elections by carrying one lane predicate through the loop. The election is deterministic for a fixed mask, so re-electing per instruction is equivalent, and it is the form the baseline uses.

### 6.2.3 W3/W4 `cluster_ctarank`, `cluster_ctaid_x/y`: rank and coordinates

```
// W3/W4 [cluster]  cute::block_rank_in_cluster, cute::block_id_in_cluster (cluster_sm90.hpp:154-158, 126-132)
__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t cluster_ctarank() { uint32_t r; asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%cluster_ctarank;\n" : "=r"(r) :); return r; }
__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t cluster_ctaid_x() { uint32_t x; asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%cluster_ctaid.x;\n" : "=r"(x) :); return x; }
__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t cluster_ctaid_y() { uint32_t y; asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %%cluster_ctaid.y;\n" : "=r"(y) :); return y; }
```
(explicit.cu:280-283)

**Purpose.** Read the CTA's linear rank in the cluster and its (x, y) coordinates in the (2,2,1) cluster.

**Decomposition.** `mov.u32 %0, %%cluster_ctarank;` copies a PTX special register into a general register. `%cluster_ctarank` is the linear rank `x + 2y` (x fastest) for a (2,2,1) cluster; `%cluster_ctaid.x/.y` are the per-dimension coordinates. `"=r"` output, no inputs (the empty `:` after the output list), no clobber. The `.z` coordinate of the CuTe original is not needed (cluster z = 1) and is not read.

**Why both forms.** The rank drives the pair arithmetic (`is_leader = (rank & 1) == 0`, `peer = rank ^ 1`, explicit.cu:1106-1107) and the barrier addressing. The coordinates drive the multicast mask `0x5 << x` and the tile halves (`128 tm + 64 y`, `128 tn + 64 x`). For this cluster shape `x == rank & 1` and `y == rank >> 1` (comments at explicit.cu:1173-1174); the kernel reads both because the baseline does.

The wrapper splits the dim3-returning original into two scalar functions.

**Callers.** explicit.cu:1104 (`rank`), 1173 (`x`), 1174 (`y`). Count: once per thread each.

**Measured lowering.** `%cluster_ctarank` is `S2UR SR_CgaCtaId`; `%cluster_ctaid.x/.y` are not read from a special register but computed from `SR_CTAID.X/Y` and a driver constant table with `I2FP`/`FMUL`/`F2I` (note D.2, G.3; reading of the sequence inferred; D.6 item 14: the only two non-epilogue `FMUL` of the kernel).
