## 6.3 Family 2: mbarrier, W5-W13

### 6.3.1 Primer: the barrier region, the parity bound, and the three addressing forms

The kernel's 344-byte barrier region (offsets 0..343) holds 43 eight-byte slots; 33 are initialised in every CTA and used (the `full[]` and `acc_empty[]` slots only in the pair leader, the `clc_empty[]` and throttle slots only in rank 0: Sections 4.4.3, 4.4.5, 7.4.5, 8.4.4), and the ten slots at `OFF_EPI_LOAD_FULL` 128, `OFF_EPI_LOAD_EMPTY` 160 and `OFF_LOAD_ORDER` 192 belong to the beta != 0 path and are never initialised (explicit.cu:141-143; Chapter 5).

The parity definition (Chapter 2, Section 2.8.3) bounds what a waiter may ask: phases k and k + 2 have the same parity. The ring discipline keeps every barrier at most one phase ahead of its slowest waiter, whatever the ring depth, so the single parity bit never names the wrong phase (my analysis; Chapter 4, Section 4.2.3, 'Why a 1-bit parity is enough'; Section 4.3.3 walks the phases through a full wrap of the 8-stage ring).

Three addressing forms appear across the mbarrier wrappers:

- `.shared::cta` with a 32-bit address of the executing CTA's own barrier (the init W5, the waits W6-W8, the arrives W9 and W12);
- `.shared::cluster` with an address produced by `mapa` (W10, W13): "arrive on CTA `b`'s barrier at my offset";
- `.shared::cluster` with the peer-bit-masked address (W11): "arrive on the pair leader's barrier at my offset" without `mapa`.

The `_` in `mbarrier.arrive... _, [addr]` is the sink for the state token the instruction could return; a remote (`shared::cluster`) arrive cannot return a state at all, and the kernel never uses one, so every arrive discards it.

### 6.3.2 W5 `mbar_init`

```
// W5 [mbarrier]  ClusterBarrier::init (barrier.h:391-403)
__device__ __forceinline__ void mbar_init(uint32_t smem_addr, uint32_t arrive_count) {
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    "mbarrier.init.shared::cta.b64 [%1], %0; \n"
    "}"
    :
    : "r"(arrive_count), "r"(smem_addr)
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:285-294)

**Purpose.** Initialise one barrier with its expected arrival count (phase 0, tx-count 0).

**Decomposition.** `mbarrier.init` / `.shared::cta` (the address is in the executing CTA's window) / `.b64` (the object is 64 bits) / `[%1]` the address / `%0` the count. The count is `%0` because CUTLASS lists `"r"(arrive_count)` first; the wrapper keeps that order so the PTX text is identical. `"memory"`: the barrier is memory that later asm statements read, and the clobber stops the compiler from reordering ordinary smem traffic across the init.

CUTLASS's `CUTLASS_ASSERT(arrive_count != 0)` is a no-op under NDEBUG and is not copied.

**Callers and counts** (explicit.cu:1128-1166, prologue only, elected lane of the initialising warp):

| Lines | Warp | Barriers | Count | Why that count (Chapter 4 derives them; one line each) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1128-1129 | 0 | mainloop full[0..7] / empty[0..7] | 1 / 2 | one `arrive.expect_tx` by the leader lane; two `tcgen05.commit` (one per pair leader, mask 0xF) |
| 1139-1140 | 4 | CLC full[0..1] / empty[0..1] | 1 / 800 | one remote `arrive.expect_tx` per CTA; 32 + 4 x (32 + 32 + 128) consuming threads cluster-wide |
| 1149-1150 | 5 | accumulator full[0..3] / empty[0..3] | 1 / 256 | the leader's commit; 2 x 128 epilogue threads |
| 1159-1160 | 3 | throttle full[0..1] / empty[0..1] | 32 / 32 | one warp arrives on each side |
| 1166 | 0 (lane_pred) | tmem_dealloc | 32 | one warp of the peer, then of the leader |

33 inits per CTA. Measured in the explicit kernel (note G.3; `trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt`): 33 `SYNCS.EXCH.64` with the init word `{(0x100000 - count) << 1, (0x100000 - count) << 11}` at the byte-map offsets (Chapter 5, Section 5.7.1; note Section 6.2). 32 of them are unpredicated uniform instructions, because ptxas folded each group's election into the warp-index branch. Only the `tmem_dealloc` init keeps a predicate, `@!UP0 SYNCS.EXCH.64 URZ, [UR7+0x150], UR4` at `0x0790` (0x150 = 336 = `OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC`): it is the one init gated by the prologue `lane_pred` (explicit.cu:1165) instead of by a fresh election inside a warp-uniform block. The baseline has the same shape, 42 of 43 unpredicated with the dealloc init behind `VOTEU.ALL UP0; @!UP0` (note D.2, D.6 item 8). The `0x100000` in the init word is 2^20: the ISA bounds the expected-arrival count of a `.layout::v0` barrier to [1, 2^20 - 1] (PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.15.16.12 and Table 43), and the 32-bit `count` operand must fit the hardware field/range behind that bound (NVIDIA internal); that the measured word holds each count in a 20-bit field is inferred (the ISA calls the object opaque and does not give its bit layout). That it stores `2^20 - count` rather than `count` is read off the measured word, not documented by the ISA.

**Pitfall.** The inits must be visible cluster-wide before any remote arrive: hence W14 after each of the four pipeline init groups (the `tmem_dealloc` init, explicit.cu:1165-1167, has no fence of its own) and the W16/W17 rendezvous before any role starts (Sections 6.4, 6.5).

### 6.3.3 W6 `mbar_wait`: the blocking wait with a suspend hint

```
// W6 [mbarrier]  ClusterBarrier::wait (barrier.h:410-430): blocking try_wait loop with the suspend-time hint in a register
__device__ __forceinline__ void mbar_wait(uint32_t smem_addr, uint32_t phase) {
  uint32_t ticks = kWaitTicks;
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    ".reg .pred       P1; \n\t"
    "LAB_WAIT: \n\t"
    "mbarrier.try_wait.parity.shared::cta.b64 P1, [%0], %1, %2; \n\t"
    "@P1 bra DONE; \n\t"
    "bra     LAB_WAIT; \n\t"
    "DONE: \n\t"
    "}"
    :
    : "r"(smem_addr), "r"(phase), "r"(ticks)
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:296-311)

**Purpose.** Block until the barrier's phase with the given parity has completed.

**Decomposition.**

| Text | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `mbarrier.try_wait.parity.shared::cta.b64 P1, [%0], %1, %2;` | `try_wait` is the *potentially blocking* test: if the phase is not complete, the thread may be suspended until it completes or a time limit expires, and the instruction then returns `P1 = true` if the phase has completed and `P1 = false` if the limit expired first. `.parity` selects the parity form (operand `%1`). `%2` is the optional **timeHint** (ISA syntax: `mbarrier.try_wait.parity{...}.b64 waitComplete, [addr], phaseParity {, timeHint};`): "The optional 32-bit unsigned integer operand timeHint specifies the time limit, in nanoseconds, that may be used for the time limit instead of the system-dependent limit" (PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.15.16.19). Earlier ISA versions named it `suspendTimeHint`; the note (Section 7.2) and explicit.cu's comments (explicit.cu:189, 296) call it the suspend-time hint. |
| `kWaitTicks = 0x989680` (explicit.cu:189) | = 10,000,000 ns = 10 ms. CUTLASS's comment: "Arbitrarily large timer value after which try-wait expires and re-tries" (barrier.h:414). It is a hint for how long the hardware may park the thread before reporting failure; the loop then retries, so correctness does not depend on the value. |
| `@P1 bra DONE; bra LAB_WAIT; DONE:` | the retry loop, in PTX rather than C++ so that one asm statement is one wait. The labels are block-local (Section 6.0.2), which is why W6 can be inlined at every blocking-wait site. |
| `uint32_t ticks = kWaitTicks;` | a local, exactly as barrier.h:415, so the hint is a register operand (PTX `mov.b32 %r, 10000000`, note 7.2); the SASS turns it into the immediate of `NANOSLEEP.SYNCS 0x989680` |

**Why the retry loop is PTX, not C++.** A C++ `while (!mbar_try_wait(addr, parity)) {}` around a one-shot asm would be semantically equivalent. Two reasons keep the production wrapper in PTX. (a) Fidelity: `ClusterBarrier::wait` is one asm statement containing the loop. (b) The hint: a C++ primitive with the hint does exist, `__mbarrier_try_wait_parity(__mbarrier_t*, bool phase_parity, uint32_t max_sleep_nanosec)` in `cuda_awbarrier_primitives.h` (CUDA Programming Guide 13.4, 5.6.1.2; used in the 4.10.3 "CUDA C primitives" example), but it takes an `__mbarrier_t*` rather than the `uint32_t` shared address the wrappers carry, and CUTLASS passes the `timeHint` from asm (barrier.h:415-420); copying that asm keeps the PTX text identical.

**Measured lowering** (note D.2, G.3): `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P, [addr], R` with the parity in bit 31 of `R`, and the retry placed out of line: `TRYWAIT; @!P NANOSLEEP.SYNCS 0x989680; @!P SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64; @!P BRA` (how the sleeping warp is woken: Chapter 12, Section 12.2.2). The explicit kernel has 30 such retry loops in total, 26 placed out of line + 4 inline, against the baseline's 47 + 5 (the 22 missing ones are C-path sites). The SASS counts reconcile: `NANOSLEEP` 31 = 30 retry loops + 1 alloc retry, and 32 plain `PHASECHK.TRANS64` (without `.TRYWAIT`) = 30 retry-path blocking checks (NVIDIA internal; one per loop, after its `NANOSLEEP`) + 2 `test_wait` (note G.3; `NANOSLEEP` 31 re-counted in `trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt`).

**Callers.** Every blocking wait goes through the `EXPLICIT_WAIT` macro (explicit.cu:237 with the trace toggle off: `mbar_wait((addr), (parity))`); the extra macro arguments vanish. Sites:

| Line | Role | Barrier (address) | Parity | When it executes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 680 | every consuming warp (`clc_consume`) | `OFF_CLC_FULL + 8 clc_idx` | `clc_phase` | once per tile |
| 735 | warp 2 | `OFF_MAIN_EMPTY + 8 prod_idx` | `prod_phase` | only when the W7 peek failed |
| 784 | rank-0 warp 2 | `OFF_THROTTLE_EMPTY + 8 thr_idx` | `thr_phase` | once per tile, no peek |
| 800 | warp 2 tail | `OFF_MAIN_EMPTY + 8 prod_idx` | `prod_phase` | 8 times at exit |
| 836, 841 | rank-0 warp 1 | throttle full, CLC empty | | once per tile each |
| 861 | rank-0 warp 1 tail | CLC empty | | at exit, only if W8 said not done |
| 918 | leader warp 0 | `OFF_ACC_EMPTY + 8 acc_stage` | `accp_phase` | once per tile, no peek |
| 923 | leader warp 0 | `OFF_MAIN_FULL + 8 cons_idx` | `cons_phase` | only when the W7 peek failed |
| 955 | leader warp 0 tail | accumulator empty | | 4 times at exit |
| 965 | warp 0 (both CTAs) | `OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC` | 0 | once at exit |
| 1034 | warps 4-7 | `OFF_ACC_FULL + 8 acc_stage` | `accc_phase` | first subtile, only when the W7 peek failed |

**Count per tile per CTA.** Unconditional: 6 CLC waits (warps 0, 2, 4-7; 7 in rank 0) + 1 accumulator-empty wait (leader) + 3 throttle/CLC-producer waits (rank 0 only). Conditional: mainloop full/empty and accumulator full, only when the peek failed. Tails at exit: 8 + 4 + 2 + 1, the 2 CLC ones only when W8 said not done.

**Why peek-then-wait.** W6 may hold the thread for a long time: it loops, parking the thread for up to the 10 ms hint on each attempt. The one-shot W7 tests once and returns a token (Section 6.3.5 table). CUTLASS peeks the *next* stage immediately after advancing the state, while the current stage's work is being issued, and enters W6 only if the peek said "not yet" (Chapter 8 and Chapter 9 show the pattern). Measured: in the MMA warp's k-tile loop `@P0 BRA` skips the blocking wait when the peek succeeded; otherwise the wait's first `TRYWAIT` runs inline and only its retry loop sits out of line, behind `@!P0 BRA` (note G.3; `trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt` `0x51f0-0x5230` and `0x6350-0x63a0`).

### 6.3.4 W7 `mbar_try_wait`: the one-shot peek

```
// W7 [mbarrier]  ClusterBarrier::try_wait (barrier.h:461-478): one peek, no suspend hint; 1 = WaitDone, 0 = WaitAgain
__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t mbar_try_wait(uint32_t smem_addr, uint32_t phase) {
  uint32_t waitComplete;
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    ".reg .pred P1; \n\t"
    "mbarrier.try_wait.parity.shared::cta.b64 P1, [%1], %2; \n\t"
    "selp.b32 %0, 1, 0, P1; \n\t"
    "}"
    : "=r"(waitComplete)
    : "r"(smem_addr), "r"(phase)
    : "memory");
  return waitComplete;
}
```
(explicit.cu:313-326)

**Purpose.** Test once whether the phase has completed; return a token (1 = done, 0 = wait again) without spinning.

**Decomposition.** The same `try_wait.parity` as W6 in its three-operand form: no `timeHint`, so the hardware uses its system-dependent limit before returning false, and no loop. `selp.b32 %0, 1, 0, P1;` converts the predicate into a 32-bit value the C++ can branch on (`if (!tok)`). `"=r"` because the asm always writes the token.

CUTLASS returns `static_cast<bool>`; the wrapper returns the `uint32_t`.

**Callers.**

| Line | Role | Barrier | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| 732 | warp 2 | mainloop empty | pre-loop peek of each `load_ktiles` call (`producer_try_acquire`, sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:604) |
| 739 | warp 2 | mainloop empty, next stage | unconditional peek after `advance` (:617) |
| 916 | leader warp 0 | mainloop full | pre-loop peek, skipped (`tok = 1`) if `k_tiles <= 0` |
| 927 | leader warp 0 | mainloop full, next stage | peek after `advance`, skipped on the last k-tile |
| 1030 | warps 4-7 | accumulator full | once per tile, consumed at subtile 0 |

**Count per tile per CTA.** Warp 2: 2 + 128 = 130 (128 consumed; the last peek of each call is discarded, note 7.5). Leader warp 0: 1 + 127 = 128. Epilogue: 1 per warp (4). Measured: `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT` without a retry loop (note D.2 for the baseline, G.3 for the explicit kernel).

### 6.3.5 W8 `mbar_test_wait`: the non-blocking test

```
// W8 [mbarrier]  ClusterBarrier::test_wait (barrier.h:435-457): CLC producer_tail only
__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t mbar_test_wait(uint32_t smem_addr, uint32_t phase, uint32_t pred) {
  uint32_t waitComplete;
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    ".reg .pred P1; \n\t"
    ".reg .pred P2; \n\t"
    "setp.eq.u32 P2, %3, 1;\n\t"
    "@P2 mbarrier.test_wait.parity.shared::cta.b64 P1, [%1], %2; \n\t"
    "selp.b32 %0, 1, 0, P1; \n\t"
    "}"
    : "=r"(waitComplete)
    : "r"(smem_addr), "r"(phase), "r"(pred)
    : "memory");
  return waitComplete;
}
```
(explicit.cu:328-343)

**Purpose.** Test the phase without any possibility of suspension; used at a single call site, in the CLC producer tail.

**Decomposition.** `mbarrier.test_wait` is the *non-blocking* sibling of `try_wait`: it returns immediately with the current completion status and never parks the thread. `setp.eq.u32 P2, %3, 1; @P2 ...` predicates the test on a C++ argument: CUTLASS's `test_wait(ptr, phase, pred)` lets callers skip the test, and the kernel always passes `1u`. If `pred` were 0, `P1` would be unwritten and the `selp` result indeterminate; the wrapper preserves the CUTLASS interface rather than fixing this, and the single caller never hits it.

**try_wait vs test_wait vs the hint, in one table.**

| Wrapper | Instruction | May suspend the thread? | Loop? | Where used |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| W6 | `try_wait.parity ... , hint` | yes, up to the hint (10 ms) then retries | PTX loop | every blocking wait |
| W7 | `try_wait.parity` (no hint) | yes, up to the system limit, once | no | peeks that decide whether to call W6 |
| W8 | `test_wait.parity` | never | no | CLC `producer_tail` (`sm100_pipeline.hpp:1041-1050`) |

Measured: the two forms stay distinguishable in SASS: an unpredicated `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64` without `.TRYWAIT` for W8 (2 sites, `0x1d70`/`0x1e50`, note G.3; note D.2 for the baseline), while the 30 other non-`.TRYWAIT` `PHASECHK.TRANS64` are the `@!P`-predicated retry-path blocking checks inside W6's loops, issued after the `NANOSLEEP` back-off (NVIDIA internal; Section 6.3.3).

**Caller.** explicit.cu:860, rank-0 warp 1, `mbar_test_wait(smem_base + OFF_CLC_EMPTY + 8u * clp_idx, clp_phase, 1u)`, twice at exit (`kClcStages = 2`); W6 follows only if the result is 0. Count per tile: 0.

### 6.3.6 W9/W10: local and remote arrive

```
// W9 [mbarrier]  ClusterBarrier::arrive (local, barrier.h:509-518)
__device__ __forceinline__ void mbar_arrive_local(uint32_t smem_addr) {
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    "mbarrier.arrive.shared::cta.b64 _, [%0];\n\t"
    "}"
    :
    : "r"(smem_addr)
    : "memory");
}

// W10 [mbarrier]  ClusterBarrier::arrive(cta_id, pred) (barrier.h:486-499): remote arrive through mapa; the `if (pred)` stays in C++
__device__ __forceinline__ void mbar_arrive_remote(uint32_t smem_addr, uint32_t cta_id) {
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    ".reg .b32 remAddr32;\n\t"
    "mapa.shared::cluster.u32  remAddr32, %0, %1;\n\t"
    "mbarrier.arrive.shared::cluster.b64  _, [remAddr32];\n\t"
    "}"
    :
    : "r"(smem_addr), "r"(cta_id)
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:345-367)

**Purpose.** W9: one arrival on a barrier of the executing CTA. W10: one arrival on the barrier at the same offset in CTA `cta_id` of the cluster.

**Decomposition of W10.** `mapa.shared::cluster.u32 d, a, b` maps the `shared::cta` address `a` to the `shared::cluster` address of the same offset in the CTA with rank `b`. `mbarrier.arrive.shared::cluster.b64 _, [d]` then arrives on that remote barrier. `.shared::cluster` is the state space that makes a cross-CTA address legal, and `_` discards the state (a remote arrive cannot return one). Calling W10 with `cta_id == rank` is a legal local arrive by another name (the dealloc handshake does the opposite: `peer`).

**The `if (pred)` moved out.** CUTLASS's `arrive(ptr, cta_id, pred)` wraps the asm in `if (pred)` (barrier.h:489). The wrapper drops the parameter. The kernel calls W10 only where it should fire (`is_cta0`, `!is_leader`, `is_leader`), so the predicate is a C++ branch at the call site for the dealloc handshake (`if (!is_leader)` / `if (is_leader)`, explicit.cu:964, 970, the only W10 calls whose CUTLASS originals pass a non-default `pred`, kernel :794, 796); the CLC and throttle releases (explicit.cu:684, 837) carry none, as CUTLASS's `consumer_release` uses the default `pred = true` (barrier.h:383), and `is_cta0` reaches the throttle release only through the role dispatch (explicit.cu:1194).

**Callers.**

| W | Line | Role | Barrier | Target CTA | Lanes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| W9 | 785 | rank-0 warp 2 | `OFF_THROTTLE_FULL + 8 thr_idx` | own | 32 (count 32) |
| W10 | 684 | every consuming warp (`clc_consume`) | `OFF_CLC_EMPTY + 8 clc_idx` | 0 | all lanes of each consuming warp: 32 + 4 x (32 + 32 + 128) = 800 cluster-wide |
| W10 | 837 | rank-0 warp 1 | `OFF_THROTTLE_EMPTY + 8 thc_idx` | 0 | 32 |
| W10 | 964 | peer warp 0, exit | `OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC` | `peer` (= the leader) | 32 |
| W10 | 970 | leader warp 0, exit | `OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC` | `peer` (= the peer) | 32 |

The CLC release always targets CTA 0 because the CLC pipeline's `consumer_release` arrives on `params_.producer_blockid` (sm100_pipeline.hpp:1132-1134), which is 0: only rank 0's scheduler produces responses, and only its `clc_empty[]` is ever waited on (Chapter 7).

**Count per tile per CTA.** W9: 32 thread-arrivals (one warp-wide call, rank 0 only). W10: 192 thread-arrivals (6 warps x 32) per CTA, 224 in rank 0 (the scheduler warp also consumes), plus 32 for the throttle release in rank 0; at exit 32 + 32 per pair. Measured lowering: `mapa` produces no instruction of its own, only a `PRMT ..., 0x654` byte-3 insert, which confirms that the rank lives in address bits [24,32); the arrive is `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0 RZ, [addr], RZ` for the remote form and `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.A1T0` for the local one (note D.2).

### 6.3.7 W11 `mbar_arrive_cluster_masked`: the peer-bit arrive

```
// W11 [mbarrier]  cutlass::arch::umma_arrive_2x1SM_sm0 (barrier.h:905-921): arrive on the pair leader's barrier through the peer-bit-masked address
__device__ __forceinline__ void mbar_arrive_cluster_masked(uint32_t smem_addr) {
  uint32_t bar_intptr = smem_addr & kPeerBitMask;
  asm volatile (
    "{\n\t"
    "mbarrier.arrive.shared::cluster.b64 _, [%0];\n\t"
    "}"
    :
    : "r"(bar_intptr)
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:369-379)

**The peer-bit mechanism.** `kPeerBitMask = 0xFEFFFFFF` (explicit.cu:187; `cute::Sm100MmaPeerBitMask`, copy_sm100_tma.hpp:45) clears bit 24, which is rank bit 0 because rank `r`'s base is `0x400 + (r << 24)` (measured, note D.1 D5). Clearing it maps rank 1 to rank 0 and rank 3 to rank 2, and leaves the even ranks unchanged:

```
  rank 0  0x00000400 + off  --&0xFEFFFFFF-->  0x00000400 + off   (itself)
  rank 1  0x01000400 + off  --&0xFEFFFFFF-->  0x00000400 + off   (its leader, rank 0)
  rank 2  0x02000400 + off  --&0xFEFFFFFF-->  0x02000400 + off   (itself)
  rank 3  0x03000400 + off  --&0xFEFFFFFF-->  0x02000400 + off   (its leader, rank 2)
```

**What nvcc emits.** The PTX carries `and.b32 %r, %r, -16777224` = `0xFEFFFFF8` and the SASS `ULOP3.LUT ... 0xfefffff8` (a vector `LOP3.LUT` in the baseline's epilogue): the three always-zero alignment bits of an 8-byte-aligned barrier address folded into the mask, semantically identical (note D.6 item 2, G.3).

**Count per tile per CTA.** Measured in the explicit kernel (`trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt`): `ULOP3.LUT UR24, UR24, 0xfefffff8, URZ, 0xc0, !UPT` at `0x44c0` (the only surviving `0xfefffff8` literal, note G.3), then `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0 RZ, [UR24], RZ` at `0x44f0`, placed between subtile 7's `LDTM.x16` and its first `FMUL`. The masked address is warp-uniform (`acc_empty_base + 8 acc_stage` has no lane term), so it lives in a uniform register. The baseline's equivalent is `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0 RZ, [R62+URZ], RZ` with `R62 = (base + 0x110 + 8 acc_stage) & 0xFEFFFFF8` at `0xb090` (note D.2; 0x110 = 272 = `OFF_ACC_EMPTY`).

### 6.3.8 W12/W13: arrive with transaction bytes

```
// W12 [mbarrier]  ClusterTransactionBarrier::arrive_and_expect_tx (local, barrier.h:588-598)
__device__ __forceinline__ void mbar_arrive_expect_tx_local(uint32_t smem_addr, uint32_t transaction_bytes) {
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    "mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx.shared::cta.b64 _, [%1], %0; \n\t"
    "}"
    :
    : "r"(transaction_bytes), "r"(smem_addr)
    : "memory");
}

// W13 [mbarrier]  ClusterTransactionBarrier::arrive_and_expect_tx(bytes, cta_id, pred) (barrier.h:606-620): every lane executes, lanes with pred == 1 act
__device__ __forceinline__ void mbar_arrive_expect_tx_remote_pred(uint32_t smem_addr, uint32_t cta_id, uint32_t pred, uint32_t transaction_bytes) {
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    ".reg .pred p;\n\t"
    ".reg .b32 remAddr32;\n\t"
    "setp.eq.u32 p, %2, 1;\n\t"
    "@p mapa.shared::cluster.u32  remAddr32, %0, %1;\n\t"
    "@p mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx.shared::cluster.b64  _, [remAddr32], %3;\n\t"
    "}"
    :
    : "r"(smem_addr), "r"(cta_id), "r"(pred), "r"(transaction_bytes)
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:381-405)

**Decomposition.** In W12 the byte count is `%0` and the address `%1` (CUTLASS's operand order, kept). W13's `setp.eq.u32 p, %2, 1` turns the C++ `pred` into a PTX predicate, so **all 32 lanes execute the same asm statement** and only the predicated lanes act, without a divergent C++ branch.

**Who, exactly.** W12: `if (is_leader_lane)` (explicit.cu:736), where `is_leader_lane` is the argument `lane_pred != 0u && is_leader` (explicit.cu:1192): the prologue-elected lane of the pair leader's warp 2, once per k-tile, before the loads are issued. W13: rank-0 warp 1, all 32 lanes execute it with `cta_id = lane` and `pred = lane < 4` (explicit.cu:842): lanes 0..3 arm CTAs 0..3's `clc_full[idx]` (count 1, explicit.cu:183) with 16 bytes each, one lane per CTA (note 13 item 6).

**Count per tile per CTA.** Measured in the explicit kernel: W12 is `@!P0 SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64 RZ, [UR10], R5` with `R5 = 0xc000` (= 49152) in both producer loops (`0x0ee0`, `0x11b0`; note G.3, `trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt`). The baseline's form is `@P0 SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64 RZ, [UR17], R2` (note D.2), the opposite predicate polarity for the same leader-lane condition. W13 is `@!P0 SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED RZ, [R11+URZ], R5` with `R5 = 0x10` at `0x1b70` (`@!P0 MOV R5, 0x10` at `0x1ad0`; `R11` is the `PRMT ..., 0x654` lane-mapped address; `trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt`, Section 12.2); the baseline's form is `@!P2 SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED RZ, [PRMT(lane)], R9` with `R9 = 0x10` at `0x2cd0` (note D.2).

**Why bytes may land before the `expect_tx`, and why that is fine.** The tx-count is signed, with range -(2^20 - 1) .. 2^20 - 1 for `.layout::v0` (PTX ISA 9.4, Table 43), so early `complete_tx` operations drive it negative until the `expect_tx 49152` brings it back to zero. "Arm before you issue" is therefore a within-thread convention (the leader's own loads follow its arrive, as in CUTLASS's `producer_acquire`), not a cross-CTA requirement. Chapter 4 ("Why this works whoever lands first") works the numbers, including a two-arrival variant.

## 6.4 Family 3: fences, W14-W15

### 6.4.1 W14 `fence_mbarrier_init_release_cluster`

```
// W14 [fence]  cutlass::arch::fence_barrier_init (barrier.h:712-720)
__device__ __forceinline__ void fence_mbarrier_init_release_cluster() {
  asm volatile(
    "{\n\t"
    "fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster; \n"
    "}"
    ::
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:407-415)

**Decomposition.** `fence.mbarrier_init` is a restricted fence that orders only prior `mbarrier.init` operations, narrower in effect than a full `fence.acq_rel.cluster`; `.release.cluster` are the only semantics and scope the ISA allows for it. The `::` (empty outputs and inputs) followed by `"memory"` is the clobber-only operand list. CUTLASS's comment (barrier.h:707-710) says it "must be composed with an appropriate sync instruction with the right scope ... eg. `__syncthreads()` or a `cluster_arrive()` + `cluster_wait()`": W14 is the release half, and W17 is the acquire half.

**Per-thread scope, per the ISA.** Only the elected lanes of the initialising warps executed inits, so only their W14 orders anything. The other threads' fences (255 of 256 at the first group) are harmless no-ops, consistent with ptxas emitting no instruction for the PTX statement.

**Callers.** explicit.cu:1133, 1144, 1154, 1164: every thread, once after each of the four init groups. CUTLASS calls it once per mbarrier-backed pipeline constructor, so the 33-init explicit kernel has 4 fences where the 43-init baseline has 6 (note E.6.3). Count: 4 per thread, prologue only. Measured: it emits no SASS instruction of its own; seven bare `FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S` precede the init groups in the baseline, and the attribution is inferred (note D.2, D.6 item 8).

### 6.4.2 W15 `fence_proxy_async_shared_cta`

```
// W15 [fence]  cutlass::arch::fence_view_async_shared (barrier.h:728-736)
__device__ __forceinline__ void fence_proxy_async_shared_cta() {
  asm volatile (
    "{\n\t"
    "fence.proxy.async.shared::cta; \n"
    "}"
    ::
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:417-425)

**Purpose.** Order generic-proxy shared-memory accesses before subsequent async-proxy accesses of the same CTA's shared memory (and vice versa).

**Decomposition.** `fence.proxy.async` is a bidirectional proxy fence between the generic and the async proxy. `.shared::cta` restricts it to objects in the CTA's shared memory (the other forms are `.global`, `.shared::cluster`, or no state space for all). `"memory"` is essential here: the fence's whole purpose is to sit *after* the C++ `st.shared` stores (explicit.cu:1047), and the clobber forbids the compiler from sinking those stores below it. CUTLASS has a clobber-less twin, `cute::tma_store_fence` (copy_sm90_tma.hpp:1214-1221: `asm volatile ("fence.proxy.async.shared::cta;");`); the kernel deliberately copies the `barrier.h` form with the clobber (note E.6.2 W15).

**Callers.**

| Line | Role | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 683 | every consuming warp (`clc_consume`), after W34 | the response slot was just read by the generic proxy (`ld.shared.b128`) and will be rewritten by the async proxy (the next `try_cancel` into this slot, two queries later) after the release; CUTLASS fences at the same point (sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:430). The ISA gives the primary reason: the response "is asynchronously written using weak async-proxy writes to the corresponding local shared memory addr of each CTA in the requesting cluster" (PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.15.18). That later query's write to this slot is therefore an async-proxy write that must be ordered after this generic-proxy `ld.shared.b128`, and the fence establishes that write-after-read order across proxies (Chapter 7 traces the two-round reuse of the slot). |
| 1050 | warps 4-7, every subtile, after the 16 `st.shared` | the TMA store (W23, async proxy) must observe the generic-proxy stores into the C/D stage |

**Count per tile per CTA.** One per consuming warp (6; 7 in rank 0) + 8 per epilogue warp (32). Measured: `MEMBAR.ALL.CTA; FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S` pairs (12 in the explicit kernel's SASS, note G.3).

## 6.5 Family 4: cluster and named barriers, W16-W19

**Two barrier kinds that are not mbarriers.** A *cluster barrier* (`barrier.cluster.*`) is one hardware rendezvous of all threads of all CTAs in the cluster: no address, no count operand, no transaction bytes; every thread arrives once per phase. A *named barrier* (`bar.sync` / `bar.arrive`, `barrier{.cta}` in the ISA) is one of the 16 per-CTA hardware barriers 0..15. It is counted in *threads* (a multiple of 32), has no transaction bytes, no cross-CTA addressing and no parity to track, and it completes when the stated number of threads has arrived and then resets itself. Neither lives in shared memory, so neither needs an init or a fence. The epilogue uses named barrier 1 rather than an mbarrier because it needs exactly a thread-count rendezvous of the 128 epilogue threads of one CTA, twice per subtile, with no asynchronous bytes to count and nothing remote. A named barrier gives that in one instruction, with no state in smem, no phase bookkeeping and no arrive/wait split (Chapter 2, Section 2.10.2 quotes the ISA rules).

### 6.5.1 W16/W17 `cluster_arrive_relaxed`, `cluster_wait`

```
// W16/W17 [cluster]  cute::cluster_arrive_relaxed, cute::cluster_wait (cluster_sm90.hpp:48-51, 66-69)
__device__ __forceinline__ void cluster_arrive_relaxed() { asm volatile("barrier.cluster.arrive.relaxed.aligned;\n" : : ); }
__device__ __forceinline__ void cluster_wait()           { asm volatile("barrier.cluster.wait.aligned;\n" : : ); }
```
(explicit.cu:427-429)

**Purpose.** The cluster-wide rendezvous of the prologue, split into its two halves so that work can be done between them.

**Decomposition.**

| Qualifier | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `barrier.cluster.arrive` | mark this thread's arrival at the cluster barrier without waiting |
| `.relaxed` | no memory ordering is attached to the arrive (the default would be `.release`); the ordering of the inits is already provided by W14, so the release here would be redundant work |
| `.aligned` | all threads of the warp execute the same `barrier.cluster` instruction; the warp must be converged (it is: both halves are executed unconditionally by all 256 threads, outside the prologue's elected-lane `if` blocks) |
| `barrier.cluster.wait` | block until every non-exited thread of every CTA in the cluster has arrived; default `.acquire` semantics make the released inits visible |

(PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.15.3, `barrier.cluster`: "If the optional .acquire qualifier is absent for barrier.cluster.wait, .acquire is assumed by default", and for the arrive ".release is assumed by default" unless `.relaxed` is written.)

**Why split.** Between explicit.cu:1170 (arrive) and :1179 (wait) the kernel computes `x`, `y`, `tm`, `tn` (W4 and pure arithmetic, no shared memory). The kernel thus overlaps the slowest CTA's arrival latency with useful work, exactly as the baseline does (kernel :580 and :615). No remote barrier operation may precede the wait (comment at explicit.cu:1178), because a peer CTA might not have initialised its barriers yet.

**No `"memory"` clobber.** CuTe's originals have none (`: : );`). This is safe: the inits carry their own clobber, W14's clobber sits between the pipeline inits and W16 (Section 6.0.2; only the tmem_dealloc init, explicit.cu:1166, follows the last W14, as in the baseline, kernel :565 before :580), and no C++ shared-memory access occurs before W17.

**Callers.** explicit.cu:1170 and 1179, once per thread. Measured: `UCGABAR_ARV` and `UCGABAR_WAIT; CCTL.IVALL`, both behind one ptxas-inserted `c[0x0][0x36c] == 1` test (reading the constant as "launched as a cluster" is inferred, note D.2), whose not-taken path is a `NOP` for the arrive and `BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x0` for the wait (note D.2, G.3).

### 6.5.2 W18/W19 `named_bar_sync`, `named_bar_arrive`

```
// W18/W19 [named barrier]  NamedBarrier::arrive_and_wait_internal / arrive_internal (barrier.h:285-288, 305-309)
__device__ __forceinline__ void named_bar_sync(uint32_t barrier_id, uint32_t num_threads) {
  asm volatile("bar.sync %0, %1;" : : "r"(barrier_id), "r"(num_threads) : "memory");
}
__device__ __forceinline__ void named_bar_arrive(uint32_t barrier_id, uint32_t num_threads) {
  asm volatile("bar.arrive %0, %1;" : : "r"(barrier_id), "r"(num_threads) : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:431-437)

**Purpose.** Synchronise a *subset* of the CTA's warps through one of the 16 hardware named barriers.

**Decomposition.** `bar.sync a, b`: barrier id `a` (0..15), `b` = number of participating threads (a multiple of 32); the thread arrives and waits until `b` threads have arrived. `bar.arrive a, b`: arrive without waiting; the barrier completes when `b` arrivals of either kind have happened. Both are warp-wide. Barrier 0 is compiler-owned: the compiler typically lowers `__syncthreads()` to a CTA barrier, commonly barrier 0, so hand-written `bar.sync 0` protocols must not be mixed with `__syncthreads()` in the same region (NVIDIA internal); barrier.h:163-164, quoted in Section 2.10.2 (other driver APIs "may use it"), warns against id 0 for the same reason, so CUTLASS reserves ids 1-7 (`ReservedNamedBarriers`, barrier.h:169-178): `EpilogueBarrier = 1`, `TmemAllocBarrier = 6` (explicit.cu:190). The ids and counts are `"r"` registers because CUTLASS passes them as run-time values; ptxas still folds them to immediates in SASS (`BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x1, 0x80`).

**The two populations.**

| Call | Id | Threads | Who | Why that number |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| explicit.cu:887 `named_bar_arrive(6, 160)` | 6 | 160 = 32 + 128 | warp 0 arrives after `tcgen05.alloc` wrote the TMEM base | only the warps that need the TMEM address participate: warp 0 (producer of the value) + warps 4-7 (consumers); warps 1-3 never read T |
| explicit.cu:997 `named_bar_sync(6, 160)` | 6 | 160 | warps 4-7 wait at the top of `epilogue_role` | after it, `T = *(smem + OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR)` is safe (explicit.cu:998) |
| explicit.cu:1051, 1071 `named_bar_sync(1, 128)` | 1 | 128 = 4 x 32 | warps 4-7, twice per subtile | (1) after the fence: all 128 threads' stores to the C/D stage are in before warp 4 issues the TMA store; (2) after the store/commit/wait: nobody starts the next subtile's `st.shared` before warp 4's `wait_group.read 1` has returned, i.e. before every store group but the one just committed has finished reading (the stage written next, `(e + 1) % 4`, was last read by the group of subtile e - 3, Section 3.5.4) |

`"memory"` on both (barrier.h:287, :308): the barrier is exactly where C++ smem stores must be complete (before `bar.sync 1,128` the epilogue's `st.shared`; after `bar.arrive 6,160` the load of T must not be hoisted; note E.6.4, `mma_role` paragraph).

**Count per tile per CTA.** W18: 16 (`bar.sync 1,128`, 2 per subtile); plus 1 `bar.sync 6,160` per CTA at start. W19: 1 per CTA at start. Measured: 16 `BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x1, 0x80`, 1 `0x6, 0xa0`, 1 `BAR.ARV 0x6, 0xa0` (note G.3).

## 6.6 Family 5: TMA, W20-W25

### 6.6.1 Primer: the TMA unit and where the maps live

The TMA unit does the address generation, the swizzle and the transfer asynchronously. All four map addresses live in the kernel parameter space (`__grid_constant__ params`), and the instructions take the generic address of each map (`"l"`).

### 6.6.2 W20 `prefetch_tensormap`

```
// W20 [TMA]  cute::prefetch_tma_descriptor (copy_sm90_desc.hpp:302-317): generic address of the parameter-space descriptor
__device__ __forceinline__ void prefetch_tensormap(void const* desc_ptr) {
  uint64_t gmem_int_desc = reinterpret_cast<uint64_t>(desc_ptr);
  asm volatile (
    "prefetch.tensormap [%0];"
    :
    : "l"(gmem_int_desc)
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:439-447)

**Purpose.** Bring a tensor map's cache line into the tensor-map descriptor cache that `cp.async.bulk.tensor` reads it from, not the L2 data cache (NVIDIA internal; the ISA names no cache), before the first `cp.async.bulk.tensor` that uses it.

**Decomposition.** `prefetch{.tensormap_space}.tensormap [a]`: with `.tensormap` the prefetch brings the cache line holding a tensor map into the tensor-map descriptor cache used by `cp.async.bulk.tensor`, not the L2 data cache (NVIDIA internal; the ISA names no cache). The prefetch is per-thread, best-effort and has no completion mechanism (NVIDIA internal): the kernel issues it and never waits on it. The optional state-space qualifier is `.const` or `.param`; **without one the address is generic** (CUTLASS's comment, copy_sm90_desc.hpp:308: "using generic addressing (i.e. no specific state space: const or param)"). That is why the operand is a 64-bit `"l"` register holding `reinterpret_cast<uint64_t>(&params.tma_a)`: nvcc emits `cvta.param` to form the generic address of the parameter-space object (note G.3: "four `cvta.param` for the map addresses"). The alignment requirement is not the ISA's. PTX describes the tensor map only as "a 128-byte opaque object either in .const space or .param (kernel function parameter) space or .global space" (PTX ISA 9.4, 5.5.8) and refers `prefetch`'s operand to the generic addressing rules. The 64-byte alignment comes from the CUDA driver API (`cuTensorMapEncodeTiled`: "tensorMap address must be aligned to 64 bytes", CUDA Driver API, Tensor Map Object Management). CUTLASS's fallback type spells it out as `struct alignas(64) { char bytes[128]; }` (copy_sm90_desc.hpp:295), and the CUDA 13.3 header over-satisfies it with `alignof(CUtensorMap) = 128` (explicit.hpp:18, :66). `"memory"` as in the source.

The wrapper takes `void const*` instead of `TmaDescriptor const*`.

**Callers.** explicit.cu:1114-1115 (warp 1, `lane_pred`: `&params.tma_a`, `&params.tma_b`) and 1118-1119 (warp 3, `lane_pred`: `&params.tma_c`, `&params.tma_d`), in every CTA, regardless of beta (C is prefetched for parity with the baseline's four `UTMACCTL.PF`, note D.7). Count: 4 per CTA, prologue only. Measured in the explicit kernel: `UTMACCTL.PF` x4 (note G.3). The parameter block's address (its generic address, by the inference of Section 12.1.1) is loaded once per prefetching warp (`LDCU.64 UR4, c[0x0][0x348]` at `0x00d0` on warp 1's path, `LDCU.64 UR6, c[0x0][0x348]` at `0x0130` on warp 3's path), and the four maps are prefetched at `+0x0`, `+0x80`, `+0x100`, `+0x180` from it (`trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt`, `0x00d0-0x0190`) = the byte map's 0/128/256/384 (explicit.hpp:20-23). The descriptors stay in parameter space, where the 640-byte block sits at constant-bank offset 0x380 (`CONSTANT[0] = 0x380 + 640`, G.3). The `+0x80/+0x180/+0x580/+0x680` of note D.2 are the baseline's map offsets inside its 2048-byte `Params`.

### 6.6.3 W21 `tma_load_2sm_mcast_3d`: the A load

```
// W21 [TMA]  SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_MULTICAST_3D::copy (copy_sm100_tma.hpp:283-305); the barrier operand is already peer-bit-masked by the caller
__device__ __forceinline__ void tma_load_2sm_mcast_3d(void const* desc_ptr, uint32_t smem_int_mbar, uint16_t multicast_mask, uint64_t cache_hint,
                                                      uint32_t smem_int_ptr, int32_t crd0, int32_t crd1, int32_t crd2) {
  uint64_t gmem_int_desc = reinterpret_cast<uint64_t>(desc_ptr);
  asm volatile (
    "cp.async.bulk.tensor.3d.cta_group::2.shared::cluster.global.mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes.multicast::cluster.L2::cache_hint"
    " [%0], [%1, {%4, %5, %6}], [%2], %3, %7;"
    :
    : "r"(smem_int_ptr), "l"(gmem_int_desc), "r"(smem_int_mbar), "h"(multicast_mask),
      "r"(crd0), "r"(crd1), "r"(crd2), "l"(cache_hint)
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:449-460)

**Purpose.** Load one 64 x 64 fp16 box of A (8192 B) from global memory into the same shared-memory offset of every CTA named in the mask, crediting the destination pair's leader barrier.

**Decomposition, qualifier by qualifier.**

| Text | Meaning in this kernel |
|---|---|
| `cp.async.bulk.tensor` | an asynchronous bulk tensor copy executed by the TMA unit, addressed through a tensor map |
| `.3d` | three coordinates: `{64 q, 128 tm + 64 y, 0}` = (k, row, batch) for the A map whose dims are (K, M, L) (Chapter 5). The third coordinate is the literal 0 because L = 1: the explicit kernel is an L = 1 kernel by construction (note G.3, "Generality"). The baseline binds it to `blockIdx.z` and then to the CLC response's `z0` (note D.2, the `UR20` operand); making it a variable is the first delta of a batched version (Chapter 13, Section 13.4.2) |
| `.cta_group::2` | the instruction participates in a CTA pair. ISA (PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.10.28.5.3): "When .cta_group::2 is specified, the mbarrier object mbar can be in shared memory of either the same CTA as the shared memory destination dstMem or in its peer-CTA", and with multicast "for each destination CTA specified in the ctaMask, the mbarrier signal is sent either to the destination CTA or its peer-CTA based on the %cluster_ctarank parity of the shared memory where the mbarrier object mbar resides". The rank parity of a 32-bit `shared::cluster` address is its rank bit 0, which the compiler places at **bit 24** (measured, note D.1 D5; not ISA text). Clearing bit 24 with `Sm100MmaPeerBitMask` therefore sends every destination's signal to the **even CTA of its pair**: with the caller's mask, the bytes landing in either CTA of a pair always credit that pair's leader (note B.6; the 49152-byte accounting, note D.1 D8). |
| `.shared::cluster.global` | destination state space `shared::cluster` (the 32-bit destination is interpreted in the cluster window; with multicast, the same CTA-relative offset as `dstMem` in each destination CTA), source `global` |
| `.mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes` | completion mechanism: when the box has landed, `complete_tx` with the number of bytes written (8192) is performed on the mbarrier |
| `.multicast::cluster` | the box is written to every CTA whose bit is set in the `ctaMask` (`%3`, `"h"`), "to the same offset as dstMem in the shared memory of each destination CTA"; each destination's complete_tx goes to the barrier selected as above. "By default, ctaMask is assumed to be of 16-bit width" (`::16b`). ISA 9.4 also offers `::32b` with a 32-bit mask, which neither CUTLASS nor a 4-CTA cluster needs |
| `.L2::cache_hint` | a 64-bit cache policy operand follows (`%7`, `"l"`): `kCacheHintEvictNormal = 0x1000000000000000` (explicit.cu:188) = `TMA::CacheHintSm100::EVICT_NORMAL` (copy_sm90_desc.hpp:193-194) = `cute::Sm100MemDescDefault` (copy_sm100_tma.hpp:46), the default policy |
| `[%0]` | destination smem address: `a_dst_base + 16384 s` with `a_dst_base = smem_base + OFF_SMEM_A + 8192 y` (explicit.cu:768): this CTA's 64-row half of the 128 x 64 stage |
| `[%1, {%4, %5, %6}]` | the tensor map's generic address and the coordinates (`int32_t`, `"r"`) |
| `[%2]` | the mbarrier: `full_masked_base + 8 s` with `full_masked_base = smem_base & kPeerBitMask` (explicit.cu:770): the pair leader's `full[s]` |
| `%3` | `a_mcast_mask = 0x5 << x` (explicit.cu:772): ranks x and x + 2, the two CTAs that share `tm` |

**Why the caller pre-masks the barrier.** CUTLASS's `SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_MULTICAST_3D::copy` masks inside the copy (copy_sm100_tma.hpp:292: `cast_smem_ptr_to_uint(mbar_ptr) & Sm100MmaPeerBitMask`, with the comment "Executed by both CTAs. Set peer bit to 0 so that the transaction bytes will update CTA0's barrier"). The kernel instead hoists `smem_base & kPeerBitMask` out of the loop as `full_masked_base` (explicit.cu:770, before the tile loop's `do {` at :776) and adds `8 s` per k-tile, so the wrapper receives the already-masked 32-bit address. The PTX instruction is identical, and the mask is applied once per CTA instead of 128 times per tile; this is the fold to `0xfefffff0` at SASS `0x0c00`, in warp 2's pre-loop setup after the role dispatch, that the note observed (G.3).

**The 49152-byte accounting, worked example (pair {0, 1}, stage s).**

```
  issuer  mask       lands in            offset in stage      credited barrier
  rank 0  0x5 {0,2}  rank 0 and rank 2   +0     (y = 0 half)  rank 0 full[s] (own) and rank 2 full[s] (own)
  rank 1  0xA {1,3}  rank 1 and rank 3   +0                   rank 0 full[s] (bit 24 cleared) and rank 2 full[s]
  rank 2  0x5 {0,2}  rank 0 and rank 2   +8192 (y = 1 half)   rank 0 full[s] and rank 2 full[s]
  rank 3  0xA {1,3}  rank 1 and rank 3   +8192                rank 0 full[s] and rank 2 full[s]
  B loads (W22, no multicast): rank 0 -> rank 0 full[s]; rank 1 -> rank 0 full[s]
  rank 0 full[s] receives: 4 x 8192 (A) + 2 x 8192 (B) = 49152 = kMainloopTxBytes
```

Each CTA ends up with the whole 128 x 64 A stage (its own half plus the half multicast by the CTA with the same `x` and the other `y`) and its own 64 x 64 B half; the 2SM MMA (W29) reads both CTAs' stages (Chapter 9).

**Constraints.** `"h"(multicast_mask)` takes the `uint16_t`: one bit per `%cluster_ctarank`, up to 16 CTAs (the ISA's 16-bit default and the unused `::32b` form are in the `.multicast::cluster` row above). In the PTX it is a `.b16` register, in the SASS a uniform register placed in bits [16,32) by `UPRMT ..., 0x5410` (note D.2). `"memory"` as in the source.

The wrapper takes `uint32_t` addresses (Section 6.0.1) and the coordinates by value; the only other change is that the barrier masking moved to the caller.

**Caller.** explicit.cu:747-748, warp 2, inside `if (elect_one_sync())`, once per k-tile: `tma_load_2sm_mcast_3d(&params.tma_a, full_masked_base + 8u * s, a_mcast_mask, kCacheHintEvictNormal, a_dst_base + kStageBytesA * s, c0, a_row, 0)` with `c0 = 64 q`, `a_row = 128 tm + 64 y`. Count per tile per CTA: 128. Measured: `UTMALDG.3D.MULTICAST.2CTA [UR16], [URtmap], URmask, desc[UR]` with `desc = {0x0, 0x10000000}` (the cache hint), unpredicated (note D.2, G.3).

### 6.6.4 W22 `tma_load_2sm_3d`: the B load

```
// W22 [TMA]  SM100_TMA_2SM_LOAD_3D::copy (copy_sm100_tma.hpp:104-128)
__device__ __forceinline__ void tma_load_2sm_3d(void const* desc_ptr, uint32_t smem_int_mbar, uint64_t cache_hint,
                                                uint32_t smem_int_ptr, int32_t crd0, int32_t crd1, int32_t crd2) {
  uint64_t gmem_int_desc = reinterpret_cast<uint64_t>(desc_ptr);
  asm volatile (
    "cp.async.bulk.tensor.3d.cta_group::2.shared::cluster.global.mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes.L2::cache_hint"
    " [%0], [%1, {%3, %4, %5}], [%2], %6;"
    :
    : "r"(smem_int_ptr), "l"(gmem_int_desc), "r"(smem_int_mbar),
      "r"(crd0), "r"(crd1), "r"(crd2), "l"(cache_hint)
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:462-473)

**Purpose.** Load this CTA's 64 x 64 fp16 half of B (8192 B) into its own stage, crediting the pair leader's `full[s]`.

**Decomposition.** Identical to W21 minus `.multicast::cluster` and the mask operand, so the operand numbering shifts (`{%3, %4, %5}` coordinates, `%6` hint). B is not multicast because the two CTAs of a pair need *different* 64-column halves of B (`128 tn + 64 x`), and the two pairs of the cluster have different `tn`: nothing is shared, so nothing is multicast. `.cta_group::2` is still needed so that the peer's bytes credit the leader's barrier.

Masking moved to the caller as for W21.

**Caller.** explicit.cu:754-755, same election as W21: `tma_load_2sm_3d(&params.tma_b, full_masked_base + 8u * s, kCacheHintEvictNormal, b_dst_base + kStageBytesB * s, c0, b_col, 0)` with `b_dst_base = smem_base + OFF_SMEM_B` (explicit.cu:769), `b_col = 128 tn + 64 x`. Count per tile per CTA: 128. Measured: `UTMALDG.3D.2CTA`.

### 6.6.5 W23 `tma_store_3d`: the D store

```
// W23 [TMA]  SM90_TMA_STORE_3D::copy (copy_sm90_tma.hpp:1003-1023)
__device__ __forceinline__ void tma_store_3d(void const* desc_ptr, uint32_t smem_int_ptr, int32_t crd0, int32_t crd1, int32_t crd2) {
  uint64_t gmem_int_desc = reinterpret_cast<uint64_t>(desc_ptr);
  asm volatile (
    "cp.async.bulk.tensor.3d.global.shared::cta.bulk_group [%0, {%2, %3, %4}], [%1];"
    :
    : "l"(gmem_int_desc), "r"(smem_int_ptr),
      "r"(crd0), "r"(crd1), "r"(crd2)
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:475-484)

**Purpose.** Store one (32 m, 16 n) fp32 box (2048 B) from the swizzled C/D smem stage to D in global memory.

**Decomposition.** `.global.shared::cta`: destination global, source the executing CTA's shared memory (a store never crosses CTAs). `.bulk_group` is the completion mechanism for stores: the operation stays uncommitted until W24 batches it, with the issuing thread's other uncommitted stores, into a new per-thread bulk async-group that W25 awaits; there is no mbarrier. Operands: `[%0, {%2, %3, %4}]` the D map and the coordinates `(128 tm + 32 i, 128 tn + 16 e, 0)` = (m, n, batch) for the (M, N, L) map (the batch coordinate is the literal 0 because L = 1, Section 6.6.3); `[%1]` the source `src_base + 2048 i` with `src_base = cd_base + 8192 (e & 3)`. This is a Hopper-era instruction (no `.cta_group`, and no cache hint is passed, though the store form accepts `.L2::cache_hint`): the epilogue is per-CTA.

CUTLASS's `synclog_emit_tma_store` is a no-op in this build and is not copied.

**Caller.** explicit.cu:1066, warp 4 only (`issue_tma_store = (w == 0u)`, explicit.cu:1018), **all 32 lanes with uniform operands and no election**, 4 boxes per subtile (`for i in 0..3`). Count per tile per CTA: 32 (4 x 8).

**PTX semantics vs. the lowering, and why no election.** At the PTX level `cp.async.bulk.tensor` is a per-thread instruction: each of the 32 lanes of warp 4 nominally issues its own store and keeps its own `commit_group` / `wait_group.read` bookkeeping on its own bulk async-group. ptxas can prove every operand warp-uniform (the map address from parameter space, `src_base + 2048 i`, coordinates built from the uniform `tm`, `tn`, `e`, `i`). The measured SASS therefore shows one uniform `UTMASTG.3D` per PTX store, issued once per warp whatever the lane count; K4b measured 32 active lanes at every issue (note D.2). The baseline issues the store the same way, without an election (`issue_tma_store = (warp_idx == 0)` in the collective epilogue, note 13 item 8), and relies on exactly the same lowering. My analysis of the alternative: an operand ptxas cannot prove warp-uniform (a coordinate routed through the lane id yet equal on every lane, say) would be legal PTX and still correct, but the compiler then "may insert a peeling loop over all active threads, which results in warp serialization" (CUDA Programming Guide 4.12.2.1, the note under "TMA write and sync"): up to 32 separate stores of the same box and 32x the TMA traffic. This is why every operand of W23 in the kernel is warp-uniform and why no election is needed here, while the loads (W21/W22) are elected because the baseline elects them.

### 6.6.6 W24/W25 `tma_store_commit_group`, `tma_store_wait_read<Count>`

```
// W24/W25 [TMA]  cute::tma_store_arrive, cute::tma_store_wait<Count> (copy_sm90_tma.hpp:1225-1231, 1248-1256)
__device__ __forceinline__ void tma_store_commit_group() { asm volatile("cp.async.bulk.commit_group;"); }
template <int Count>
__device__ __forceinline__ void tma_store_wait_read() {
  asm volatile(
    "cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read %0;"
    :
    : "n"(Count)
    : "memory");
}
```
(explicit.cu:486-495)

**Purpose.** W24: commit the four stores just issued as one new bulk async-group. W25: wait until at most `Count` of this thread's groups are still *reading* their shared-memory source.

**Decomposition.** `cp.async.bulk.commit_group` bundles all prior uncommitted bulk async operations of the executing thread into one group. `cp.async.bulk.wait_group N` waits until at most `N` of the most recent groups are pending. The `.read` modifier relaxes this to "pending *reads*": the wait returns as soon as the groups' source reads from shared memory are complete, even if their global writes are still in flight. This is exactly what the epilogue needs: it only wants to reuse the smem stage, not to know that D is globally visible (the latter is left to kernel completion, note D.1 D15 and Section 10.11). `"n"(Count)`: the ISA wants an integer constant, so the template parameter becomes an immediate (`cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read 1` keeps its immediate in the PTX, note 7.2).

**Why `Count = 1`.** After committing group `e`, `wait_group.read 1` guarantees that group `e - 1` has finished reading stage `(e - 1) % 4`. The stage written next, `(e + 1) % 4`, was last read by group `e - 3` and is therefore already free. Waiting for 0 would serialise the TMA read with the next subtile's `tcgen05.ld` and arithmetic (CUTLASS: `producer_acquire` of `PipelineTmaStore<4,1>` with `UnacquiredStages = 1`, note 13 item 16; Chapter 10, Section 10.10.4). CUTLASS's `store_tail` also has a `wait_group.read 0`. Beta is a run-time value, so the baseline compiles it unconditionally (`DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x0` at SASS `0xb760`) but reaches it only when `is_producer_load_needed()` is true, i.e. beta != 0 (note D.6 item 11, D.1 D15, note Section 7.7). The explicit kernel is a beta = 0 kernel by construction and omits it (note G.3: `wait_group.read 0` = 0, `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x0` = 0), so the CTA exits with at most one bulk group whose smem read was not awaited and the global writes complete with the kernel (D15; Chapter 10, Section 10.11).

**Clobbers.** Section 6.0.2 gives both arguments. W24 has none (CuTe has none): it only groups operations that W23's clobbered asm already issued. W25 has `"memory"`: the C++ `st.shared` that reuses the released stage (explicit.cu:1047) comes three subtiles after the wait (four after the store that read that stage), in the same unrolled body or the next tile's, and must stay below the wait.

**Callers.** explicit.cu:1068 and 1069, warp 4, once per subtile each. Count per tile per CTA: 8 + 8. Measured: `UTMACMDFLUSH` and `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x1` (note D.2, G.3).
