## 10.10 Fence, first barrier, warp 4's four stores, commit, wait (explicit.cu:1049-1070)

```
1049:       // tma_store_fn (:766-800)
1050:       fence_proxy_async_shared_cta();                                                            // smem writes visible to the async proxy
1051:       named_bar_sync(kBarEpilogue, kEpilogueThreads);                                           // bar.sync 1, 128
1052:       if (issue_tma_store) {
1053:         uint32_t const src_base = cd_base + kEpiStageBytes * uint32_t(e & 3);
1054:         #pragma unroll
1055:         for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {                                                            // four (32 M, 16 N) boxes per subtile (Section 5.3)
1056:           int32_t const c0 = 128 * tm + 32 * i;
1057:           int32_t const c1 = 128 * tn + 16 * e;
```

(lines 1058-1065 are the `[TRACE]` K4b record)

```
1066:           tma_store_3d(&params.tma_d, src_base + kStoreBoxBytes * uint32_t(i), c0, c1, 0);
1067:         }
1068:         tma_store_commit_group();                                                                // store_pipeline.producer_commit
1069:         tma_store_wait_read<1>();                                                                // producer_acquire (always_wait): at most 1 group pending on its smem read
1070:       }
```

This is CUTLASS's `tma_store_fn` lambda (sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:766-800):

```
        cutlass::arch::fence_view_async_shared(); // ensure smem writes are visible to TMA
        synchronize(); // ensure all threads have issued their async fence
        if (issue_tma_store) {
          copy(params.tma_store_d, bSG_sD(_,_,_,store_pipe_producer_state.index()), bSG_gD(_,_,_,epi_m,epi_n));
        }
        ...
        if (issue_tma_store) {
          store_pipeline.producer_commit(store_pipe_producer_state);
        }
        ++store_pipe_producer_state;
        // Wait for the next smem buffer to be available
        if (issue_tma_store) {
          store_pipeline.producer_acquire(store_pipe_producer_state);
        }
        synchronize();
```

with `synchronize = NamedBarrier::sync(ThreadCount, EpilogueBarrier)` (`:723`), `ThreadCount = 128`.

### 10.10.1 fence.proxy.async.shared::cta (1050; W15 at 417-425, Section 6.4.2)

PTX does not order the generic and async proxies by default: a generic write followed by an async-proxy read of the same byte needs `fence.proxy.async` (the CUDA Programming Guide's TMA store sequence is fence, `__syncthreads()`, `cp.async.bulk.tensor`, `commit_group`, `wait_group.read`; Asynchronous Data Copies). `.shared::cta` restricts the fence to this CTA's shared memory, the only state involved. Every one of the 128 threads executes it, because a proxy fence orders *the executing thread's* prior accesses; one thread fencing would say nothing about the other 127 threads' stores.

### 10.10.2 The first bar.sync 1,128 (1051; W18 at 431-434, Section 6.5.2)

Barrier id 1 is `EpilogueBarrier` (barrier.h:170), 128 the four epilogue warps (`kBarEpilogue = 1, kEpilogueThreads = 128`, explicit.cu:190-191). Warp 4 may issue the TMA store only after all four warps have written their M-blocks of the stage *and fenced them*; `bar.sync` is the CTA-scope point at which "all 128 threads passed line 1050" becomes true. SASS `BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x1, 0x80` (note D.2).

### 10.10.3 Four TMA stores from warp 4, no election (1052-1067; W23 at 475-484, Section 6.6.5)

Reading the store mnemonic. `.3d`: every tensor map this kernel uses is rank 3. The four maps of the parameter block, `tma_a/b/c/d` at offsets 0/128/256/384 (explicit.hpp:50-53), all keep the L mode of extent 1 (note Section 5.3). `.global.shared::cta`: destination global, source this CTA's shared memory (the store form has no cluster variants and no mbarrier). `.bulk_group`: completion is tracked by the issuing thread's *bulk async-group*, hence `commit_group`/`wait_group` rather than an mbarrier. Operands: `[%0, {%2,%3,%4}]` is the tensor map and the three coordinates. The tensor map is a 64-bit generic address of `params.tma_d` in parameter space; in the SASS it is a uniform 64-bit pair `c[0x0][0x348] + 0x180`, the D map at parameter offset 384 (note G.3). The coordinates are *in elements*: `c0 = 128 tm + 32 i` along M (the inner, contiguous dimension), `c1 = 128 tn + 16 e` along N, `0` for the batch. `[%1]` is the 32-bit `shared::cta` source address `cd_base + 8192 (e & 3) + 2048 i` (`kStoreBoxBytes = 2048`, explicit.cu:120). Box `i` moves rows `[128 tm + 32 i, +32)` x columns `[128 tn + 16 e, +16)` of D from M-block `i` of the stage (10.5.2).

The banner's example (line 993): tile `(5, 9)`, `e = 3`, `i = 2` gives `c0 = 640 + 64 = 704`, `c1 = 1152 + 48 = 1200`, source `OFF_SMEM_CD + 8192 x 3 + 4096 = 512 + 24576 + 4096 = 29184`, i.e. "stage 3 + 4096 B".

**All 32 lanes, uniform operands, no election.** `issue_tma_store = (w == 0u)` is warp-uniform, so all 32 lanes of warp 4 execute the four `cp.async.bulk.tensor` with identical operands, exactly as every lane of the baseline executes `copy(params.tma_store_d, ...)` under `if (issue_tma_store)` (`:740, :771`); there is no `elect.sync` anywhere in the store path (note, Section 13 item 8). Measured: each PTX store lowers to **one** uniform-datapath `UTMASTG.3D` per warp, unpredicated, issued once whatever the lane count; the K4b probe recorded 32 active lanes at every one of its 256 records (the record cap; note D.2, D.1 D8). That is 32 `UTMASTG.3D` per tile per CTA. An election would add an `ELECT` and a predicate for no gain; the explicit kernel keeps the baseline's granularity (note E.6.6).

### 10.10.4 commit_group and wait_group.read 1 (1068-1069; W24/W25 at 486-495, Section 6.6.6)

`cp.async.bulk.commit_group` batches the thread's uncommitted stores into a new bulk async-group: the four stores just issued become "group `e`". The PTX ISA (cp.async.bulk.wait_group, Description): "A bulk async operation includes the following: Optionally, reading from the tensormap. Reading from the source locations. Writing to their respective destination locations. Writes being made visible to the executing thread. The optional .read modifier indicates that the waiting has to be done until all the bulk async operations in the specified bulk async-group have completed: reading from the tensormap; the reading from their source locations." (The CUDA Programming Guide's one-line gloss for `cp_async_bulk_wait_group_read` is "Wait for the group to have completed reading from shared memory.") The global writes may still be in flight. That is exactly the property smem reuse needs and nothing more: nobody in this kernel reads D back, so waiting for global completion inside the tile loop would only add latency.

Why `N = 1`: `tma_store_wait_read<1>` is `store_pipeline.producer_acquire` with `StorePipeline = PipelineTmaStore<StagesC, StagesD-1>` because `ReuseSmemC` (sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:202-204). Its `producer_acquire(stage, count)` is `if (params_.always_wait || count > UnacquiredStages) { tma_store_wait<UnacquiredStages>(); }` (sm90_pipeline.hpp:697-700) with `UnacquiredStages = StagesD - 1`. The builder gives `StagesD = min(EpiTiles, 2) = 2` and `StagesC = ReuseSmem ? max(min(EpiTiles, 4), StagesD + 1) : min(EpiTiles, 4) = 4` with `ReuseSmem = sizeof_bits_v<ElementC_> > 8` true for fp32 (sm100_builder.inl:1109-1115; the measured policy is `Sm100TmaWarpSpecialized<4,2,16,true,false>`, note D.1 D1). So `UnacquiredStages = 1`, and because the kernel sets `epi_store_pipeline_params.always_wait = true` (sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:491) the kernel executes the wait on *every* subtile. SASS: `UTMACMDFLUSH` then `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x1` (note D.2; the explicit kernel has the same 8 `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x1`, note G.3).

The `always_wait` flag changes the executed instruction stream. `producer_acquire(state)` passes `state.count()` (sm90_pipeline.hpp:675-677), the number of advances the store state has made since kernel entry (`make_producer_start_state` sets it to 0, sm90_pipeline.hpp:254-260; `operator++` increments it, `:203-212`). The generic test `count > UnacquiredStages` would *skip* the wait while `count <= 1`. The acquire runs after `++store_pipe_producer_state` (header `:781-785`), so the first acquire of the CTA's lifetime sees `count = 1` and would skip the wait; the second sees 2 and waits. The explicit kernel's unconditional `tma_store_wait_read<1>()` on every subtile is therefore equivalent to the baseline *only because* of `always_wait = true`. Without that flag the baseline would execute one `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x1` fewer per CTA lifetime (derived from source); the static count of 8 `wait_group.read 1` sites (note E.7.4) would still pass, but the executed instruction stream would differ. When you mirror a pipeline class, read its `Params`.

**What the wait guarantees and which stage it protects.** After committing group `e`, `wait_group.read 1` returns when all groups except possibly the newest one (group `e`) have finished reading smem. The second clause of the ISA's `cp.async.bulk.wait_group` definition (quoted in Chapter 2, Section 2.7.5), "and all the prior bulk async-groups ... are complete", is what makes the wait cover *every* group older than the newest, not just the one four subtiles back; without it the wait would say nothing about groups other than the N most recent. The newest *older* group is `e - 1`, which read stage `(e - 1) & 3`; so at the end of subtile `e`, stage `(e - 1) & 3` is known free. Here is the ring over the eight subtiles of a tile (and across tiles, since `e & 3` restarts at 0 but the groups keep flowing):

```
 subtile e :      0      1      2      3      4      5      6      7   | next tile 0 ...
 writes stage :   0      1      2      3      0      1      2      3   |     0
 commits group:   0      1      2      3      4      5      6      7   |     8
 wait.read 1  : groups <= -1 (none) ; <= 0 ; <= 1 ; <= 2 ; <= 3 ; <= 4 ; <= 5 ; <= 6   |  <= 7
 so free after:   -    stage 0  st 1  st 2   st 3   st 0   st 1   st 2  |  st 3
 next write to:  st 1   st 2    st 3  st 0   st 1   st 2   st 3   st 0  |  st 1
 that stage was last read by group: (none) (none) (none)  0      1      2      3      4   |     5
```

The stage written at subtile `e + 1` is `(e + 1) & 3`, last read by group `e - 3`. The wait at subtile `e` guarantees groups `<= e - 1`, which includes `e - 3`: safe, with two subtiles of slack. Waiting for 0 instead would stall on the stores just issued and serialise the TMA read with the next subtile's `tcgen05.ld` and arithmetic; 1 overlaps them. In fact the wait at subtile `e - 2` already guaranteed group `e - 3`, so with four stages the ring should essentially never stall on a TMA read (my hypothesis, not measured: when warp 4 reaches the wait, the group it waits for was committed one subtile, about 80 SASS instructions, earlier and only had to read 8 KB of smem). The protocol is nevertheless *exactly* sufficient for a two-stage ring (stage `(e + 1) & 1 = (e - 1) & 1` is precisely the one freed by `wait.read 1`), the `Stages = 2` instance of the class's default `PipelineTmaStore<Stages, Stages - 1>`, whose `wait.read Stages - 1` frees exactly the stage written next for any `Stages`.

The four stages are a compile-time consequence of the C *type*, not of beta's run-time value: the builder evaluates `ReuseSmem = sizeof_bits_v<ElementC_> > 8` and `StagesC = ReuseSmem ? max(min(EpiTiles, 4), StagesD + 1) : min(EpiTiles, 4)` on `float` (sm100_builder.inl:1109-1115), and the D ring takes `ReuseSmemC ? StagesC : StagesD` stages (sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:163), so this instantiation has 4 stages for `beta = 0` too. The depth serves the `beta != 0` *path* of the same instantiation. There warp 3 prefetches C tiles into the same union (`CollectiveStorageReuseC`, header `:190-193`), and the stage is released to the C loader only one subtile after its D store was committed: the "lag 1" of `UnacquiredStages` (note Section 13 item 16; `store_finished = count > UnacquiredStages` at `:791-797`). For `beta = 0` that release bookkeeping is dead state and the explicit kernel omits it, but it keeps the 4 x 8192-byte layout so that the smem map, the SASS immediates and the TMA sources are the baseline's (note, Section 6.2).

### 10.10.5 The second bar.sync 1,128 (1071) and the tile update (1073-1075)

```
1071:       named_bar_sync(kBarEpilogue, kEpilogueThreads);                                           // bar.sync 1, 128
1072:     }
1073:     tm = tm_next; tn = tn_next;                                                                  // (:932-933)
1074:     ++tile;
1075:   } while (valid);
```

`cp.async.bulk.wait_group` is *thread-scoped*: it tells warp 4 that the group has finished reading, and nobody else. Warps 5-7 are about to write stage `(e + 1) & 3` in the next subtile (line 1047), so warp 4's knowledge must reach all 128 threads before anyone writes: that is the second `bar.sync 1, 128`, the baseline's second `synchronize()` (`:787`). With four stages, the stage written next was already guaranteed free two subtiles ago, by the wait of subtile `e - 2` followed by the barriers of subtiles `e - 2` and `e - 1` (10.10.4), so for this configuration the second barrier is redundant for the smem hazard (my analysis). It is load-bearing in the class's default configuration (`UnacquiredStages = Stages - 1`, sm90_pipeline.hpp:653), e.g. the two-stage `PipelineTmaStore<StagesD = 2>` of the non-`ReuseSmemC` epilogue (sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:204), where the stage written next is exactly the one this subtile's wait has just freed, and it is kept here because 16 `bar.sync 1,128` per tile is part of the measured instruction stream the explicit kernel reproduces (note D.7, G.3). The general rule is the one to carry to other kernels: *a TMA store's `wait_group` must be followed by a CTA-level barrier before other threads reuse the buffer.* A production kernel with exactly this pattern was reported in NVIDIA/TransformerEngine issue #3474, which describes the defect class of PR #3417 as "calling `cp_async_bulk_wait_group_read()` from only the issuing thread without a subsequent CTA-wide `__syncthreads()` handoff lets cooperative writers begin overwriting a shared-memory output ring buffer while the TMA engine is still reading it" and quotes that PR's expected symptom, "rare, timing-dependent output corruption, particularly under global-memory backpressure". The issue's own symptom was `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` faults on a subset of ranks on GB200 (sm_100); the thread traced those to a different bug (per-expert metadata in dynamic shared memory overwritten by TMA loads, fixed in PR #3483), so there the missing handoff was the reporter's hypothesis, not the confirmed cause (quoted from the issue and its thread).

Lines 1073-1075 make the tile fetched at line 1028 current (`:932-933`), count the tile, and loop while that tile is valid. When `clc_consume` returned false, `tm_next/tn_next` were not written and the copies are dead; the loop exits after the current tile has been fully stored.

---

## 10.11 After the loop: no store_tail (explicit.cu:1076-1080)

```
1076:   // store_tail executes nothing for beta = 0 (is_producer_load_needed() is false): no cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read 0 (Section 7.7, D15, E.6.7)
1080: }
```

The baseline's `store_tail` (sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:1269-1291) is

```
    if constexpr (ReuseSmemC) {
      if (fusion_callbacks.is_producer_load_needed()) {
        // wait for all TMA stores to complete
        store_pipeline.producer_tail(store_pipe_producer_state);
        ...
```

and `producer_tail` is `tma_store_wait<0>()` (sm90_pipeline.hpp:687-689). For `beta = 0`, `is_producer_load_needed()` is false (note, Section 8), so nothing executes: the `cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read 0` exists in the binary (`DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x0` at `0xb760`) behind that test, and the epilogue warps take the `EXIT` before it (note D.1 D15, D.6 item 11). The explicit kernel has no tail code at all; its PTX has 8 `wait_group.read 1` and 0 `wait_group.read 0` (note G.3).

**What "exit with at most one bulk group whose smem read is not awaited" means.** After subtile 7 of the last tile, warp 4 executed `wait_group.read 1` (group 6 has finished reading smem) and exits. Group 7 (the four stores of the last subtile, 8 KB from stage 3) may still be reading shared memory, and its global writes may still be in flight. Whether any other warp of the CTA is still resident at that moment is not established by the source: warp 2's 8-wait tail is released by the per-k-tile `tcgen05.commit`s to `empty[s]` (explicit.cu:942), all issued before the `acc_full` commit (explicit.cu:944) that lets this last epilogue start (Section 4.8.1), and warp 0's deallocation handshake follows the epilogue's subtile-7 release (Sections 4.8.3, 10.8), so both may already have exited when warp 4 does (derived, not measured); the global writes complete as part of kernel completion (the note's reading of the hardware semantics, Section 7.7 and B.7 D15; not measured).

Whether PTX formally guarantees that a CTA's shared memory outlives a pending bulk group of an exited thread is unverified: the PTX ISA 9.4 text has no sentence about bulk async-groups still pending when the issuing thread or CTA exits (every occurrence of "bulk async-group" concerns the `.bulk_group` completion mechanism, `commit_group` or `wait_group`). The only rule about kernel exit in the tcgen05 area is "All of the Tensor Memory that was allocated in a kernel, must be explicitly deallocated before the kernel exits". The CUDA Programming Guide's examples end with `cp_async_bulk_wait_group_read` with `N = 0`, waiting for every bulk group's smem read (not for the global writes) before termination. The baseline relies on it, and the explicit kernel mirrors the baseline exactly.

**Why one must not loosen it.** "Loosen" means allowing more than one group to be un-awaited, e.g. dropping or delaying the per-subtile `wait_group.read 1`, or waiting with `N = 2`. Inside the loop that breaks the ring (10.10.4); at exit it widens the window in which the TMA reads smem after its owners have gone. The note's contract is "preserve or tighten, never loosen" (Section 7.7, D.7). *Tightening*, a `cp.async.bulk.wait_group 0` (or `.read 0`) before the epilogue warps exit, is safe and costs one instruction (on warp 4's path) per CTA, but the explicit kernel does not do it: the acceptance criteria count `wait_group.read 0 = 0` and `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x0 = 0` as hard, so that the executed instruction stream is the baseline's (note E.6.7, E.7.4). If you write your own kernel from this template, add the full wait at exit.

---

## 10.12 Per-tile accounting, bandwidth, and why the epilogue is off the critical path

Per CTA tile (128 x 128 fp32 = 65536 B = 64 KB of D), counted from Section 9 and confirmed by the SASS inventory (note G.3, D.7):

| item | static count in one epilogue warp's program, per tile | dynamic warp-instructions per CTA tile (4 warps) | where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tcgen05.ld.32x32b.x16` (`LDTM.x16`) | 8 (one per subtile, 2 KB each) | 32, 64 KB read from TMEM | 10.7 |
| `tcgen05.wait::ld` | 1 (no SASS instruction at this site) | 4 | 10.8 |
| `mbarrier.arrive` on the leader's `acc_empty[st]` | 1 instruction (32 lanes -> 32 arrivals) | 4 instructions = 128 arrivals (x 2 CTAs = 256 = the count) | 10.8 |
| `FMUL` + `FFMA` | 128 + 128 | 512 + 512; 0 `FADD` | 10.9 |
| `st.shared.b32` (`STS`) | 128 (16 per subtile; 128 B per warp-instruction) | 512, 64 KB | 10.9 |
| `fence.proxy.async.shared::cta` | 8 | 32 (`MEMBAR.ALL.CTA; FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S` pairs) | 10.10.1 |
| `bar.sync 1,128` | 16 (two per subtile) | 64 executed (16 per warp) = 16 barrier completions | 10.10.2, 10.10.5 |
| `cp.async.bulk.tensor` store (`UTMASTG.3D`) | 32 on warp 4's path (4 per subtile, 2048 B each); 0 on warps 5-7 | 32, 64 KB written to D | 10.10.3 |
| `commit_group` / `wait_group.read 1` | 8 / 8 on warp 4's path | 8 / 8 | 10.10.4 |
| CLC consume (remote `mbarrier.arrive` on CTA 0's `clc_empty`) | 1 instruction (32 arrivals) | 4 x 32 = 128 of this CTA's 192 arrivals; 512 of the cluster's 800 = 32 + 4 x (32 + 32 + 128) | 10.6 |
| SASS instructions on the per-tile path | 696 = setup 56 + subtiles 77/78/78/78/78/78/81/92 (the baseline: 1265 incl. its dead C path) | - | note G.3 |

Whole problem: `8192^2 x 4 B = 268435456 B = 256 MiB` of D; 1024 cluster tiles x 4 CTA tiles x 64 KB. Over the measured 0.889354 ms this is an average write stream of about 302 GB/s GPU-wide, 2.3-2.4 GB/s per active SM (302 GB/s over the 132 active SMs; 64 KB per ~27.8 us on a critical-path cluster): 3.8 % of a B200's HBM3e bandwidth (NVIDIA's DGX B200 product page: "64 TB/s HBM3e bandwidth" for its eight GPUs, i.e. 8 TB/s per GPU). Memory bandwidth is not what the epilogue is about; latency and overlap are.

**Why it is off the critical path (analysis, with the measured anchors).** The per-tile period is *at most* about 27.8 us: the explicit kernel's 0.889354 ms over the 32 tiles of a critical-path cluster. It is an upper bound, because the `Avg runtime` interval also contains the per-iteration host encodes and attribute calls (note D.4; Chapter 3, Section 3.9.2). That is about 54,600 cycles at 1965 MHz, and the mainloop sets it: 128 k-tiles x 4 `tcgen05.mma` of 256 x 128 x 16. The epilogue of tile `t` runs while the MMA warp computes tiles `t + 1 ..`: the 4-stage TMEM ring lets the MMA warp get up to three tiles ahead before it would block on `acc_empty` (up to about 83 us of slack), and the epilogue only has to *average* one tile per ~27.8 us.

Its actual work is 696 instructions per warp plus eight short dependency chains (`LDTM` -> 32 FP ops -> 16 `STS` -> fence -> barrier -> 4 `UTMASTG` -> commit -> wait on the previous group's 8 KB smem read -> barrier). Even at a pessimistic average of 20 cycles per instruction the instruction stream is `696 x 20 = 13,920` cycles, 7.1 us at 1965 MHz. Adding a generous 1,000-2,000 cycles per subtile for the eight TMA round trips (8,000-16,000 cycles, 4.1-8.1 us) gives about 11-15 us per tile under these deliberately pessimistic assumptions (my estimate, not measured: the trace build timestamps the CLC and TMA *issues*, not the epilogue's end). That is well under 27.8 us; the epilogue warps spend the difference blocked in the `acc_full` wait of 10.6.

The epilogue is exposed once per CTA: after the last tile's last MMA its 8 subtiles run with nothing to overlap, plausibly a few microseconds and at most the 11-15 us estimated above, once per kernel. (At the start the epilogue warps idle in the `acc_full` wait while the first tile's mainloop runs, but nothing waits on them, so that idle time is not a cost.) The measured ratio to the CUTLASS kernel (0.99937, note G.2) is consistent with the explicit epilogue costing the same as the baseline's, which has the same 8 x (1 `LDTM`, 16 `FMUL`, 16 `FFMA`, 16 `STS`, fence, 2 `bar.sync`, 4 `UTMASTG`, commit, wait) skeleton (note G.3).

Two design consequences worth carrying to other kernels (my analysis): the accumulator ring depth trades TMEM (4 x 128 = 512 columns, all of it) for tolerance of epilogue jitter, and the release *before* the last subtile's arithmetic (10.8) is free latency for the producer. Neither helps once the epilogue itself becomes longer than the mainloop (small K, or a heavy fusion); then the epilogue is the kernel.

---

## 10.13 The whole data path for one subtile: tile (5, 9), e = 3

Assume this tile landed on accumulator stage `st` (whatever the CTA's tile counter mod 4 is; the example below uses `st = 1` where a number is needed) in the CTA at `(x, y)` with rank `r`. Rows of the CTA tile are `m = 128 x 5 + (32 w + l) = 640 + 32 w + l`; the subtile's columns are `n = 128 x 9 + 48 + j = 1200 + j`, `j = 0..15`.

```
 (1) TMEM, stage st = 1, subtile e = 3: columns 128*1 + 48 .. +63 = 176..191, all 128 lanes
     warp w reads lanes [32 w, 32 w + 32) at address T + ((32 w) << 16) + 128 + 48:
        w = 0: 0x0000B0   w = 1: 0x2000B0   w = 2: 0x4000B0   w = 3: 0x6000B0
     tcgen05.ld.sync.aligned.32x32b.x16.b32 {r0..r15}, [addr]
        lane l of warp w:  r[j] = acc[640 + 32 w + l][1200 + j]      (j = 0..15)

 (2) registers: t = alpha * r[j]; d = fmaf(beta, 0.0f, t)          (16 FMUL + 16 FFMA per thread)

 (3) smem stage e & 3 = 3, bytes [OFF_SMEM_CD + 24576, +8192) = [25088, 33280) = [0x6200, 0x8200)
     thread (w, l), value j  ->  25088 + 2048 w + 128 j + 4 ((l & 7) + 8 (((l >> 3) & 3) ^ (j & 3)))
     e.g. (w = 1, l = 5, j = 2): 25088 + 2048 + 256 + 4 (5 + 8 (0 ^ 2)) = 27476 = 0x6B54
          M-block 1, line 2, chunk 2 (lanes 0..7 of warp 1 sit in chunk 0 ^ 2 = 2 for j & 3 = 2), word 5
     fence.proxy.async.shared::cta ; bar.sync 1,128

 (4) warp 4: four TMA stores, source smem_base + 25088 + 2048 i, coordinates (640 + 32 i, 1200, 0), i = 0..3
     box 0: rows 640..671   box 1: rows 672..703   box 2: rows 704..735   box 3: rows 736..767   x columns 1200..1215
     the engine reads box i as 16 lines (n' = 0..15) x 128 B, un-swizzling chunk c of line n' to m' in [8 (c ^ (n' & 3)), +8)
     cp.async.bulk.commit_group ; cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read 1 ; bar.sync 1,128

 (5) global D (M-major, element (m, n) at D + 4 (m + 8192 n) = D + 4 m + 32768 n):
     box i, line n'  ->  128 contiguous bytes at  D + 32768 (1200 + n') + 4 (640 + 32 i)
                                               =  D + 0x2580A00 + 0x8000 n' + 0x80 i
       box 0, n' =  0 : D + 0x2580A00    (m 640..671, n 1200)
       box 1, n' =  0 : D + 0x2580A80    (m 672..703, n 1200)
       box 2, n' =  0 : D + 0x2580B00    (m 704..735, n 1200)
       box 3, n' =  0 : D + 0x2580B80    (m 736..767, n 1200)
       box 0, n' =  1 : D + 0x2588A00    (m 640..671, n 1201)
       ...
       box 3, n' = 15 : D + 0x25F8B80    (m 736..767, n 1215)
     per output column n the four boxes together write the 512 contiguous bytes [D + 32768 n + 0xA00, +0x200): rows 640..767.
     the element of step (3), (w = 1, l = 5, j = 2) = (m, n) = (677, 1202): D + 4*677 + 32768*1202 = D + 0x2590A94, inside box 1, line 2.
```

Check the arithmetic of step (5): `32768 x 1200 = 39321600`, `4 x 640 = 2560`, sum `39324160 = 0x2580A00`; the stride between lines is one D column = `4 x 8192 = 32768 = 0x8000` bytes; the stride between boxes is 32 rows = 128 bytes = `0x80`. The whole 128 x 16 subtile is 16 column-segments of 512 contiguous bytes, which is as friendly to the memory system as an M-major fp32 store of 128 rows can be.

---

## 10.14 If you write this role yourself

The eight invariants to get right, in the order you will hit them:

1. Four consecutive warps whose indices cover all residues mod 4, each reading only its TMEM quadrant: `lane_off = (32 (warp % 4)) << 16`. Any other mapping is unaddressable.
2. Wait for the TMEM base with a named barrier that includes the allocating warp (`bar.sync id, 32 + 128` against its `bar.arrive`), then read the base; never hard-code 0.
3. One `try_wait` peek per tile on your own `acc_full[st]`, the blocking wait before the first load; `tcgen05.ld` addresses warp-uniform, `16 e` as immediates by unrolling.
4. After the last load of the tile: `tcgen05.wait::ld` (the ISA-required anti-dependency fence: the register consumers of the loads need no wait, the TMEM overwrite by the producer's next MMA does), then every thread arrives on the *producer's* `acc_empty[st]` (peer-bit-masked address for the pair, count = all consumer threads of both CTAs), then advance the state. Release before the remaining arithmetic.
5. Keep alpha and beta as kernel parameters; compute `fmaf(beta, c, alpha * acc)` with `c = 0`, never `alpha * acc` alone.
6. Derive the smem byte formula from the layout you give the TMA descriptor (atom, tiling order, swizzle on absolute address bits), check it with `cute::Swizzle` at compile time, and align the stage base to the swizzle period (512 B for `SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B`, 1024 B for `SWIZZLE_128B`). C++ dereferences through the generic pointer; asm operands through the 32-bit `shared::cta` address.
7. Per subtile: all threads `fence.proxy.async.shared::cta`; `bar.sync`; one warp issues the boxes (uniform operands, no election needed), `commit_group`, `wait_group.read (Stages_D - 1)`; `bar.sync` again before anyone writes the next stage. The wait is thread-scoped; the barrier is what publishes it.
8. At exit, the baseline leaves one group un-awaited; in your own kernel add `cp.async.bulk.wait_group 0` before the storing warp exits.

---

# Chapter 11. The Frame: Kernel Prologue, Dispatch, and the Host Launch Mirror

Chapters 7-10 covered the four role functions; this chapter is the frame around them: everything that runs before the roles start and everything on the host that makes the kernel start.

---

## 11.1 Where we are in the file

```
explicit.cu
  ...
  1082  } // namespace (anonymous)              <- roles (Chapters 7-10) end here
  1085  // 10. [PROD] The kernel                 <- THIS CHAPTER, 11.2-11.7
  1095  __global__ void __launch_bounds__(256, 1)
  1096  explicit_blackwell_fp16_gemm_kernel(const __grid_constant__ ExplicitGemmParams params) {
  ...
  1203  }
  1206  // 11. [HOST] [PROD] run()               <- 11.8
  1212  #if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)  (watchdog, 1212-1263)
  1265  cutlass::Status run(ExplicitGemmParams const& params) {
  1329  }
  1332  // 12. [HOST] [TRACE] trace_begin / trace_end / mismatch dump
  1337  #if defined(CUTLASS_DEABSTRACTION_TRACE)
  1449  #endif
  1451  } // namespace explicit_gemm
```

The kernel lives in `namespace explicit_gemm`, outside the anonymous namespace that closes at explicit.cu:1082. Two things refer to it from outside that namespace: the host function `run()` at 1275 takes its address, and the trace build prints its name (`TRACE_HOST explicit_kernel_name explicit_blackwell_fp16_gemm_kernel`, explicit.cu:1352) and takes its address for the post-run attribute probe (explicit.cu:1443). Everything the kernel calls (the W1-W36 wrappers, the helper functions and the role functions; W37 is the `__syncwarp()` intrinsic) is in the anonymous namespace and `__forceinline__`, so the compiled kernel is one function with no source-level call left (note G.3: 1640 SASS instructions, `STACK 0`); the only two `CALL`s in its SASS, at 0x5b70 and 0x5ba0, are the failure paths of the ptxas-inserted `tcgen05.dealloc` consistency checks and target the `BPT.TRAP` stubs at 0x6530 and 0x6560 (Section 12.2).

---

## 11.2 The signature (explicit.cu:1095-1098)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1095-1098
__global__ void __launch_bounds__(256, 1)
explicit_blackwell_fp16_gemm_kernel(const __grid_constant__ ExplicitGemmParams params) {
  extern __shared__ char smem[];
  uint32_t const smem_base = smem_u32(smem);                                                   // 0x400 + (rank << 24) measured (D.1 D5); computed, never assumed
```

Four decisions are packed into these four lines. The first three copy what CUTLASS's `device_kernel` does (`include/cutlass/device_kernel.h:112-126`); the fourth, the `smem_u32` conversion of 11.2.4, has no counterpart there: `device_kernel` passes the generic `smem` pointer on, and CUTLASS converts at the point of use through `cute::cast_smem_ptr_to_uint` (`cute/arch/util.hpp:93-108`; `barrier.h`, `sm100_pipeline.hpp`):

```cpp
// device_kernel.h:112-126 (verbatim)
template <typename Operator>
CUTLASS_GLOBAL
#ifdef __CUDACC__
// Enclosing this in __CUDACC__ suppresses MSVC warnings.
__launch_bounds__(Operator::MaxThreadsPerBlock, Operator::MinBlocksPerMultiprocessor)
#endif // __CUDACC__
void device_kernel(CUTLASS_GRID_CONSTANT typename Operator::Params const params)
{
  // Dynamic shared memory base pointer
  extern __shared__ char smem[];
  Operator op;
  op(params, smem);
  cutlass::arch::synclog_print();

}
```

(`CUTLASS_GLOBAL` is `__global__ static`, `include/cutlass/detail/helper_macros.hpp:67`; the explicit kernel omits `static`, so its symbol has external linkage; this is not forced by `run()` or the trace build, which refer to it from the same translation unit (11.1) and could do so under internal linkage too.)

### 11.2.1 `__launch_bounds__(256, 1)`

`MaxThreadsPerBlock = 256` and `MinBlocksPerMultiprocessor = 1` are the baseline kernel's values (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:144-147`: `32 + 32 + 32 + 32 + 128 = 256` threads, one block per SM). The CUDA Programming Guide (appendix "Launch Bounds", section 5.4.3.2 of the v13 guide) states what the attribute does: "If launch bounds are specified, the compiler first derives the upper limit, `L`, on the number of registers that the kernel should use. This ensures that `minBlocksPerMultiprocessor` blocks (or a single block, if `minBlocksPerMultiprocessor` is not specified) of `maxThreadsPerBlock` threads can reside on the multiprocessor". A launch with more than `maxThreadsPerBlock` threads fails.

The arithmetic for this kernel: the SM has 64 K = 65536 32-bit registers (Blackwell Tuning Guide; Programming Guide "Compute Capabilities" table for CC 10.x). One block of 256 threads may therefore use `65536 / (256 x 1) = 256` registers per thread, which the hardware caps at the per-thread maximum of 255 (same table; Blackwell Tuning Guide: "The maximum number of registers per thread is 255"). The derived limit `L` is the architectural maximum, so the attribute constrains nothing the hardware does not already constrain. The measured kernel uses 26 registers (note G.3, `REG:26`), the baseline 68.

The value 1 is exact, not a conservative lower bound. The 230400 bytes of dynamic shared memory plus the 1 KB the system reserves per block consume 231424 of the SM's 233472 bytes (228 KB; the per-block opt-in maximum is 227 KB = 232448 bytes: note D.5 `device_max_smem_per_block_optin 232448`, `device_reserved_smem_per_block 1024`; Blackwell Tuning Guide). So at most one CTA fits regardless of registers (note, Section 6.2): `2 x 231424 = 462848 > 233472`.

### 11.2.2 `const __grid_constant__ ExplicitGemmParams params`

The parameter block is passed **by value** (640 bytes on CUDA 13.3, explicit.hpp:74; note G.1 `sizeof_ExplicitGemmParams 640`; G.3 `CONSTANT[0]` = 0x380 + 640). Three kinds of device-side consumer (seven address-taking expressions in all) take its **address**:

| Site | Expression | Instruction |
|---|---|---|
| explicit.cu:1114-1115, 1118-1119 | `&params.tma_a` ... `&params.tma_d` | `prefetch.tensormap [addr]` (W20) |
| explicit.cu:747, 754 (producer_role, Chapter 8) | `&params.tma_a`, `&params.tma_b` | `cp.async.bulk.tensor.3d ... [addr, {...}]` (W21, W22) |
| explicit.cu:1066 (epilogue_role, Chapter 10) | `&params.tma_d` | `cp.async.bulk.tensor.3d.global.shared::cta.bulk_group [addr, ...]` (W23) |

The TMA unit reads the 128-byte `CUtensorMap` through that address. The PTX ISA defines the tensor map as a 128-byte opaque object living in `.const`, `.param` (kernel parameter) or `.global` space, and `prefetch.tensormap` reads it from `.const` or `.param` space (PTX ISA, `prefetch`; `cp.async.bulk.tensor`; the ISA sentence is quoted in 11.4.3). The address must therefore name the **original** parameter-space object.

`__grid_constant__` makes that true. The CUDA Programming Guide (appendix 5.4.1.5, "`__grid_constant__` Parameters") allows the annotation on `const`-qualified non-reference kernel parameters. With it, the compiler creates no per-thread local copy, all threads in the kernel see the same address, and modifying the object is undefined behaviour. The hpp's byte map (explicit.hpp:18-29) records where the block lands in SASS: it starts at `c[0x0][0x380]`, so `k` is read as `ld.param.b32 [+520]` -> `c[0x0][0x588]`, `alpha, beta` as `ld.param.v2.b32 [+528]` -> `c[0x0][0x590]`/`[0x594]`, and the D descriptor address is `c[0x0][0x348] + 0x180` (note G.3; the baseline's is `c[0x0][0x348] + 0x680`, note D.2).

**What would happen without it (my analysis, from the guide's wording).** Taking the address of a plain by-value parameter forces a per-thread copy in local memory, and the TMA would be handed a generic address of local memory, which is in none of the three state spaces the ISA allows for a tensor map (Chapter 5, Section 5.3.2). The measured `LOCAL:0 STACK:0` (note G.3) is the evidence that no copy exists.

The `const` is not decoration: the guide permits `__grid_constant__` only on `const`-qualified parameters. `run()` strips the constness on the host side only to satisfy the `void**` signature of `cudaLaunchKernelExC` (explicit.cu:1311, `const_cast<void*>(static_cast<void const*>(&params))`).

### 11.2.3 `extern __shared__ char smem[]` and the absent alignment attribute

The whole 230400-byte working set is **dynamic** shared memory, requested at launch (`launch_config.dynamicSmemBytes = kSmemBytes`, explicit.cu:1302). No other `__shared__` declaration exists in the translation unit: `grep -n __shared__` finds the declaration at explicit.cu:1097 and the banner comments at 1085-1086, nothing else. CUTLASS does the same (`device_kernel.h:121`; note, Section 6.2: `cudaFuncGetAttributes` reports `sharedSizeBytes 0`).

Why no static shared memory and no `__align__` on the declaration:

1. **The system-reserved kilobyte determines the base address.** The 32-bit `shared::cta` address of the first byte of dynamic shared memory is `0x400 + (rank << 24)` in every CTA (`0x00000400`, `0x01000400`, `0x02000400`, `0x03000400`; measured, note D.1 item D5, K0 and K1 agree; ptxas forms it from `SR_CgaCtaId`, Chapter 2, Section 2.9.2). The kilobyte below it is the system-reserved shared memory that `cuobjdump` reports as `SHARED:1024`, that the `tcgen05.alloc` lowering uses for its pair handshake (note D.2, "Resource facts"), and that makes the per-block opt-in maximum 227 KB rather than the SM's 228 KB ("CUDA reserves 1 KB of shared memory per thread block", Blackwell Tuning Guide; Chapter 5, Section 5.7.1): the `0x400` base, the `SHARED:1024` resource line and the `static_assert(kSmemBytes <= 232448)` at util.hpp:46 are three views of one fact. The rank sits in address byte 3, bits [24,32) (compiler lowering, note D.2; Section 2.9.2; only bits 24-25 vary for a 4-CTA cluster, note D.1 D5), and the peer-bit mask `0xFEFFFFFF` (explicit.cu:187), which clears bit 24, relies on that placement (Chapter 4, Chapter 8).

2. **Every `OFF_*` keeps its alignment.** With the base at `0x400` (1024-aligned), `smem_base + OFF_SMEM_A = 0x400 + 33792 = 0x8800` and `smem_base + OFF_SMEM_B = 0x400 + 164864 = 0x28800` are 1024-aligned, as the SWIZZLE_128B TMA writes and the UMMA descriptor's SBO/LBO arithmetic require (note Section 7.5), and `smem_base + OFF_SMEM_CD = 0x600` is 512-aligned (SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B, note Section 7.7). The `static_assert`s at explicit.cu:162-163 check the offsets. The base alignment is a launch property the asserts cannot see. That is why the comment at 1098 says "computed, never assumed": `smem_base` is always obtained from `__cvta_generic_to_shared` at run time.

3. **The 14-bit UMMA start-address field cannot overflow.** The smem descriptor stores `(addr >> 4) & 0x3FFF`, i.e. it addresses 2^18 = 262144 bytes (Chapter 9). `static_assert(kSmemBaseLow24 + kSmemBytes < (1u << 18))` at explicit.cu:165 checks `0x400 + 230400 = 231424 < 262144`. Where static shared memory would sit relative to the dynamic buffer is not a source-level contract (NVIDIA internal), so any static declaration could move the base away from the measured `0x400` (my analysis; see item 4).

4. **What static `__shared__` would do.** Suppose the kernel declared `__shared__ uint32_t flag;`. `sharedSizeBytes` would no longer be 0, and the dynamic base could move away from the measured `0x400`: the placement of static `__shared__` objects relative to each other and to the dynamic buffer is not a source-level contract (NVIDIA internal), so the shift cannot be read off the declaration. (The guide says only that all `extern __shared__` arrays start at the same address.) `OFF_SMEM_A` could then lose its 1024-byte alignment, the TMA SW128 writes and the UMMA reads would disagree on the swizzle phase, and `D` would be wrong (my analysis of the consequence). That is why the kernel declares no static `__shared__` and reads the base at run time (item 2). In addition `230400 + static` must not exceed the 232448-byte opt-in limit, so at most 2048 bytes of static data would even fit. CUTLASS avoids all of this by putting every barrier, response slot and pointer into the same dynamic `SharedStorage` struct (note, Section 6.2 table); the explicit kernel keeps those exact offsets (explicit.cu:139-155).

The declaration carries no alignment attribute, as `device_kernel.h:121` carries none and as note E.6.7 requires ("no `__align__` on the dynamic buffer"). Whether an alignment attribute on an `extern __shared__` declaration would move the dynamic buffer is not documented in the sources used here (unverified). It is moot for this kernel: with `sharedSizeBytes 0` the base is the measured `0x400`, every address the kernel hands to hardware is an integer computed from `smem_base`, and the compiler never needs an alignment assumption on `smem`.

### 11.2.4 `smem_u32` and the address-space rule

```cpp
// explicit.cu:258
__device__ __forceinline__ uint32_t smem_u32(void const* p) { return static_cast<uint32_t>(__cvta_generic_to_shared(p)); }
```

`smem` is a **generic** pointer (64-bit, usable by C++ loads and stores); `smem_base` is the **32-bit shared-window address** that every `.shared::cta`/`.shared::cluster` PTX operand needs. The rule stated once in the file header (explicit.cu:22-23) and in note E.6.1:

| Use | Form | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| any asm operand naming shared memory (`mbarrier.*`, `cp.async.bulk.tensor.*`, `tcgen05.*`, `clusterlaunchcontrol.*`, `mapa`) | `smem_base + OFF_*` (`"r"` constraint) | all of Chapters 7-10 |
| any C++ dereference of shared memory | `smem + OFF_*` (generic pointer) | the TMEM base read `*reinterpret_cast<uint32_t const*>(smem + OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR)` (explicit.cu:888, 998); the epilogue's 16 `st.shared.b32` written as `*reinterpret_cast<uint32_t*>(smem + ...)` (explicit.cu:1047) |

Mixing them is not a subtle bug: indexing the generic `smem` by a value that already contains the shared-window offset is off by `0x400` in rank 0 and by `0x01000400`, `0x02000400`, `0x03000400` (16-48 MiB) in ranks 1-3 (note E.6.1). The kernel passes both `smem` and `smem_base` to the two roles that need a C++ dereference (`mma_role`, `epilogue_role`, explicit.cu:1198, 1201) and only `smem_base` to the other two.

One compiler detail for reading the PTX (note B.6, D.2): nvcc emits no `cvta.to.shared` instruction for this conversion. It folds it into `mov.b32 %r, smem` + `add.s32 offset`, and in SASS the base is the literal `0x400 | (SR_CgaCtaId << 24)`.

## 11.3 Step 1: identity (explicit.cu:1100-1107)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1100-1107
  // 7.3 step 1: warp index, election, cluster identity (kernel :417-430)
  int const warp_idx = warp_idx_sync();
  uint32_t const lane = threadIdx.x & 31u;
  uint32_t const lane_pred = elect_one_sync();
  uint32_t const rank = cluster_ctarank();
  bool const is_cta0 = (rank == 0u);
  bool const is_leader = ((rank & 1u) == 0u);                                                   // cta_coord_v = rank % 2 == 0
  uint32_t const peer = rank ^ 1u;
```

"kernel :417-430" is `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:417-430`:

```cpp
// sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:418-430 (verbatim)
    int warp_idx = canonical_warp_idx_sync();
    WarpCategory warp_category = warp_idx < static_cast<int>(WarpCategory::Epilogue) ? WarpCategory(warp_idx)
                                                                                     : WarpCategory::Epilogue;

    uint32_t lane_predicate = cute::elect_one_sync();
    auto cluster_shape = cutlass::detail::select_cluster_shape(ClusterShape{});
    int cluster_size = size(cluster_shape);
    uint32_t cta_rank_in_cluster = cute::block_rank_in_cluster();
    bool is_first_cta_in_cluster = cta_rank_in_cluster == 0;
    int cta_coord_v = cta_rank_in_cluster % size<0>(typename TiledMma::AtomThrID{});
    bool is_mma_leader_cta = cta_coord_v == 0;
    constexpr bool has_mma_peer_cta = size(AtomThrShapeMNK{}) == 2;
    [[maybe_unused]] uint32_t mma_peer_cta_rank = has_mma_peer_cta ? cta_rank_in_cluster ^ 1 : cta_rank_in_cluster;
```

| Variable | Wrapper / PTX | Value in this run | Why this form |
|---|---|---|---|
| `warp_idx` | W1 `__shfl_sync(0xffffffff, static_cast<int>(threadIdx.x / 32), 0)` (explicit.cu:261; `cutlass.h:127-133`) | 0..7 | see below |
| `lane` | `threadIdx.x & 31` | 0..31 | needed only by the scheduler (lanes 0..3 arm the CLC barriers, Chapter 7) and the epilogue (row ownership, Chapter 10) |
| `lane_pred` | W2 `elect.sync` (explicit.cu:264-278; `cluster_sm90.hpp:180-197`) | 1 in exactly one lane per warp | the prologue election, reused where the baseline reuses it (11.3.2) |
| `rank` | W3 `mov.u32 %0, %cluster_ctarank` (explicit.cu:281) | 0..3 | the PTX special register giving the linear CTA rank in the cluster; measured `rank = x + 2y` with `(x, y) = %cluster_ctaid` (note Section 7.1; the K0 probe's `cluster_ctaid` fields in `launch0.csv` and D.1 D8's per-rank TMA coordinates confirm it; Section 2.1.2) |
| `is_cta0` | `rank == 0` | true in one CTA per cluster | the CLC scheduler warp and the owner of the CLC/throttle `empty` barriers live in CTA 0 (Chapter 7) |
| `is_leader` | `(rank & 1) == 0` | ranks 0, 2 | `cta_coord_v = rank % size<0>(AtomThrID) = rank % 2` in the baseline: the even CTA of a pair issues the 2SM MMAs (Chapter 9) |
| `peer` | `rank ^ 1` | 1, 0, 3, 2 | the other CTA of the MMA pair; used only for the TMEM dealloc handshake (`mbar_arrive_remote(..., peer)`, explicit.cu:964, 970) |

### 11.3.1 Why the warp index goes through a shuffle

`threadIdx.x / 32` is already the same in every lane of a warp, but the compiler cannot prove it: it sees a per-thread expression. `__shfl_sync(0xffffffff, v, 0)` returns lane 0's value in every lane, so the result is **warp-uniform by construction**, and the full mask forces warp convergence at that point. CUTLASS's own comment says so (`cutlass.h:124-125`: "Returns a warp-uniform value indicating the canonical warp index of the calling threads. Threads within the warp must be converged."). The payoff is in the SASS: every plain `if (warp_idx == N)` in the prologue (the four init groups) and the dispatch becomes a *uniform* branch (`UISETP`/`BRA.U`; the three guards that also test `lane_pred`, explicit.cu:1113, 1117, 1165, keep a per-lane `ISETP ... !P0`), and the role selection becomes a three-entry jump table on a uniform register (`BRXU UR10`, 11.7.2). The explicit kernel emits **one** `SHFL.IDX` for this. The baseline's PTX has nine `shfl.sync.idx.b32` sites: one in the kernel body and one or two per pipeline constructor, because the `PipelineTmaAsync` base constructor runs `canonical_warp_idx_sync()` and `init_barriers` runs it again (note B.5 and B.2 step 12). Seven of the nine survive as `SHFL.IDX` in SASS (note D.2 "7 of 9 PTX sites"; G.3 "one `SHFL.IDX` for the warp index instead of seven").

### 11.3.2 The one prologue election, and where fresh elections are made

`elect.sync d|p, membermask` elects one leader lane of `membermask` deterministically ("the same leader thread is elected for the same membermask every time") and its mandatory `.sync` makes it a warp convergence point (PTX ISA 9.7.15.15, quoted in Chapter 2, Section 2.10.3). *Which* lane is not specified: measured, lane 0 in all 1184 trace records written under an election (note B.2 step 4, whose wording "may differ between calls" the ISA text supersedes; the practical rule is unchanged: never hard-code lane 0). Every `elect_one_sync()` in the kernel (W2, explicit.cu:264-278, always with mask `0xFFFFFFFF`) is therefore also a convergence point, one reason the role functions can rely on the whole warp being together at each election, and `lane_pred` (explicit.cu:1103) stays valid because no role function has a lane-divergent exit (note E.6.3 "warp-convergence contract"). It is **reused** exactly where the baseline reuses `lane_predicate`, and **fresh** elections are made exactly where the baseline's helpers make their own:

| Site | Election | Baseline anchor | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| explicit.cu:1113, 1117 prefetch of A, B (warp 1) and C, D (warp 3) | reuse `lane_pred` | kernel `:440, :443` `&& lane_predicate` | one `prefetch.tensormap` per descriptor per CTA; any lane will do |
| explicit.cu:1165 `tmem_dealloc` init (warp 0) | reuse `lane_pred` | kernel `:564` `if (has_mma_peer_cta && lane_predicate)` | one `mbarrier.init` |
| explicit.cu:1192 producer `is_leader_lane` = `lane_pred != 0u && is_leader` | reuse `lane_pred` | kernel `:465` `is_leader = lane_predicate && is_mma_leader_cta && is_participant.main_load` | the per-k-tile `arrive.expect_tx` (Chapter 8) is issued by this one lane of the pair leader's warp 2 for the whole kernel |
| explicit.cu:1125, 1136, 1146, 1156 the four `mbarrier.init` groups | **fresh** `elect_one_sync()` each | `initialize_barrier_array_pair_aligned` does its own `if(cute::elect_one_sync())` (`barrier.h:134`, `:146`) | PTX-level parity: the baseline's constructors do not see `lane_predicate` |
| explicit.cu:740 TMA A+B pair (Chapter 8) | fresh, one per pair | `sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:619-622` | one election guards both loads |
| explicit.cu:932 each `tcgen05.mma` (Chapter 9) | fresh | `mma_sm100_umma.hpp:563-586` (election inside the CUTLASS `fma`) | one election per MMA |
| explicit.cu:942, 944 each `tcgen05.commit` | fresh | `barrier.h:848-861` | one election per commit |
| explicit.cu:843 each CLC query (Chapter 7) | fresh | `sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:445-446` at cb424739 (`:445` and `:452` in the working tree) | one election per `try_cancel` |

Functionally, reusing `lane_pred` for the init groups would be equivalent (note E.6.3 step 1 says so), and the ISA's determinism guarantee makes that strictly true: every election in this kernel uses the same `membermask` `0xFFFFFFFF`, so `lane_pred` from the prologue and any fresh `elect_one_sync()` in a role select the **same** lane. "Reuse" and "re-elect" differ only in the instruction stream, never in which lane does the work. The fresh elections exist so that the PTX inventory matches the baseline's contract (14 `elect.sync` sites in the explicit kernel, note G.3). None of the in-loop elections survives in SASS: ptxas folds them away because the guarded instructions (`UTMALDG`, `UTCHMMA`, `UTCBAR`, `UGETNEXTWORKID`) are uniform-datapath instructions that issue once per warp anyway (note D.6 item 6, G.3: `ELECT` 4 sites, all outside the loops). The same determinism licenses that folding (my analysis). Write the PTX form anyway: it is the documented contract, and it costs nothing after ptxas.

## 11.4 Step 2: scalars, k-tile count, descriptor prefetch (explicit.cu:1109-1120)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1109-1120
  // 7.3 step 2: run-time scalars and k-tile count (every thread); descriptor prefetch (kernel :439-445)
  float const alpha = params.alpha;
  float const beta = params.beta;
  int const k_tiles = (params.k + 63) >> 6;
  if (warp_idx == 1 && lane_pred) {                                                            // Sched warp of every CTA: A, B
    prefetch_tensormap(&params.tma_a);
    prefetch_tensormap(&params.tma_b);
  }
  if (warp_idx == 3 && lane_pred) {                                                            // EpilogueLoad warp of every CTA, regardless of beta: C, D
    prefetch_tensormap(&params.tma_c);
    prefetch_tensormap(&params.tma_d);
  }
```

### 11.4.1 `alpha`, `beta`

Every thread reads both once from parameter space (`ld.param.v2.b32 [+528]`, one instruction for both; note G.3), and only the epilogue uses them (`t = alpha * acc; d = fmaf(beta, 0.0f, t)`, explicit.cu:1045-1046, Chapter 10). They are **run-time** values on purpose (note D.7 "Arithmetic"). With compile-time `1.0f`/`0.0f` the compiler would fold `1.0f * acc` to `acc` (an exact identity) and `fmaf(0.0f, 0.0f, t)` to at most one `FADD` of `+0.0f + t` (not to `t`: `+0.0 + (-0.0) = +0.0`, so nvcc cannot drop the add without fast-math); the fold is inferred, not measured (note Section 0 and D.7). The 128 `FMUL` + 128 `FFMA` per tile that match the baseline's would disappear from the explicit kernel's instruction stream. `D` would **stay bit-identical** under that fold (the baseline's own `FFMA` computes the same `+0.0 + t`); what would be lost is the instruction-stream parity that note D.7 requires (verified in G.3), and with it the ability to compare the two epilogues opcode for opcode. Chapter 10 has the `-0.0` arithmetic and the reason the C term is kept as an FFMA with the run-time `beta`. The baseline reads the same two values in the epilogue collective's constructor (kernel `:437`). Note B.2 step 9 lists the stride and pointer tests the baseline performs first; the explicit struct has none because it has no pointer path (the host guard at explicit.cu:1271 rejects non-null `alpha_ptr`/`beta_ptr`).

**What ptxas does with the two loads (measured, note G.3 and D.2).** Although the PTX reads `alpha, beta` in the prologue, ptxas sinks the load in the explicit kernel to the epilogue entry: one `LDCU.64 UR26, c[0x0][0x590]` (`params + 528`), `alpha` in `UR26`, `beta` in `UR27`, used as `FMUL Rk, Rk, UR26` and `FFMA Rk, RZ, UR27, Rk`. The baseline loads at kernel entry instead: `alpha` into a vector register (`LDC R2, c[0x0][0x8a0]`, used as `FMUL Rk, R2, Rk`) and `beta` into a uniform register (`LDCU UR21, c[0x0][0x880]`). When you read the SASS of your own rewrite, expect the load wherever ptxas finds the shortest live range, not where the C++ put it; both placements compute the same IEEE operations on the same operands.

### 11.4.2 `k_tiles = (params.k + 63) >> 6`

The number of 64-wide k-tiles per output tile, `ceil(K / kTileK)` with `kTileK = 64` (util.hpp:30): `(8192 + 63) >> 6 = 8255 >> 6 = 128`. It is a ceiling division because a K that is not a multiple of 64 would still need its last partial k-tile (the TMA unit zero-fills out-of-bounds elements, `CU_TENSOR_MAP_FLOAT_OOB_FILL_NONE` in the encode, note Section 5.3). The baseline computes it as `ceil_div(get<2>(problem_shape), get<2>(tile_shape))` in `PersistentTileSchedulerSm100::get_work_k_tile_count` (`sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:502-506` at cb424739, `:533-537` in the working tree), and its SASS computes `(K + 63) >> 6` once at `0x1640-0x1700` (note D.2). For the fixed run the host guard makes `k == 8192` a precondition (explicit.cu:1268), so `k_tiles` is always 128. The device code keeps the general formula so that its instruction stream reads `k` exactly as the baseline does (`ld.param.b32 [+520]`, the only field of the problem shape the device reads; note G.3: `m`, `n`, `l` are never read). One measured difference: the baseline re-reads `K` from `c[0x0][0x38c]` on **every tile** for its `k_tile_count >= 1` test (note D.2, the re-load at `0x3770`), whereas the explicit kernel keeps `k_tiles` in the uniform register `UR14`, loaded once at `0x0a70`, for the whole of the producer and MMA roles (the epilogue code, which never needs it, reuses `UR14`). That is why its accumulator-empty wait and commit block is 15 instructions against the baseline's 18 (note G.3). Note E.6.6 allows either ("`k_tiles` may be held in a register (the baseline re-reads `K` per tile; either is fine, D.2)"); it is one of the few permitted instruction-stream differences.

### 11.4.3 `prefetch.tensormap` by warps 1 and 3

- **Why prefetch.** The wrapper is W20 (Section 6.6.2). The first `cp.async.bulk.tensor` that names a descriptor must fetch the 128-byte tensor map from parameter space into the tensor-map descriptor cache (the ISA leaves it unnamed), not the L2 data cache (NVIDIA internal) before it can compute a single address. `prefetch.tensormap` starts that fetch in the prologue, well before the producer issues its first load. The rest of the 175-instruction prologue (note G.3), the cluster rendezvous, `griddepcontrol.wait` and the first `empty[]` wait all lie between the two. (The distance itself was not measured; no trace record covers `prefetch.tensormap`, and none could observe its completion: the instruction is per-thread, best-effort and has no completion mechanism (NVIDIA internal).) This is the PTX-documented purpose of the instruction (PTX ISA, `prefetch{.tensormap_space}.tensormap [a]`, `.tensormap_space = {.const, .param}`: "brings the cache line containing the specified address in the .const or .param memory state space for subsequent use by the cp.async.bulk.tensor instruction"). The kernel uses the generic-address form (no `.const`/`.param` suffix; "If no state space is given, the prefetch uses Generic Addressing"), exactly as CUTLASS does, so the generic address must resolve to the parameter-space object. nvcc makes that explicit by emitting one `cvta.param` of the parameter block at each of the four code sites that take a `&params.tma_*` address (warp 1's and warp 3's prefetch blocks, the producer, the epilogue; the maps at non-zero offsets follow as `add.s64` +128/+256/+384; note G.3: "four `cvta.param` for the map addresses"): PTX-level evidence that the `__grid_constant__` address of 11.2.2 is the parameter-space object and not a copy.
- **Why warps 1 and 3.** Copied from kernel `:439-445` into explicit.cu:1113-1120: the `Sched` warp prefetches the mainloop's descriptors and the `EpilogueLoad` warp the epilogue's, in **every** CTA (not only rank 0 for warp 1, not only when `beta != 0` for warp 3). Warp 1 is otherwise idle in the prologue, warp 3 issues only the throttle `mbarrier.init` group (explicit.cu:1155-1163), and warp 1 of ranks 1-3 and warp 3 everywhere exit at the dispatch, so the prefetch is free work for threads that would otherwise do nothing. (My analysis of the motive; the fact is derived from source.)
- **Why C is prefetched although `beta = 0` never reads it.** Parity with the baseline's four `UTMACCTL.PF` (note D.2: `0x0310`/`0x0320` for A, B by warp 1 and `0x03d0`/`0x03e0` for C, D by warp 3; note D.7 and E.10 item 7 made the four-prefetch form the default). The explicit kernel's SASS has the same four (note G.3, `UTMACCTL.PF 4`), and its PTX inventory keeps `prefetch.tensormap` 4. Dropping `tma_c` would be harmless for correctness; it was kept so that the compiled-artefact comparison is like for like. The prefetch costs one best-effort fill of the tensor map's line in the tensor-map descriptor cache in the prologue, not an L2 data-cache line (NVIDIA internal), and keeps the C map live for a future `beta != 0` path. A from-scratch `beta = 0` kernel could drop the C map and its prefetch and shrink the parameter block to 512 bytes (5.3.2).
- **Why `lane_pred`.** One prefetch per descriptor per CTA is enough; the elected lane issues it, as in the first row of the election table in 11.3.2 (kernel `:440, :443`).

The descriptors are never modified on the device (note 7.3 step 2: "descriptors are never modified on the device"; the PTX inventories of note D.2 and G.3 contain no `tensormap.replace`), so one prefetch per descriptor at entry is all the kernel needs: no re-prefetch and no `fence.proxy.tensormap` appears in the persistent loop (the four `prefetch.tensormap` are all in the prologue, explicit.cu:1114-1119).
