## 11.5 Step 3: the 33 `mbarrier.init` calls (explicit.cu:1122-1167)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1122-1167
  // 7.3 step 3: barrier initialisation in the baseline's constructor order (33-init variant, E.10 item 6):
  // the elected lane of the initialising warp issues the inits (initialize_barrier_array*_aligned, barrier.h:120-150), every thread fences once per group
  if (warp_idx == 0) {                                                                         // mainloop pipeline (kernel :457-472; sm100_pipeline.hpp:555-573)
    if (elect_one_sync()) {
      #pragma unroll
      for (uint32_t i = 0; i < uint32_t(kStages); ++i) {
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_MAIN_FULL + 8u * i, kMainFullCount);
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_MAIN_EMPTY + 8u * i, kMainEmptyCount);
      }
    }
  }
  fence_mbarrier_init_release_cluster();
  // (epi_load pipeline, warp 1, and load_order barrier, warp 3: beta != 0 only; not initialised, E.10 item 6)
  if (warp_idx == 4) {                                                                         // CLC pipeline (kernel :501-518)
    if (elect_one_sync()) {
      #pragma unroll
      for (uint32_t i = 0; i < uint32_t(kClcStages); ++i) {
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_CLC_FULL + 8u * i, kClcFullCount);
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_CLC_EMPTY + 8u * i, kClcEmptyCount);
      }
    }
  }
  fence_mbarrier_init_release_cluster();
  if (warp_idx == 5) {                                                                         // accumulator pipeline (kernel :520-536)
    if (elect_one_sync()) {
      #pragma unroll
      for (uint32_t i = 0; i < uint32_t(kAccStages); ++i) {
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_ACC_FULL + 8u * i, kAccFullCount);
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_ACC_EMPTY + 8u * i, kAccEmptyCount);
      }
    }
  }
  fence_mbarrier_init_release_cluster();
  if (warp_idx == 3) {                                                                         // CLC throttle pipeline (kernel :538-550)
    if (elect_one_sync()) {
      #pragma unroll
      for (uint32_t i = 0; i < uint32_t(kThrottleStages); ++i) {
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_THROTTLE_FULL + 8u * i, kThrottleCount);
        mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_THROTTLE_EMPTY + 8u * i, kThrottleCount);
      }
    }
  }
  fence_mbarrier_init_release_cluster();
  if (warp_idx == 0 && lane_pred) {                                                            // tmem_dealloc barrier (kernel :562-565), no fence of its own
    mbar_init(smem_base + OFF_TMEM_DEALLOC, kTmemDeallocCount);
  }
```

`mbar_init` is W5 (explicit.cu:286-294), the asm string of `ClusterBarrier::init` (`barrier.h:391-403`): `mbarrier.init.shared::cta.b64 [addr], count;`. A freshly initialised mbarrier is in phase 0 with `count` pending arrivals and a zero tx-count, which `arrive.expect_tx` later raises on the transaction barriers; Chapter 4 explained why producers start at parity 1 and consumers at parity 0 against such a barrier. The ISA puts two constraints on the operands (PTX ISA, `mbarrier.init` and "Size and alignment of mbarrier object"). `count` must lie in `[1, 2^20 - 1]` for the default `.layout::v0` object, so 800 and 256 are nowhere near the limit. (The `count` operand is 32-bit, but its value must fit the hardware field/range behind this bound (NVIDIA internal). The SASS init word `{(0x100000 - count) << 1, (0x100000 - count) << 11}` of note D.2 is consistent with this 20-bit bound: it holds `2^20 - count`, read as the count's complement in a 20-bit field; that reading is inferred from the SASS, as in 4.2.1 and 12.2, and the ISA states only the range.) And the object is an opaque `.b64` that must be 8-byte aligned in `.shared`, which every `OFF_*` below satisfies (all multiples of 8).

### 11.5.1 The map of the 512-byte control region

Every init writes 8 bytes at `smem_base + OFF_* + 8 i`. The region (note, Section 6.2; constants at explicit.cu:139-152):

```
offset  bytes  object                         count     init warp   this kernel
   0     64    main full[0..7]                1 (+tx)   0           yes
  64     64    main empty[0..7]               2         0           yes
 128     32    epi_load full[0..3]            32 (+tx)  1           NO  (beta != 0 only)
 160     32    epi_load empty[0..3]           128       1           NO
 192     16    load_order[0..1]               32        3           NO
 208     16    clc full[0..1]                 1 (+tx)   4           yes
 224     16    clc empty[0..1]                800       4           yes
 240     32    acc full[0..3]                 1         5           yes
 272     32    acc empty[0..3]                256       5           yes
 304     16    throttle full[0..1]            32        3           yes
 320     16    throttle empty[0..1]           32        3           yes
 336      8    tmem_dealloc                   32        0           yes
 344      8    (pad: PipelineStorage is aligned_struct<16>)
 352     32    clc_response[0..1]             16-byte CLC responses (written by hardware)
 384      4    tmem_base_ptr                  written by tcgen05.alloc
 388    124    (pad to 512: tensors need 512-byte alignment)
 512 ...       smem_C/D, smem_A, smem_B       (Chapters 8-10)
```

The 43 mbarrier slots occupy bytes 0..343 (344 bytes). CUTLASS's `PipelineStorage` is 352 bytes including its pad (note D.1 D2, `PipelineStorage 352`). The control objects end at 388 (`OFF_TMEM_BASE_PTR + 4`), and the pad to 512 gives the first tensor stage its 512-byte alignment. (The file header at explicit.cu:59 writes "barriers 0..391": that is 388 rounded up to the next multiple of 8, my reading; the number is not derived anywhere in the note.) Initialised barriers: `8 + 8 + 2 + 2 + 4 + 4 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 33`. The baseline initialises `33 + 4 + 4 + 2 = 43` (note D.2: 43 `SYNCS.EXCH.64`).

### 11.5.2 Where each count is derived

The constants and their one-line derivations are at explicit.cu:180-185 (Chapter 4, Section 4.4 reads each one); `static_assert(kMainloopTxBytes == 49152 && kClcEmptyCount == 32 + 4 * (32 + 128 + 32))` at explicit.cu:192 pins the two that are easiest to get wrong.

### 11.5.3 Why 33 and not 43

The baseline's `epi_load` pipeline (`PipelineTransactionAsync<4>`, counts 32/128, initialising warp 1, kernel `:474-487`) and `load_order` barrier (`OrderedSequenceBarrier<1,2>`, count 32, warp 3, kernel `:494-499`) serve the C-load path (`beta != 0`), which this kernel omits (Chapter 3). When `beta = 0` their ten barriers are **initialised but never arrived on or waited for** (note 7.2 table, rows "initialized but never used"). The explicit kernel leaves those ten 8-byte slots as reserved, uninitialised space (comment at explicit.cu:1134). Nothing reads an uninitialised slot. The fence count follows: 4 groups here, 6 in the baseline (note E.6.3 step 3). Note E.10 item 6 recorded this as the recommended variant; D.7 accepts either.

The failure modes of a wrong `clc_empty` count are asymmetric (my analysis). An under-count completes the phase before every consumer has released the slot, so the surplus arrivals spill into the next phase and a response slot can be re-armed while a warp is still decoding it. An over-count never completes the phase and hangs CTA 0's scheduler warp at its next `clc_empty` wait (Chapter 7).

### 11.5.4 Why the fence is executed by all 256 threads, and what it orders

The fence is W14 (Section 6.4.1), copied from `cutlass::arch::fence_barrier_init`, `barrier.h:711-724`, whose comment at `barrier.h:707-710` says: "Helps with visibility of barrier init operations across warps / cta / cluster ... It must be composed with an appropriate sync instruction with the right scope to ensure visibility eg. `__syncthreads()` or a `cluster_arrive()` + `cluster_wait()`".

**What it orders.** `fence.mbarrier_init` is a restricted fence whose synchronising effect applies only to the executing thread's prior `mbarrier.init` operations on `.shared::cta` barriers, made visible at cluster scope with release semantics (PTX ISA `.op_restrict`, quoted in Chapter 2, Section 2.10.1). It pairs with the acquire of `barrier.cluster.wait` in step 6: init (release.cluster) -> arrive -> every CTA waits (acquire) -> every CTA's threads may now arrive on any CTA's barriers. This is the shape of the ISA's own examples for a relaxed cluster barrier (both quoted in Section 2.10.1), publish with a fence and then arrive relaxed, and `fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster` is the narrowest fence that satisfies it for `mbarrier.init` stores: it covers nothing else and, as shown below, emits no SASS instruction.

**Why all threads execute it although one lane per group did the inits (derived from source + my analysis).** In every mbarrier-backed CUTLASS pipeline constructor the fence sits **outside** the `if (warp_idx == initializing_warp)` test: `sm100_pipeline.hpp:559-573` (mainloop), `:139-149` (accumulator, `PipelineUmmaAsync`), `:963-979` / `:981-1000` (CLC), `sm90_pipeline.hpp:1040-1055` (throttle, `PipelineAsync`). So all 256 threads of every CTA execute it once per constructor, and the explicit kernel copies that shape (four unconditional calls at explicit.cu:1133, 1144, 1154, 1164). Three reasons:

1. The fence is a per-thread operation and a no-op for a thread that issued no init. Making it unconditional therefore costs nothing and avoids a second election or a divergent branch.
2. A thread that *did* init must fence **before** its `barrier.cluster.arrive`. A fence straight after each init group guarantees that for whichever lane was elected.
3. In SASS the instruction emits nothing at all (note D.2 and 7.3 step 3: "`fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster` emits no instruction"; the bare `FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S` seen before the init groups are attributed to the init lowering, inferred). The baseline has seven such bare `FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S` before its init groups (note D.2); the explicit kernel's prologue has five: one before each of the four init groups and one before the `tmem_dealloc` init, which has no fence of its own (`trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt` 0x0290, 0x0460, 0x0570, 0x0680, 0x0780; note G.3 counts the same five, two fewer than the baseline's seven).

The `tmem_dealloc` init at explicit.cu:1165-1167 has no fence of its own because the baseline has none there (kernel `:562-576` is followed directly by `pipeline_init_arrive_relaxed` at `:580`). This init comes *after* the fourth fence, so no `fence.mbarrier_init` covers it, and the arrive is `.relaxed`. It is the one init for which the ISA's "fence prior to arrive" pattern is **not** followed, so as far as I can read the PTX memory model, the prologue does not formally establish its visibility to the peer's remote arrive at explicit.cu:964 (unverified). What is certain: the ordering is the baseline's own (derived from source), the explicit kernel copies it, the first remote arrive on this barrier happens at kernel exit, roughly 0.9 ms after the init, and no recorded run of either kernel has hung there (measured, note G.1). If you want a provably ordered variant when you rewrite the kernel, move the `tmem_dealloc` init before the fourth fence; the protocol does not change.

### 11.5.5 Why this order and these warps

The groups appear in the order of the baseline's constructors: mainloop (kernel `:457-472`), [epi_load `:474-487`, load_order `:494-499`, omitted], CLC (`:501-518`), accumulator (`:520-536`), throttle (`:538-550`), tmem_dealloc (`:562-565`). The initialising warp of each pipeline is the baseline's `initializing_warp` parameter: 0 (`:467`), 4 (`:517`), 5 (`:531`), 3 (`:549`), and warp 0's `lane_predicate` for `tmem_dealloc` (`:564`).

**Functionally none of this matters.** An `mbarrier.init` is one 8-byte write of the encoded init word by whichever thread executes it. In SASS it is `SYNCS.EXCH.64 URZ, [UR29 + off], R` (`UR29` holds the baseline's smem base; the explicit kernel's is `UR7`, Chapter 12) with `R = {(0x100000 - count) << 1, (0x100000 - count) << 11}`, the init word of 11.5 (note D.2): a synchronisation-unit exchange on the opaque mbarrier object (`SYNCS` is "Sync Unit" in the CUDA Binary Utilities manual's Blackwell instruction set table), not an `STS`. The exchange is atomic: it reads the old word, writes the supplied one and returns the old (NVIDIA internal), here into `URZ`, so the old word is discarded (`trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt` 0x02a0). The ISA requires the object to be created by `mbarrier.init` and nothing else. The operation has no cross-thread dependency, so any thread may initialise any barrier as long as (a) each barrier is initialised exactly once before its first arrive, and (b) the init is made visible before any remote CTA can arrive on it, which the fence + cluster rendezvous guarantee for all of them together. The baseline spreads the 43 inits over warps 0, 1, 3, 4, 5 so that they proceed in parallel instead of serialising 43 stores in one warp (my analysis of the motive; the mapping itself is derived from source). The explicit kernel keeps the mapping for parity, so that the prologue's SASS can be compared row by row (note G.3: "33 `SYNCS.EXCH.64` inits with the same init words at the same Section 6.2 offsets as the baseline's corresponding 33 of 43"). If you rewrite the kernel, you may put all 33 inits in one elected lane of warp 0 followed by one fence; the protocol does not change.

---

## 11.6 Steps 4-6: the split cluster rendezvous and the initial tile (explicit.cu:1169-1179)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1169-1179
  // 7.3 step 4: cluster rendezvous, part 1 (kernel :580)
  cluster_arrive_relaxed();

  // 7.3 step 5: warp-uniform setup; the initial tile from the launch coordinate (swizzle_and_rasterize + AlongN transpose, sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:365-371, 666-677)
  uint32_t const x = cluster_ctaid_x();                                                        // == rank & 1
  uint32_t const y = cluster_ctaid_y();                                                        // == rank >> 1
  int tm = static_cast<int>(2u * (blockIdx.y >> 1) + (blockIdx.x & 1u));
  int tn = static_cast<int>(2u * (blockIdx.x >> 1) + (blockIdx.y & 1u));

  // 7.3 step 6: cluster rendezvous, part 2 (kernel :615); no remote barrier operation before this point
  cluster_wait();
```

W16/W17 (explicit.cu:428-429) are `barrier.cluster.arrive.relaxed.aligned;` and `barrier.cluster.wait.aligned;`, copied from `cute::cluster_arrive_relaxed` / `cute::cluster_wait` (`cluster_sm90.hpp:48-55, 66-73`). The baseline reaches them through `pipeline_init_arrive_relaxed(cluster_size)` and `pipeline_init_wait(cluster_size)` (`sm90_pipeline.hpp:1377-1384`, `:1364-1371`), which fall back to `__syncthreads()` for a cluster of size 1; the explicit kernel knows its cluster is 4 and calls the cluster forms directly. (ptxas nevertheless wraps both in a run-time test `c[0x0][0x36c] == 1` with `NOP` / `BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x0` fallbacks, in both kernels: note D.2 and G.3; the PTX carries no guard.)

### 11.6.1 What `barrier.cluster` does, and why `.relaxed` + split

- **Why `.relaxed`.** A `.release` arrive would order every other prior store of the thread (none matters) and cost a heavier fence. CUTLASS chose `.relaxed` and named the helper accordingly (`pipeline_init_arrive_relaxed`). (Derived from source and the PTX semantics; the cost judgement is my analysis.)
- **Why split the arrive from the wait.** Between arrive and wait, in the baseline: `load_init` (the TMA coordinate tensors), the pipeline start states, `%cluster_ctaid`, the two multicast masks, the scheduler object with the initial tile, and the TMEM accumulator tensor (kernel `:582-613`; note B.2 steps 21-25). In the explicit kernel: the two `%cluster_ctaid` reads and the two tile-coordinate lines (the rest became compile-time constants or per-role locals). The slowest CTA of the cluster is still finishing its inits while the others compute this, so the rendezvous latency overlaps the setup instead of adding to it. For the explicit kernel the window holds only a handful of instructions, but the shape is kept because it is correct, free, and makes the SASS comparable (note G.3: `UCGABAR_ARV` ... `UCGABAR_WAIT; CCTL.IVALL` behind the same ptxas-inserted `c[0x0][0x36c] == 1` guard as the baseline).
- **Why `.aligned`.** What the implementation gains from the `.aligned` promise (Section 2.10.1) is not documented; that the arrival is then processed per warp rather than per thread is my inference, not an ISA statement. The cute helpers the kernel copies (11.6) use the `.aligned` forms, so the explicit kernel does too.
- **What `CCTL.IVALL` is (NVIDIA internal information and my analysis, as marked; Chapter 12 has the listing).** The SASS pairs `UCGABAR_WAIT` with a `CCTL.IVALL` (note G.3). It is an all-invalidate cache-control operation emitted by the compiler's lowering, here after the cluster-barrier wait; it should not be read as ordinary program dataflow or as a generic CTA barrier, and which cache domain it invalidates is not a stable SASS contract (NVIDIA internal). The PTX requests only the wait's default `.acquire` (PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.15.3); that the invalidate is how that acquire is realised is my analysis, not an ISA statement.

### 11.6.2 `(x, y)` from `%cluster_ctaid`

W4 (explicit.cu:282-283) reads `%cluster_ctaid.x` and `%cluster_ctaid.y` (`cute::block_id_in_cluster`, `cluster_sm90.hpp:126-137`). The PTX ISA defines `%cluster_ctaid` as "the CTA identifier in a cluster in each dimension", unique per CTA and bounded by `0 <= %cluster_ctaid.x < %cluster_nctaid.x` (likewise y, z), and `%cluster_ctarank` as the "unique CTA identifier across all dimensions". For the (2,2,1) cluster, `x, y` are each 0 or 1 and `rank = x + 2y` (note Section 7.1; the K0 probe's `cluster_ctaid` fields in `launch0.csv` and D.1 D8's per-rank TMA coordinates confirm it, Section 2.1.2).

The second identity this chapter relies on is `x = blockIdx.x & 1`, `y = blockIdx.y & 1`, i.e. `%cluster_ctaid == blockIdx mod clusterDim`. It follows from two facts. The CUDA Programming Guide describes how clusters are formed: "Specifying clusters groups adjacent thread blocks into clusters", "Thread blocks within a cluster are always adjacent to each other within the grid", "Specifying clusters does not change the grid dimensions or the indices of a thread block within a grid" (Programming Guide 1.2.2.1.1 "Thread Block Clusters"). And `check_cluster_dims` enforces that each cluster dimension divides the grid (11.8.3). So the grid is tiled by 2 x 2 blocks of adjacent `blockIdx`, and the position inside a tile is `blockIdx mod 2`. Neither the guide nor the ISA writes the modular relation as a formula; measurement confirms it (the K0 probe records `cluster_ctaid.x/.y == (blockIdx.x & 1, blockIdx.y & 1)` and `rank = x + 2y` in all 16 CTAs, and every `launch0.csv` record has `rank == (bx & 1) + 2 (by & 1)`; note D.3: all 991 valid CLC first-CTA ids were even in both coordinates, i.e. every cluster starts at an even `blockIdx`; the other 33 of the 1024 responses were not-cancelled and carry no valid id). The comments `// == rank & 1` and `// == rank >> 1` record the identity. The kernel still reads the special registers rather than deriving `x, y` from `rank`, as the baseline also does. (In SASS the special-register read becomes arithmetic on `SR_CTAID.X/Y` with a constant-bank table, attribution inferred, note D.2 and D.6 item 14 — "irrelevant to the protocol".) `x` and `y` feed the A multicast mask `0x5 << x` and the A/B coordinates and destinations (Chapter 8), the accumulator commit mask `0x3 << 2y` (Chapter 9), and the CLC tile mapping (Chapter 7, explicit.cu:692-693).

### 11.6.3 Deriving `tm`, `tn` from the launch coordinate

The two formulas at explicit.cu:1175-1176 end a chain that starts on the host. Each link is in source.

**Link 1: the logical CTA grid is (M tiles, N tiles, L).** `GemmUniversalAdapter::run` calls `get_grid_shape(params)` (`gemm_universal_adapter.h:381`) -> `GemmUniversal::get_grid_shape` (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:383-396`) -> `TileScheduler::get_grid_shape` (`sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:220-232`) -> `get_tiled_cta_shape_mnl` (`:593-605`):

```cpp
// sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:597-600 (verbatim)
    auto [tiles_m, tiles_n, tiles_l] = product_each(ceil_div(select<0,1,3>(problem_shape_mnkl), take<0,2>(tile_shape_mnk)));
    auto ctas_m = round_nearest(tiles_m * size<0>(atom_thr_shape_mnk), size<0>(cluster_shape_mnk));
    auto ctas_n = round_nearest(tiles_n * size<1>(atom_thr_shape_mnk), size<1>(cluster_shape_mnk));
    auto ctas_l = tiles_l;
```

The kernel calls it with `TileShape{} = (256, 128, 64)` and `AtomThrShapeMNK{} = (2, 1, 1)` (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:389-393`). With `tile_shape_mnk = (256, 128, 64)` (the **pair's** MMA tile, Chapter 3), `atom_thr_shape = (2, 1, 1)` and `cluster = (2, 2, 1)`: `tiles_m = ceil(8192/256) = 32`, `ctas_m = round_nearest(32 * 2, 2) = 64`; `tiles_n = ceil(8192/128) = 64`, `ctas_n = round_nearest(64 * 1, 2) = 64`; `ctas_l = 1`. Logical grid `(64, 64, 1)` indexed (M, N, L). The `x 2` on M and `x 1` on N are the `AtomThrShape`: one 2SM MMA atom spans two CTAs along M, so the 256-row MMA tile is two 128-row CTA tiles, whereas along N one CTA owns the whole 128 columns. Note 7.4 states the same result, "ctas_m = round_up(ceil_div(8192, 256) * 2, 2) = 64, ctas_n = round_up(ceil_div(8192, 128), 2) = 64", and note 13 item 5 records that this is "`ceil_div(M, 256) * 2` (MMA tile, then times AtomThrShape), not `ceil_div(M, 128)`"; identical here. With these two formulas you can reproduce the grid for any other problem shape.

**Link 2: the launched grid is transposed for AlongN.** `possibly_transpose_grid` (`:235-250`):

```cpp
// sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:238-248 (verbatim)
    if (raster_order == RasterOrder::AlongN) {
      // Swap grid.x and grid.y for AlongN rasterization order, since the CLC scheduler
      // will schedule in AlongM order by default.
      //
      // Each grid dimension must also be a multiple of the corresponding cluster dimension,
      // so we convert the untransposed x into the number of clusters along the M mode,
      // and multiply this by cluster.n (and vice-versa for y).
      auto tmp = grid.x;
      grid.x = divmod_cluster_shape_n.divide(grid.y) * divmod_cluster_shape_m;
      grid.y = divmod_cluster_shape_m.divide(tmp) * divmod_cluster_shape_n;
    }
```

`grid.x = (64 / 2) * 2 = 64`, `grid.y = (64 / 2) * 2 = 64`. The numbers do not change for a square problem, but the **meaning** does: after this, `blockIdx.x` walks the N tiles and `blockIdx.y` the M tiles. `raster_order` is `AlongN` here because the heuristic `tiles_n > tiles_m ? AlongM : AlongN` (`tile_scheduler_params.h:338-343`, under `RasterOrderOptions::Heuristic`) gives `AlongN` for equal counts (note 13 item 4; measured `raster_order AlongN 1`, note D.1 D10, D.5 H4). The counts it compares are *cluster*-tile counts, not CTA-tile counts: `PersistentTileSchedulerSm100Params::initialize` sets `problem_tiles_m_ = problem_blocks.x / cluster_shape.m()` and `problem_tiles_n_ = problem_blocks.y / cluster_shape.n()` (`tile_scheduler_params.h:1920-1921`), and `initialize_swizzle` calls `get_rasterization_order(problem_tiles_m_, problem_tiles_n_, raster_order_option)` (`:1881`): 64 / 2 = 32 against 64 / 2 = 32 here. A second guard follows at `:1882-1896`. The AlongN transpose puts the M clusters on grid y, whose limit is 65535, so `new_grid_y = problem_tiles_m_ * cluster_shape.n()` is checked against `(1 << 16) - 1`, and the order reverts to AlongM if it would overflow. Here 32 x 2 = 64 does not trigger it (note 7.4: "the 65535 grid-Y guard not triggering").

**Why AlongN is the right answer for this GEMM (my analysis, built on measured D.3).** The CLC hands out cluster ids roughly in increasing launch-linear order (note D.3). With the grid transposed, consecutive ids walk along **N** inside one row of cluster tiles, so at any moment the 33 resident clusters work on two or three adjacent 256 x 8192 fp16 A panels (4 MiB each; measured, note D.3: never on one) and A is re-read from HBM about once per row of 32 cluster tiles rather than once per tile: the L2 reuse argument of Chapter 3, Section 3.8.2 (Chapter 7, Section 7.5.6 gives the measured band occupancy, and Chapter 7 applies the same `(tm, tn)` map to CLC responses). The heuristic rasters along the shorter tile axis and takes `AlongN` as the tie-break for a square problem (Chapter 3, Section 3.8.2). `enum class RasterOrder { AlongM, AlongN }` (`tile_scheduler_detail.hpp:38-41`) is why the host guard compares against the literal 1 (`kRasterOrderAlongN = 1`, util.hpp:36), and the explicit host function hard-codes the result, `dim3 const grid(kGridX, kGridY, kGridZ)`, i.e. (64, 64, 1) (explicit.cu:1282; util.hpp:32 `kGridX = kFixedN / kCtaTileN, kGridY = kFixedM / kCtaTileM`: x is computed from N and y from M, the transposed order).

**Link 3: on the device, `initial_work_tile_info` feeds `blockIdx` through `swizzle_and_rasterize`.**

```cpp
// sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:366-371 (verbatim)
  template <class ClusterShape>
  CUTLASS_DEVICE
  WorkTileInfo
  initial_work_tile_info(ClusterShape cluster_shape) {
    return swizzle_and_rasterize(blockIdx.x, blockIdx.y, blockIdx.z, /*valid=*/true, /*cluster_offset_m=*/0, /*cluster_offset_n=*/0);
  }
```

In `swizzle_and_rasterize` (`:697-814`) the whole swizzle block (`:711-795`) is skipped because `divmod_swizzle_size_.divisor == 0` ("Swizzling is enabled if the swizzle size is greater than 0", `:710`; measured `swizzle_divisor 0`, note D.1 D10; the host guard at explicit.cu:1269 enforces it). What remains is the transpose (`:796-802`, quoted in Section 7.5.1).

The two in-cluster offsets are 0 for the initial tile, and `possibly_transpose_work_tile` is `:668-677` (quoted in Section 7.5.1).

Substitute `M_idx = blockIdx.x`, `N_idx = blockIdx.y`, both cluster divisors 2:

```
cluster_m   = blockIdx.x / 2      remainder_m = blockIdx.x % 2
cluster_n   = blockIdx.y / 2      remainder_n = blockIdx.y % 2
tm = M_idx' = cluster_n * 2 + remainder_m = 2 (blockIdx.y >> 1) + (blockIdx.x & 1)
tn = N_idx' = cluster_m * 2 + remainder_n = 2 (blockIdx.x >> 1) + (blockIdx.y & 1)
```

which is explicit.cu:1175-1176 exactly (note B.4, first row). Read it as: **the cluster index** comes from the transposed grid axis (`blockIdx.y / 2` picks the cluster row in M, `blockIdx.x / 2` the cluster column in N), and **the position inside the cluster** stays with the original axis (`blockIdx.x % 2 = x` picks the M half, `blockIdx.y % 2 = y` the N half). Hence `tm % 2 == x` for every tile a CTA ever receives (also for CLC tiles, Chapter 7), which is what makes "CTAs x and x+2 share tm, hence the A rows" true (Chapter 8).

### 11.6.4 Worked examples

| `blockIdx` (x, y) | `x = bx & 1`, `y = by & 1` -> rank | `by >> 1`, `bx >> 1` | `tm = 2 (by >> 1) + (bx & 1)` | `tn = 2 (bx >> 1) + (by & 1)` | D rows / columns |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (5, 2) | x = 1, y = 0 -> rank 1 | 1, 2 | 2 * 1 + 1 = **3** | 2 * 2 + 0 = **4** | rows [384, 512), cols [512, 640) |
| (4, 2) | x = 0, y = 0 -> rank 0 | 1, 2 | 2 | 4 | rows [256, 384), cols [512, 640) |
| (4, 3) | x = 0, y = 1 -> rank 2 | 1, 2 | 2 | 5 | rows [256, 384), cols [640, 768) |
| (5, 3) | x = 1, y = 1 -> rank 3 | 1, 2 | 3 | 5 | rows [384, 512), cols [640, 768) |
| (0, 0) | rank 0 | 0, 0 | 0 | 0 | rows [0, 128), cols [0, 128) |
| (63, 63) | x = 1, y = 1 -> rank 3 | 31, 31 | 63 | 63 | rows [8064, 8192), cols [8064, 8192) |
| (1, 0) | rank 1 | 0, 0 | 1 | 0 | rows [128, 256), cols [0, 128) |
| (0, 1) | rank 2 | 0, 0 | 0 | 1 | rows [0, 128), cols [128, 256) |

The first four rows are the four CTAs of one cluster (the cluster containing `blockIdx` (4..5, 2..3)). Together they cover the 256 x 256 cluster tile at cluster coordinates (M cluster 1, N cluster 2):

```
                 N tiles:   tn = 4            tn = 5
                          cols 512..639     cols 640..767
              +------------------+------------------+
 tm = 2       |  rank 0 (x0,y0)  |  rank 2 (x0,y1)  |   rows 256..383
 rows 256..   |  blockIdx (4,2)  |  blockIdx (4,3)  |
              +------------------+------------------+
 tm = 3       |  rank 1 (x1,y0)  |  rank 3 (x1,y1)  |   rows 384..511
 rows 384..   |  blockIdx (5,2)  |  blockIdx (5,3)  |
              +------------------+------------------+
                 pair {0,1}: tn = 4         pair {2,3}: tn = 5
                 (same y, adjacent tm)      (same y, adjacent tm)
```

The MMA pairs `{0,1}` and `{2,3}` are the two **columns** of this picture (same y, hence same tn, adjacent tm): one `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2` covers the pair's 256 rows x 128 columns (Chapter 9). Rank 0 and rank 2 have the same A rows (tm = 2), which is the multicast relation `0x5 << x` (Chapter 8).

### 11.6.5 The 4096 launch coordinates cover the 4096 CTA tiles exactly once

Both maps below are well defined on `{0..63} x {0..63}` because `2 (v >> 1) + (w & 1)` lies in `{0..63}` whenever `v, w` do. Define

```
F : (bx, by) -> (tm, tn) = (2 (by >> 1) + (bx & 1),  2 (bx >> 1) + (by & 1))
G : (tm, tn) -> (bx, by) = (2 (tn >> 1) + (tm & 1),  2 (tm >> 1) + (tn & 1))
```

Apply G after F: `bx' = 2 (tn >> 1) + (tm & 1) = 2 (bx >> 1) + (bx & 1) = bx` (since `tn >> 1 = bx >> 1` and `tm & 1 = bx & 1`), and `by' = 2 (tm >> 1) + (tn & 1) = 2 (by >> 1) + (by & 1) = by`. So `G o F = id`; by the same computation `F o G = id`. F is therefore a bijection of the 64 x 64 grid onto the 64 x 64 tile space: every one of the 4096 CTA tiles is the **initial** tile of exactly one CTA. (The CLC hand-out later reuses the same map on cancelled clusters' first-CTA ids, Chapter 7; its exactly-once coverage of the 1024 cluster tiles was measured, note D.7 "CLC".)

### 11.6.6 The invariant: no remote operation before `cluster_wait`

Until a CTA has itself passed `barrier.cluster.wait` (which completes only once every thread of the cluster has executed `barrier.cluster.arrive`, PTX ISA 9.7.15.3, i.e. after every CTA's `mbarrier.init`s and fences), it may not touch another CTA's shared memory or barriers: the other CTA might not have executed its `mbarrier.init`s yet (its warps may not even be running), and an arrive on an uninitialised mbarrier is undefined. The explicit kernel's remote operations all sit inside the role functions (after explicit.cu:1179):

| Operation | Wrapper | Sites | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| remote `mbarrier.arrive` via `mapa` | W10 | explicit.cu:684 (CLC release), 837 (throttle release), 964/970 (dealloc handshake) | CTA 0's `clc_empty`, CTA 0's `throttle_empty`, the peer's `tmem_dealloc` |
| arrive on the pair leader's barrier via the peer-bit mask | W11 | explicit.cu:1039 | leader's `acc_empty[st]` |
| remote `arrive.expect_tx` via `mapa` | W13 | explicit.cu:842 | CTAs 0..3's `clc_full[i]` |
| 2SM TMA loads (A data into ranks `x` and `x+2`, B data into this CTA's own smem; tx bytes to the leader's `full[s]`) | W21, W22 | explicit.cu:747, 754 | ranks `x`, `x+2` (A data); the pair leader's `full[s]` |
| `tcgen05.commit ... multicast::cluster` | W30 | explicit.cu:942, 944 | all four CTAs' `empty[s]`; the pair's `acc_full[st]` |
| `clusterlaunchcontrol.try_cancel ... multicast::cluster::all` | W33 | explicit.cu:847 | every CTA's `clc_response[i]` and `clc_full[i]` |
| `tcgen05.alloc/dealloc.cta_group::2` | W26, W27 | explicit.cu:885, 971 | the pair's TMEM (the SASS handshake uses the peer's reserved smem, note D.2) |

Everything before line 1179 is CTA-local: parameter reads, special registers, 33 local inits, the fences, the relaxed arrive. That is the sentence at explicit.cu:1178 ("no remote barrier operation before this point") and note B.2 step 26.

## 11.7 Step 7: dispatch and the fall-through warps (explicit.cu:1190-1203)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1190-1203
  // 7.3 step 7: role dispatch in the baseline's branch order (kernel :617, 681, 726, 807, 869); warp 3 and warp 1 of ranks 1-3 fall through and exit
  if (warp_idx == 2) {
    producer_role(params, smem_base, x, y, is_cta0, lane_pred != 0u && is_leader, k_tiles, tm, tn);
  }
  else if (warp_idx == 1 && is_cta0) {
    scheduler_role(smem_base, x, y, lane, tm, tn);
  }
  else if (warp_idx == 0) {
    mma_role(smem, smem_base, x, y, rank, is_leader, peer, lane_pred, k_tiles, tm, tn);
  }
  else if (warp_idx >= 4) {
    epilogue_role(params, smem, smem_base, x, y, rank, is_leader, warp_idx, lane, alpha, beta, tm, tn);
  }
}
```

The baseline's chain is `if (is_participant.main_load) ... else if (is_participant.sched) ... else if (is_participant.mma) ... else if (is_participant.epi_load) ... else if (is_participant.epilogue)`, with `is_participant = {mma: warp 0, sched: warp 1 && rank 0, main_load: warp 2, epi_load: warp 3 && is_epi_load_needed, epilogue: warps 4-7}` (kernel `:449-455`). The explicit kernel drops the `epi_load` branch (never taken for `beta = 0`) and keeps the other four in the same order.

| Branch | Warps | Role (chapter) | Arguments worth noticing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `warp_idx == 2` | 2 of every CTA | `producer_role` (8) | `is_cta0` (throttle producer only in CTA 0); `lane_pred != 0u && is_leader` = the one lane of the pair leader's warp that issues `arrive.expect_tx 49152` |
| `warp_idx == 1 && is_cta0` | 1 of rank 0 | `scheduler_role` (7) | `lane` (lanes 0..3 arm the four CTAs' `clc_full`) |
| `warp_idx == 0` | 0 of every CTA | `mma_role` (9) | `smem` (generic, for the TMEM base read), `is_leader`, `peer`, `lane_pred` (trace only) |
| `warp_idx >= 4` | 4-7 of every CTA | `epilogue_role` (10) | `smem`, `warp_idx` (-> `w = warp_idx - 4`), `lane`, `alpha`, `beta` |
| (none) | 3 of every CTA; 1 of ranks 1-3 | fall through to `}` at 1203 and exit | |

Every argument other than `params` (the kernel parameter block, by `const&`) and `smem` (the dynamic shared-memory array) is a value computed in the prologue; the roles receive no pointers to prologue state and share nothing but shared memory. `tm, tn` are the initial tile; each role carries its own copy forward through the CLC loop (Chapter 7).

### 11.7.1 Why the fall-through warps may exit early

One warp per CTA (warp 3), and a second in ranks 1-3 (warp 1), leave at line 1203 while the others run for ~0.9 ms. Rank 0 loses one warp and ranks 1-3 lose two, so `7 + 3 x 6 = 25` of the cluster's 32 warps stay, which is exactly the `25 x 32 = 800` of the CLC empty count (11.5.2): every warp that stays consumes CLC responses, and no warp that consumes leaves. The exit is safe because **no synchronisation object counts the leavers**:

| Object | Population | Includes warp 3? warp 1 of ranks 1-3? |
|---|---|---|
| `bar.sync 6, 160` / `bar.arrive 6, 160` (TMEM alloc hand-off, explicit.cu:887, 997; `kTmemAllocBarThreads = 160` at explicit.cu:191) | 32 (warp 0 arrives) + 128 (warps 4-7 sync) = 160 = `NumMMAThreads + NumEpilogueThreads` (kernel `:558`) | no |
| `bar.sync 1, 128` (epilogue subtile barrier, explicit.cu:1051, 1071) | the 128 epilogue threads | no |
| `barrier.cluster` | all 1024 threads of the cluster, **already passed** at 1179 before anyone exits (and the ISA counts only non-exited threads anyway, Section 2.10.1) | (passed) |
| `clc_empty` 800 | `32 + 4 * (32 + 32 + 128)`: rank 0's warp 1, every CTA's warps 0, 2, 4-7 | no: `NumSchedThreads` is counted once, not `cluster_size` times, and `NumEpilogueLoadThreads` only when `is_epi_load_needed` |
| `main full/empty`, `acc full/empty`, `throttle`, `tmem_dealloc` | see 11.5.1 and Chapter 4, Section 4.4 | no |

A warp that exits does not end the CTA (the CTA stays resident until its last warp exits), does not release the shared memory, and does not disturb the named barriers, which count only the threads whose `bar.sync`/`bar.arrive` name them. Apart from the exit condition of the last bulk store group (Section 4.8.5; note D.1 D15), the only exit hazard in this kernel is the one of note Section 7.10: a CTA must not exit while remote CTAs may still arrive on **its** barriers. The four tails inside the roles handle that (Chapters 7-9), not the frame. Warp 1 of ranks 1-3 does its only useful work, the A/B prefetch, at 1113-1116 before it leaves; warp 3 likewise prefetches C/D (1117-1120) and initialises the throttle barriers (1155-1163).

### 11.7.2 What ptxas made of the dispatch

Note G.3 (measured): the explicit binary carries a three-entry jump table in constant bank 2 (`CONSTANT[2]:12`): `UISETP.LT.U32 UP0, UR20, 0x2; USEL UR4, UR20, 0x2, UP0; USHF.L.U32 UR4, UR4, 0x2; LDCU UR10, c[0x2][UR4]; BRXU UR10` at `0x0a60-0x0ae0`. Index `min(warp_idx, 2) * 4` selects the target for warp 0, warp 1 or warp >= 2. The warp >= 2 target is split again by `UISETP.NE.U32.AND UP0, UPT, UR20, 0x2; BRA.U` (warp 2 vs the rest), and the `BRA.U` target `0x1ee0` holds the `warp_idx >= 4` test (`UISETP.GE.AND UP0, UPT, UR20, 0x4, UPT; PLOP3.LUT P0, PT, PT, PT, UP0, 0x80, 0x8`; measured, `trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt`; the source is explicit.cu:1200) that separates the epilogue warps from the `EXIT` at `0x1f00` that G.3 attributes to warps 1 of ranks 1-3 and warp 3. (G.3 does not quote that compare for the explicit kernel, whereas note D.2 quotes the baseline's: warp 1 of ranks 1-3 and warp 3 "traverse the dispatch chain to `UISETP.GE.AND UP0, UR18, 0x4; @!P0 EXIT`" at `0x6580`/`0x65a0`. That jump-table entry 1 leads to `0x19a0` is inferred (the table's contents are not in the dump); the `is_cta0` half of the `warp_idx == 1 && is_cta0` test is visible there (`UISETP.NE.U32.AND UP0, UPT, UR15, URZ, UPT; BRA.U UP0, 0x1ee0` at `0x19a0`/`0x19b0`, `UR15` = `SR_CgaCtaId`, the rank).) The CUTLASS kernel compiles the same chain to compare-and-branch. Both execute once per thread in the prologue, so their cost is of the same order: a handful of instructions, once per thread. Chapter 12 has the listing.

## 11.8 Section 11: the host launch mirror `run()` (explicit.cu:1265-1329)

What follows is the non-template function, quoted in pieces; only its `[TRACE]` block (explicit.cu:1317-1324, compiled out in the performance binary) is elided.

### 11.8.1 The guards (explicit.cu:1265-1272)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1265-1272
cutlass::Status run(ExplicitGemmParams const& params) {
  // E.5.1 guards: the kernel hard-codes the Section 0 configuration; refuse anything else loudly (device code has no checks)
  if (params.mode != kModeGemm) { return cutlass::Status::kErrorInvalidProblem; }
  if (params.m != kFixedM || params.n != kFixedN || params.k != kFixedK || params.l != kFixedL) { return cutlass::Status::kErrorInvalidProblem; }
  if (params.raster_order != kRasterOrderAlongN || params.swizzle_divisor != 0) { return cutlass::Status::kErrorInvalidProblem; }
  if (params.tiles_m != kProblemTilesM || params.tiles_n != kProblemTilesN || params.tiles_l != kProblemTilesL) { return cutlass::Status::kErrorInvalidProblem; }
  if (params.alpha_ptr != nullptr || params.beta_ptr != nullptr) { return cutlass::Status::kErrorNotSupported; }   // no pointer path (D.6 item 13)
  if (params.beta != 0.0f) { return cutlass::Status::kErrorNotSupported; }   // the C path is omitted (Section 0; E.10 item 5); -0.0f passes like is_zero()
```

| Guard | Rejects | Why the kernel cannot handle it | Status (string printed by `CUTLASS_CHECK`, `examples/common/helper.h:43-52`; `cutlass.h:74-77`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode != 0` | anything but `GemmUniversalMode::kGemm` | batched/array modes change the parameter semantics | `kErrorInvalidProblem` ("Error Invalid Problem") |
| shape != (8192, 8192, 8192, 1) | any other M, N, K, L | the grid is hard-coded to (64,64,1); the device never reads M, N, L; the TMA store has a literal 0 batch coordinate; partial tiles are not handled | `kErrorInvalidProblem` |
| `raster_order != 1` or `swizzle_divisor != 0` | AlongM raster, any swizzle | the `tm, tn` formulas of 11.6.3 and the CLC mapping (Chapter 7) are the AlongN, swizzle-0 specialisation | `kErrorInvalidProblem` |
| tiles != (32, 32, 1) | an inconsistent scheduler state | consistency check on the host-only fields | `kErrorInvalidProblem` |
| `alpha_ptr` or `beta_ptr` non-null | scalars passed by device pointer | the explicit kernel has no `ld.global` path for them (note D.6 item 13: compiled but never taken in the baseline) | `kErrorNotSupported` ("Error Not Supported") |
| `beta != 0.0f` | a real C term | the C load path (`epi_load` pipeline, 32 C TMA loads per tile, `load_order`) is omitted; the epilogue computes `fmaf(beta, 0.0f, t)` with a literal-zero C fragment | `kErrorNotSupported` |

`alpha` is deliberately **not** guarded: any value is handled identically to the baseline (`alpha * acc`). `-0.0f` passes the `beta` test because `-0.0f != 0.0f` is false under IEEE comparison, which matches the baseline's `is_zero()` test (`is_C_load_needed = !beta.is_zero()`, note B.2 step 11, Section 8). With `beta = -0.0f` both kernels then compute `fmaf(-0.0f, 0.0f, t)` with the same run-time `beta`, so `D` stays bit-identical to the baseline's. The only input where the sign of `beta` is observable is `t = -0.0f` (`-0.0 + -0.0 = -0.0` against `+0.0 + -0.0 = +0.0`), which is exactly why the C term is kept as an FFMA with the run-time `beta` instead of being dropped (Chapter 10, note D.7). The baseline's `run()` has no guards at all (they live in `can_implement`, which the harness still calls on the CUTLASS side at `70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:407`); these six are the documented deviation (b) of 11.8.6.

### 11.8.2 The kernel pointer and step 1: the dynamic-smem opt-in (explicit.cu:1274-1279)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1274-1279
  // E.5.2: the run() mirror (gemm_universal_adapter.h:375-575 -> cluster_launch.hpp:260-296)
  void const* kernel = reinterpret_cast<void const*>(&explicit_blackwell_fp16_gemm_kernel);
  cutlass::Status launch_result = cutlass::Status::kSuccess;

  // 1. MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize opt-in on the explicit kernel (initialize() does it for the CUTLASS kernel, :342-352); every call, not hoisted (E.5.4)
  launch_result = status_from_cuda(cudaFuncSetAttribute(kernel, cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, static_cast<int>(kSmemBytes)));
```

- **Why needed.** By default a kernel may launch with at most 48 KB of dynamic shared memory; "kernels relying on shared memory allocations over 48 KB per block are architecture-specific ... and require an explicit opt-in using `cudaFuncSetAttribute`" (CUDA Programming Guide, section 3.2.6 of the v13 guide). The Runtime API reference adds that the value plus the static `sharedSizeBytes` cannot exceed `cudaDevAttrMaxSharedMemoryPerBlockOptin`: the 227 KB = 232448 bytes of CC 10.0 (11.2.1), checked by the `static_assert` at util.hpp:46 (11.2.3). Without this call `cudaLaunchKernelExC` with `dynamicSmemBytes = 230400` is rejected and nothing runs (the exact error code was not measured).
- **Who does it for the CUTLASS kernel.** `GemmUniversalAdapter::initialize()` (`gemm_universal_adapter.h:342-352`): `if (smem_size >= (48 << 10)) cudaFuncSetAttribute(device_kernel<GemmKernel>, cudaFuncAttributeMaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, smem_size)`. The explicit kernel is a different function and needs its own opt-in.
- **Why every call, not hoisted behind a `static bool`.** Note E.5.4: the baseline makes two attribute calls per iteration on the kernel it launches (the opt-in inside `initialize()` and `NonPortableClusterSizeAllowed` inside `run()`). Doing the opt-in on every call keeps the explicit path at two attribute calls on the launched kernel per iteration, so the per-iteration host sequence stays the same **in kind** (23 non-synchronising host API calls against 22). A `cudaFuncSetAttribute` is a host-only call costing low microseconds, hidden behind the previous ~0.889 ms kernel for iterations 1-9 and exposed only in iteration 0 (cost and hiding both inferred, not measured; note E.5.4). Hoisting it would save nothing measurable and would make the comparison harder to argue.

### 11.8.3 Steps 2-4: geometry, `check_cluster_dims`, the non-portable-cluster attribute (explicit.cu:1281-1295)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1281-1295
  // 2. launch geometry (Section 5.4): grid (64,64,1) = the AlongN-transposed (N/128, M/128, 1); block (256,1,1); 230400 bytes of dynamic smem
  dim3 const grid(kGridX, kGridY, kGridZ);
  dim3 const block(kBlockThreads, 1, 1);
  dim3 const cluster(kClusterX, kClusterY, kClusterZ);

  // 3. check_cluster_dims (cluster_launch.hpp:103-112)
  if (launch_result == cutlass::Status::kSuccess) {
    bool const ok = (cluster.x * cluster.y * cluster.z <= 32u) && (grid.x % cluster.x == 0u) && (grid.y % cluster.y == 0u) && (grid.z % cluster.z == 0u);
    if (!ok) { launch_result = cutlass::Status::kInvalid; }
  }

  // 4. ClusterLauncher::init: NonPortableClusterSizeAllowed on every launch (cluster_launch.hpp:141-143, called from :280)
  if (launch_result == cutlass::Status::kSuccess) {
    launch_result = status_from_cuda(cudaFuncSetAttribute(kernel, cudaFuncAttributeNonPortableClusterSizeAllowed, 1));
  }
```

- **Geometry.** `grid = (64, 64, 1)` (util.hpp:32, the transposed order of 11.6.3), `block = (256, 1, 1)` (`GemmKernel::get_block_shape()` = `dim3(MaxThreadsPerBlock, 1, 1)`, kernel `:399-401`), `cluster = (2, 2, 1)` (util.hpp:31). In the baseline `grid` comes from `get_grid_shape(params)` at run time (`gemm_universal_adapter.h:381`); here it is a constant because the guards have already pinned the shape (deviation (b)).
- **`check_cluster_dims`** is a copy of `cluster_launch.hpp:103-112`: cluster size `<= MaxClusterSize = 32` (`:82`) and each grid dimension divisible by the cluster dimension. For this run `4 <= 32`, `64 % 2 == 0`, `64 % 2 == 0`, `1 % 1 == 0`; util.hpp:42-43 also `static_assert`s the same conditions, so the run-time test can never fail here. It is kept because `launch_with_fallback_cluster` performs it on every launch (`:274-278`) and returns `kInvalid` when it fails.
- **`NonPortableClusterSizeAllowed`.** `ClusterLauncher::init` (`:141-144`) sets `cudaFuncAttributeNonPortableClusterSizeAllowed = 1` on every launch (`:280`). It is *needed* only for clusters larger than the portable maximum of 8 ("the maximum portable cluster size supported is 8; however, NVIDIA Blackwell B200 GPU allows for a nonportable cluster size of 16 by opting in. Launching a kernel with a nonportable cluster size requires setting the `cudaFuncAttributeNonPortableClusterSizeAllowed` function attribute", Blackwell Tuning Guide). A cluster of 4 does not need it; it is kept for parity with the baseline's call sequence (note E.5.2 item 4 marks the "functionally irrelevant" judgement as inferred).

### 11.8.4 Steps 5-6: the launch configuration and `cudaLaunchKernelExC` (explicit.cu:1297-1313)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1297-1313
  // 5.-6. make_cluster_launch_config (:151-213): one attribute, cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension = {2,2,1}; legacy default stream; then cudaLaunchKernelExC (:294)
  if (launch_result == cutlass::Status::kSuccess) {
    cudaLaunchConfig_t launch_config = {};
    launch_config.gridDim = grid;
    launch_config.blockDim = block;
    launch_config.dynamicSmemBytes = kSmemBytes;
    launch_config.stream = nullptr;
    cudaLaunchAttribute launch_attribute[1];
    launch_attribute[0].id = cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension;
    launch_attribute[0].val.clusterDim.x = cluster.x;
    launch_attribute[0].val.clusterDim.y = cluster.y;
    launch_attribute[0].val.clusterDim.z = cluster.z;
    launch_config.attrs = launch_attribute;
    launch_config.numAttrs = 1;
    void* kernel_params[] = { const_cast<void*>(static_cast<void const*>(&params)) };
    launch_result = status_from_cuda(cudaLaunchKernelExC(&launch_config, kernel, kernel_params));
  }
```

This is `ClusterLauncher::make_cluster_launch_config` (`cluster_launch.hpp:150-213`) evaluated for this build and this call:

| `make_cluster_launch_config` | Value here | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `launch_attribute[0] = {cudaLaunchAttributeClusterDimension, {2,2,1}}` (`:166, :177`) | the one attribute kept | no fallback cluster (`have_fallback = false`, `:168`, since `fallback_cluster_dims = {0,0,0}` from `gemm_universal_adapter.h:400`) |
| `numAttrs` starts at 3 (`CUDA_ENABLE_PREFERRED_CLUSTER` is defined for nvcc >= 12.8, `cluster_launch.hpp:55-57`; `:89`) | 3 -> 2: `numAttrs--` because there is no fallback (`:192-194`) | the preferred-cluster attribute is dropped |
| `launch_attribute[numAttrs - 1] = PDL` (`:199-200`) | written but not counted: `numAttrs = launch_with_pdl ? numAttrs : numAttrs - 1 = 1` (`:206`) | `launch_with_pdl = false` (default argument of the `run()` overload the harness calls, `gemm_universal_adapter.h:614`, forwarded at `:615` to the static `run()`; the harness never sets it); so the kernel's `griddepcontrol.wait` returns immediately and `launch_dependents` has no dependent (Chapters 8 and 9; note E.5.4 "absence of PDL", inferred) |
| `gridDim, blockDim, dynamicSmemBytes` (`:202-204`) | (64,64,1), (256,1,1), 230400 | |
| `stream` (`:205`) | `nullptr` = the legacy default stream | `gemm.run()` is called with its default `stream = nullptr` (`gemm_universal_adapter.h:612`) |

`cudaLaunchKernelExC(&config, func, args)` (CUDA Runtime API, "Execution Control") enqueues the kernel asynchronously with the attributes in `config`. `args` is an array of pointers to the kernel's parameters, here one pointer to the 640-byte `ExplicitGemmParams`, which the runtime copies into the launch's parameter buffer (the baseline copies its 2048-byte `Params`, note D.1 D2). The call is `cluster_launch.hpp:293-294` (`synclog_setup()` is a no-op without `CUTLASS_ENABLE_SYNCLOG`, note D.1 D14).

**Where the parameter-size limit comes from.** Kernel parameters "are passed to the device through constant memory and have been limited to 4,096 bytes"; "CUDA 12.1 increases this parameter limit from 4,096 bytes to 32,764 bytes on all device architectures including NVIDIA Volta and above" (NVIDIA developer blog, "CUDA 12.1 Supports Large Kernel Parameters"; an R530 or newer driver is required, and the limit stays 4,096 bytes below Volta). That constant-memory placement is what 11.2.2 showed: the block lands in constant bank 0 at `c[0x0][0x380]`, so the resource line reads `CONSTANT[0]:1536 = 0x380 + 640` (note G.3). explicit.hpp:76 keeps the classic bound as a guard, `static_assert(sizeof(ExplicitGemmParams) <= 4096, "kernel parameter block limit");`. The 640-byte block (and the baseline's 2048) is far below either limit, so the assert documents the constraint rather than guarding a live risk.

### 11.8.5 Step 7: `cudaGetLastError` and the Status mapping (explicit.cu:1315-1329)

```cpp
// explicit.cu:1315-1329; the [TRACE] block at 1317-1324 is elided (compiled out in the performance binary)
  // 7. cudaGetLastError -> kSuccess / kErrorInternal (gemm_universal_adapter.h:564-574)
  cudaError_t const result = cudaGetLastError();
  ...   // [TRACE] branch elided (explicit.cu:1317-1324, compiled out in the performance binary)
  if (cudaSuccess == result && cutlass::Status::kSuccess == launch_result) {
    return cutlass::Status::kSuccess;
  }
  return cutlass::Status::kErrorInternal;
}
```

The last four lines are `GemmUniversalAdapter::run` `:564-574` verbatim in logic. `cudaGetLastError()` "returns the last error that has been produced by any of the runtime calls in the same instance of the CUDA Runtime library in the host thread and resets it to `cudaSuccess`" (CUDA Runtime API, Error Handling). The reset clears the per-thread error state (CUDA Programming Guide 2.1.7.1, "Error State"): a launch rejection is cleared here, so some later unrelated `cudaGetLastError` does not pick up a stale error (note E.5.2 item 7: "clears the per-thread error variable so that a stale non-sticky error is not picked up"). A device fault (an illegal address) behaves differently: it "leaves the process in an inconsistent state and any further CUDA work will return the same error" (CUDA Runtime API, `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`), informally a "sticky" error. Every failure path (`kInvalid` from any step, or a non-success `result`) collapses to `kErrorInternal`, exactly as the adapter does. On the `[PROD]` path the function therefore returns in one of two ways: `kSuccess` with the kernel **enqueued, not finished**, or an error status, normally with nothing launched (if `cudaLaunchKernelExC` succeeds but `cudaGetLastError` then reports an error left in the per-thread error state, `kErrorInternal` is returned with the kernel enqueued; CUDA Programming Guide 2.1.7.1-2.1.7.2).

### 11.8.6 Side by side with `GemmUniversalAdapter::run()` and `ClusterLauncher`

| # | `explicit_gemm::run` (explicit.cu) | CUTLASS | Same? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | six guards (1267-1272) | none in `run()`; `can_implement()` on the host side | **deviation (b)**: documented, affects only arguments outside the fixed configuration |
| 1 | `cudaFuncSetAttribute(kernel, MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize, 230400)` (1279) | in `initialize()` `:342-352`, on `device_kernel<GemmKernel>` | **deviation (a)**: the same attribute, on the kernel that is actually launched; the baseline's call still runs on the never-launched kernel |
| 2 | `grid(64,64,1)`, `block(256,1,1)`, `cluster(2,2,1)` (1282-1284) | `block = get_block_shape()`, `grid = get_grid_shape(params)` (`:380-381`), `cluster` from `ClusterShape` (`:395-397`) | same values; grid hard-coded (part of deviation (b)) |
| 3 | `check_cluster_dims` (1287-1290) | `cluster_launch.hpp:103-112` via `:274-278` | same |
| 4 | `cudaFuncSetAttribute(kernel, NonPortableClusterSizeAllowed, 1)` (1294) | `ClusterLauncher::init` `:141-144` via `:280` | same |
| 5 | `cudaLaunchConfig_t` with one `ClusterDimension` attribute, stream `nullptr` (1299-1310) | `make_cluster_launch_config` `:151-213` (3 -> 2 -> 1 attributes) | same configuration |
| 6 | `cudaLaunchKernelExC(&cfg, kernel, {&params})` (1311-1312) | `:293-294` | same API; 640-byte vs 2048-byte parameter copy |
| 7 | `cudaGetLastError` -> `kSuccess` / `kErrorInternal` (1316, 1325-1328) | `:564-574` | same |

**Why nothing synchronises.** `cudaFuncSetAttribute` and `cudaGetLastError` are host-side; `cudaLaunchKernelExC` enqueues and returns. There is no `cudaDeviceSynchronize`, `cudaStreamSynchronize`, `cudaMemcpy`, `cudaFuncGetAttributes`, occupancy query or `printf` on the `[PROD]` path (note E.5.2 "Not in the function").

The result of all this: median `Avg runtime` 0.889354 ms for the explicit path against 0.889917 ms for the pristine binary on the same day, ratio 0.99937 (measured, note G.2); 23 host API calls per iteration against 22 (counted from the code, not traced: note G.2 C4 and E.5.4).

---

## 11.9 The frame as a timeline, and a rewriting checklist

```
 host (one call of explicit_gemm::run)           device (every CTA, 256 threads; t ->)
 ------------------------------------------      --------------------------------------------------------
 guards (6 checks)                               entry: smem_base = cvta(smem)            [all threads]
 FuncSetAttribute MaxDynSmem 230400              step 1  shfl -> warp_idx; elect -> lane_pred;
 grid/block/cluster constants                            %cluster_ctarank -> rank, is_cta0, is_leader, peer
 check_cluster_dims                              step 2  alpha, beta, k_tiles = (k+63)>>6
 FuncSetAttribute NonPortableCluster 1                   warp 1 lane: prefetch A, B; warp 3 lane: prefetch C, D
 cudaLaunchConfig_t {64x64x1, 256, 230400,       step 3  w0: 16 inits | fence | w4: 4 inits | fence |
   stream 0, [ClusterDimension 2x2x1]}                   w5: 8 inits | fence | w3: 4 inits | fence | w0 lane: 1 init
 cudaLaunchKernelExC  ---- enqueue ---->         step 4  barrier.cluster.arrive.relaxed.aligned
 cudaGetLastError -> Status                      step 5  x, y = %cluster_ctaid; tm, tn from blockIdx
 return (kernel not finished)                    step 6  barrier.cluster.wait.aligned   <- first point at which
                                                                                            remote smem may be touched
                                                 step 7  w2 -> producer | w1&rank0 -> scheduler | w0 -> mma |
                                                         w4-7 -> epilogue | w3, w1 of ranks 1-3 -> exit
```

If you rewrite this frame from a blank file, the order of decisions is:

1. **Parameter block.** A POD struct with the `CUtensorMap`s first (alignment 64/128), scalars after; pass it `const __grid_constant__`; take addresses of the maps only.
2. **Shared memory.** One `extern __shared__ char smem[]`, no static `__shared__`, every object at a fixed `OFF_*`; `static_assert` the alignments (1024 for SW128 stages, 512 for the SW128_32B epilogue stages, 16 for the CLC responses) and the total; compute `smem_base` once; never mix it with the generic pointer.
3. **Identity.** Warp index through `shfl`, one election you may reuse for one-off work, `%cluster_ctarank` and `%cluster_ctaid`; derive leader/peer/cta0 from the rank.
4. **Prefetch** every descriptor you will use, from an idle warp, before the rendezvous.
5. **Barriers.** Initialise every barrier you will arrive on with the exact count of arrivals per phase (one line of justification each), fence, and only then the cluster rendezvous; leave unused barriers uninitialised and keep their counts out of the others (800, not 928).
6. **Rendezvous.** `arrive.relaxed` -> local setup -> `wait`; no remote operation before the wait; derive the initial tile from `blockIdx` by inverting whatever raster/transposition the host applied.
7. **Dispatch** on the warp-uniform index; let non-participating warps exit; make sure no `bar.sync` population or mbarrier count includes them.
8. **Host.** Opt in to the dynamic smem, set the cluster attribute, launch with `cudaLaunchKernelExC` on the stream the timer watches, map errors, never synchronise.

Chapter 13 expands this list into a construction plan (13.2) and generalises it to other GEMM configurations (13.4).

# Chapter 12. The Artifact: What ptxas Made of It, and What Was Measured

Evidence tags used in this chapter: **[M]** measured (note Parts D and G, or my own reading of the committed dumps in `trace_out_v2/`), **[S]** derived from source (explicit.cu, the CUTLASS headers, or the documents cited inline), **[H]** my analysis or hypothesis; **(NVIDIA internal)** marks NVIDIA engineering information that is not publicly documented. Every SASS line quoted below is copied from `trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt` with the trailing `/* 0x... */` control-word comment removed.

---

## 12.1 Three artifacts, one toolchain

The kernel you studied in Chapters 5-11 is a C++ file. What runs on the B200 is a cubin: `nvcc`'s front end turns the file into PTX, and `ptxas` turns the PTX into SASS. The asm strings of the wrappers (Chapter 6; all but W1 and W37, which are the `__shfl_sync` and `__syncwarp()` intrinsics) reach the PTX verbatim. Everything after that, including how every `tcgen05.*`, `cp.async.bulk.tensor.*` and `mbarrier.*` instruction becomes machine instructions, is `ptxas`'s decision. This chapter is about those decisions and about what the finished binary did when it ran.

```
 explicit.cu ──nvcc front end──> PTX (compute_100a, embedded in the fatbin)
                                   │  1552 instruction lines, 92 predicates, 1014 .b32 regs       [M]
                                   └──ptxas──> SASS (sm_100a cubin)
                                                 1640 instructions, REG 26, LOCAL 0, STACK 0     [M]
```

The build is the fixed Section 0 command of the note. Its two `--generate-code` clauses, `arch=compute_100a,code=[sm_100a]` and `arch=compute_100a,code=[compute_100a]`, make the fatbin carry both the cubin and the PTX (note D.5). Every dump this chapter reads came from `cuobjdump` on the saved toggle-off binary `trace_out_v2/70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.explicit` (note Part H.2.2).

### 12.1.1 The PTX entry header [M]

```
.visible .entry _ZN13explicit_gemm35explicit_blackwell_fp16_gemm_kernelENS_18ExplicitGemmParamsE(
.param .align 128 .b8 ..._param_0[640]
.maxntid 256
.minnctapersm 1
.reg .pred %p<92>;
.reg .b16 %rs<7>;
.reg .b32 %r<1014>;
.reg .b64 %rd<29>;
```

Why each line is what it is:

| PTX line | Comes from | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `.param .align 128 .b8 [640]` | `const __grid_constant__ ExplicitGemmParams params` (explicit.cu:1096) | `sizeof(ExplicitGemmParams)` is 640 because `alignof(CUtensorMap)` is 128 in the CUDA 13.3 headers: four 128-byte maps (512) + 12 ints/floats (48) + two pointers (16) = 576, padded to the next multiple of 128 (explicit.hpp byte map; note G.3). |
| `.maxntid 256` / `.minnctapersm 1` | `__launch_bounds__(256, 1)` (explicit.cu:1095) | 256 threads = 8 warps (Chapter 11). 230400 B of dynamic shared memory forces 1 CTA per SM anyway. |
| `%p<92> %rs<7> %r<1014> %rd<29>` | virtual registers before allocation | The CUTLASS kernel's entry declares `%p<248> %rs<16> %r<1635> %rd<55>` (note D.2); the explicit kernel carries fewer live values (no C path, no scheduler bookkeeping). Six of the seven `.b16` registers are used. Three carry mask operands: `%rs3` (`mov.b16 %rs3, 15`, `kMainloopReleaseMask`, the `"h"` operand of W30), `%rs4` (`cvt.u16.u32` of `3 << 2y`, the accumulator commit mask, W30) and `%rs6` (`cvt.u16.u32` of `5 << x`, the A multicast mask, W21). The other three are rank bookkeeping that the front end narrowed to 16 bits and re-tests with `setp.ne.b16` in the role tests: `%rs2 = cvt.u16.u32 %cluster_ctarank`, `%rs1 = %rs2 & 1` (`rank & 1`: 1 on the peer, 0 on the pair leader) and `%rs5 = %rs1 & 255` (`trace_out_v2/ptx_explicit.txt` lines 34-35, 406-407, 419, 1104, 1112, 1384-1387, 1415, 1430, 1516) [M]. |

The device performs only two parameter reads: `ld.param.v2.b32 {%r5, %r6}, [..._param_0+528]` (alpha and beta) and `ld.param.b32 %r36, [..._param_0+520]` (k) [M]. The four tensor-map addresses are formed with `cvta.param` and passed to `prefetch.tensormap` and the TMA instructions; `m`, `n`, `l` are never read (note G.3).

In SASS the parameter block begins at constant-bank offset `c[0x0][0x380]`. So k is read by `LDCU UR14, c[0x0][0x588]` (0x380 + 520 = 0x588) and alpha/beta by `LDCU.64 UR26, c[0x0][0x590]` (0x380 + 528 = 0x590) [M]. `c[0x0][0x348]` is read as a 64-bit value at four sites: `@!UP1 LDCU.64 UR4` at 0x00d0 and `LDCU.64 UR6` at 0x0130 for the prefetches, `LDCU.64 UR22` at 0x0c10 in the producer, `LDCU.64 UR30` at 0x1f50 in the epilogue. The value is then offset by `+0x0`, `+0x80`, `+0x100`, `+0x180`, exactly the explicit.hpp byte offsets of the four maps: `+0x100`/`+0x180` feed the `UTMACCTL.PF` of C and D, `+0x80` is `tma_b` in the producer, `+0x180` is `tma_d` in the epilogue [M]. Since the PTX forms those operands with `cvta.param`, I read the slot as the generic address of the parameter block, which note D.2 calls the "descriptor base" [H: the constant-bank layout itself is not documented in any source I used].

### 12.1.2 The resource line [M]

```
Function _ZN13explicit_gemm35explicit_blackwell_fp16_gemm_kernelENS_18ExplicitGemmParamsE:
  REG:26 STACK:0 SHARED:1024 LOCAL:0 CONSTANT[2]:12 CONSTANT[0]:1536 TEXTURE:0 SURFACE:0 SAMPLER:0
```

(`trace_out_v2/resources.txt`; the CUDA Binary Utilities manual states that `REG`, `TEXTURE`, `SURFACE`, `SAMPLER` are counts and the other fields are bytes.)

| Field | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `REG` | 26 | The SASS names 24 distinct vector registers, `R0..R23`; the epilogue's live set sets the maximum (register by register in Section 12.4.1). ptxas reports 26, two more than the number named; the CUTLASS kernel names `R0..R65` (66) and reports 68 [M]. The reason for the +2 is not documented in the sources I used (unverified). After a rebuild, `nvcc -Xptxas -v` (or `--resource-usage`) prints the same figure at compile time, quicker than `cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage`. |
| `STACK` / `LOCAL` | 0 / 0 | No spills (`LDL`/`STL` count 0 [M]). No local array survived: the `mask[8]` of W29 and the `r[16]` of the epilogue are fully promoted to registers. |
| `SHARED` | 1024 | **Not** static `__shared__` of this kernel. It is the system-reserved kilobyte below the dynamic buffer, reported for every kernel in the binary: `cudaFuncGetAttributes` reports `sharedSizeBytes 0` (`TRACE_HOST kernel_sharedSizeBytes 0` in `trace_out_v2/host.txt`), and the device attribute `cudaDevAttrReservedSharedMemoryPerBlock` reports the same 1024 (`TRACE_HOST device_reserved_smem_per_block 1024`) [M] (note D.6 item 4, G.3). This kilobyte is why `smem_base` is `0x400 + (rank << 24)` and not 0 (Chapter 5). |
| `CONSTANT[0]` | 1536 | 0x380 + 640: the kernel's parameter block sits at `c[0x0][0x380]` in constant bank 0, so the bank holds 896 bytes of driver/launch data plus the 640-byte block (explicit.hpp header; note G.3). The CUTLASS kernel's is 2944 = 0x380 + 2048. |
| `CONSTANT[2]` | 12 | A three-entry jump table that ptxas built for the role dispatch (Section 12.2, row "role dispatch"). The CUTLASS kernel has none; it uses a compare-and-branch chain [M]. |

### 12.1.3 Three decoding prerequisites: control words, truth-table immediates, byte selectors [S, H where marked]

The dictionary in Section 12.2 and the listings in Section 12.5 use three pieces of SASS literacy that no CUDA course teaches. Read them once here.

**Control words and scoreboards.** `cuobjdump` prints every instruction as a 128-bit encoding in two `/* 0x... */` comments: the first on the instruction's line, the second alone on the next line (`/*5410*/ UTCHMMA.2CTA ... ; /* 0x00ff1c0c0a0075ea */` followed by `/* 0x0009e20008200024 */` in `sass_explicit.txt`). Part of that encoding is **control information** that the compiler fills in, not the hardware's dependency logic: a stall count (cycles to wait before the next instruction issues), a yield flag, a write-scoreboard index and a read-scoreboard index (which of six dependency barriers this instruction sets when its result is written, or when its operands have been read), and a wait mask (which barriers must be clear before this instruction may issue).

The reverse-engineering literature documents the field list. For Maxwell, the maxas wiki ("Control Codes") states "Maxwell has 6 barrier resources for this purpose"; write barriers serve "variable latency instructions"; read barriers keep a later instruction from "overwrite the operand values" before they are read; a wait mask makes an instruction "wait on a previously set barrier of either type"; one 64-bit control word covers three instructions. For Volta, Jia et al. (2018) show the control word moved into each 128-bit instruction. That `sm_100a` keeps a scheme of this kind is confirmed by NVIDIA internal information: a producer's `&wr=x` decoration reads "this instruction produces/completes scoreboard token x", a consumer's `&req={x}` reads "the consumer requires token x to be released", and the exact scheduling/control-code fields are implementation details (the `cuobjdump --dump-sass` listings in `trace_out_v2/` print no such decorations). The `SB0`/`SB1` operands of the listing's `DEPBAR.LE` (no `SB2..SB5` operand occurs) and note D.2's decode of the baseline's control words (`SB1`, `SB4`) are consistent with it; the field list and six-barrier count above, and the field-level decode of this listing, remain inferred for `sm_100a` [H].

Fixed-latency ALU instructions need only the stall count. **Variable-latency instructions** (`LDTM`, `LDS`, `LDCU`, `S2UR`, `SYNCS.*`, `UTMA*`, and the TC-pipe operations) set a scoreboard, and their consumers carry the matching wait bit. This is where `tcgen05.wait::ld` went (Section 12.2, row `tcgen05.wait::ld`). The one explicit form you will meet is `DEPBAR.LE SBn, k` ("Dependency Barrier" in the Blackwell instruction table of the CUDA Binary Utilities manual): wait until scoreboard bank n has at most k outstanding committed async groups; `SBn` comes from the preceding commit/flush result and is not a barrier id (NVIDIA internal). The manual gives only the name; `.LE` and the 8-for-8 match with `wait_group.read 1`, Section 12.2, corroborate the reading. So `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x1` is `cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read 1` (at most one bulk store group still reading shared memory), and `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x0` would be `wait_group.read 0` (absent here). The two `DEPBAR.LE SB1, 0x36` at 0x4b20/0x4b80 inside the alloc sequence drain scoreboard 1 down to 54 before the TMEM allocator atomic: a compiler-inserted ordering inside the `tcgen05.alloc` lowering that guards the two attempts of the same allocation loop, one immediately before the first `UTCATOMSWS.2CTA.FIND_AND_SET.ALIGN` (0x4b30) and one after `NANOSLEEP 0x64` before the retry (0x4b90); they are not two separate allocations, and each ensures that prior async/scoreboard work is sufficiently retired before that attempt (NVIDIA internal; placement [M]).

**Truth-table immediates.** `LOP3.LUT d, a, b, c, LUT` computes, bit by bit, the three-input Boolean function whose truth table is the 8-bit immediate: bit `(a << 2) | (b << 1) | c` of `LUT` is the result for inputs `(a, b, c)`. This is the convention of PTX `lop3.b32 d, a, b, c, immLut` (`immLut = F(0xF0, 0xCC, 0xAA)`), so `0xc0` = `a & b`, `0x3c` = `a ^ b`, `0x33` = `~b`, `0xf6` = `a | (b ^ c)`, `0xf8` = `a | (b & c)`, `0xf4` = `a | (b & ~c)` [S].

Worked examples from this kernel. `LOP3.LUT R9, R9, UR11, RZ, 0x3c, !PT` (0x52f0) is `cons_phase ^= flip`. `LOP3.LUT P2, RZ, R6, 0x1, RZ, 0xc0, !PT` (0x1ce0) writes the predicate `P2 = (R6 & 1) != 0` and discards the register result into `RZ`. In the epilogue entry (0x1f30-0x2000), `R20 = threadIdx.x << 2` (the masks below keep only bits 2-6, i.e. `l << 2`), `R0 = ((w << 11) | ((l & 7) << 2))` and `R21 = R20 & 0x60 = ((l >> 3) & 3) << 5`; the four store bases are then `LOP3.LUT R23, R0, 0x60, R20, 0xf8` = `R0 | R21`, `LOP3.LUT R22, R0, 0x20, R21, 0xf6` = `R0 | (0x20 ^ R21)`, `LOP3.LUT R21, R0, 0x40, R21, 0xf6` = `R0 | (0x40 ^ R21)`, `LOP3.LUT R20, R0, 0x60, R20, 0xf4` = `R0 | (0x60 ^ R21)`. That is the `Swizzle<2,5,2>` XOR of the column class `c = 0..3` into bits 5-6 of the lane term (Chapter 10), one `LOP3` per class [M for the listing, S for the decode].

`PLOP3.LUT` and `UPLOP3.LUT` apply the same idea to predicates. With three constant-true inputs the index is 7, so LUT `0x80` (bit 7 set) writes **true** and LUT `0x40` (bit 6 set) writes **false**. `PLOP3.LUT P2, PT, PT, PT, UP2, 0x80, 0x8` copies the uniform predicate `UP2` into the vector predicate `P2` (inputs `11x` select bit 7 or bit 6 of `0x80`). The trailing second immediate (`0x8` with `0x80`, `0x4` with `0x40`) is a further encoding field that I have not decoded (unverified). This is what the annotations `P0 = true`, `P2 = UP2`, `UP0 = false` / `UP0 = true` in Section 12.5.1 mean.

**Byte selectors.** `PRMT d, a, sel, b` (and `UPRMT`) assembles each of the four result bytes from the eight bytes of the pair `{b, a}`: "The bytes in the two source registers are numbered from 0 to 7: {b, a} = {{b7, b6, b5, b4}, {b3, b2, b1, b0}}" and "the 3 lsbs of the selection value specify which of the 8 source bytes should be moved into the target position" (PTX ISA, `prmt`). Nibble k of the selector (least significant first) names the source of result byte k. That the SASS operand order is `a, sel, b` is my reading of the listing [H], but it is the only reading under which the three kinds of use below make sense. `PRMT R4, RZ, 0x654, R4` = `{R4.b0, R4.b1, R4.b2, RZ.b0}`: the shared::cta address with byte 3 replaced by 0, i.e. `mapa(addr, 0)`. `UPRMT UR6, UR9, 0x654, UR8` = the address in `UR8` with byte 3 = `UR9` = the target rank. `UPRMT UR34, URZ, 0x5410, UR25` = `{0, 0, UR25.b0, UR25.b1}`: the 16-bit multicast mask moved into bits [16, 32) of the `UTMALDG` mask operand.

---

## 12.2 The PTX-to-SASS dictionary

The table covers every instruction family the kernel emits. "Sites" are counts in the explicit kernel's SASS (my recount of `trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt`, which agrees with note G.3); the CUTLASS kernel's counts, where different, are in note D.2. "Uniform" means a uniform-datapath instruction (Section 12.3): `U*` mnemonic, `UR`/`UP` operands, issued once per warp.

| PTX (wrapper, explicit.cu line) | SASS in the explicit kernel (sites) | What the lowering teaches |
|---|---|---|
| `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::f16 [tmem], descA, descB, idesc, {8 masks}, p` (W29, :517) | `UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR10], gdesc[UR12], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UP0` (4: 0x5410, 0x5440, 0x5460, 0x5470) | Uniform, unpredicated: the `elect.sync` around it is folded away. The 64-bit descriptors are UR pairs whose high words are `UMOV URn, 0x40004040` (8 per k-tile). The scale-c predicate `p` becomes the uniform predicate `UP0` on the first MMA and the constant-true `UPT` on the other three (`scale_c = 1u` after k-block 0 is a compile-time fact for kb 1..3). The eight zero mask registers do not appear. `UR28` is held at 0 by `UMOV UR28, 0x0` (0x5390), and `tmem[UR28]`, the second `tmem[]` slot, is the sparse-metadata TMEM operand (E), zero for a dense MMA, here via `UR28 = 0`; the first slot, `tmem[UR36]`, is the accumulator (NVIDIA internal); a `tmem[URx]` operand is an address, not intrinsically zero, and the register number is an allocator artifact (NVIDIA internal). The slot has no PTX counterpart in the dense form: `[sp-meta-tmem]` is an operand of the sparse forms `tcgen05.mma.sp` and `tcgen05.mma.ws.sp` only (PTX ISA 9.7.18.10.10.2 and 9.7.18.10.10.4, `[d-tmem], a-desc, b-desc, [sp-meta-tmem], idesc, ...`), and the dense `tcgen05.mma` syntax of 9.7.18.10.10.1 is `[d-tmem], a-desc, b-desc, idesc, ...`. |
| `tcgen05.commit.cta_group::2.mbarrier::arrive::one.shared::cluster.multicast::cluster.b64 [bar], mask` (W30, :532) | `UTCBAR.2CTA.MULTICAST [UR32], URZ, UR37` (2: 0x5480 with `UR37 = 0xf`; the accumulator commit with `UR33 = 0x3 << 2y`, note G.3) | Uniform; the commit is a TC-pipe barrier instruction, not a memory op. The mainloop commit is the instruction after the fourth `UTCHMMA`. The compile-time mask 0xF becomes `UMOV UR37, 0xf` inside the loop; the run-time pair mask stays in a UR computed once. |
| `tcgen05.alloc.cta_group::2.sync.aligned.shared::cta.b32 [smem+384], 512` (W26, :498) | `UTCATOMSWS.2CTA.FIND_AND_SET.ALIGN UP0, UR6, UR6` with `UR6 = 0x10` (2 copies: 0x4b30 and the retry 0x4b90 after `NANOSLEEP 0x64`) inside a 69-instruction sequence 0x4a90-0x4ed0 [M] | One allocation unit = 32 TMEM columns, so 512 columns = `0x10` units. ptxas executes the "whole warp, both CTAs" PTX op as a handshake. The **leader's** elected lane does the atomic, stores the result (`STS [UR7+0x180], R6` with `R6 = R2 << 5`, i.e. units -> columns), forwards it to the peer with `STAS [R4.64], R2` (st.async), which completes a barrier in the peer's reserved shared memory at `(rank << 24) + 0x48`, and keeps bookkeeping words at `+0x50/+0x54/+0x58` with `ATOMS.OR/XOR`. The peer's elected lane waits (`SYNCS...TRYWAIT [UR4+0x8]`), rescales and acknowledges. `WARPSYNC.ALL` runs twice; then `BAR.ARV 0x6, 0xa0`. The reserved kilobyte (`SHARED:1024`) is where this handshake lives. The sequence has the same length and skeleton as the CUTLASS kernel's (note G.3; Section 9.4.1 lists the eight mnemonic differences). |
| `tcgen05.dealloc.cta_group::2.sync.aligned.b32 T, 512` (W27, :504) | `UTCATOMSWS.AND URZ, UR4` (1: 0x5ae0) + `ATOMS.AND` clears of the reserved words + two ptxas-inserted consistency checks whose failure paths `CALL` stubs containing `BPT.TRAP 0x1` (0x6530, 0x6560) | Both CTAs execute it. `UR4 = ~(0xffff << ((T & 0xffff) >> 5))` clears the 16 unit bits of the allocation. The PTX has no `trap`; the two `BPT.TRAP` are ptxas's own sanity checks on the reserved words [M]. |
| `tcgen05.relinquish_alloc_permit.cta_group::2.sync.aligned` (W28, :512) | no `UTC*` mnemonic; `UVIRTCOUNT.DEALLOC.SMPOOL 0x80` (0x55f0), immediately before `PREEXIT` (0x5600); the neighbouring `ELECT` (0x55d0) and `ELECT`-guarded `STS.U8 [UR6+0x1c], R2` (0x5630) are not part of the lowering (NVIDIA internal) | The `UVIRTCOUNT` is the relinquish lowering (`UVIRTCOUNT 128`, i.e. `0x80`); an older compiler mapping made the relinquish a no-op, so successor CTAs stayed serialised through CTA exit (NVIDIA internal). The `ELECT` elects the one thread for mbarrier/TMA/commit-side work and the `STS.U8` is an ordinary surrounding shared-memory byte store; the relinquish is warp-collective and lies outside the elected-thread region, so position alone attributes neither to it (NVIDIA internal; the inference of note D.2 is withdrawn, and what emits the `STS.U8` is unresolved). ptxas emitted the `UVIRTCOUNT` **before** `PREEXIT`, the reverse of the PTX order (`griddep_launch_dependents()` at :950 precedes `tmem_relinquish_2sm()` at :951). |
| `tcgen05.ld.sync.aligned.32x32b.x16.b32 {16 regs}, [addr]` (W31, :543) | `LDTM.x16 R4, tmem[UR29+0x10*e]` (8: 0x2290, 0x2760, 0x2c40, 0x3120, 0x3600, 0x3ae0, 0x3fc0, 0x44d0) | The TMEM address `T + ((32w) << 16) + 128 st` is warp-uniform (`UR29`, built by `ULEA UR17, UR16, UR17, 0x15` = `w << 21` plus the base); the subtile term `16e` is folded into the immediate `0x10*e`. Sixteen vector destination registers `R4..R19` per lane. |
| `tcgen05.wait::ld.sync.aligned` (W32, :558) | **no instruction** | Scoreboards in the control words track the asynchronous register writes of `LDTM`: the first `FMUL R4` after an `LDTM` waits on the scoreboard the `LDTM` set, the next `LDTM` waits on the `STS` read scoreboard (WAR), and the subtile-7 `SYNCS.ARRIVE` at 0x44f0 waits on the eighth `LDTM` (0x44d0). The absence of a wait opcode is measured; the scoreboard decode is inferred (note D.2, G.3; Section 12.1.3). The PTX still needs exactly one `wait::ld`, before the release. The ISA (9.7.18.6.4.5, "Register dependencies, same thread") guarantees that "an intra-thread ordering through true register dependency will be respected regardless of the presence or absence of other forms of synchronization", so the `FMUL`s of every subtile are legal without any wait. But that dependency "does not imply any other form of ordering", and "to enforce such memory orderings and avoiding anti-dependency hazards around tcgen05.ld, tcgen05.wait::ld must be used". The `mbarrier.arrive` that releases the accumulator stage (explicit.cu:1039) is not a register consumer, so without the `wait::ld` at explicit.cu:1038 the release could precede the completion of the eighth load. |
