Four rows deserve the long form.

### 12.2.1 `UTCHMMA` and its operands [M]

```
        /*5410*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR10], gdesc[UR12], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UP0 ;
        /*5440*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR16], gdesc[UR18], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UPT ;
        /*5460*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR20], gdesc[UR22], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UPT ;
        /*5470*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR24], gdesc[UR26], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UPT ;
        /*5480*/                   UTCBAR.2CTA.MULTICAST [UR32], URZ, UR37 ;
```

Compare with the PTX source of the wrapper (W29, explicit.cu:517-529, quoted in Section 6.7.2).

- `gdesc[UR10]` is the 64-bit A descriptor in `{UR10, UR11}`: `UR10 = ULEA UR8, UR30, 0xa` (= `desc_lo_a + 1024 s`, the `+16384 B per stage` in 16-byte units of explicit.cu:928), `UR11 = 0x40004040` (`kSmemDescHi`). The three later k-blocks use `UR16/18/20/22/24/26 = UR10/12 + 0x2/0x4/0x6` (`+ 2 kb`, explicit.cu:933-934) with their own `0x40004040` high words `UR17/19/21/23/25/27`. That is why eight `UMOV URn, 0x40004040` appear per k-tile.
- `tmem[UR36]` = `tmem_c = T + 128 st` (explicit.cu:919), computed once per tile: the accumulator, the PTX `[d-tmem]`. The second slot `tmem[UR28]`, held at 0, is the sparse-metadata TMEM operand, zero for a dense MMA (NVIDIA internal); the dense PTX form has no operand for it (Section 12.2).
- `idesc[UR29]` = `0x10200010` (`kInstrDesc`), re-materialised per k-tile by `UMOV UR29, 0x10200010`.
- `UP0` / `UPT`: the `setp.ne.b32 p, scaleC, 0` of the wrapper. In the loop `scale_c` is 0 only for `kb = 0` of the first k-tile of a tile (explicit.cu:917, :940), so ptxas keeps a uniform predicate `UP0`. It is cleared (set false) once per tile by `UPLOP3.LUT UP0, UPT, UPT, UPT, UPT, 0x40, 0x4` at 0x51c0, before the k-tile loop. It is set true by `UPLOP3.LUT UP0, UPT, UPT, UPT, UPT, 0x80, 0x8` at 0x54b0, after the first k-tile's four MMAs have issued, so every later k-tile's first `UTCHMMA` runs with `scale_c = 1` (LUT decode in Section 12.1.3; entry sequence and loop listing in Section 12.5.1). The other three MMAs are hard-wired to `UPT`. The CUTLASS kernel shows the same two-site pattern on `UP2` at 0x3860 / 0x3a90 (note D.2).
- The `if (elect_one_sync())` around the call (explicit.cu:932) is gone. The whole warp reaches the instruction; the hardware executes it once (Section 12.3).

### 12.2.2 The barrier wait, inline and out of line [M]

The wrapper (W6, explicit.cu:297-311, quoted in Section 6.3.3) is a `bra` loop.

ptxas emits the first attempt inline and moves the loop out of the hot path. In the MMA loop:

```
        /*51f0*/               @P0 BRA 0x5240 ;                                   <- peek succeeded: skip the wait
        /*5200*/                   ULEA UR4, UR8, UR7, 0x3 ;                       <- full[s] = smem_base + 8 s
        /*5210*/                   SHF.L.U32 R2, R9, 0x1f, RZ ;                    <- parity -> bit 31
        /*5220*/                   SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P0, [UR4], R2 ;
        /*5230*/              @!P0 BRA 0x6350 ;                                    <- not yet: go to the out-of-line retry loop
```

and the retry-loop shape (this copy, one of the four inline loops of lesson 3, is the producer tail's last wait, which ends in `EXIT`):

```
        /*1950*/                   SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P0, [R3+URZ], R0 ;
        /*1960*/              @!P0 NANOSLEEP.SYNCS 0x989680 ;
        /*1970*/              @!P0 SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64 P0, [R3+URZ], R0 ;
        /*1980*/               @P0 EXIT ;
        /*1990*/                   BRA 0x1940 ;
```

Three lessons.

1. The parity operand is a 32-bit register whose bit 31 is the parity. So `phase ^= 1` in C++ costs a `LOP3 ... 0x3c` (XOR) plus the `SHF`.
2. The `NANOSLEEP.SYNCS 0x989680` carries the 10 ms `timeHint`. The ISA says the suspended thread "resumes execution when the specified phase completes OR before the phase completes following a system-dependent time limit", and that the operand "specifies the time limit, in nanoseconds, that may be used for the time limit instead of the system-dependent limit" (PTX ISA, `mbarrier.test_wait`/`mbarrier.try_wait`). It is a hint for the time limit of one suspension, not a guaranteed bound. In the SASS sequence the `NANOSLEEP` is the back-off on a miss and the bare `PHASECHK.TRANS64` after it is the retry-path blocking check before the branch back (NVIDIA internal); the ISA's wake-up on phase completion is realised by a wake trigger: a failed `PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT` arms it, and the barrier's phase completion wakes the sleeping warp (the wake condition is a phase toggle, or a lock assertion), so the `NANOSLEEP` back-off is not ordinary periodic polling (NVIDIA internal).
3. Of the 30 retry loops counted in the W6 row of Section 12.2, the 4 inline ones sit in the role tails: the producer tail's last wait (0x1960, ending in `EXIT`), the scheduler tail's (0x1ea0, also ending in `EXIT`) and the last wait of warp 0's accumulator tail, whose retry ptxas emitted twice (0x5860, a peeled first retry with no back-branch, and 0x58a0, the loop). This matches note G.3's "26 out-of-line + 4 inline loops against 47 + 5" for the CUTLASS kernel, whose counts are 116 `TRYWAIT` + 54 `PHASECHK` against the explicit kernel's 65 + 32 (note D.2, G.3). Adding the 2 `test_wait` to the 30 gives 32 `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64` without `.TRYWAIT`. The counts are ptxas's and not part of the contract (note D.7).

### 12.2.3 The epilogue element: `LDTM`, `FMUL`, `FFMA`, `STS` [M]

```
        /*2290*/                   LDTM.x16 R4, tmem[UR29] ;
        /*22a0*/                   UISETP.NE.U32.AND UP1, UPT, UR16, URZ, UPT ;
        /*22b0*/                   FMUL R4, R4, UR26 ;
        /*22c0*/                   FMUL R5, R5, UR26 ;
        ...
        /*2300*/                   FFMA R4, RZ, UR27, R4 ;
        ...
        /*23a0*/                   STS [R23+UR7+0x200], R4 ;
        ...
        /*23e0*/                   STS [R22+UR7+0x280], R5 ;
        ...
        /*2420*/                   STS [R21+UR7+0x300], R6 ;
        ...
        /*2460*/                   STS [R20+UR7+0x380], R7 ;
        ...
        /*24a0*/                   STS [R23+UR7+0x400], R8 ;
```

The source is explicit.cu:1036 for the `LDTM` and explicit.cu:1043-1048 for the arithmetic and stores (quoted in Sections 10.7 and 10.9).

Read the `STS` immediates against the store-address formula of explicit.cu:1047, `st_off[j & 3] + 512 (j >> 2) + 8192 (e & 3)`. `st_off[c]` contributes `OFF_SMEM_CD (0x200) + 128 c (0x80 c)` plus the warp-and-lane term `2048 w + 4 (l & 7) + 32 (((l >> 3) & 3) ^ c)` that lives in `R20..R23`; `512 (j >> 2)` is `0x200 (j >> 2)`; `8192 (e & 3)` is `0x2000 (e & 3)`. For `j = 0..4` the immediates are `0x200, 0x280, 0x300, 0x380, 0x400` with base registers `R23, R22, R21, R20, R23`: exactly `0x200 + 0x80 (j & 3) + 0x200 (j >> 2)`. ptxas interleaves `FMUL`, `FFMA` and `STS` so that the stores overlap the remaining arithmetic: the `STS` of `R4..R8` issue 10, 12, 14, 16 and 18 instructions after their `FFMA`s, one store every fourth slot. The first `FMUL R4` is the instruction that waits, through the scoreboard, for the asynchronous `LDTM` (inferred from the control words, Section 12.1.3).

### 12.2.4 The CLC query line [M]

```
        /*1b70*/              @!P0 SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED RZ, [R11+URZ], R5 ;     <- lanes 0..3: arm CTA (lane)'s clc_full[idx] with R5 = 0x10 bytes
        ...
        /*1bc0*/                   UGETNEXTWORKID.BROADCAST [UR8], [UR9] ;         <- the try_cancel: response slot UR8, barrier UR9
        ...
        /*1c60*/                   LDS.128 R4, [R4+0x160] ;                        <- the 16-byte response (OFF_CLC_RESPONSE = 352 = 0x160)
        /*1c90*/                   MEMBAR.ALL.CTA ;
        /*1ca0*/                   FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S ;                            <- with the MEMBAR.ALL.CTA above: fence.proxy.async.shared::cta
        /*1cc0*/                   SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0 RZ, [R2+URZ], RZ ; <- consumer release on CTA 0's clc_empty[idx] (R2 = PRMT(.., RZ, 0x654, ..))
        /*1ce0*/                   LOP3.LUT P2, RZ, R6, 0x1, RZ, 0xc0, !PT ;        <- valid = bit 0 of response word 2
```

This is Chapter 7's scheduler loop in the seven machine instructions above plus the three blocking waits and the throttle release that the listing omits, and bookkeeping; the whole loop is 50 instructions (Section 12.5.3).

## 12.3 The uniform datapath, or why the elections disappeared

### 12.3.1 What `UR`, `UP`, `URZ`, `UPT` are

Since Turing, every SM sub-partition has a scalar **uniform datapath** (integer-only on Turing; Blackwell's uniform instruction set also has FP32 arithmetic such as `UFADD`, `UFMUL`, `UFFMA`) next to the 32-lane vector datapath: "this scalar unit executes instructions where all threads use the same input and generate the same output" (Nsight Compute Profiling Guide, pipeline descriptions). Its state is a separate file of **uniform registers** `URn` (one 32-bit value per warp, not per lane), 64 of them on Turing including a uniform zero register, `UR0`-`UR62` plus `URZ` in SASS notation; the baseline's Blackwell SASS (`trace_out_v2/sass_gemm.txt`) uses up to `UR77`, and Blackwell's uniform register file holds 80 x 32-bit addressable uniform registers `UR0`-`UR79` per warp, 320 B per warp and 5 KB per SM sub-partition at 16 warps per sub-partition, with `URZ` a separate constant-zero register not counted among the 80, so the Turing count of 64 includes `URZ` and the Blackwell count of 80 does not (NVIDIA internal; the Turing count is a paraphrase of Jia, Maggioni, Smith, Scarpazza, *Dissecting the NVidia Turing T4 GPU via Microbenchmarking*, arXiv:1903.07486, Section 3.5.2 "Uniform Registers", which states "we were able to enumerate the 64 uniform registers supported by Turing (including a Uniform Zero Register URZ and 63 general-purpose uniform registers UR0–UR62)"), and **uniform predicates** `UPn`. `URZ` is the uniform zero register and `UPT` the constant-true uniform predicate, mirrors of the per-lane `RZ` and `PT`; any of the four used as a destination discards the write (NVIDIA internal). Instructions whose mnemonic starts with `U` (`UMOV`, `UIADD3`, `ULEA`, `USHF`, `ULOP3`, `UISETP`, `USEL`, `UPRMT`, `UPLOP3`) and the file's loads and moves (`LDCU`, `S2UR`, `R2UR`; NVIDIA's instruction table files all of these under Uniform Datapath Instructions) read and write that file; the uniform branches `BRA.U` and `BRXU` branch on it. PTX has no control over it: ptxas decides whether a value lives in `UR` or `R` by proving that it is identical across the warp.

This matters for a GEMM kernel because the operands of a TMA load (destination address, barrier, coordinates, mask), of a `tcgen05.mma` (descriptors, TMEM address, instruction descriptor) and of a `tcgen05.commit` (barrier address, mask) are warp-uniform by construction. They depend on the cluster rank, the tile coordinates, the stage index and compile-time constants, never on the lane. ptxas therefore keeps them in `UR`s and issues the instruction itself as a **single warp-level operation**: `UTMALDG`, `UTMASTG`, `UTCHMMA`, `UTCBAR`, `UGETNEXTWORKID`, `UTMACCTL` all take only `UR`/`UP` operands and issue once per warp, which is what this lecture means by a uniform-datapath instruction (NVIDIA's Blackwell instruction table files only `UGETNEXTWORKID` under Uniform Datapath Instructions; `UTMALDG`/`UTMASTG`/`UTMACCTL` are Tensor Memory Access and `UTCHMMA`/`UTCBAR` Tensor Core Memory instructions, the latter executed by the `tc` pipe per the Nsight Compute guide); even the 32-lane TMA store of warp 4 costs one `UTMASTG` per box (K4b: 32 active lanes at every issue).

### 12.3.2 Why `elect.sync` vanished from the loops [M]

The PTX contract of CUTLASS (and of explicit.cu, Chapters 8-9) is "one elected lane issues the TMA/MMA/commit/query": `if (elect_one_sync()) { ... }` around W21/W22 (explicit.cu:740), W29 (:932), W30 (:942, :944) and W33 (:843). The PTX has 14 `elect.sync` sites and the SASS 4 `ELECT` instructions, all outside the role loops (addresses in the `elect.sync` row of Section 12.2); the CUTLASS kernel's 19 PTX sites survive as 5 SASS `ELECT` (note D.2, G.3). Inside the producer, MMA and scheduler loops there is **none**: the uniform instruction executes once per warp anyway, so predicating it on one lane changes nothing, and ptxas removes the election (note D.6 item 6).

The election survives only where the issue genuinely is per-lane or where a vector side effect depends on it: the prologue's `lane_pred` (it predicates `UTMACCTL.PF` through `VOTEU.ALL UP1, P1`, a vector-to-uniform predicate conversion), the alloc atomics (one lane performs the `STS`/`STAS`/`ATOMS` handshake) and the `ELECT`-guarded `STS.U8` at 0x5630, whose origin is unresolved (not the relinquish, which is warp-collective; NVIDIA internal).

`elect.sync` is deterministic ("the same leader thread is elected for the same membermask every time", PTX ISA), which is why "leader lane" is a stable identity across the producer's `expect_tx` predicate and its TMA issue (Chapter 8).

The lesson is **not** "drop the `elect.sync`". The PTX ISA gives `tcgen05.mma` "single thread semantics, unlike the collective instructions mma.sync or wgmma.mma_async. So, a single thread issuing the tcgen05.mma will result in the initiation of the whole matrix multiply and accumulate operation". This does not forbid more issuing threads; it means every issuing thread starts a whole MMA. An election, or as here a uniform instruction executed once per warp, is therefore needed to avoid issuing it 32 times. CUTLASS's contract is the election; the SASS shows that keeping it costs nothing. The lesson is the converse: **an issue instruction whose operands are not provably uniform will not become a `U*` instruction**. Then the election matters, lane-dependent address arithmetic appears in vector registers, and `R2UR` moves (vector to uniform) are needed before the instruction. The explicit kernel has 13 `R2UR` against the CUTLASS kernel's 150 (106 plain `R2UR` plus the 44 `R2UR.FILL` counted next), and 0 `MOV.SPILL`/`R2UR.FILL` against 44 + 44 (note G.3). The uniform file, not the vector file, was the CUTLASS kernel's tight resource (note D.7, inferred).

### 12.3.3 What this implies for how you write issue code [H, grounded in the measurements above]

1. Compute every TMA/MMA/barrier operand from warp-uniform sources only: `%cluster_ctarank`/`%cluster_ctaid`, `blockIdx`, the pipeline `{index, phase}` state, loop counters, compile-time constants, and values read from shared memory by every lane (e.g. `T` at `smem + 384`). Never from `threadIdx.x & 31` or lane-dependent loads.
2. Keep the number of loop-invariant uniform values small (descriptor bases, barrier bases, masks, map addresses). The explicit kernel's three extra `UMOV` and one extra `ULEA` per k-tile in the MMA loop, and its five re-materialisations of four loop invariants per k-tile in the producer, are ptxas choosing to recompute rather than hold a `UR` (note G.3; counts in Sections 12.5.1-12.5.2). Harmless here, because the loops are not issue-bound (Section 12.5.5), but the mechanism is worth knowing for a loop that is.
3. Lane-dependent work belongs to the vector lanes: the epilogue's `STS` bases (`R20..R23`), the per-lane `expect_tx` predicate, the CLC arming by lanes 0..3. ptxas separates the two datapaths cleanly if the code does.
4. A warp-uniform branch becomes `BRA.U UPn` (the loop back-edges at 0x12f0 and 0x54d0 are `BRA.U UP0`/`BRA.U UP1`): the uniform predicate makes the branch provably non-divergent [H: interpretation of the `.U` suffix].

---

## 12.4 Registers: 26 versus 68

### 12.4.1 Where 26 comes from [M]

| Register range | Holds | Why it is needed |
|---|---|---|
| low registers, per role | per-lane pipeline state and scratch, reused by every role. The MMA warp keeps `cons_phase` in `R9` (`LOP3.LUT R9, R9, UR11, RZ, 0x3c` at 0x52f0) and the shifted parity in `R2` (`SHF.L.U32 R2, R9, 0x1f`), and touches only `R2` and `R9` inside its k-tile loop (0x51f0-0x54d0); the once-per-tile entry 0x5100-0x5180 adds `R0` (the accumulator phase, shifted into `R2` at 0x5130) and `R4` (the peek parity at 0x5160). The producer keeps `prod_phase` in `R0` (`LOP3.LUT R0, R0, UR8, ...` at 0x1190) and uses `R4`, `R5`. The scheduler loop uses `R0` and `R2..R12` (response words `R4..R7`, arming address `R11`, barrier base `R12`). The epilogue uses `R0`, `R2`, `R3`, `R8` and `R9` (its `acc_full` parity: `TRYWAIT P0, [UR24+0xf0], R9` at 0x2180) besides the two ranges below [M] | the phase bits are vector values because the wrappers take them as `"r"` operands. Since every role reuses the low registers, the epilogue's live set alone sets the kernel's maximum |
| `R4..R19` | the 16 `LDTM.x16` destinations = 16 fp32 accumulator values of one lane for one subtile; also the `FMUL`/`FFMA` results in place | `tcgen05.ld.32x32b.x16` writes 16 registers per lane (W31) |
| `R20..R23` | the four lane-dependent `STS` bases `st_off[c]` (explicit.cu:1011-1014): `R23` for `j & 3 = 0`, `R22` for 1, `R21` for 2, `R20` for 3 | the lane term `4 (l & 7)` and the `Swizzle<2,5,2>` XOR term `32 (((l >> 3) & 3) ^ c)` both depend on the lane (Chapter 10) |
| `R1` | the compiler's per-thread local-memory stack base by codegen convention (NVIDIA internal); `LDC R1, c[0x0][0x37c]` at 0x0000 is the only reference to `R1` | ABI/codegen convention, not an architectural promise (NVIDIA internal); unused here, no `STL`/`LDL` addresses it and `STACK` is 0 |

Everything else (barrier addresses, descriptors, coordinates, alpha, beta, `k_tiles`, pipeline states) lives in uniform registers. The CUTLASS kernel's highest register is `R65`. It additionally carries the zero-filled C fragment (`R21..R36`, 16 registers: the `beta != 0` path's operand, dead for beta = 0 but still allocated), the `epi_load` pipeline state, the per-tile CLC decode in vector registers for the scheduler bookkeeping, and the 44 `MOV.SPILL`/`R2UR.FILL` pairs (a uniform value parked in a vector register and moved back, 88 instructions), 40 of them in the never-executed C-load path (note D.2, G.3).

### 12.4.2 Why it does not matter here, and when it would [S, H]

- Shared memory fixes occupancy at **1 CTA per SM**: 230400 B of dynamic smem out of 232448 B opt-in (util.hpp `static_assert`), and `__launch_bounds__(256, 1)` only asks for at least that one (Section 11.2.1). 256 threads x 68 registers = 17408 of the SM's 65536 32-bit registers; even 255 x 256 = 65280 would fit. Register count cannot change occupancy, and it did not change the issue rate (Section 12.5). Registers are allocated in rounded chunks at warp/block granularity, the "register allocation unit size" of Nsight Compute's occupancy data (NVIDIA internal: an occupancy-accounting quantum, not a SASS register width or an instruction encoding; the Nsight Compute guide says registers are "allocated by the HW in fixed-size chunks"), so a difference of a few registers changes nothing until a chunk boundary is crossed; the granularity varies by compute capability, so read it for CC 10.0 from that data (`reg_allocation_unit_size`, `warp_reg_allocation_granularities`) rather than deriving it from a register-number range in the disassembly (NVIDIA internal); its value is not verified here.
- It would matter in three situations. (a) A kernel designed for 2 or more CTAs per SM (smaller smem footprint), where 256 threads x >128 registers would halve occupancy. (b) A register-hungry epilogue (e.g. `tcgen05.ld.32x32b.x32` = 32 registers per load, plus conversion temporaries and multiple subtiles in flight), where ptxas would start spilling; a spill (`STL`/`LDL`) inside the per-subtile loop would be on the epilogue's critical path. (c) Hopper-style `setmaxnreg` register reallocation between producer and consumer warps, which this kernel does not use because 1 CTA/SM with 8 warps leaves the register file about 90 % empty anyway (256 x 26 = 6656 of 65536 registers; 73 % empty even at the CUTLASS kernel's 68).
- The numbers to watch are therefore not `REG` but `LOCAL` and `STACK` (both 0) and the absence of `LDL`/`STL` in the hot loops.

---

## 12.5 The four hot loops

All addresses and counts in this section are my recount of `trace_out_v2/sass_explicit.txt`; they agree with note G.3 except where stated.

### 12.5.1 MMA warp: 47 instructions per k-tile (0x51f0-0x54d0) [M]

How warp 0 reaches the loop, once per tile (0x5180-0x51e0, verbatim; comments mine):

```
/*5180*/                   SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P2, [UR35+0x110], R2 ;   acc_empty[st] blocking wait (UR35 = base + 8 st, +0x110 = OFF_ACC_EMPTY)
/*5190*/              @!P2 BRA 0x62f0 ;                                             out-of-line retry loop
/*51a0*/                   BRA.U !UP0, 0x54e0 ;                                     UP0 = (k_tiles >= 1), set at 0x5100: skip the k-tile loop (not the commit) when there is none; the non-leader CTA already left at 0x50f0
/*51b0*/                   ULEA UR36, UR5, UR15, 0x7 ;                              tmem_c = T + 128 st   (UR5 = st, UR15 = T)
/*51c0*/                   UPLOP3.LUT UP0, UPT, UPT, UPT, UPT, 0x40, 0x4 ;          UP0 = false: scale_c = 0 for the first MMA of the tile
/*51d0*/                   UMOV UR6, UR14 ;                                         k = k_tiles
/*51e0*/                   UMOV UR8, UR4 ;                                          s = cons_idx
```

Three things to read here. First, `UP0` is overloaded. At 0x51a0 it holds `k_tiles >= 1` (`UISETP.GE.AND UP0, UPT, UR14, 0x1, UPT` at 0x5100), the `while (k > 0)` guard of explicit.cu:922: with no k-tiles the loop is skipped and only the commit at 0x54e0 runs. The non-leader CTA's warp 0 never reaches this block: `BRA.U UP0, 0x5510` at 0x50f0 (`UP0 = UR34 != 0` from 0x5020, `UR34 = rank & 1` from 0x0730, i.e. `!is_leader`, explicit.cu:1106) jumps over the `acc_empty` wait, the four MMAs and the commit to the accumulator state advance at 0x5510, so per tile it executes only the CLC consume and that advance (Chapter 9). From 0x51c0 on, `UP0` is the scale-c predicate: cleared once per tile here and set at 0x54b0 inside the loop (Section 12.2.1). Second, `UR36` (`tmem_c`), the loop counter `UR6 = k_tiles` (`UR14`, computed once at 0x0a70-0x0ac0 as `(k + 63) >> 6` from the `k` loaded from `c[0x0][0x588]`) and the stage `UR8` are formed once per tile, which is why the loop body below contains none of them. Third, the `acc_empty[st]` wait is on the leader's own barrier (`UR35 = ULEA(st, base, 3)` at 0x5120, unmasked), the one all 256 epilogue threads arrive on (Chapter 4). After the loop, 0x54e0 forms `acc_full[st]` from the same register (`UIADD3 UR6, UR35, 0xf0`) for the accumulator commit.

The loop body, complete and in order, grouped by purpose (the SASS is verbatim; the right-hand comments are mine):

```
--- blocking wait on full[s], skipped when the peek succeeded (4 instructions, off the fast path) ---
/*51f0*/               @P0 BRA 0x5240 ;
/*5200*/                   ULEA UR4, UR8, UR7, 0x3 ;              full[s] = base + 8 s
/*5210*/                   SHF.L.U32 R2, R9, 0x1f, RZ ;           parity -> bit 31
/*5220*/                   SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P0, [UR4], R2 ;
/*5230*/              @!P0 BRA 0x6350 ;                           out-of-line retry loop
--- pipeline state: rs = s; advance {s, phase}; decide whether to peek (C++: k > 0 after --k; SASS: UR6 != 1 before the decrement at 0x54a0) ---
/*5240*/                   UISETP.NE.U32.AND UP2, UPT, UR6, 0x1, UPT ;   UP2 = (k != 1): peek the next stage
/*5250*/                   PLOP3.LUT P0, PT, PT, PT, PT, 0x80, 0x8 ;      P0 = true (tok = 1 when no peek)
/*5260*/                   UIADD3 UR4, UPT, UPT, UR8, 0x1, URZ ;          s + 1
/*5270*/                   ULEA UR10, UR8, UR30, 0xa ;                    lo_a = desc_lo_a + 1024 s
/*5280*/                   UISETP.NE.U32.AND UP1, UPT, UR4, 0x8, UPT ;    wrap test (s + 1 == 8)
/*5290*/                   PLOP3.LUT P2, PT, PT, PT, UP2, 0x80, 0x8 ;     P2 = UP2 as a vector predicate
/*52a0*/                   ULEA UR12, UR8, UR31, 0x9 ;                    lo_b = desc_lo_b + 512 s
/*52b0*/                   USEL UR11, URZ, 0x1, UP1 ;                     phase flip bit
/*52c0*/                   USEL UR4, UR4, URZ, UP1 ;                      s = wrap ? 0 : s + 1
/*52d0*/                   ULEA UR32, UR8, UR7, 0x3 ;                     (base + 8 rs) -> empty[rs] after + 0x40
/*52e0*/               @UP2 ULEA UR8, UR4, UR7, 0x3 ;                     full[s] address for the peek (s already advanced and wrapped at 0x52c0)
/*52f0*/                   LOP3.LUT R9, R9, UR11, RZ, 0x3c, !PT ;         cons_phase ^= flip
--- descriptor low words for k-blocks 1..3 (+2, +4, +6 = +32, +64, +96 bytes) ---
/*5300*/                   UIADD3 UR16, UPT, UPT, UR10, 0x2, URZ ;
/*5310*/                   UIADD3 UR18, UPT, UPT, UR12, 0x2, URZ ;
/*5320*/               @P2 SHF.L.U32 R2, R9, 0x1f, RZ ;                   peek parity
/*5330*/                   UIADD3 UR20, UPT, UPT, UR10, 0x4, URZ ;
/*5340*/                   UIADD3 UR22, UPT, UPT, UR12, 0x4, URZ ;
/*5350*/               @P2 SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P0, [UR8], R2 ; the peek of the next stage (predicated off on the last k-tile)
/*5360*/                   UIADD3 UR24, UPT, UPT, UR10, 0x6, URZ ;
/*5370*/                   UIADD3 UR26, UPT, UPT, UR12, 0x6, URZ ;
/*5380*/                   UIADD3 UR32, UPT, UPT, UR32, 0x40, URZ ;        empty[rs] = base + 64 + 8 rs
--- constants the PTX materialises per k-block (mov.b32 for UR29, the idesc; UR28 = 0 fills the sparse-metadata slot, which the dense PTX form has no operand for, Section 12.2; the 0x40004040 high words come from the PTX or.b64 immediate 0x4000404000000000, one per descriptor) ---
/*5390*/                   UMOV UR28, 0x0 ;                               tmem[UR28]: sparse-metadata TMEM operand, zero for a dense MMA (NVIDIA internal)
/*53a0*/                   UMOV UR29, 0x10200010 ;                        idesc
/*53b0*/                   UMOV UR11, 0x40004040 ;                        descriptor high words x 8
/*53c0*/                   UMOV UR13, 0x40004040 ;
/*53d0*/                   UMOV UR17, 0x40004040 ;
/*53e0*/                   UMOV UR19, 0x40004040 ;
/*53f0*/                   UMOV UR21, 0x40004040 ;
/*5400*/                   UMOV UR23, 0x40004040 ;
--- the four MMAs and the release ---
/*5410*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR10], gdesc[UR12], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UP0 ;
/*5420*/                   UMOV UR25, 0x40004040 ;
/*5430*/                   UMOV UR27, 0x40004040 ;
/*5440*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR16], gdesc[UR18], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UPT ;
/*5450*/                   UMOV UR37, 0xf ;                               kMainloopReleaseMask
/*5460*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR20], gdesc[UR22], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UPT ;
/*5470*/                   UTCHMMA.2CTA gdesc[UR24], gdesc[UR26], tmem[UR36], tmem[UR28], idesc[UR29], UPT ;
/*5480*/                   UTCBAR.2CTA.MULTICAST [UR32], URZ, UR37 ;      tcgen05.commit -> empty[rs] of all four CTAs
--- loop counter, scale-c, back-edge ---
/*5490*/                   UISETP.GT.U32.AND UP1, UPT, UR6, 0x1, UPT ;    k > 1 ?
/*54a0*/                   UIADD3 UR6, UPT, UPT, UR6, -0x1, URZ ;         --k
/*54b0*/                   UPLOP3.LUT UP0, UPT, UPT, UPT, UPT, 0x80, 0x8 ; UP0 = true: scale_c = 1 from now on
/*54c0*/                   UMOV UR8, UR4 ;                                cons_idx = s
/*54d0*/                   BRA.U UP1, 0x51f0 ;
```

Composition, grouped by datapath: 32 uniform-datapath ALU operations (12 `UMOV`, 9 `UIADD3`, 5 `ULEA`, 2 `UISETP.NE`, 1 `UISETP.GT`, 2 `USEL`, 1 `UPLOP3`), 5 TC-pipe (4 `UTCHMMA`, 1 `UTCBAR`), 2 barrier operations (2 `TRYWAIT`), 5 vector-datapath (2 `SHF`, 1 `LOP3`, 2 `PLOP3` predicate moves) and 3 branches; 5 + 2 + 5 + 3 + 32 = 47. Apart from the two `TRYWAIT`s (parity from the per-lane `R2`, result in the vector predicate `P0`) and the branches, the vector lanes of warp 0 issue at most those 5 instructions per k-tile (4 on the fast path: the `SHF` at 0x5210 sits in the skipped blocking wait): they are essentially idle. The CUTLASS kernel's loop (0x3890-0x3b40 in `sass_gemm.txt`) is 44 [M]. The +3 is `UMOV UR28/UR29` (hoisted out of the loop only in the CUTLASS kernel), `UMOV UR37, 0xf` (the CUTLASS kernel builds the mask at run time before the tile loop) and the `ULEA` that recomputes `empty[rs]`, minus one loop-counter instruction (note G.3). Two things to notice. The first iteration is **not peeled**: the C++ `tok` of explicit.cu:916 becomes `P0`, carried across the back-edge. And the peek at 0x5350 is predicated off on the last k-tile (`(k <= 0) ? 1u : mbar_try_wait(...)` at explicit.cu:927), giving exactly 1 + 127 = 128 peeks per tile (Chapter 9).

### 12.5.2 Producer warp 2: 37 instructions per k-tile (0x10b0-0x12f0), 33 on the fast path [M]

```
/*10b0*/               @P1 BRA 0x1100 ;                                  peek succeeded: skip the blocking wait
/*10c0*/                   ULEA UR4, UR28, UR7, 0x3 ;
/*10d0*/                   SHF.L.U32 R4, R0, 0x1f, RZ ;
/*10e0*/                   SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P1, [UR4+0x40], R4 ;      empty[s] = base + 64 + 8 s
/*10f0*/              @!P1 BRA 0x5c80 ;
/*1100*/                   UIADD3 UR4, UPT, UPT, UR28, 0x1, URZ ;                   s + 1
/*1110*/              @!P0 MOV R5, 0xc000 ;                                         49152 (leader lane only)
/*1120*/                   VOTEU.ALL UP1, P0 ;
/*1130*/                   USHF.L.U32 UR18, UR13, 0x6, URZ ;                        c0 = 64 q
/*1140*/                   UISETP.NE.U32.AND UP0, UPT, UR4, 0x8, UPT ;              wrap
/*1150*/              @!UP1 ULEA UR10, UR28, UR7, 0x3 ;                             full[s] (unmasked, local) for the expect_tx
/*1160*/                   USEL UR8, URZ, 0x1, UP0 ;
/*1170*/                   USEL UR4, UR4, URZ, UP0 ;
/*1180*/                   UIADD3 UR30, UP0, UPT, UR22, 0x80, URZ ;                 &params.tma_b = param base + 0x80 (low word)
/*1190*/                   LOP3.LUT R0, R0, UR8, RZ, 0x3c, !PT ;                    prod_phase ^= flip
/*11a0*/                   ULEA UR8, UR28, UR7, 0xd ;                               base + (s << 13)
/*11b0*/              @!P0 SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64 RZ, [UR10], R5 ;                    mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx full[s], 49152
/*11c0*/                   ULEA UR9, UR4, UR7, 0x3 ;                                empty[next] for the peek (UR4 = s + 1, wrapped at 0x1170)
/*11d0*/                   SHF.L.U32 R4, R0, 0x1f, RZ ;
/*11e0*/                   ULEA UR17, UR28, UR35, 0x3 ;                             masked full[s] = (base & 0xfefffff0) + 8 s
/*11f0*/                   ULEA UR16, UR28, UR24, 0xe ;                             A dst = (base + 0x8400 + 8192 y) + (s << 14)
/*1200*/                   UPRMT UR34, URZ, 0x5410, UR25 ;                          multicast mask (0x5 << x) into bits [16,32)
/*1210*/                   UIADD3 UR8, UPT, UPT, UR8, 0x28400, URZ ;                B dst = base + 0x28400 + (s << 13)
/*1220*/                   UIADD3.X UR31, UPT, UPT, URZ, UR23, URZ, UP0, !UPT ;     &params.tma_b high word
/*1230*/                   UMOV UR20, URZ ;                                         z coordinate = 0
/*1240*/                   UMOV UR32, 0x0 ;                                         cache hint low
/*1250*/                   UMOV UR33, 0x10000000 ;                                  cache hint high -> 0x1000000000000000
/*1260*/                   SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P1, [UR9+0x40], R4 ;      peek empty[next]
/*1270*/                   UMOV UR9, UR17 ;                                         B's barrier
/*1280*/                   UMOV UR10, UR18 ;                                        B's c0
/*1290*/                   UMOV UR12, UR20 ;                                        B's z
/*12a0*/                   UTMALDG.3D.MULTICAST.2CTA [UR16], [UR22], UR34, desc[UR32] ;   A
/*12b0*/                   UIADD3 UR13, UPT, UPT, UR13, 0x1, URZ ;                  ++q
/*12c0*/                   UMOV UR28, UR4 ;                                         prod_idx = s + 1 (wrapped)
/*12d0*/                   UISETP.NE.U32.AND UP0, UPT, UR13, UR39, UPT ;            q != end ?
/*12e0*/                   UTMALDG.3D.2CTA [UR8], [UR30], desc[UR32] ;              B
/*12f0*/                   BRA.U UP0, 0x10b0 ;
```

The issue order is the one the source dictates (explicit.cu:732-755): wait, `expect_tx`, advance, peek, A load, B load. The CUTLASS kernel's loop (0x1d60-0x1f40 in `sass_gemm.txt`) is 31 (28 fast path). Matching the two bodies instruction by instruction leaves 28 shared, 9 explicit-only and 3 baseline-only, net +6 [M]. The nine explicit-only instructions fall into three groups. (1) Five re-materialised invariants: `@!P0 MOV R5, 0xc000` (the baseline hoists `@P0 MOV R2, 0xc000` in front of each loop, 0x1a10 and 0x1cf0), `UIADD3 UR30` + `UIADD3.X UR31` (the `tma_b` address pair), `UPRMT UR34` (the mask insert) and `UMOV UR20, URZ` (z = 0). (2) The `VOTEU.ALL UP1, P0` and the `@!UP1 ULEA UR10` it predicates. (3) Two further `full[s]` address formations: `ULEA UR4` for the blocking wait and `ULEA UR17` for the masked TMA barrier. The baseline forms `full[s]` once (`ULEA UR17, UR4, UR29, 0x3` at 0x1d60, before its `@P1 BRA`, serving both the wait and the `expect_tx`) and masks it in place with `ULOP3.LUT UR17, UR17, 0xfefffff8` (0x1e80). The three baseline-only instructions are that `ULEA`, that `ULOP3`, and `UIADD3 UR16, UR16, 0x8400` (0x1e90), which the explicit kernel folds into the hoisted `UR24 = base + 0x8400 + 8192 y`. Note G.3 states the same net as "eight explicit-only in-loop instructions minus two baseline-only ones"; its eight and two are exactly the instructions it names, `@!UP1 ULEA UR10` and the baseline's unconditional `ULEA` included, so it implicitly pairs the wait-block `ULEA UR4` with the `0x8400` add, neither of which it mentions. The 8-k-tile prologue loop (0x0de0-0x1020) has the same 37, against the baseline's 32, with its own two `UTMALDG` at 0x0fc0/0x1000.

### 12.5.3 Scheduler warp 1 of CTA 0: 50 instructions per tile (0x1a20-0x1d30) [M]

The head is at 0x1a20 (target of `@P2 BRA 0x1a20` at 0x1d30), so the body is `(0x1d30 - 0x1a20) / 16 + 1 = 50`, the same count and structure as the CUTLASS kernel's CLC loop (0x2b60-0x2e70 in `sass_gemm.txt`); eight integer add/move slots are spelled differently (`IADD3`/`MOV`/`LEA` here against `VIADD`/`IMAD.U32`/`IMAD.MOV.U32`/`IMAD` there; note G.3 says the same). In order: throttle wait (`TRYWAIT [R5+URZ+0x130]`) and remote release (`PRMT R4, RZ, 0x654, R4; SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0 RZ, [R4+URZ], RZ`), CLC empty wait (`TRYWAIT P1, [UR6+0xe0], R6`), arming by lanes 0..3 (`@!P0 SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED RZ, [R11+URZ], R5`, `R5 = 0x10`), `UGETNEXTWORKID.BROADCAST [UR8], [UR9]`, response wait (`TRYWAIT P2, [R12+URZ+0xd0], R5`), `LDS.128`, `MEMBAR.ALL.CTA; FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S`, release to CTA 0, decode. The tail (0x1d40-0x1ed0) is the two `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64` test-waits with their blocking fallbacks; the warp exits through `@P0 EXIT` at 0x1e60 or 0x1ec0, and the `BRA 0x1e80` at 0x1ed0 is the second fallback's retry back-edge.

### 12.5.4 Epilogue warps 4-7: 674 per tile in the loop, 696 in the function [M]

The epilogue role spans 0x1f10 (`BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x6, 0xa0`, the `named_bar_sync(kBarTmemAlloc, ...)` of explicit.cu:997) to 0x4a80 (`EXIT`): 696 instructions, the number note G.3 reports "per tile". My recount splits it into three parts. The one-time entry 0x1f10-0x2050 is 21 instructions: the `LDCU.64` of alpha/beta and of the parameter base, the four `st_off` bases `R20..R23`, `T` from `[UR7+0x180]`, `UR17 = T + ((32 w) << 16)` (`ULEA UR17, UR16, UR17, 0x15` at 0x2050). The tile loop 0x2060-0x4a70 is 674 instructions (back-edge `BRA.U UP0, 0x2060` at 0x4a70). Then the `EXIT`. Inside the loop:

| Segment | Addresses | Instructions | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| per-tile setup | 0x2060-0x2280 | 35 | `clc_consume` (CLC wait, `LDS.128`, fence, release to CTA 0, decode to `tm/tn`), the `acc_full[st]` peek, the TMEM address `UR29 = T + ((32w) << 16) + 128 st` |
| subtile 0 | 0x2290-0x2750 | 77 | `LDTM.x16`, 16 `FMUL`, 16 `FFMA`, 16 `STS`, `MEMBAR.ALL.CTA + FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S`, `BAR.SYNC 0x1, 0x80`, the warp-4-only store block (`BRA.U UP1` around it, with `UP1 = (w != 0)` set once per tile at 0x22a0: `UIADD3`/`UMOV` bookkeeping for the four `{src, c0, c1, c2}` tuples, 4 `UTMASTG.3D`, `UTMACMDFLUSH`, `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x1`), `BAR.SYNC 0x1, 0x80` |
| subtiles 1-5 | 0x2760-0x3fb0 | 78 each | same content; the net one-instruction difference from subtile 0 is two more bookkeeping instructions (`UIADD3 UR10, UR22, 16 e` for `c1` and `UMOV UR9, UR21` for box 0's `c0`, values subtile 0 takes from `UR22`/`UR21` directly) minus the once-per-tile `UISETP.NE.U32.AND UP1` that only subtile 0 carries [M] |
| subtile 6 | 0x3fc0-0x44c0 | 81 | same, plus the `ULOP3 ... 0xfefffff8` and `UIADD3 ... 0x110` that build the masked `acc_empty[st]` address for subtile 7, and the `UIADD3 UR4, UR4, 0x1` of the accumulator state advance (`st + 1`, explicit.cu:1040) that ptxas scheduled here |
| subtile 7 | 0x44d0-0x4a70 | 91 | `LDTM.x16 R4, tmem[UR29+0x70]; NOP; SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0 RZ, [UR24], RZ` (the `tcgen05.wait::ld` + release of explicit.cu:1038-1039, the arrive waiting on the `LDTM` scoreboard), the arithmetic and stores, the accumulator state advance, `tm = tm_next` etc., the loop test |

The store block of subtile 0 (0x25f0-0x2740, verbatim) shows how warp 4 forms the four `{src, c0, c1, c2}` tuples that the `UTMASTG` operand blocks name:

```
        /*25f0*/                   UIADD3 UR36, UP2, UPT, UR30, 0x180, URZ ;
        /*2600*/                   UIADD3 UR20, UPT, UPT, UR7, 0x200, URZ ;
        /*2610*/                   UIADD3.X UR37, UPT, UPT, URZ, UR31, URZ, UP2, !UPT ;
        /*2620*/                   UIADD3 UR9, UPT, UPT, UR21, 0x20, URZ ;
        /*2630*/                   UIADD3 UR8, UPT, UPT, UR7, 0xa00, URZ ;
        /*2640*/                   UIADD3 UR13, UPT, UPT, UR21, 0x40, URZ ;
        /*2650*/                   UIADD3 UR12, UPT, UPT, UR7, 0x1200, URZ ;
        /*2660*/                   UIADD3 UR33, UPT, UPT, UR21, 0x60, URZ ;
        /*2670*/                   UIADD3 UR32, UPT, UPT, UR7, 0x1a00, URZ ;
        /*2680*/                   UMOV UR23, URZ ;
        /*2690*/                   UMOV UR10, UR22 ;
        /*26a0*/                   UMOV UR11, UR23 ;
        /*26b0*/                   UTMASTG.3D [UR20], [UR36] ;
        /*26c0*/                   UMOV UR14, UR22 ;
        /*26d0*/                   UMOV UR15, UR23 ;
        /*26e0*/                   UMOV UR34, UR22 ;
        /*26f0*/                   UMOV UR35, UR23 ;
        /*2700*/                   UTMASTG.3D [UR8], [UR36] ;
        /*2710*/                   UTMASTG.3D [UR12], [UR36] ;
        /*2720*/                   UTMASTG.3D [UR32], [UR36] ;
        /*2730*/                   UTMACMDFLUSH ;
        /*2740*/                   DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x1 ;
```

`UR30:UR31` is the parameter-block address (`LDCU.64 UR30, c[0x0][0x348]` at 0x1f50), so `UR36:UR37 = +0x180` is `&params.tma_d`. `UR7` is `smem_base`, so the four sources are `OFF_SMEM_CD + 2048 i` = `0x200, 0xa00, 0x1200, 0x1a00` (one 32-row x 16-column fp32 box is 2048 B). `UR21 = 128 tm` and `UR22 = 128 tn` are formed once per tile (`USHF.L.U32 UR21, UR21, 0x7` and `USHF.L.U32 UR22, UR29, 0x7` at 0x2120-0x2130). So `c0 = 128 tm + 32 i` is `UR21`, `UR9 = UR21 + 0x20`, `UR13 = UR21 + 0x40`, `UR33 = UR21 + 0x60`. `c1 = 128 tn + 16 e` is `UR22` for subtile 0, copied into `UR10`, `UR14`, `UR34` for boxes 1-3. `c2 = 0` is `UR23 = URZ`, copied into `UR11`, `UR15`, `UR35`. The tuples are thus `{UR20, UR21, UR22, UR23}`, `{UR8, UR9, UR10, UR11}`, `{UR12, UR13, UR14, UR15}`, `{UR32, UR33, UR34, UR35}` [H for the block reading, M for the arithmetic]. For subtile e only two values change. `c1` becomes `UR22 + 16 e` (subtile 1: `UIADD3 UR10, UR22, 0x10` at 0x2ac0, then `UMOV UR9, UR21` for box 0's `c0`). The sources move to the epilogue smem stage `0x200 + 0x2000 (e & 3) + 0x800 i` (subtile 1: `UR7 + 0x2200, 0x2a00, 0x3200, 0x3a00`). The D-map address keeps its value, but ptxas re-forms it per unrolled subtile, into `UR36` in subtile 0, `UR40` in subtiles 1-6 and `UR8` in subtile 7 (`UIADD3 UR40, UP2, UPT, UR30, 0x180` at 0x2ab0, so subtile 1 stores `UTMASTG.3D [UR8], [UR40]`). A reader comparing `[UR36]` in subtile 0 with `[UR40]` in subtile 1 is looking at the same 64-bit value in two registers, not at an error.

Per subtile both kernels have 1 `LDTM.x16`, 16 `FMUL`, 16 `FFMA`, 16 `STS`, 1 fence pair, 2 `BAR.SYNC`, 4 `UTMASTG`, 1 `UTMACMDFLUSH`, 1 `DEPBAR`. The CUTLASS kernel's 1265 per tile adds, per subtile, its 16 dead `LDS` of C behind a never-taken predicate, three `SYNCS` of the dead `epi_load` pipeline, an `R2UR`, a `NOP` and predicate bookkeeping, plus a 309-instruction setup (note G.3).

### 12.5.5 Why none of this is on the critical path [M for the inputs, H for the model]

The time budget per k-tile follows from the measured runtime (note D.4). A cluster on the critical path processes 32 tiles in 0.888 ms, so one tile takes at most 27.75 us and one k-tile 27.75 us / 128 = 216.8 ns = **426 cycles** at 1965 MHz. One 256 x 128 x 16 MMA therefore has 106.5 cycles. If the 1024 tiles were spread as the mean 31.03 per cluster, the figures would be 3.1 % larger (32 / 31.03 = 1.031): 28.6 us per tile, 439 cycles per k-tile, 109.8 cycles per MMA, the second figure note D.4 quotes.

Issue model: an SM has four sub-partitions, each with one warp scheduler (Nsight Compute Profiling Guide, Hardware Model). The guide's Scheduler Statistics section description says "From the set of eligible warps the scheduler selects a single warp from which to issue one or more instructions." I take **one instruction per cycle per scheduler** as the issue bound [H: the guide states no per-cycle rate; if more than one instruction can issue per cycle, the utilisation figures below are upper bounds]. Eight warps on four schedulers means two warps per scheduler; which two is `warp_id % 4` on the architectures I know, unverified for this chip.

| Warp | Instructions per k-tile (static, fast path) | Share of one scheduler's 426 slots |
|---|---|---|
| 0 (MMA, leader CTA) | 43 (47 minus the 4 skipped wait instructions) | 10.1 % |
| 2 (producer) | 33 | 7.7 % |
| 4-7 (epilogue), each | 674 per tile / 128 k-tiles = 5.3 | 1.2 % |
| 1 (scheduler, CTA 0 only) | 50 per tile / 128 = 0.4 | 0.1 % |
| 1 (ranks 1-3), 3 | exited | 0 |

Even if warps 0 and 4 share a scheduler, their combined demand is about 11 % of its issue capacity: the busiest scheduler is idle nine cycles out of ten. Moreover, the uniform-datapath instructions of warp 0 do not compete with the epilogue's `FMUL`/`FFMA`/`STS`, which use the vector pipes. The MMA warp could become the bottleneck only if the tensor core finished four MMAs in fewer than ~43 cycles, i.e. if the hardware were about ten times faster than it is. The loop length is irrelevant as long as the next k-tile's `UTCHMMA`s issue before the tensor core drains. The 8-stage ring and the peek-then-wait idiom (the `full[s]` wait almost always succeeds on the inline try) make that the common case. The same reasoning applies to the producer: 33 issue slots put 49152 bytes in flight per k-tile per pair, running up to 8 stages ahead (Chapter 8).

What **is** on the critical path is the dependency chain the loops encode: `full[s]` completion (TMA bytes landed) -> `UTCHMMA` issue -> tensor-core execution -> `UTCBAR` -> `empty[s]` -> next `UTMALDG` into stage s; and per tile `acc_full[st]` -> `LDTM` -> `STS` -> `UTMASTG` -> `acc_empty[st]`. Chapter 3 derives the speed-of-light bound of that chain; Section 12.7.5 lists the counters that measure where it actually waits.

### 12.6.1 Performance: five interleaved pairs [M]

`trace_out_v2/baseline.txt` and `timing_summary.txt` (five runs of the pristine toggle-off binary of the original example interleaved with five runs of the explicit binary, same day, same GPU, `nvidia-smi` sampling clocks every 100 ms):

| Run (interleaved order) | pristine `Avg runtime` (ms) | explicit `Avg runtime` (ms) | explicit / pristine |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.888653 | 0.889261 | 1.00068 |
| 2 | 0.890288 | 0.890307 | 1.00002 |
| 3 | 0.889411 | 0.888947 | 0.99948 |
| 4 | 0.889990 | 0.889517 | 0.99947 |
| 5 | 0.889917 | 0.889354 | 0.99937 |
| median | **0.889917** | **0.889354** | **0.99937** |
| mean / stdev | 0.889652 / 0.000641 | 0.889477 / 0.000508 | 0.99980 |
| min / max | 0.888653 / 0.890288 | 0.888947 / 0.890307 | |

- The 0.06 % advantage by medians lies inside the run-to-run spread ((max - min) / median: 0.15 % for the explicit binary, 0.18 % for the pristine one). It means nothing except "indistinguishable".
- `GFLOPS` is `2 m n k / Avg runtime` exactly (`Options::gflops`, 70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:256-262): 2 x 8192^3 = 1.0995 x 10^12 FLOP; / 0.889354 ms = 1.2363 x 10^15 FLOP/s, printed as `1.2363e+06`.
- Kernel-only time would need `nsys` (note, Section 12 item 2) and was not measured.
- Clocks: 101 of 101 steady-state samples at 1965 MHz SM / 3996 MHz memory; power 196.5-306.1 W (median 300.0 W) over those 101 samples; temperature 31-37 C over all 108. The seven earlier samples (three at 120 MHz, four at 787 MHz) are the idle ramp before the first kernel; the 188.6 W floor and 299.9 W median that the note quotes include them (my recount of `clocks.csv`). That the 9 ms timed loops themselves ran at 1965 MHz is inferred from the surrounding samples (note G.2 C1, D.4).

| `Disposition: Passed` in 1 toggle-on + 5 toggle-off runs | `verify()` runs the device reference GEMM with the same alpha/beta/C and compares all M x N outputs with `cutlass::reference::device::BlockCompareEqual` (70_blackwell_fp16_gemm.cu:351-378): **exact** equality, no tolerance | D is value-equal to the reference |
| sentinel fill | `trace_begin()` fills D with `0xFF` bytes before the traced launch (explicit.cu:1349: `cudaMemset(d_ptr, 0xFF, d_bytes)`), so any element never stored reads as NaN and fails `==` | every one of the 2^26 elements was written by the kernel; a tile skipped by a scheduling bug could not pass |

| no `TRACE_HANG` / `TRACE_HANG_HB` line | the 4 s bounded wait and the 20 s watchdog of the trace build never fired | no barrier wait blocked for 4 s or more, so no wait sat on a phase that never completed; a wait that passes too early (the other parity names the immediately preceding, already complete phase and returns true at once, PTX ISA `mbarrier.try_wait.parity`; a too-small arrival count completes the phase early) does not hang, and the tail records above and the exact-equality result, not this row, are the evidence against it |

### 12.6.3 CLC dynamics [M, with the inferences marked]

**Residency.** 33 clusters launched natively (launch-linear ids 0..32), equal to `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters` for this configuration (`max_active_clusters 33` in `host.txt`). 132 of 148 SMs host CTAs; SMs 64, 65, 122-129 and 142-147 stay idle for the whole launch (my recount of the `smid` column agrees with note D.3). The naive 148 / 4 = 37 is not reached.

Why 33 (note D.3; Section 2.1.1 adds the GPC skyline, NVIDIA internal information): every MMA pair sits on an SM pair `(2j, 2j + 1)`, a TPC, and both pairs of a cluster sit in the same SM-id group:

| Cluster ids | pair {0, 1} on SMs | pair {2, 3} on SMs |
|---|---|---|
| 0-7 | `2k`, `2k + 1` | `+16` |
| 8-15 | `2k + 16`, `2k + 17` | `+16` |
| 16-22 | `66 + 2(k - 16)`, `+1` | `+14` |
| 23-29 | `94 + 2(k - 23)`, `+1` | `+14` |
| 30-31 | `130 + 2(k - 30)`, `+1` | `+6` |
| 32 | 134, 135 | 140, 141 |

The inference (note D.3): a 2 x 2 cluster needs two whole TPCs inside one GPC, the groups above have an even number of usable TPCs, and the 8 leftover TPCs (16 SMs) cannot be paired, hence 33 and not 37. Chapter 2, Section 2.1.1 completes it with the GPC skyline, the number of TPCs enabled per GPC (NVIDIA internal): each odd-sized GPC idles one TPC, and this B200's skyline, 10/10/10/9/9/9/9/5/1/1/1 (NVIDIA internal), has eight odd-sized GPCs and idles exactly 8 TPCs = 16 SMs, the measured count, while the other B200 skyline, 10/10/9/9/9/9/9/9 (8 GPCs; also NVIDIA internal), with six odd-sized GPCs, would not (arithmetic there, with two cautions on SM-id groups and GPC membership). For a designer: the cluster shape costs 10.8 % of the machine before the first instruction runs, and the loss depends on the chip's skyline, not on the kernel. A (2,1,1) cluster or a non-clustered kernel would fill more SMs but lose the A multicast; Chapter 3 weighs this.

**Tiles per cluster.** 32 tiles for 13 clusters, 31 for 19, and 19 for cluster (0, 0), the probed cluster, slowed to 59.7 us per tile by its K3/K4 probes in the trace build (attribution inferred in the note; Section 3.8.1), 1.68x the 35.46 us of the other clusters (medians of the scheduler warp's K5a query-issue intervals in `trace_out_v2/launch0.csv`, a recount; 1.70x and 54.35 us in the CUTLASS kernel's trace, note D.3); sum 13 x 32 + 19 x 31 + 19 = 416 + 589 + 19 = 1024 (my recount). Dynamic scheduling absorbed the probe-induced slowness automatically: the slow cluster simply received fewer tiles. [H] The Release binary has no probed cluster. With 1024 tiles over 33 clusters (33 x 31 = 1023, one tile over) the expected split is 31 or 32 per cluster, faster clusters taking the extra tiles; a balanced hand-out forces one cluster with 32 tiles and thirty-two with 31 (32 + 32 x 31 = 1024; derived, not measured). The Release runs record only `Disposition`, `Problem Size`, `Avg runtime` and `GFLOPS`, so the split was not measured. Under that expectation the tail imbalance is at most one tile in 31, about 3 % of the runtime: the price of 256 x 256 cluster tiles on 33 clusters.

**Hand-out order** (CUTLASS kernel's trace, note D.3). The 991 cancelled ids are 33..1023, each exactly once. Within each cluster the successive ids are strictly increasing. Sorted by query issue time, the ids are ascending except 25 adjacent swaps among 990 pairs (933 of 991 at their sorted position). No id is displaced by more than 4. The count 25 holds with same-tick ties broken by ascending id: the 991 issue timestamps fall on 950 distinct 32 ns `%globaltimer` ticks, and other tie orderings give 32-62 inversions. The first hand-out was id 33 to cluster (0, 0), 1.28 us after the first query; the last was id 1023 at 959.2 us. With `AlongN` and no swizzle, id L is cluster tile `(L / 32, L % 32)`, so a cluster's successive tiles are about 33 ids apart: `m` advances by one per tile while `n` drifts. At any moment the 33 clusters work on two (834 of 991 hand-outs) or three (157) adjacent 256-row bands of A. That is good L2 behaviour obtained for free from the launch order.

**Query latency** (issue by the scheduler's elected lane to consumption by the same warp):

| Trace | min | p10 | median | p90 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUTLASS kernel (note D.3, 1024 queries) | 736 ns | 800 | 1408 | 1536 | 2336 |
| explicit kernel (my recount, 1024 queries) | 928 ns | 960 | 1024 | 1184 | 1408 |

The CUTLASS trace's p75 is 1472 ns and its p99 1792 ns; the distribution is bimodal by cluster placement (768-928 ns for 14 clusters, 1408-1504 ns for 19; the split repeats at the same SM offsets inside each group of the placement table, and note D.3 infers position inside the GPC as the cause); the 33 not-cancelled responses are not slower (median 1376, max 1504 ns); and the MMA warp's consume record K5c of rank 0 follows the scheduler warp's K5b by 96 ns median, the only measured datum on the MMA warp's wait on `clc_full`, and an indirect one: both records follow their warp's wait, so the 96 ns dates the MMA warp's consume relative to the scheduler's, not the wait's duration (all note D.3; Chapter 7, Section 7.6.9 builds on it). The difference between the rows is probe placement in the scheduler warp, not hardware (note G.2's explanation, "Trace build, for the record only"). Either way the latency is irrelevant. In the CUTLASS kernel's trace the throttle gap between consuming response n and issuing query n + 1 is 28.8-37.7 us (median 30.8 us over the 32 unprobed clusters; cluster (0, 0) is excluded, note D.3); with its 1.41 us median latency a query is in flight 4.6 % of the time. In the explicit kernel's trace the gap is 33.7-41.0 us (median 34.4 us over the 973 consume-to-issue pairs of the 32 unprobed clusters, my recount) against a 1.02 us median: about 3 %. Per-tile time is median 31.90 us in the CUTLASS kernel's trace (note D.3; the trace build runs with probes on and 108/72 registers) and 35.46 us in the explicit kernel's trace (note G.2, which drops the first interval of each cluster and on that basis gives 31.84 us for the CUTLASS trace; the explicit figure is 35.46 us on either basis, a recount), against 0.889 ms / 32 tiles = 27.8 us per tile in the Release build (at most 27.75 us: note D.4's 0.888 ms over the 32 tiles of a critical-path cluster; the explicit kernel's 0.889354 ms gives 27.8 us). Never more than one query is outstanding per cluster, at most 25 GPU-wide (note D.3).

A designer takes three lessons. The CLC round trip is about 1 us, so one query per tile (about 28 us) hides it completely, and a CLC pipeline deeper than 2 slots would buy nothing. The throttle (Chapter 7) is what keeps "one outstanding query per cluster" true. And the exactly-once coverage of 1024 tiles must be verified by a checker, because no run-time assertion exists for it.

---

## 12.7 How to reproduce and inspect

### 12.7.1 The full-speed run (note Section 0, Part H.1)

```
./build/examples/70_blackwell_gemm/70_blackwell_fp16_gemm --m=8192 --n=8192 --k=8192
```

Expected: `Disposition: Passed`, `Problem Size: 8192x8192x8192`, `Avg runtime: 0.889 ms` (0.888-0.891 on the B200 at 1965 MHz), `GFLOPS: 1.236e+06` (1.235e+06-1.237e+06 over the five explicit runs; the harness prints both values with six significant digits, e.g. `Avg runtime: 0.889354 ms` and `GFLOPS: 1.2363e+06`).

### 12.7.2 Dumping the binary yourself (note H.2.2)

```
BIN=./build/examples/70_blackwell_gemm/70_blackwell_fp16_gemm
cuobjdump --dump-sass "$BIN" > sass.txt
cuobjdump --dump-ptx  "$BIN" > ptx.txt
cuobjdump --dump-resource-usage "$BIN"
cuobjdump --list-elf "$BIN"            # two sm_100a cubins expected, one per translation unit
awk '/^Fatbin /{p=0} /Function :/{p=index($0, "explicit_blackwell_fp16_gemm_kernel") > 0} p' sass.txt > sass_explicit.txt
awk '/^Fatbin /{p=0} /^\.visible \.entry|^\.entry/{p=index($0, "explicit_blackwell_fp16_gemm_kernel") > 0} p' ptx.txt > ptx_explicit.txt
```

`--dump-sass` "dumps CUDA assembly for a single cubin file or all cubin files embedded in the binary", `--dump-resource-usage` "dumps resource usage for each ELF", `--list-elf` "lists all the ELF files available in the fatbin" (CUDA Binary Utilities manual). The `awk` cut works because `cuobjdump` prints one `Function : <mangled name>` header per kernel and a `Fatbin ...` header per embedded image.

### 12.7.3 The checklist: what to grep for [M]

The executed-path inventory you should see, with the counts I recounted:

| Family | Expected in the explicit kernel | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `UTCHMMA.2CTA` | 4 | the four k-blocks |
| `UTCBAR.2CTA.MULTICAST` | 2 | mainloop release, accumulator commit |
| `UTMALDG.3D.MULTICAST.2CTA` / `UTMALDG.3D.2CTA` / plain `UTMALDG.3D` | 2 / 2 / 0 | one A and one B per rolled producer loop; no C load |
| `UTMASTG.3D` / `UTMACMDFLUSH` / `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x1` / `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x0` | 32 / 8 / 8 / 0 | 4 boxes x 8 subtiles; no `store_tail` |
| `LDTM.x16` | 8 | |
| `UGETNEXTWORKID.BROADCAST` | 1 | the CLC query (grep for this, not for "CLC") |
| `ACQBULK` / `PREEXIT` | 2 / 1 | GDC |
| `UTMACCTL.PF` | 4 | A, B, C, D prefetch |
| `UTCATOMSWS.2CTA.FIND_AND_SET` / `UTCATOMSWS.AND` | 2 / 1 | alloc (+ retry copy), dealloc |
| `SYNCS.EXCH.64` | 33 | the 33 `mbarrier.init` |
| `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT` / `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64` without `.TRYWAIT` / `NANOSLEEP` | 65 / 32 / 31 | ptxas's retry structure; not a contract |
| `SYNCS.ARRIVE*` | 14 | 9 remote `.RED.A1T0`, 2 `.RED` (expect_tx remote and alloc handshake), 1 `.A1T0`, 2 plain (expect_tx local) |
| `BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x1, 0x80` / `0x6, 0xa0` / `BAR.ARV 0x6, 0xa0` | 16 / 1 / 1 | plus one `BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING 0x0`, the non-cluster fallback |
| `FMUL` / `FFMA` / `FADD` | 130 / 128 / 0 | 128 + the two of the `%cluster_ctaid` lowering (attribution inferred, note D.2) |
| `STS` / `LDS` | 131 / 11 | 128 + 3 bookkeeping; 4 `LDS.128` + 7 reserved/tmem_base reads |
| `LDL` / `STL` / `MOV.SPILL` / `R2UR.FILL` | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 | |
| `ELECT` | 4 | none between the `UTCHMMA`s |
| `0xfefffff8` / `UPRMT ..., 0x5410` / `PRMT` or `UPRMT ..., 0x654` | 1 / 2 / 11 | peer mask, mask insert, `mapa` lowering |
| `UMOV URn, 0x40004040` | 8 | the descriptor high words, all in the MMA loop |
| resources | `REG` 26 (<= 68), `STACK` 0, `LOCAL` 0, `SHARED` 1024, `CONSTANT[0]` 1536 | |

### 12.7.4 Reading a SASS line [M, H for the operand-block reading]

```
        /*5220*/                   SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P0, [UR4], R2 ;
        ^addr   ^predicate slot (empty = always; "@!P0" = if not P0; "@UP2" = uniform predicate)
                                   ^mnemonic.modifiers           ^dst   ^address  ^source
```

- `SYNCS.*`: the barrier unit. `TRANS64` = the instruction operates on a 64-bit transaction-barrier state in shared memory, which tracks an arrival count and a transaction count and advances its phase only when both are satisfied (64 is the width of the barrier state, not a thread count); `PHASECHK.TRANS64` = tests that phase; `.TRYWAIT` = the initial non-blocking probe of the same phase, not equivalent to the bare form: on a miss the standard sequence backs off with `NANOSLEEP` and then uses the bare `PHASECHK.TRANS64` as the retry-path blocking check before branching back (NVIDIA internal; the measured loop, whose `NANOSLEEP.SYNCS 0x989680` immediate is the `timeHint` value of PTX `try_wait`, is in Section 12.2.2); `EXCH.64` = atomic exchange (read the old word, write the supplied one, return the old; the uniform form uses uniform-register addressing and data), the lowering of `mbarrier.init`; `ARRIVE.TRANS64[.RED][.A1T0|.A0TR]` = arrive or transaction-count update (`.RED` = reduction-style arrive, required for a remote peer-CTA target and also valid locally, with the destination writeback suppressed; `A1T0` = arrival +1, transaction delta 0; `A0TR` = no arrival, transaction count updated from the source register `Rb` (NVIDIA internal); measured: the baseline's 8 bare `mbarrier.expect_tx` sites lower to `.RED.A0TR` with the byte count in the source register (`R3 = 0x2000`; not executed for beta = 0, note D.2; none in the explicit kernel), issued after the epilogue's TMA copy so the bytes may land first (Sections 2.8.2 and 14.2.4); how the update changes the transaction count (its sign, and whether it is the expect-side or the completion-side update) is unresolved, because no supporting material is available; without either suffix the source register carries the transaction count, as in the `expect_tx` with `R5 = 0xc000`) (the suffix definitions are NVIDIA internal information that no public document gives; the reading of the source register without a suffix is inferred from note D.2's PTX-to-SASS mapping [H]).
- `UTC*`: the Tensor Core (TC) pipe, which the Profiling Guide says "is different from the Tensor pipeline" (the two pipes' metrics: Section 12.7.5): `UTCHMMA` = the MMA, `UTCBAR` = the commit, `UTCATOMSWS` = the TMEM allocator atomics. The Nsight Compute Profiling Guide: "The TC pipeline executes UTCBAR, UTCCP, UTC*MMA, UTCSHIFT and UTC*SWS instructions"; `UTCCP` (`tcgen05.cp`) and `UTCSHIFT` (`tcgen05.shift`) do not occur in this kernel.
- `UTMA*`: the TMA unit: `UTMALDG` load global-to-shared, `UTMASTG` store shared-to-global, `UTMACMDFLUSH` commit group, `UTMACCTL.PF` descriptor prefetch. The operand in the first bracket names the first register of a block of consecutive uniform registers (`{dst, mbarrier, c0, c1, c2}` for a load, `{src, c0, c1, c2}` for a store); the second bracket is the 64-bit tensormap pointer; `desc[URn]` is the 64-bit cache-hint descriptor [H].
- `LDTM.x16 R4, tmem[UR29+0x70]`: a TMEM load of 16 x 32-bit per lane from the lane group and column in `UR29` plus the immediate column offset.
- `UR`, `UP`, `URZ`, `UPT`, `RZ`, `PT`: uniform register, uniform predicate; `RZ`/`URZ` are the constant zero of the per-lane (`Rn`) and uniform (`URn`) register files (`URZ` is a separate register, not one of Blackwell's 80 addressable `UR0`-`UR79`), `PT`/`UPT` the always-true predicate of the per-lane (`Pn`) and uniform (`UPn`) predicate files, and any of the four used as a destination discards the write (NVIDIA internal). The CUDA Binary Utilities manual names the `RX`/`URX`/`PX`/`UPX` register classes but does not define these four.
- The trailing `/* 0x... */` comments (stripped above) are the 128-bit encoding, including the control fields of Section 12.1.3. Those fields are where `tcgen05.wait::ld` went. Decoding them needs third-party tools and is not needed for this course.

### 12.7.5 Attributing the remaining gap to the speed of light [S for the metric definitions, H for the numbers]

The measured 1.2363 x 10^15 FLOP/s is 4.25 kFLOP per cycle per SM over 148 SMs at 1965 MHz, 4.77 k over the 132 active SMs (runtime from note G.2, the 132 active SMs from note D.3; note D.4 derives the same two figures for its 1.237e15). The vendor's dense FP16/BF16 Tensor Core figure for the 1000 W B200 is 2.25 PFLOPS (Lenovo ThinkSystem product guide for the HGX B200 180 GB 1000 W GPU, "2.25 / 4.5 petaFLOPS" without/with sparsity). The ratio is 55 %, but the datasheet conditions are not this run's: the measured power was about 300 W at 1965 MHz, and the datasheet's clock is unknown. If the 2.25 PFLOPS corresponds to 8192 dense FP16 FLOP/cycle/SM, the implied clock is 1.856 GHz, and a 256 x 128 x 16 pair-MMA would take 64 cycles against the 106.5-cycle upper bound derived from the measured 0.888 ms runtime (note D.4; Section 12.5.5) [H]. Chapter 3 derives the bound from first principles; this section gives you the `ncu` metrics that settle it.

Three practicalities first. (a) "Speed Of Light" in `ncu` is the `GPU Speed Of Light Throughput` section: "For each unit, the throughput reports the achieved percentage of utilization with respect to the theoretical maximum" (Profiling Guide), the busiest unit's share of its peak sustained rate, the same notion Chapter 3 applies analytically. (b) `--launch-skip 1 --launch-count 1` count only launches that match `--kernel-name` ("The number takes into account only launches that match the kernel filters"; "The count is only incremented for launches that match the kernel filters", Nsight Compute CLI manual). So `ncu` skips launch 0 of the explicit kernel, the harness's warm-up, and profiles its first timed launch; it does not count the reference GEMM and the compare kernels. (c) `ncu` locks the GPU clocks while profiling ("Nsight Compute locks SM clocks by default", Profiling Guide, Range and Precision, "Workload Durations"). `--clock-control base` locks GPC and memory clocks to the base frequency; the current CLI manual (v2026.3.1) documents `boost` as the default with a fallback to `base` where boost locking is unsupported (older releases documented `base` as the default; unverified here). Either way the clock can differ from the 1965 MHz of the timing runs. Cycle-based figures will therefore not line up with the 426-cycle budget of Section 12.5.5 unless you pass `--clock-control none` and confirm the clock from `sm__cycles_elapsed` against `gpu__time_duration`; the guide's recommendation for comparisons with unlocked measurements is to lock the clocks externally with `nvidia-smi` and use `--clock-control none`. Profile one timed launch:

```
ncu --kernel-name regex:explicit_blackwell --launch-skip 1 --launch-count 1 \
    --section SpeedOfLight --section ComputeWorkloadAnalysis --section WarpStateStats --section MemoryWorkloadAnalysis \
    ./build/examples/70_blackwell_gemm/70_blackwell_fp16_gemm --m=8192 --n=8192 --k=8192
```

and read, in this order:

| Question | Metric or section | What a designer concludes |
|---|---|---|
| Is the tensor pipe busy? | `sm__pipe_tc_cycles_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed` (the broader tcgen05 TC pipe: the MMA math plus `UTCCP`, `UTCBAR` and the TMEM allocation atomics, NVIDIA internal) and, distinct from it, `sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_active` (the UMMA math, the tensor pipe, NVIDIA internal); among the other `sm__pipe_tensor_*` metrics, `sm__pipe_tensor_op_hmma_cycles_active` is a tensor-pipe-active metric to request for utilisation, not by itself proof that `UTCHMMA` incremented it (NVIDIA internal); opcode/mode proof is the counter ending `...op_utchmma_utcqmma_utcomma_scope_{1cta,2cta}.sum` (NVIDIA internal; the `2cta` form is the one to request for this kernel's `cta_group::2`, my reading; take the elided prefix from the installed version's `ncu --query-metrics`); on the TC/tensor distinction, NVIDIA staff on the developer forum (thread 355164) state that "A tcgen05 instruction will result in both sm__pipe_tc_cycles_active (singleton per SM) and sm[sp]__pipe_tensor_cycles_active (per SMSP) counters being updated" and that "The TC unit is also responsible for some of the other tcgen05 (not .mma) instructions so activity of TC could exceed Tensor Cycles Active"; the Profiling Guide itself only lists the TC pipe's instructions and says it "is different from the Tensor pipeline" | if the tensor-pipe metric is near 100 % on the active SMs, the kernel is at the tensor-core speed of light for its clock and the only lever left is the 16 idle SMs and the tail |
| Are the 16 idle SMs visible? | `sm__cycles_active.avg` vs `.max` and `sm__cycles_elapsed`; the `LaunchStats` section (cluster size, waves) | a 10.8 % gap between average and maximum active cycles is the cluster-packing loss, not a kernel bug |
| Where do warps wait? | `WarpStateStats`: `smsp__average_warp_latency_issue_stalled_*` (barrier, long scoreboard, wait, membar, ...; in an examined SM100 warp-specialised GEMM the mbarrier `TRYWAIT` wait path is sampled as `long scoreboard` (the `_long_scoreboard` suffix of this metric family), a wait-path attribution rather than proof that the `TRYWAIT` itself is the cause, NVIDIA internal, Section 3.5.1; the `NANOSLEEP` retries as `sleeping`, Profiling Guide) | a leader warp 0 stalled on the `full[s]` barrier means TMA is late (L2/DRAM bound or multicast imbalance); epilogue warps stalled on `acc_full` means the mainloop is the limiter, as designed |
| Is the issue rate anywhere near the limit? | `smsp__issue_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_active`, `smsp__inst_executed.sum` | Section 12.5.5 predicts under 15 % on the busiest sub-partition |
| How much traffic? | `lts__t_bytes.sum` (L2 slice tag-stage bytes per the Profiling Guide; not DRAM bytes and not necessarily payload bytes, NVIDIA internal information; Section 3.9.4), the TMA byte family `lts__t_bytes_equiv_l1sectormiss_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_tma*` (an L2 tag-stage request/sector metric: its expected value is the L2-side traffic, which falls with the unique request traffic under multicast; request the `.sum` form the installed version offers; NVIDIA internal), `l1tex__m_xbar2l1tex_read_bytes_mem_global_op_tma_ld.sum` (bytes delivered into shared memory, unchanged by multicast since every receiving CTA still gets a full tile, so do not infer multicast from this aggregate; for the multicast split compare the `..._dest_multicast.sum` and `..._dest_self.sum` counters, and read `lts__t_sectors_srcunit_tex_op_read.sum` for the L2 read-pressure reduction; NVIDIA internal; Section 3.9.3), `smsp__inst_executed_op_tma_ld.sum` (TMA-load instruction count, not bytes, NVIDIA internal; 2 per CTA per k-tile here, W21 and W22), `dram__bytes.sum`, `dram__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed` | the operands need 8 GiB of L2-to-SM traffic (1024 cluster tiles x 128 k-tiles x 64 KiB: 32 KiB of A delivered by multicast and 32 KiB of B per cluster per k-tile) in 0.889 ms = about 9.7 TB/s from L2 [H] (the `lts__t` TMA family is expected to track that L2-side 8 GiB, while the landed-byte metric `l1tex__m_xbar2l1tex_read_bytes_mem_global_op_tma_ld.sum` is expected to read 12 GiB, 4096 CTAs x 128 k-tiles x 24576 B, Section 3.9.3, with or without multicast; NVIDIA internal), but only 128 + 128 MiB of unique A and B plus 256 MiB of D from/to DRAM if L2 reuse is perfect (0.6 TB/s against 7.7 TB/s HBM3e); the measured `dram__bytes` tells you how far from perfect |
| Kernel-only time without the host encodes | `nsys profile --stats=true` on the same command, or `gpu__time_duration.sum` in `ncu` | separates the 23 host API calls per iteration from the kernel |

Metric names other than those quoted from the Profiling Guide or supplied as NVIDIA internal information (`lts__t_bytes.sum`, the TMA byte family `lts__t_bytes_equiv_l1sectormiss_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_tma*`, whose available `.sum` form must be requested on the installed Nsight Compute, `smsp__inst_executed_op_tma_ld.sum`, `l1tex__m_xbar2l1tex_read_bytes_mem_global_op_tma_ld.sum` and the `..._dest_multicast.sum` and `..._dest_self.sum` counters, `lts__t_sectors_srcunit_tex_op_read.sum`, `sm__pipe_tensor_op_hmma_cycles_active`, `sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_active`, the opcode/mode counter ending `...op_utchmma_utcqmma_utcomma_scope_{1cta,2cta}.sum` (prefix elided; take the full name from `ncu --query-metrics`), and the bank-conflict and shared-memory wavefront counters of Section 3.9.3) follow its `unit__(subunit?)_(pipestage?)_quantity_(qualifiers?)` convention and should be checked with `ncu --query-metrics` on the installed version (unverified for CUDA 13.3's Nsight Compute).

## 12.8 Lessons: what "performance-equivalent" required, and what was free

### 12.8.1 Required (the structural contract) [S, M]

| Requirement | Where the explicit kernel does it | Where CUTLASS does it | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rolled k-tile loops in the producer and the MMA warp | `#pragma unroll 1` at explicit.cu:733 and :921 | `CUTLASS_PRAGMA_NO_UNROLL` at sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp:607 and :680 | a full unroll is impossible (run-time trip count; Section 13.3, pitfall 18) and a partial unroll would only lengthen the straight-line body, toward 128 x 47 instructions in the limit, with likely instruction-cache misses (my analysis: the instruction-cache size is undocumented and no unrolled variant was measured) and no gain, because the loop is not issue-bound (Section 12.5.5) |
| Unrolled k-blocks | `#pragma unroll` at explicit.cu:930 | `CUTLASS_PRAGMA_UNROLL` at :699 | lets ptxas hard-wire `scale_c` to `UPT` for k-blocks 1..3 and issue the four `UTCHMMA` in one straight-line run (0x5410-0x5470, separated only by three `UMOV`s) |
| Fully unrolled epilogue subtiles | `#pragma unroll` at explicit.cu:1032 | `#pragma unroll(UnrollEpiLoop ? NumEpiSubtilesN : 1)` at sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:818 | the `16 e` term becomes the `LDTM` immediate, the `8192 (e & 3)` the `STS` immediate, the store coordinates compile-time offsets; the single `tcgen05.wait::ld` and release land in subtile 7 by construction |
| Warp-uniform issue operands | every TMA/MMA/commit/query operand from rank, tile, stage, constants | same | otherwise no `U*` lowering, vector address arithmetic and `R2UR` traffic in the loops (Section 12.3) |
| The same barrier protocol: counts, parities, masks, peer-bit addressing, peek-then-wait, four exit tails | Chapters 4, 7-11 | the CUTLASS headers cited inline in Chapter 4 | the protocol **is** the pipeline; a different count or an extra wait changes the overlap, and a missing tail is a use-after-exit hazard |
| Run-time alpha and beta, `t = alpha * acc; d = fmaf(beta, 0, t)` | explicit.cu:1045-1046, `ld.param +528` | the fusion tree's `FMUL`/`FFMA` | bit-identical D including the sign of zero; constant 1.0f/0.0f would fold the pair away, leaving at most an `FADD` (note D.7, inferred) |
| TMA issue order wait -> expect_tx -> peek -> A -> B; MMA order wait -> 4 MMAs -> commit; store order fence -> bar.sync -> 4 stores -> commit_group -> wait_group.read 1 -> bar.sync | Sections 12.5.1-12.5.4 | same | the order is what hides latency: the peek is issued before the loads so that the next iteration's wait is usually satisfied |

### 12.8.2 Free to change (and changed) [M]

| Changed | Explicit | CUTLASS | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vector registers | 26 | 68 | none (1 CTA/SM) |
| Parameter block | 640 B, `CONSTANT[0]` 1536 | 2048 B, 2944 | none |
| Role dispatch | `BRXU` jump table (`CONSTANT[2]:12`) | compare-and-branch chain | once per thread; same cost class |
| Barrier inits | 33 (`epi_load`, `load_order` omitted) | 43 | 10 fewer `SYNCS.EXCH.64` in the prologue |
| Prologue length | 175 instructions to the dispatch | 359 | one `SHFL.IDX` instead of 7, four `ULOP3` for the initial tile instead of the rasterisation arithmetic |
| Dead C path | absent | compiled, never executed (32 `UTMALDG.3D`, 128 `LDS`, 8 `expect_tx`, `DEPBAR.LE SB0, 0x0`, a third `ACQBULK`) | SASS 1640 vs 3224 instructions |
| Loop-invariant handling | some re-materialised per k-tile (`UMOV`s, mask insert, `tma_b` address) | hoisted, at the inferred price (note D.2, D.7) of 44 uniform-to-vector spill/fill pairs elsewhere, none in the hot loops | +3 / +6 instructions per k-tile, invisible |
| `k_tiles` | kept in `UR14` | re-read from `c[0x0][0x38c]` per tile | the accumulator acquire/commit block is 15 vs 18 instructions |
| CLC z coordinate | constant 0 (L = 1 kernel by construction; the host guard rejects `l != 1`) | bound to the response's `L_idx` | an L > 1 kernel would restore it |
| Multicast masks | `0x5 << x` and `0xf` from constants | computed from the cluster shape at run time | same values |
| The `elect.sync` count in PTX | 14 | 19 | both become 4-5 `ELECT` in SASS |
