For a K-major swizzled layout the ISA says the leading-dimension stride is "not used, assumed to be 1" and its example table gives "Encoding of LBO in descriptor: 1 (assumed)" (PTX ISA 9.4 section 9.7.18.3.1.1 "Relative offset mode" and the example table of section 9.7.18.3.3 "Canonical Layouts"; field position bits 16-30 in Table 49, section 9.7.18.4.1). CUTLASS fixes it to 1 for every swizzled K-major canonical layout (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp:822-832`: `static_assert(stride_10 == expected_stride_10)` with `expected_stride_10 = 1`, then `desc.leading_byte_offset_ = stride_10`). Bits [32,46): stride byte offset = 64 (1024 B, the distance between consecutive 8-row groups of a 128-byte-row SW128 atom). Bits [46,48): version = 1. Bits [61,64): layout type = 2 = SWIZZLE_128B. High word: `64 | (1 << 14) | (2 << 29)` = 0x40004040 (`static_assert` at `explicit.cu:175`). Instruction descriptor (`mma_sm100_desc.hpp:416-443` [S]): bits [4,6) c_format = 1 (F32) -> 0x10; a/b formats 0 (F16); a/b major 0 (K-major); [17,23) n_dim = 128 >> 3 = 16 -> 0x200000; [24,29) m_dim = 256 >> 4 = 16 -> 0x10000000; total 0x10200010 (`static_assert` at `explicit.cu:176`). Measured first-MMA values `desc_a = 0x4000404000010880`, `desc_b = 0x4000404000012880`, `idesc = 0x10200010` [M, D.1 D7].
</details>

**R11. A colleague runs `cuobjdump --dump-sass` on the whole binary and reports "it has 40 `UTMALDG` and 151 `LDS`, the explicit kernel is bloated". What went wrong, and what are the right numbers?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

They counted the whole binary, which still contains the never-launched CUTLASS kernel (the unchanged `gemm.initialize()` odr-uses it): 40 = 36 + 4 and 151 = 140 + 11 (my recount of `trace_out_v2/sass.txt`, `sass_gemm.txt`, `sass_explicit.txt`). Of the CUTLASS kernel's 36 `UTMALDG`, 32 are the plain `UTMALDG.3D` of its compiled-but-dead C path; the other 4 are its own A/B pairs in the prologue and main loops. Of its 140 `LDS`, 128 are the dead C reads. Cut the explicit kernel out by its `Function :` header (the `awk` in Section 12.7.2): 2 `UTMALDG.3D.MULTICAST.2CTA` + 2 `UTMALDG.3D.2CTA`, 11 `LDS` (4 `LDS.128` CLC decodes + 7 reads of `tmem_base_ptr` and the reserved alloc words), 1640 instructions in total against the CUTLASS kernel's 3224.
</details>

### 14.2.2 DERIVE

**D1. Compute `desc_a` and `desc_b` for rank 2, stage s = 5, k-block kb = 3.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

Formulas [S], `explicit.cu:896-897` (quoted in Section 9.4.4), `928-929`, `933-934` (quoted in Section 9.5).

Rank 2: `smem_base = 0x02000400`. A: `0x02000400 + 33792 = 0x02008800`; `>> 4` = 0x200880; `& 0x3FFF` = 0x0880 (the rank bits fall out of the 14-bit field); `| 0x10000` = 0x10880. Stage 5: + 5 x 1024 = 0x11C80; kb 3: + 6 = 0x11C86. **`desc_a = 0x4000404000011C86`**. B: `0x02000400 + 164864 = 0x02028800`; `>> 4 & 0x3FFF` = 0x2880; `| 0x10000` = 0x12880; + 5 x 512 = 0x13280; + 6 = 0x13286. **`desc_b = 0x4000404000013286`**. Cross-check against the file's own example (`explicit.cu:170`): rank 0, s = 3, kb = 2 gives 0x10880 + 3072 + 4 = 0x11484 and 0x12880 + 1536 + 4 = 0x12E84, matching `0x4000404000011484` / `0x4000404000012E84`. Rank 2's descriptors equal rank 0's for the same (s, kb) [M, D.1 D7: rank 0 and rank 2 identical], as the 2SM MMA requires: it reads the peer's halves at the same CTA-relative addresses. The largest low word is `0x10880 + 7 x 1024 + 6 = 0x12486` (A) and `0x12880 + 7 x 512 + 6 = 0x13686` (B). The two adds are plain 32-bit additions into a word whose bits [0,14) are the start-address field, [14,16) are unused (bit 15 is reserved in the ISA; Section 5.8.1) and [16,30) hold LBO = 1. A carry out of the field would corrupt bits [14,16) or LBO, so the construction is legal only because the field cannot overflow: the largest field value is `0x13686 & 0x3FFF = 0x3686 < 0x3FFF`, so no carry is ever generated. The `static_assert` at `explicit.cu:165` (`kSmemBaseLow24 + kSmemBytes < (1u << 18)`) is that guarantee for the whole buffer: `0x400 + 230400 = 0x38800 < 2^18` bytes, so every 16-byte-unit address inside the dynamic smem fits the 14-bit field. The `& 0x3FFF` at `:896-897` strips the rank bits [24,26) of `smem_base` (and everything above bit 17), so the per-stage add starts from a rank-independent word.
</details>

**D2. Which barrier address and parity does warp 2 wait on for q = 20 of its 4th tile (tile counter t = 3), and which does the MMA warp wait on for the same k-tile?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] The producer state is carried across tiles (`explicit.cu:724`), and 128 k-tiles per tile is a multiple of 8, so the global use count is `n = 128 t + q = 404`. Stage `s = n % 8 = 4`; earlier uses of stage 4: `n / 8 = 50`; producer parity = `1 ^ (50 & 1) = 1` (Section 4.2.3). Address: `empty_base + 8 s = smem_base + OFF_MAIN_EMPTY + 32 = smem_base + 96`, i.e. `0x00000460` for rank 0, `0x01000460` for rank 1, `0x02000460` for rank 2, `0x03000460` for rank 3. Each CTA waits on its own empty barrier; the two leaders' commits with mask 0xF complete all four. In the code the wait is the peek `mbar_try_wait(empty_base + 8u * st.prod_idx, st.prod_phase)` issued one k-tile earlier (`explicit.cu:739`), plus the blocking `EXPLICIT_WAIT` on the same operands only if the peek failed (`explicit.cu:735`). Meaning: parity 1 succeeds once phase 49 (the 50th completion, the release of use 49 = q = 12 of this tile) is done, i.e. once both leaders' MMAs that read stage 4 for q = 12 have completed (each leader's `tcgen05.commit` arrives then, not when issued; Section 4.2.2).

The leader's MMA warp waits `full[4]` at `smem_base + 32` with consumer parity `50 & 1 = 0`: phase 50 must complete, i.e. the 51st fill (this k-tile's six boxes plus the leader lane's `expect_tx`) must have landed. The blocking wait is `explicit.cu:923` (`if (!tok) { EXPLICIT_WAIT(full_base + 8u * cons_idx, cons_phase, WAIT_MAINLOOP_FULL, ...) }`). It is normally satisfied in advance by the peek at `:916` (first k-tile of the tile) or `:927` (every later k-tile); `:924` captures the stage index as `rs`.
</details>

**D3. For the cluster tile that contains CTA tile (12, 7), at q = 100, give every rank's TMA coordinates, destinations, multicast mask and barrier operand.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

CTA tile (12, 7) belongs to one specific CTA, because `tm % 2 == x` and `tn % 2 == y` for every tile a CTA receives (the `explicit.cu:777` comment states the first; Section 8.5.4 proves both from `explicit.cu:1175-1176` and `:692-693`). So (12, 7) is computed by the CTA with x = 0, y = 1 (rank 2) of the cluster working on cluster tile (6, 3). The four CTAs of that cluster hold (12 + x, 6 + y). Formulas [S], `explicit.cu:777-778`, `768` (quoted in Section 8.6), `747-748`, `754-755` (quoted in Section 8.4).

`c0 = 64 x 100 = 6400`; stage `s = 100 % 8 = 4` (tile starts are stage-aligned); A destination offset `33792 + 16384 x 4 + 8192 y = 99328 + 8192 y`; B destination offset `164864 + 8192 x 4 = 197632`; barrier `(smem_base + 8 x 4) & 0xFEFFFFFF`.

| rank (x,y) | CTA tile | A box (k, row, 0) = rows | lands at offset, in ranks (addresses) | mask | B box (k, col, 0) = cols | B at | barrier |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 (0,0) | (12,6) | (6400, 1536, 0) = 1536..1599 | 99328 in ranks 0, 2 (0x00018800, 0x02018800) | 0x5 | (6400, 768, 0) = 768..831 | 0x00030800 | 0x00000420 |
| 1 (1,0) | (13,6) | (6400, 1664, 0) = 1664..1727 | 99328 in ranks 1, 3 (0x01018800, 0x03018800) | 0xA | (6400, 832, 0) = 832..895 | 0x01030800 | 0x00000420 |
| 2 (0,1) | (12,7) | (6400, 1600, 0) = 1600..1663 | 107520 in ranks 0, 2 (0x0001A800, 0x0201A800) | 0x5 | (6400, 896, 0) = 896..959 | 0x02030800 | 0x02000420 |
| 3 (1,1) | (13,7) | (6400, 1728, 0) = 1728..1791 | 107520 in ranks 1, 3 (0x0101A800, 0x0301A800) | 0xA | (6400, 960, 0) = 960..1023 | 0x03030800 | 0x02000420 |

Reading the table: ranks 0 and 2 together assemble the 128 rows 1536..1663 of tm = 12 in BOTH their A stages (rows 1536..1599 at +0, rows 1600..1663 at +8192); ranks 1 and 3 do the same for tm = 13. The pair {0,1} holds B columns 768..895 = the 128 columns of tn = 6 (64 in each CTA); the pair {2,3} holds tn = 7. The barrier operand is the pair leader's `full[4]` (ranks 0/1 -> rank 0's, ranks 2/3 -> rank 2's), so each leader's barrier receives 2 A boxes landing in the leader + 2 landing in the peer + 2 B boxes = 6 x 8192 = 49152 bytes. The file's example at `explicit.cu:718-719` has the same structure (tile (5, 9), q = 7, rank 1: A (448, 640, 0) -> 0x01024800 and 0x03024800; B (448, 1216, 0) -> 0x01036800), recomputed and confirmed (the addresses; the inputs themselves are not a reachable state, Section 8.7.1).
</details>

**D4. Compute `st_off[0..3]` for epilogue thread (w = 2, l = 17) and the smem byte written for value j = 11 of subtile e = 5. Which stage and which store box does it fall into?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] `explicit.cu:1013` and `1047`:

```
    st_off[c] = OFF_SMEM_CD + 2048u * w + 4u * (l & 7u) + 128u * c + 32u * (((l >> 3) & 3u) ^ c);
```
```
        *reinterpret_cast<uint32_t*>(smem + st_off[j & 3] + 512u * uint32_t(j >> 2) + kEpiStageBytes * uint32_t(e & 3)) = __float_as_uint(d);   // 16 scalar st.shared.b32 (B.3.3 step 17)
```

w = 2, l = 17: `l & 7 = 1`, `(l >> 3) & 3 = 2`. `st_off[c] = 512 + 4096 + 4 + 128 c + 32 (2 ^ c)`: c = 0: 4612 + 64 = **4676**; c = 1: 4612 + 128 + 96 = **4836**; c = 2: 4612 + 256 + 0 = **4868**; c = 3: 4612 + 384 + 32 = **5028**. For j = 11, e = 5: `j & 3 = 3`, `j >> 2 = 2`, `e & 3 = 1`: byte = 5028 + 1024 + 8192 = **14244 = 0x37A4**. Stage `e % 4 = 1` (bytes 8704..16895); within the stage the offset is 14244 - 8704 = 5540, box `i = 5540 / 2048 = 2 = w` (box i always equals w, because rows 32 w .. 32 w + 31 of the subtile are box w). Cross-check with the unswizzled form: pre-swizzle byte = `512 + 8192 x 1 + 2048 x 2 + 128 x 11 + 4 x 17 = 14276 = 0x37C4`; `epi_swz` (`explicit.cu:197`: `o ^ ((o & 0x180u) >> 2)`): `0x37C4 & 0x180 = 0x180`, `>> 2 = 0x60`, `0x37C4 ^ 0x60 = 0x37A4`. Both forms agree, as the `static_assert`s at `explicit.cu:199-202` check against `cute::Swizzle<2,5,2>`. The file's own worked example (`explicit.cu:992`: w = 0, l = 9, j = 5, e = 6 -> 17540) recomputes as `st_off[1] = 644`, `+ 512 + 16384 = 17540`. The row written is 32 w + l = 81 of the CTA tile, column 16 e + j = 91. Why the XOR is there at all [S/A]: for one `st.shared.b32` instruction (fixed j and e) the 32 lanes write `4 (l & 7) + 32 (((l >> 3) & 3) ^ (j & 3))` plus a warp-uniform base, i.e. the four 32-byte chunks of one 128-byte row in a lane-dependent but bijective order: all 32 banks exactly once. The store is therefore conflict-free with or without the XOR, which only permutes chunks within the same 128-byte row (`j & 3` is warp-uniform). The kernel must compute the XOR because the D tensor map is encoded with `SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B` [M, D.1 D3]: the TMA unit un-swizzles on read, so the smem image must be in the swizzled layout, exactly as for A/B. The difference is that for A/B the TMA unit swizzles on write and the UMMA unit un-swizzles on read, so there the kernel computes nothing (`explicit.cu:203`). The swizzle is dictated by the tensor map; the conflict-free STS pattern is a property of the (32, 16) subtile mapping that happens to hold either way.
</details>

**D5. Which TMEM address does warp 6 load at accumulator stage st = 2, subtile e = 4, and what does lane 3 receive?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] `explicit.cu:1006`, `1031`, `1036`:

```
  uint32_t const tmem_lane_off = (32u * w) << 16;                                               // TMEM lanes [32 w, 32 w + 32): row 32 w + l of the CTA tile (0, 0x200000, 0x400000, 0x600000)
```
```
    uint32_t const taddr = T + tmem_lane_off + 128u * acc_stage;                                // warp-uniform TMEM address of this warp's 32 rows
```
```
      tmem_ld_32x32b_x16(taddr + 16u * uint32_t(e), r);                                        // columns 16e..16e+15 of row 32 w + l (:881-883)
```

Warp 6 is epilogue warp w = 2; T = 0 [M]. `tmem_lane_off = 64 << 16 = 0x400000`; `128 x 2 = 256 = 0x100`; `16 x 4 = 64 = 0x40`; address **0x00400140** = lane 64, column 320. The `32x32b.x16` shape gives lane l the 16 consecutive 32-bit columns of TMEM lane (row) `64 + l`: lane 3 receives row 67 of the CTA tile, accumulator columns 64..79 (absolute TMEM columns 320..335 of stage 2) as `r[0..15]`. Warp 6 may only address lanes 64..95 (warp id % 4 = 2) [B.6; Colfax TMEM tutorial]. The file's own example (`explicit.cu:982`: w = 2, st = 1, e = 3 -> 0x4000B0) recomputes as 0x400000 + 128 + 48 = 0x4000B0.
</details>

**D6. Compute the global byte address of the D element written by thread (w = 1, l = 20), register j = 9, subtile e = 2, of CTA tile (5, 9); then the smem byte it passes through and the TMA store box that carries it.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] Row `m = 128 tm + 32 w + l = 640 + 32 + 20 = 692`; column `n = 128 tn + 16 e + j = 1152 + 32 + 9 = 1193`. D is fp32, M-major (column-major) with leading dimension 8192 (stride 32768 B per column, D.1 D3), so the byte offset from the base of D is `(n x 8192 + m) x 4 = (9773056 + 692) x 4 = 39094992 = 0x2548AD0`. Smem: `st_off[1]` for (w = 1, l = 20) = `512 + 2048 + 16 + 128 + 32 x (2 ^ 1 = 3) = 2800`; byte = `2800 + 512 x 2 + 8192 x 2 = 20208 = 0x4EF0` (stage 2, box 1). Check: pre-swizzle `512 + 16384 + 2048 + 128 x 9 + 80 = 20176 = 0x4ED0`, `epi_swz` XORs 0x20 -> 0x4EF0. The box coordinates are `explicit.cu:1056-1057` and the store itself is `:1066` (both quoted in Section 10.10).

Box i = 1 has coordinates (672, 1184, 0) and source `cd_base + 8192 x 2 + 2048 x 1`; the element sits at (20, 9) inside the 32 x 16 box; the TMA unit un-swizzles (SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B) on read and writes 16 runs of 128 contiguous bytes (one per column) into D.
</details>

**D7. A cluster processes T = 29 tiles. Give the index and parity of every wait in the three tails.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] Each tail continues the producer state after N producer steps. The two lines a tail step executes are, for the mainloop (`explicit.cu:800` and `:805`):

```
    EXPLICIT_WAIT(empty_base + 8u * st.prod_idx, st.prod_phase, TAIL_MAINLOOP, tile, uint32_t(i));
```
```
    advance<kStages>(st.prod_idx, st.prod_phase);
```

and the same pair for the CLC tail (`:860-861` test-then-wait on `smem_base + OFF_CLC_EMPTY + 8u * clp_idx` with `clp_phase`, then `:866` `advance<kClcStages>(clp_idx, clp_phase);`) and the accumulator tail (`:955` wait on `acc_empty_base + 8u * accp_idx` with `accp_phase`, then `:960` `advance<kAccStages>(accp_idx, accp_phase);`). `advance` (`:612`) increments the index and flips the phase at each wrap. The producer started at `{0, 1}` and has taken N steps. Step i of the tail therefore waits `empty[(N + i) % Stages]` with parity `1 ^ (((N + i) / Stages) & 1)` (the formula note 7.2 derives for `producer_tail`; tails at `explicit.cu:799-806`, `859-867`, `954-961`). Mainloop: N = 128 x 29 = 3712, Stages 8: indices 0..7, parity `1 ^ ((464 + 0..0) & 1) = 1` for all eight (3712 / 8 = 464 is even; in general 128 T / 8 = 16 T is always even, so the mainloop tail parity is 1 for every T [M, G.1: every K_TAIL mainloop step waited parity 1]). Accumulator: N = 29, Stages 4: i = 0..3 -> indices (29, 30, 31, 32) % 4 = **1, 2, 3, 0**, parities `1 ^ ((29/4 = 7) & 1) = 0`, `1 ^ (7 & 1) = 0`, `1 ^ (7 & 1) = 0`, `1 ^ ((32/4 = 8) & 1) = 1` -> **0, 0, 0, 1**. CLC (rank 0 only): N = 29, Stages 2: indices (29, 30) % 2 = **1, 0**, parities `1 ^ ((14) & 1) = 1`, `1 ^ ((15) & 1) = 0` -> **1, 0**. Sanity check against the measured tile counts [M, G.1]: T = 32 gives accumulator indices 0,1,2,3 all parity 1 and CLC 0,1 parity 1,1; T = 31 gives 3,0,1,2 with 0,1,1,1 and CLC 1,0 with 0,1 - exactly the recorded `{idx, phase}` pairs. This is why a tail must continue the state rather than apply one parity to all barriers.
</details>

**D9. Which CTA tile does a CLC response with first-CTA id (x0, y0) = (18, 44) give to rank 3, and what are its A rows and D columns?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] The mapping is `explicit.cu:692-693` (quoted in Section 7.4, derived in Section 7.5).

First-CTA ids are always even (cluster-aligned) [M, D.3], so `x0 & 1 = y0 & 1 = 0`. Rank 3 has (x, y) = (1, 1): `tm = 2 x 22 + 0 + 1 = 45`, `tn = 2 x 9 + 0 + 1 = 19`. The cancelled cluster's launch-linear id is `(y0 / 2) x 32 + x0 / 2 = 22 x 32 + 9 = 713` = cluster tile (m, n) = (22, 9) in 256-unit coordinates [M, D.3]. A rows `[128 x 45, +128) = [5760, 5888)`; D columns `[128 x 19, +128) = [2432, 2560)`. The transpose (grid x indexes N, grid y indexes M) is the AlongN raster order. The file's example (`explicit.cu:672`: (10, 6) in CTA (1, 0) -> (7, 10)) recomputes as `2 x 3 + 0 + 1 = 7`, `2 x 5 + 0 + 0 = 10`.
</details>

**D10. The launch coordinate is blockIdx = (41, 26). Which rank is the CTA, who is its pair leader and its A-multicast partner, and what is its initial tile?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S] `x = blockIdx.x & 1 = 1`, `y = blockIdx.y & 1 = 0`: the cluster is 2 x 2 in grid coordinates, so `%cluster_ctaid = (blockIdx.x % 2, blockIdx.y % 2)` (`explicit.cu:1173-1174` read them and comment `== rank & 1`, `== rank >> 1`). Rank `r = x + 2y = 1` is odd, so this CTA is the peer; its pair leader is rank 0 (`peer = rank ^ 1`, `explicit.cu:1107`); its A-multicast partner is rank x + 2 = 3 (mask 0x5 << 1 = 0xA). Initial tile (`explicit.cu:1175-1176`, quoted in Section 11.6):

`tm = 2 x 13 + 1 = 27`, `tn = 2 x 20 + 0 = 40`: rows [3456, 3584) and columns [5120, 5248) of D. Its cluster (CX, CY) = (20, 13) has launch-linear id 13 x 32 + 20 = 436. Only the 33 clusters with ids 0..32 were natively resident in the measured run [M, D.3]; id 436 is not among them, so this CTA never runs with this tile: CLC hands the tile to a resident cluster instead. The file's example (`explicit.cu:1093`: blockIdx (5, 2) -> (3, 4)) recomputes as `2 x 1 + 1`, `2 x 2 + 0`.
</details>

**D11. Explain the 2048 unused bytes of shared memory and why making the kernel use them would require more than a constant change.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

232448 - 230400 = 2048 = 1728 (the floor remainder of 198464 / 24592) + 320. The 320 is the gap between the builder's estimate and the real layout. The builder counts 192 (carveout) + 33792 (epilogue) + 8 x 24592 (stages, each with 16 B of barrier storage) = 230720. The real `SharedStorage` is 512 (head: 43 barrier slots, CLC slots, TMEM pointer, 388 B used) + 33280 (D stages + FusionStorage pad) + 8 x 24576 = 230400. The head plus the D stages and pad (512 + 33280 = 33792) equals the builder's epilogue estimate alone, so the 192 and the 8 x 16 = 128 are over-estimates (Section 3.4.1). A ninth A/B stage needs 24576 bytes, so the slack cannot hold one; the only ways to use it are a different stage shape or a smaller epilogue buffer, both of which change the smem map, the alignments and the barrier counts.
</details>

**D12. The CUDA 12.x headers give `alignof(CUtensorMap) = 64`. What is `sizeof(ExplicitGemmParams)` then, which `static_assert`s in `explicit.hpp` change their verdict, and does the device code need to change?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

576 bytes: the fields end at 576, and 576 is already a multiple of 64, so there is no tail padding. No assert changes its verdict: `alignof >= 64` still holds, the map offsets are multiples of `sizeof(CUtensorMap) = 128` regardless of alignment, the scalar offsets are pinned relative to `4 * 128`, and the size assert admits both 576 and 640. The device reads `k`, `alpha`, `beta` at fixed offsets 520/528/532 and the four maps at 0/128/256/384, all unchanged, so no device code changes. Only the two records of the block's size change: the PTX `.param` declaration would read `.align 64 .b8 [576]` instead of `.align 128 .b8 [640]`, and `CONSTANT[0]` in the SASS resource line `0x380 + 576` instead of `0x380 + 640`.
</details>

**D13. Recompute `desc_b` for rank 1, `s = 5`, `kb = 1`, and explain why the result is the same as for rank 0.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

Rank 1's base is `0x01000400`. Shared address `0x01000400 + 164864 + 5 x 8192 + 32 = 0x01000400 + 0x28400 + 0xA000 + 0x20 = 0x01032820`; `>> 4 = 0x103282`; `& 0x3FFF = 0x3282` (the rank bit at address bit 24 becomes bit 20 after the shift and is dropped by the 14-bit mask). `lo = 0x10000 | 0x3282 = 0x13282`; `desc_b = 0x4000404000013282`. Increment form: `0x12880 + 5 x 512 + 2 = 0x12880 + 0xA00 + 0x2 = 0x13282`. Rank 0 gives the identical value because the masked field only sees the low 18 bits of the address, which are the same in every CTA; the MMA unit interprets the start address CTA-relative in both CTAs of the pair.
</details>

**D14. Apply `Swizzle<2,5,2>` by hand to byte offset `0x2A8` and state which atom line and chunk it is before and after.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

`0x2A8 = 680`. Line index = bits [7,9) = `(0x2A8 >> 7) & 3 = 5 & 3 = 1` (within the 512-byte atom period: `680 - 512 = 168`, line 1 of the second atom). Chunk = bits [5,7) = `(0x2A8 >> 5) & 3 = 21 & 3 = 1`. `yyy = 0x2A8 & 0x180 = 0x080`; `>> 2 = 0x20`; `0x2A8 ^ 0x20 = 0x288`. After: chunk `1 ^ 1 = 0`, same line, same offset 8 inside the chunk. So logical chunk 1 of line 1 is stored at chunk 0.
</details>

**D15. W2 declares `pred` with `"+r"` and initialises it to 0. What goes wrong with `"=r"` and no initialisation, and in which lanes?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

Only the elected lane executes `@%%px mov.s32 %1, 1`. With `"=r"` the compiler assumes the asm always writes `pred`, so a preceding `pred = 0` is dead and may be removed; in the 31 non-elected lanes `pred` then holds whatever the register contained, and `if (elect_one_sync())` may be true in several lanes (duplicate TMA/MMA issue) or none. `"+r"` declares the register as an input too, so the 0 is materialised and survives in the lanes the asm does not write (explicit.cu:265-277; note E.6.2 W2).
</details>

**D16. Rank 3's epilogue thread calls W11 with `acc_empty_base + 8 st`. Show the address arithmetic for `st = 1`, name the barrier it arrives on, and explain why W21/W22 receive an already-masked address while W11 masks inside.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

`smem_base(3) = 0x03000400`; `acc_empty_base + 8 = 0x03000400 + 272 + 8 = 0x03000518`; `& 0xFEFFFFFF` clears bit 24 -> `0x02000518` = rank 2's `acc_empty[1]` (the pair leader). W11 masks inside because the CUTLASS function `umma_arrive_2x1SM_sm0` does (barrier.h:909) and the wrapper copies it. The CUTLASS TMA copy functions mask inside too (copy_sm100_tma.hpp:292), but the kernel hoists `smem_base & kPeerBitMask` out of the k-tile loop as `full_masked_base` (explicit.cu:770) and adds `8 s` per k-tile, so W21/W22 take the masked address. The PTX instruction is identical, and the mask is applied once per CTA, before the tile loop, instead of 128 times per tile (nvcc folded it to `0xfefffff0` at SASS `0x0c00`, in the producer's setup after the dispatch, note G.3).
</details>

**D17. Which TMEM lanes may warp 6 read with W31, and what address does it pass for stage 2, subtile 5 (T = 0)?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

`w = 6 - 4 = 2 = 6 % 4`, lanes [64, 96). `taddr = ((32 x 2) << 16) + 128 x 2 = 0x400000 + 256 = 0x400100`; plus `16 x 5 = 80` -> `0x400150`: lane 64, column 336. Lane `l` receives `D[64 + l][80..95]` of stage 2 (explicit.cu:1006, 1031, 1036).
</details>

**D18. Derive the parity the producer waits for on `empty[3]` at k-tile `q = 19` of tile `t = 5`, and the parity of tail step `i = 3` after `n_tiles = 31` tiles.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

Step number <code>n = 128 x 5 + 19 = 659</code>; slot <code>659 % 8 = 3</code> (consistent); parity <code>1 ^ ((659 / 8) &amp; 1) = 1 ^ (82 &amp; 1) = 1</code>. Tail: <code>n = 128 x 31 + 3 = 3971</code>; slot <code>3</code>; <code>3971 / 8 = 496</code>, even, parity <code>1 ^ 0 = 1</code>. Every tail step has parity 1 for every <code>n_tiles</code> because <code>128 n_tiles / 8 = 16 n_tiles</code> is even (Section 8.6.8; measured in all 1056 mainloop tail records among the 1518 <code>K_TAIL</code> records, note G.1).
</details>

**D19. The explicit kernel passes the constant `0` as the third TMA coordinate and `kCacheHintEvictNormal` as the cache policy. Which of the two could you change for this fixed run without changing D, and what would you have to prove first?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

The cache hint: EVICT_NORMAL is the default policy of CUTLASS's <code>with()</code> and only steers L2 replacement; EVICT_FIRST/EVICT_LAST (<code>copy_sm90_desc.hpp:193-197</code>) would change timing, never values. It is still a deviation from the baseline, so you would have to re-measure (note Section 12) and show no regression before calling it semantics-preserving at the performance level. The batch coordinate must stay 0: the maps are rank 3 with an L extent of 1 (note Section 5.3), and the explicit kernel is an <code>L = 1</code> kernel by construction (its <code>run()</code> rejects <code>l != 1</code>; note G.3 "Generality"). Changing it would address out-of-range coordinates (zero-filled by TMA) and corrupt D.
</details>

**D20. Rank 2 (x = 0, y = 1) is a pair leader. Give the 32-bit `shared::cta` address of the barrier its `tcgen05.commit` releases after reading stage s = 5, the 16-bit mask of that commit, and the address and mask of its accumulator commit for st = 1.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

`smem_base = 0x400 + (2 << 24) = 0x02000400`. Mainloop release: `empty[5] = smem_base + OFF_MAIN_EMPTY + 8 x 5 = 0x02000400 + 64 + 40 = 0x02000468`, mask `kMainloopReleaseMask = 0xF` (explicit.cu:942, 186). The multicast delivers an arrival to offset `64 + 40` of every CTA's smem, i.e. each CTA's own `empty[5]`. Accumulator commit: `acc_full[1] = smem_base + 240 + 8 = 0x020004F8` (the file's own example at explicit.cu:138), mask `0x3 << (2 x 1) = 0xC` (explicit.cu:902), reaching ranks 2 and 3 only.
</details>

**D21. A cluster processed T = 30 tiles. List the four `(index, parity)` pairs of the leader's accumulator tail and say which tile's release each one waits for.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

State after 30 tiles: `idx = 30 % 4 = 2`, `phase = 1 ^ ((30 >> 2) & 1) = 1 ^ (7 & 1) = 0`. Steps: i = 0: `acc_empty[2]`, parity 0 (tile 30's acquire, waits for the release of tile 26); i = 1: `acc_empty[3]`, parity 0 (tile 31 -> release of tile 27); i = 2: `acc_empty[0]`, parity `1 ^ ((32 >> 2) & 1) = 1` (tile 32 -> release of tile 28); i = 3: `acc_empty[1]`, parity 1 (tile 33 -> release of tile 29). Rule: tail step i waits for the release of tile `T + i - 4` with parity `1 ^ (((T + i) >> 2) & 1)` (Section 9.6.3).
</details>

**D22. Thread `(w = 2, l = 20)` stores value `j = 11` of subtile `e = 5`. Compute the smem byte offset from the generic base, name the stage, the TMA box, the line and the chunk it lands in, and the element `(m', n')` the TMA will read there.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

`explicit.cu:989`: `512 + 8192 (5 % 4 = 1) + 2048 x 2 + 128 x 11 + 4 ((20 & 7 = 4) + 8 (((20 >> 3) & 3 = 2) ^ (11 & 3 = 3) = 1)) = 512 + 8192 + 4096 + 1408 + 4 x 12 = 14256 = 0x37B0`. Via line 1013: `st_off[3] = 512 + 4096 + 16 + 384 + 32 x 1 = 5040`, plus `512 (11 >> 2 = 2) = 1024`, plus `8192 (5 & 3 = 1) = 8192`: 14256. Stage 1 (bytes 8704..16895), offset inside the stage 5552: box `i = 5552 / 2048 = 2` (= `w`), line `n' = (5552 - 4096) / 128 = 11` (= `j`), byte 48 inside the line: chunk 1, word 4. The TMA un-swizzles chunk 1 of line 11 to `m'` in `[8 (1 ^ (11 & 3)) , +8) = [16, 24)`, word 4 gives `m' = 20 = l`. The element is `(m', n') = (20, 11)` of box 2: row `128 tm + 64 + 20`, column `128 tn + 80 + 11` of D.
</details>

**D23. Compute the `shared::cta` address of rank 2's `acc_full[1]` and of its A stage 3, and state why both are correctly aligned.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

`smem_base = 0x400 + (2 << 24) = 0x02000400`. `acc_full[1] = smem_base + OFF_ACC_FULL + 8 = 0x02000400 + 240 + 8 = 0x020004F8` (8-byte aligned, as every mbarrier must be). A stage 3 = `smem_base + OFF_SMEM_A + 3 * 16384 = 0x02000400 + 33792 + 49152 = 0x02000400 + 82944 = 0x02014800`; `0x14800 % 1024 = 0` because the base `0x400` and `OFF_SMEM_A = 33792 = 33 * 1024` are both 1024-multiples and the stage stride 16384 is too. The alignment of the base is a property of the launch (no static `__shared__`), measured as `0x400`, not something the declaration can enforce.
</details>

**D24. Derive `(tm, tn)` for `blockIdx = (6, 1)`, name the rank, and state which other CTA of its cluster shares its A rows.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

`x = 6 & 1 = 0`, `y = 1 & 1 = 1`, rank `= x + 2y = 2`. `tm = 2 * (1 >> 1) + (6 & 1) = 0 + 0 = 0`; `tn = 2 * (6 >> 1) + (1 & 1) = 6 + 1 = 7`. Tile (0, 7): D rows [0, 128), columns [896, 1024). The CTA sharing its A rows is the one with the same tm and the other y, i.e. rank `x + 2(1-y) = 0`, `blockIdx = (6, 0)` -> `(tm, tn) = (0, 6)`. The A multicast mask of both is `0x5 << x = 0x5` (ranks 0 and 2).
</details>

**D25. The explicit kernel uses 26 registers and the CUTLASS kernel 68. Give the register-by-register reason for 26, and state precisely why the difference is worth zero nanoseconds here.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

`R4..R19` are the 16 `LDTM.x16` destinations (one lane's 16 fp32 values of a subtile); `R20..R23` are the four lane-dependent `STS` bases carrying the `Swizzle<2,5,2>` term; the low registers are per-role scratch and per-lane phase bits (`R9` is the MMA warp's `cons_phase` and the epilogue's `acc_full` parity, `R0` the producer's `prod_phase`); `R1` is the compiler's per-thread local-memory stack base by codegen convention (NVIDIA internal), loaded once (`LDC R1, c[0x0][0x37c]` at 0x0000) and never read (no `STL`/`LDL` addresses it, `STACK 0`). The SASS names 24 registers `R0..R23` and ptxas reports 26, two more than the number named (`R0..R65` = 66 -> 68 for the CUTLASS kernel). The CUTLASS kernel adds the 16-register zero C fragment for the dead beta != 0 path, the `epi_load` state, scheduler bookkeeping in vector registers and 44 uniform-to-vector spill/fill pairs (`R65` -> 68). Occupancy is 1 CTA/SM because of 230400 B of shared memory (`__launch_bounds__(256, 1)` only asks for at least one resident CTA, Section 11.2.1), so register count cannot change residency. Neither kernel spills (`LOCAL 0`). The hot loops are not issue-bound (Section 12.5.5), so the extra moves of the CUTLASS kernel cost nothing either. The count would matter for multi-CTA/SM kernels or when spills land in a hot loop.
</details>

**D26. A kernel passes `Disposition: Passed` on the fixed command. Name three defects that this cannot detect and the check that catches each.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

(1) A different arithmetic (folded `alpha * acc`, a dropped `fmaf`, a different MMA sequence): the data are integers in [-8, 8], so any summation order is exact; catch it with the PTX/SASS inventory (128 `FMUL` + 128 `FFMA`, 0 `FADD` in the epilogue; the SASS total is 130 `FMUL`, the two extra from the `%cluster_ctaid` lowering) and a bitwise compare on non-integer data (Section 13.5 step 8). (2) A coverage defect that writes a tile twice with identical values, or leaves stale correct values from a previous run in D: catch it with the sentinel fill (0xFF -> NaN) and the K5 exactly-once check. (3) A dropped tail or a missing dealloc handshake, which is an intermittent exit race: catch it with five consecutive runs, the "Passed then hang in iteration 2" symptom (note E.7.2, failure-mode table), and the 46 `K_TAIL` records per cluster.
</details>

### 14.2.3 MODIFY

**M1. The accumulator empty barrier is initialised with count 128 instead of 256. What happens?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, from the [S] protocol] Exactly 256 arrivals land on the leader's `acc_empty[st]` per use (128 from each CTA's epilogue, `explicit.cu:1039`), so with count 128 the barrier completes two phases per use. Two failure modes, depending on timing. (1) The leader's 128 arrivals alone complete the phase, the MMA warp's `producer_acquire` for tile t + 4 passes, and the 2SM MMA (which writes BOTH CTAs' TMEM) overwrites stage st while the peer's epilogue may still be issuing `tcgen05.ld` on it: silently wrong D in the peer. (2) The parity bookkeeping drifts: after both CTAs have arrived, the barrier is two phases ahead. The producer's next parity wait then either passes without any new arrivals (another overwrite) or, if the interleaving leaves the barrier mid-phase, blocks for 128 arrivals. Those arrivals can only come from an epilogue that is itself waiting on `acc_full`: a hang. The epilogue is far shorter than the 27.8 us per-tile period (derived, 0.889354 ms / 32 tiles; the epilogue's own wall time was not measured in the note, which records only the whole-tile period and the 77-92 SASS instructions per subtile per warp, G.3; "a few microseconds" is therefore (unverified)). With 4 accumulator stages and that short epilogue, the race window is small and the bug may stay latent in this run. It would surface with fewer stages or a slower epilogue. Count 256 is the only value equal to the number of arrivals per phase.
</details>

**M4. The cluster becomes (2, 1, 1). Which constants, masks, counts and formulas change?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, with the [S] formulas] Ranks are {0, 1} only (y = 0 always), one pair. A has no multicast partner: each CTA loads its full 128 x 64 A stage itself. A single (64, 128, 1) fp16 box of 16384 B is encodable, because `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` limits each `boxDim` entry to 256 elements ("must be non-zero and less than or equal to 256") and `SWIZZLE_128B` constrains only the inner extent ("CU_TENSOR_MAP_SWIZZLE_128B* require the bounding box inner dimension to be <= 128" bytes; 64 fp16 = 128 B) [S, CUDA Driver API `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled`]. The leader's `full[s]` then expects 2 x (16384 + 8192) = 49152 bytes as before, but from 4 boxes instead of 6 (or keep two 64-row boxes and 6 arrivals of bytes; both balance). The TMA A wrapper no longer needs `.multicast::cluster` (or uses mask 0x1 << x trivially). Mainloop empty count becomes `2/2 + 1/1 - 1 = 1` with release mask 0x3 (only the one leader reads either CTA's smem). Accumulator commit mask 0x3. CLC: full arming by lanes 0..1; empty count `32 + 2 x (32 + 32 + 128) = 416`. The (tm, tn) mapping from the launch coordinate and from the first-CTA id must be re-derived from `swizzle_and_rasterize` / `possibly_transpose_work_tile` with cluster divisors (2, 1) (`sm100_tile_scheduler.hpp:666-677, 695-814`); it is not the 2 x 2 formula of D9/D10. Cluster tiles are 256 x 128, so there are 32 x 64 = 2048 of them. Cost: L2-to-SM traffic per output rises by 1.5x (per k-tile 32768 A + 16384 B = 49152 B for 32768 outputs vs 65536 B for 65536 outputs). Residency could rise to one cluster per TPC (74 clusters, all 148 SMs) instead of 33 clusters on 132 SMs [A; the hardware placement for 2-CTA clusters was not measured]. Whether that is a net win is a Chapter 3 measurement, not a derivation.
</details>

**M5. `alpha` and `beta` become `constexpr float alpha = 1.0f, beta = 0.0f`. Does D change? Does anything else?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, from note Section 0/8] D does not change: `1.0f * acc` is an exact identity, and `fmaf(0.0f, 0.0f, t)` folds to `+0.0f + t`, which equals the FFMA result for every t including `t = -0.0f` (both give `+0.0f`). A `-0.0` can arise only from `alpha * acc` when alpha < 0 or acc = -0.0, and acc = -0.0 would need every one of the 8192 products to be -0.0 under IEEE arithmetic (practically never for the harness's random integers in [-8, 8], harness:307-312; not proven for the MMA, Section 10.9); either way D is unaffected. What changes is the instruction stream: the 128 FMUL + 128 FFMA per tile per epilogue warp disappear (an FADD at most, or nothing), the `ld.param.v2.b32 [+528]` and its `LDCU.64 UR26, c[0x0][0x590]` vanish, freeing the two uniform registers that hold alpha/beta (note G.3; whether the per-thread register count changes is unverified), and the kernel can no longer run any other alpha/beta. The host guard `explicit.cu:1272` (`if (params.beta != 0.0f) { return cutlass::Status::kErrorNotSupported; }`) would still reject beta != 0, but alpha != 1 would now silently compute the wrong result. Performance would be unchanged within noise because the epilogue is not on the critical path [A].
</details>

**M7. Warp 2 consumes the CLC response before issuing its tile's loads instead of after.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, with [M] latencies] No deadlock: rank 0's warp 2 arrives on `throttle_full[t]` at tile start, before `load_ktiles` (`explicit.cu:783-786`). That arrival is what allows the scheduler to issue query t, so a consume-before-load would still be satisfied. But it exposes the CLC latency: warp 2 would wait for response t (min 736, median 1408, max 2336 ns from issue to consumption [M, D.3, trace build]) before issuing tile t's loads. The ring bounds that exposure. At the tile boundary the producer has run up to 8 stages ahead, so the MMA warp holds at most 8 k-tiles = 8 x 217 ns = 1.74 us of work, and the first new stage becomes consumable one TMA latency after the first new issue. The bubble per tile is therefore `max(0, response latency + first-load TMA latency - 1.74 us)`: about `max(0, first-load TMA latency - 0.33 us)` at the median latency (zero only if that latency is under about 0.33 us; about 0.7 us at the ~1 us of Section 7.6.9), and up to about 0.6 us plus the refill latency at the 2.34 us maximum, i.e. **0 to roughly 2-5% of a 27.8 us tile** [A]. A flat "1.4 us = 5%" would be the upper bound that assumes the ring is already drained when the response is awaited. The baseline order lets the response arrive during tile t's 256 loads. The scheduler's measured gap from consuming response n to issuing query n+1 (its throttle wait) is 28.8-37.7 us (median 30.8) in the unprobed clusters of the trace build [M, D.3 and Section 7.4], so the latency is fully hidden. The fetched tile replaces the current one only at the end of the loop body (`explicit.cu:794`). Why the CUTLASS kernel orders it this way [S, cb424739 `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:617-679`]: in the producer branch the two `collective_mainloop.load` calls (`:640-647`, `:654-661`) return before `scheduler.fetch_next_work` (`:665-669`), so tile t's TMA issues overlap the CLC round trip. And because the throttle `producer_acquire` + `producer_commit` (`:632-636`) is advanced exactly once per loop iteration, consuming before loading would also delay query t+1 by the whole load phase of tile t. The consume-after order also matches the 800-count: the number of arrivals per response does not depend on the order, only their timing does.
</details>

**M9. The epilogue's `cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read 1` is changed to `.read 0`; then to `.read 3`.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S/A] `explicit.cu:1069` `tma_store_wait_read<1>();` is issued by warp 4 right after committing subtile e's group. `.read N` guarantees that all but the most recent N bulk groups have finished reading their smem source. Stage `(e + 1) % 4` is written next and was last read by group e - 3, so the loosest legal value is N = 3; `read 1` is conservative. Where the 1 comes from [S]: the CUTLASS store pipeline is `PipelineTmaStore<4,1>` [M, D.1 D1], i.e. `Stages = 4`, `UnacquiredStages = 1` ("the number of committed TMA store batches that can be in flight upon return of producer acquire", `include/cutlass/pipeline/sm90_pipeline.hpp:650-700`). `producer_acquire` runs `tma_store_wait<UnacquiredStages>()` when `params_.always_wait || count > UnacquiredStages` (`:698-699`), and the kernel sets `epi_store_pipeline_params.always_wait = true` (`sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:491`). That is why every subtile, including the first, executes the `.read 1` instead of skipping it while fewer than two groups are pending. `.read 0` is legal but serialises every subtile behind its own store's smem read, adding one TMA-read latency per subtile to the epilogue; that is still off the critical path in this kernel, so probably invisible here, but visible in an epilogue-bound kernel [A]. `.read 3` is legal with 4 stages and allows three groups in flight; whether it helps is unmeasured. Whatever N you choose, the exit condition is unchanged: `store_tail` executes nothing for beta = 0, so the CTA exits with the last group's smem read un-awaited [M, D15]; the measured runs passed with that exit condition, and the claim that the global writes complete as part of kernel completion is the note's reading of the hardware semantics (note B.7 D15), not a measurement.
</details>

**M10. A colleague proposes to save work by having the peer CTA skip its `arrive.expect_tx` *and* letting the leader expect only its own 24576 bytes. What breaks?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

The peer already skips the arrive (only <code>is_leader_lane</code> arrives, explicit.cu:736). The byte count cannot be halved: the peer's A boxes and B box carry the leader's <code>full[s]</code> as their barrier through the peer-bit mask (<code>full_masked_base + 8 s</code>, explicit.cu:747/754), so 49152 bytes will complete on it per stage whatever the leader expects. With <code>expect_tx = 24576</code> the outcome depends on how many of the six boxes land before the leader's <code>arrive.expect_tx</code>: tx-count starts at 0 and each early <code>complete_tx</code> drives it to <code>-8192 k</code> (Section 8.4.4). If 0..3 boxes landed first, the expect brings tx-count to <code>24576 - 8192 k &gt;= 0</code> and the phase completes as soon as three boxes in total have landed — possibly before the peer's half of the stage is in smem — so the leader's <code>tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2</code> reads stale peer smem: silent wrong results. If 4 or more landed first, the expect leaves tx-count at <code>24576 - 32768 = -8192</code> or lower with the pending-arrival count already 0, the remaining boxes only drive it further negative, and it never returns to 0: the leader's warp 0 hangs on <code>full[s]</code> — the "mainloop deadlock at <code>q = 0</code> -&gt; <code>expect_tx != 49152</code>" row of the note's failure-mode table (E.7.2). So: silent corruption or a hang, depending on landing order. The 49152 is the sum of everything that lands in the pair (Section 8.5.3).
</details>

**M11. `OFF_SMEM_CD` is 512 and the stage stride is 8192. Suppose a refactor moved the stages to offset 256 (keeping 8192-byte stages). What breaks, and how would it show up?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

The TMA applies the `SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B` permutation to absolute shared-memory address bits [5,9), and the thread formula applies `Swizzle<2,5,2>` to offsets from the stage base assuming the base is a multiple of the 512-byte period. At offset 256 (absolute `0x500 + (r << 24)`), the stage base contributes `(0x500 >> 7) & 3 = 2` to address bits [7,9), so for line `n'` the engine's phase is `(n' + 2) & 3 = (n' & 3) ^ 2`: it reads chunk `g ^ (n' & 3) ^ 2` for row group `g` where the threads wrote chunk `g ^ (n' & 3)`. Within every 128-byte line the 32-byte chunks `0 <-> 2` and `1 <-> 3` are swapped, i.e. rows `[8a, 8a + 8)` land where rows `[8 (a ^ 2), +8)` belong (rows 0-7 <-> 16-23, 8-15 <-> 24-31), and D would be value-wrong in that regular 8-row pattern while the per-column 512-byte segments stay in place (checked by enumerating all 8 x 4 x 16 x 32 cases for base `0x500` while preparing this chapter). The `static_assert(OFF_SMEM_CD % 512 == 0, ...)` at explicit.cu:163 is there to make this a compile error instead.
</details>

### 14.2.4 DESIGN

**G1. Size the pipelines for a 256 x 256 pair tile (CTA tile 128 x 256 x 64) with the same fp16 inputs and fp32 TMEM accumulator.**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, using the builder arithmetic of note Section 6.1 and the [S] constants] Per CTA per stage: A 128 x 64 x 2 = 16384 B (unchanged), B now 128 columns x 64 x 2 = 16384 B (each CTA holds half of the pair's 256 N columns), plus 16 B of barriers: 32784 B. Epilogue storage with the same (128, 16) subtile: 4 x 8192 + pad = 33792 B. Carveout 160 B (192 - 32: the accumulator pipeline's barrier storage halves with 2 stages, Section 3.9.7). Stages = floor((232448 - 160 - 33792) / 32784) = floor(6.05) = **6**, using 160 + 33792 + 6 x 32784 = 230656 B. TMEM: a stage is 128 lanes x 256 fp32 columns, so only **2 accumulator stages** fit in 512 columns (still one full tile of slack between the MMA and the epilogue). Barriers: mainloop full tx = 2 x (16384 + 16384) = **65536 B**. A keeps its 4 x 8192 multicast boxes. For B each CTA loads either one (64, 128, 1) fp16 box of 16384 B or two 64-column boxes; the single box is encodable for the reasons given in M4 (each `boxDim` entry up to 256 elements, swizzle limit on the 128-byte inner extent only [S, CUDA Driver API `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled`]). Empty count stays 2 / mask 0xF; acc full 1 / empty 256; CLC and throttle unchanged. MMA: `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2` 256 x 256 x 16 (2 MFLOP each), still 4 per k-tile; instruction descriptor n_dim = 256 >> 3 = 32 -> **idesc = 0x10400010**; the B descriptor's start address steps by 16384 B per stage (1024 in 16-byte units) like A's. Epilogue: 16 subtiles of 128 x 16 per tile, TMEM address `T + ((32 w) << 16) + 256 st + 16 e`. Time per k-tile doubles (about 434 ns at the measured MMA rate), so 6 stages buffer about 2.6 us of MMA work against 1.7 us before: deeper in time, shallower in count. The trade: 1.33x FLOP per L2 byte (128 -> 171, Sections 3.9.7 and 13.6: A traffic per k-tile unchanged, so A bytes per output halve; B traffic doubles with the tile, so B bytes per output are unchanged) against 2 TMEM stages, 6 smem stages and a 2x longer epilogue per tile. The Colfax cluster tutorial makes a related point about the 256 x 256 pair MMA, comparing it with two separate single-CTA 128 x 256 MMAs ("the same number of FLOPs but transfers half the operand data"). Note the assumption: the builder's rule for `CtaN > 128` gives `N_perf = 32`, a (128, 32) subtile, 66560 B of epilogue smem (4 x 16384 plus the same padding) and **5** mainloop stages (Sections 3.9.7 and 13.6); the 6 above holds only if the (128, 16) subtile is kept.
</details>

**G2. Design the barrier table for beta != 0 (C must be read).**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[S, note 7.2 table and 7.8/B.3.5; initialisation already laid out in the smem map] Add warp 3 as the C producer and initialise the three reserved regions:

| Barrier | Count / tx | Who |
|---|---|---|
| epi_load full[4] at 128 | 32 arrivals + 8192 tx bytes | `PipelineTransactionAsync<4>` separates the two: ONE thread's `mbarrier.expect_tx.shared::cta.b64 [full], 8192` (`producer_expect_transaction`, "Must be called by 1 thread", `sm90_pipeline.hpp:941-946` -> `barrier.h:626-637`, no arrival) plus 32 plain `mbarrier.arrive` from warp 3's lanes through `mapa` to `dst_blockid` (`producer_commit`, `:948-951`). If all 32 lanes did `arrive.expect_tx(8192)` the tx-count would be 32 x 8192 = 262144 and the phase would never complete. The 8192 bytes are one 128 x 16 fp32 C subtile = four (32, 16) boxes of 2048 B into the C/D stage. Order in the CUTLASS epilogue (`sm100_epilogue_tma_warpspecialized.hpp:528-541`): `producer_acquire` -> TMA copy -> `producer_expect_transaction` -> `producer_commit` (bytes may land before the expectation, R2). SASS: the bare `expect_tx` is `@!P2 SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A0TR RZ, [UR29+0x80..0x98], R3` with `R3 = 0x2000` = 8192 (8 sites, `0x5240-0x6460` in `sass_gemm.txt`, not executed for beta = 0; `A0TR` = no arrival, transaction count updated from the source register, NVIDIA internal; Section 12.7.4) [M, D.2] |
| epi_load empty[4] at 160 | 128 | the 128 epilogue threads release after reading C from smem |
| load_order[2] at 192 | 32 each | warp 2 arrives once, after its first `load()` call (the 8-k-tile prologue), so that C loads do not compete with the A/B prologue (my analysis of the purpose); warp 3 waits once, before its first C load |
| CLC empty[2] | **928** = 32 + 4 x (32 + 32 + 32 + 128) | warp 3 now consumes CLC responses too |

Who initialises them and in what order they are used [S, note 7.2 "Init warp" column; cb424739 `sm100_gemm_tma_warpspecialized.hpp`]: warp 1 initialises the 8 `epi_load` barriers and warp 3 the 2 `load_order` barriers (`OrderedSequenceBarrier<1,2>`, count 32 each), so the init total becomes 43 (`SYNCS.EXCH.64` 43 in the baseline [M, D.2]). Warp 2 arrives on `load_order` once per kernel, between its first `load()` call (the 8-k-tile prologue, `:640-647`) and its second (`:654-661`): `:649-652` `if (do_load_order_arrive) { load_order_barrier.arrive(); do_load_order_arrive = false; }`. The C loads of the first tile therefore cannot compete with the A/B prologue for TMA bandwidth. Warp 3 waits on it once, before its first C load (`:832-835` `if (do_load_order_wait) { load_order_barrier.wait(); do_load_order_wait = false; }`), and never again. The epilogue reads C with 16 `ld.shared.b32` per thread per subtile (one per register; 128 per tile per thread, the 128 static `ld.shared.b32` C reads of the PTX [M, D.2]) into the C fragment and computes `d = fmaf(beta, c, t)` with the real c. `store_tail` must now execute `cp.async.bulk.wait_group.read 0` because C stages are reused. The C path's `elect.sync`-guarded TMA loads are the only TMA instructions that keep an election predicate [M, D.2]. Everything else (mainloop, accumulator, throttle, tails 1-4) is unchanged. The explicit kernel's host guard rejects beta != 0 precisely because none of this is implemented (`explicit.cu:1272`).
</details>

**G3. Estimate the speed-of-light fraction this kernel would reach on 4096^3 (same tile, same cluster).**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, anchored on [M]] Cluster tiles: (4096 / 256)^2 = 256; k-tiles per tile: 4096 / 64 = 64. With 33 resident clusters [M, D.1 D4], 256 / 33 = 7.76 -> 8 waves: 25 clusters do 8 tiles, 8 do 7, a wave-quantisation efficiency of 7.76 / 8 = 0.97. Per-tile time at the measured per-k-tile rate (0.889354 ms / 32 tiles / 128 = 217 ns per k-tile [M/A]; an upper bound on kernel time, Section 3.9.2 caveat) is 64 x 217 ns = 13.9 us, so the mainloop critical path is 8 x 13.9 = 111 us. Two points about the comparison. First, wave quantisation is *not* a differential term. The 8192^3 reference has the same 0.97 (1024 / 33 = 31.03 -> 32 waves), and the 217 ns rate was derived from that run's 32-tile critical path. At 111 us the 4096^3 run would therefore reproduce the 8192^3 throughput exactly (2 x 4096^3 = 1.374e11 FLOP / 111 us = 1.238 PFLOP/s against 1.236 PFLOP/s [M, G.2]). Second, the only differential term is the fixed cost F (prologue, TMEM allocation, first-tile pipeline fill, the last tile's epilogue, the tails: Chapter 12), amortised over 8 tiles instead of 32. F was not measured in the note (unverified). If it is 2-6 us the run takes 113-117 us, i.e. 1.17-1.22 PFLOP/s, **0.95-0.98 of the 8192^3 throughput**; at F = 9 us (120 us) it would be 0.93 (1.145 PFLOP/s). The ceiling itself is set by 132 of 148 SMs being usable by 2 x 2 clusters [M, D.3], which no tile change recovers; a (2,1,1) cluster might (M4), at the cost of 1.5x L2 traffic per output. A dense-FP16 peak spec number for the B200 was not fetched for this chapter and is therefore not used (unverified).
</details>

**G4. Choose a cluster shape and raster order for M = 1024, N = 65536, K = 8192 (same data types).**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, with the [S] scheduler heuristic] FLOP = 2 x 1024 x 65536 x 8192 = 1.0995e12, identical to 8192^3. A is 16 MiB (assumed to stay L2-resident; not measured), B is 1 GiB, D 256 MiB. CTA tiles 8 x 512 = 4096 (same count), cluster tiles 4 x 256 = 1024 with (2,2,1). The CUTLASS heuristic `tiles_n > tiles_m ? AlongM : AlongN` (note 7.4) selects **AlongM** here (cluster-tile counts 256 > 4), which is the right choice. The CLC hands out ids in approximately increasing order [M, D.3], and with AlongM four consecutive ids share one 256-column band of B, so each B band is read from HBM about once (about 1 GiB total). With AlongN the 33 clusters would march along n within one m band, and each B band would be re-fetched for each of the 4 m bands: about 4 GiB. At 7.7 TB/s (Lenovo LP2226, Section 2.2; 8 TB/s in other NVIDIA material) that is about 0.56 ms of HBM time against 0.89 ms of compute: tight. Cluster shape: L2-to-SM bytes per k-tile per 1K outputs are 1536 for (2,1,1), **1024 for (2,2,1)**, 1280 for (4,1,1), 768 for (4,2,1) and (2,4,1) (A loaded once per x, B once per y; see Chapter 3's model). So (2,2,1) is the best 4-CTA shape, and (4,2,1) would cut traffic a further 25% at the price of 8-CTA clusters (fewer resident clusters: 8 CTAs need 4 TPCs in one GPC [A]) and M = 1024 = only 2 cluster rows of 512. Recommendation: keep (2,2,1) + AlongM (the heuristic's own answer), measure, and try (4,2,1) only if L2-to-SM bandwidth is shown to be the limiter.
</details>

**G5. Replace CLC by a static persistent schedule (as one would on sm_90). What changes, and what does CLC buy on this very problem?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

[A, with [M] residency] Static: launch exactly N_resident clusters and let cluster c process tile ids c, c + N, c + 2N, ...; every warp computes the next id locally. Delete the CLC pipeline (2 + 2 barriers, 800-count, arming lanes, `try_cancel`, decode, the proxy fence, tail 2), the throttle (4 barriers) and the scheduler warp; keep every other barrier. The subtle part is N_resident: the naive 148 / 4 = 37 is wrong on this machine. Measured: 33 native clusters, 132 SMs busy, 16 idle (64, 65, 122-129, 142-147), every MMA pair on an SM pair (2j, 2j+1), and `cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters` = 33 [M, D.3, D.1 D4]. The explanation, that a 2 x 2 cluster needs two whole TPCs in one GPC and each odd-sized GPC of the chip's skyline leaves one TPC unpaired, 8 in all, is the note's inference completed by the skyline [A, D.3 "Inferred"; skyline (NVIDIA internal), arithmetic in Section 2.1.1]. Launching 37 statically would make the last 4 clusters run as a second wave after the first 33 finish (each with about 28 tiles of work): the run time would nearly double. With N = 33 a static round-robin gives 1 cluster x 32 tiles + 32 clusters x 31 (1024 = 32 + 992). The CLC hand-out recorded in the TRACE build was 13 clusters x 32 + 19 x 31 + 1 x 19 (the probe-slowed cluster (0,0); 416 + 589 + 19 = 1024, 13 + 19 + 1 = 33) [M, D.3, G.1]: every unprobed cluster received 31 or 32 tiles, the same balance as the static split up to one tile, and the 13 clusters that got 32 were exactly the 13 with the shortest per-tile time [M, D.3]. (The Release-build hand-out was not recorded; the trace build's per-tile time is 31.9 us against the Release bound of 27.75 us, D.4, and its CLC latency figures are the ones quoted throughout this chapter.) So on this uniform problem CLC buys no balance, only robustness: it does not need to know N_resident, it tolerates another kernel occupying SMs, and its latency (median 1.4 us) is hidden behind the 28.8-37.7 us throttle wait per tile [M, D.3, trace build]. It also costs almost nothing: 8 barriers, one 50-instruction warp loop [M, G.3], a query in flight about 4% of the time [M, D.7]. Where tile costs vary (ragged K, mixed problem sizes, grouped GEMM) its balancing becomes the point (Colfax CLC article).
</details>

**G6. A colleague proposes passing a `CUtensorMap const*` (pointer to a global-memory copy) in the parameter block instead of the maps by value. What changes on the device, and what did the by-value choice buy?**

<details><summary>Answer</summary>

TMA accepts a tensor map in `.param`, `.const` or `.global` space, so it would work, but the descriptor would live in global memory. Every `cp.async.bulk.tensor` would take a global address and `prefetch.tensormap` would not apply (the PTX ISA defines it only for `.const` and `.param` maps, 9.7.10.16), the kernel would need the generic-proxy/tensormap fence discipline if the map were ever modified, and the first touch would be a global-memory read instead of a constant-bank read. By value in a `const __grid_constant__` parameter, the four maps are copied into constant bank 0 at launch, `&params.tma_a` is a `cvta.param` address with no local copy, `prefetch.tensormap` brings the map's cache line in for the later `cp.async.bulk.tensor` (into the tensor-map descriptor cache, not the L2 data cache, NVIDIA internal information; the ISA names no cache; in SASS it is the TMA control instruction `UTMACCTL.PF`), and the bytes are exactly those `gemm.initialize()` encoded (the explicit path copies them out of `gemm.params()`). It also keeps the launch a single 640-byte parameter copy with no extra allocation.
</details>

---

## 14.3 Glossary

Each entry: what it is, how this kernel uses it, where to look. "W" numbers are the PTX wrappers of `explicit.cu` section 3 (W1 at `explicit.cu:260` ... W37 at `:601`).

**2SM MMA (`cta_group::2`)** - A `tcgen05.mma` issued by one thread of the even CTA of a pair that reads A and B halves from both CTAs' shared memory at identical CTA-relative addresses and writes each CTA's 128 rows of the 256 x 128 result into that CTA's own TMEM. The kernel issues 4 per k-tile (W29, `explicit.cu:516-529`).

**Accumulator stage (`st`)** - One 128-column slice of the 512 TMEM columns: `tmem_c = T + 128 st` (`explicit.cu:919`); 4 stages form the accumulator pipeline (full count 1 by commit, empty count 256 by the epilogues).

**AlongN raster order** - The tile-scheduler rasterisation in which the launch grid's x dimension indexes N and y indexes M after a transpose, giving `tm = 2 (y >> 1) + (x & 1)`, `tn = 2 (x >> 1) + (y & 1)`; chosen by the heuristic `tiles_n > tiles_m ? AlongM : AlongN` on equal counts (note 7.4). Consecutive CLC ids then walk N for a fixed 256-row band of A.

**Arithmetic intensity** - FLOP per byte moved across a given interface; for this mainloop 128 FLOP per L2 byte and 85.3 FLOP per byte TMA delivers to shared memory (at most 42.7 if the tensor core's reads of those bytes are counted too: they are read at least once, and `cta_group::2` does not imply a read-once B, NVIDIA internal information), per cluster per k-tile (Sections 3.3.1 and 13.5), the reason the kernel is compute-bound.

**Async proxy / generic proxy** - Two views of memory in the PTX memory model: ordinary loads and stores (generic proxy) and the asynchronous engines - TMA (`cp.async.bulk.*`), `tcgen05.*`, CLC responses (async proxy). Ordering between them needs `fence.proxy.async` (W15); the kernel issues it before every TMA store and after every CLC decode (PTX ISA 9.4 "Async Proxy"; CUDA Programming Guide 4.12.2.1).

**Atom (layout atom)** - The smallest repeating tile of a swizzled smem layout: SW128 K-major `Swizzle<3,4,3> o (8,64):(64,1)` for A/B (8 rows x 128 B = 1024 B, hence 1024-byte stage alignment), `Swizzle<2,5,2> o (32,4):(1,32)` for D (32 fp32 x 4 columns = 512 B, hence 512-byte alignment).

**Bank conflict** - Two or more lanes of a warp accessing different 32-bit words that map to the same shared-memory bank in one instruction, serialising the access; swizzles exist to avoid this for the row/column access patterns of TMA, UMMA and the epilogue stores.

**Barrier (named) / `bar.sync`, `bar.arrive`** - Hardware CTA barriers selected by id with a thread count: id 1 x 128 synchronises the 4 epilogue warps twice per subtile; id 6 x 160 lets warp 0 (`bar.arrive`) hand the TMEM base to warps 4-7 (`bar.sync`) without warp 0 waiting (W18/W19; ids from `cutlass/arch/barrier.h:169-178`).

**`barrier.cluster.arrive.relaxed` / `.wait`** - The cluster-wide rendezvous (W16/W17): every thread of every CTA arrives, then waits; it makes the fenced `mbarrier.init`s visible before any remote barrier operation. The kernel computes the initial tile between the two halves.

**Box (TMA)** - The per-instruction tile a tensor map transfers: (64, 64, 1) fp16 = 8192 B for A/B, (32, 16, 1) fp32 = 2048 B for D. SWIZZLE_128B requires the inner box extent to be at most 128 B (CUDA Driver API `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled`; CUDA Programming Guide 4.12.2.2.5, Table 25, stated there for compute capability 9).

**Bulk group (`cp.async.bulk.commit_group` / `wait_group.read N`)** - The completion mechanism for TMA stores: the issuing thread batches stores into a group, commits it, and `wait_group.read N` blocks until at most N groups still read shared memory (W24/W25). Only the issuing thread can wait, which is why only warp 4 issues stores.

**Cache hint (`L2::cache_hint`, EVICT_NORMAL)** - The 64-bit operand `0x1000000000000000` on every TMA load (`kCacheHintEvictNormal`, `explicit.cu:188`), CUTLASS's default `Sm100MemDescDefault`.

**Carveout** - The shared-memory budget the collective builder divides among pipelines: opt-in 232448 B minus the builder's 192 B kernel carveout (152 B of small barriers, 32 B of CLC response slots, 8 B of TMEM base pointers) minus 33792 B of epilogue storage gives floor(198464 / 24592) = 8 mainloop stages (note 6.1); the resulting 230400 B forces one CTA per SM.

**CLC (Cluster Launch Control)** - Blackwell's hardware work-stealing primitive. `clusterlaunchcontrol.try_cancel` requests the atomic cancellation of a not-yet-launched cluster of the same grid (the request can fail) and returns a 16-byte response, multicast to every CTA of the requesting cluster and completing an mbarrier with 16 tx bytes. (Section 2.12)

**CTA tile / cluster tile / MMA tile** - CTA tile: the 128 x 128 output block one CTA owns (its TMEM accumulator and its D stores). Cluster tile: the 256 x 256 block the 2 x 2 cluster owns, the unit the CLC hands out (1024 of them). MMA tile: the 256 (M) x 128 (N) x 16 (K) block one `tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2` computes for a pair.

**Descriptor (smem, UMMA)** - The 64-bit operand describing an A or B operand tile in shared memory: 14-bit start address in 16-byte units, LBO = 1 (16 B), SBO = 1024 B, version 1, layout type SWIZZLE_128B (high word `0x40004040`, low word `0x10000 | ((addr >> 4) & 0x3FFF)`, e.g. `0x4000404000010880` for A at stage 0, k-block 0; R7). The kernel forms it with a 32-bit add on the low word per stage and k-block.

**Descriptor (instruction, `idesc`)** - The 32-bit operand encoding data formats, majorness and M/N of a `tcgen05.mma`: 0x10200010 here (F32 accumulate, F16 inputs, K-major, N = 128, M = 256).

**DSMEM (distributed shared memory)** - The ability of CTAs in a cluster to address each other's shared memory through `shared::cluster` addresses; used here only for barriers (remote `mbarrier.arrive`, TMA/commit multicast, the peer-bit trick) and the multicast TMA destinations, never for generic loads/stores.

**`elect.sync`** - Returns a predicate true in exactly one lane of a converged warp (W2). For a given `membermask` the election is deterministic: the same lane is elected every time (PTX ISA 9.4; Chapter 6, Section 6.2.2 and Chapter 11, Section 11.3.2 quote the rule), and `.sync` makes each election a warp convergence point. (Section 2.10.3)

**Epilogue** - The phase that turns the TMEM accumulator into D: per subtile `tcgen05.ld` -> FMUL/FFMA -> swizzled `st.shared` -> `fence.proxy.async` -> `bar.sync` -> 4 TMA stores -> `commit_group` -> `wait_group.read 1` -> `bar.sync` (`explicit.cu:1034-1071`).

**`expect_tx` vs `arrive.expect_tx`** - `mbarrier.expect_tx` only adds bytes to the current phase's tx-count (no arrival is counted); `mbarrier.arrive.expect_tx` adds the bytes and performs one arrival in the same operation. (Section 2.8.2)

**`fence.mbarrier_init`** - `fence.mbarrier_init.release.cluster` (`cutlass/arch/barrier.h:712-720`, `fence_barrier_init`): a release fence issued after each of the four pipeline groups of `mbarrier.init` (the lone `tmem_dealloc` init, explicit.cu:1165-1167, has no fence of its own), so that the initialised barrier words are visible cluster-wide before the `barrier.cluster` rendezvous lets any remote arrive, TMA `complete_tx` or `tcgen05.commit` touch them. (Section 6.4.1)

**`FusionStorage`** - The epilogue fusion callbacks' shared-memory struct; for `Sm90LinearCombination` it is a `cute::tuple` of the visitor nodes' empty `SharedStorage` types, itself an empty type of `sizeof` 1. (Section 5.7.1)

**GDC / PDL (`griddepcontrol`, Programmatic Dependent Launch)** - `griddepcontrol.wait` blocks until all prerequisite grids have completed and flushed (W35). `griddepcontrol.launch_dependents` signals that a dependent grid may begin launching (warp 0 after its last tile, W36). (Section 2.13)

**`__grid_constant__`** - Qualifier on the by-value kernel parameter block that lets the kernel take its address (needed for `prefetch.tensormap` and the TMA descriptor operands) and keeps it in parameter/constant space (`c[0x0][0x380]` onwards [M, G.3]).

**HBM** - The GPU's main (high-bandwidth) memory; the run's unique HBM bytes are 512 MiB (A 128 MiB, B 128 MiB, D 256 MiB); the traffic the raster implies lies between 0.54 and 4.70 GB depending on whether B survives in L2, at most about two thirds of the HBM bandwidth, so HBM is not the limiter (Section 3.9.5, hypothesis, not measured).

**K-major / MN-major** - Which dimension is contiguous in memory for an MMA operand: K-major means consecutive k values are adjacent (A row-major M x K and B "column-major" N x K here are both K-major); encoded as `a_major = b_major = 0` in the instruction descriptor and selecting the K-major SW128 atom.

**k-tile (`q`) / k-block (`kb`)** - A k-tile is the 64-wide K slab one smem stage holds (128 per tile); a k-block is the 16-wide K slice one `tcgen05.mma` consumes (4 per k-tile), addressed by `+ 32 B` (2 in 16-byte units) on the descriptor.

**L2 promotion (128 B)** - A tensor-map encode option (`CU_TENSOR_MAP_L2_PROMOTION_L2_128B`) setting the L2 fetch size, the byte granularity at which L2 requests are filled from DRAM, to 128 bytes; set on all six maps [M, D.1 D3].

**`__launch_bounds__(256, 1)`** - Tells ptxas the kernel is launched with at most 256 threads per block and should fit at least 1 resident CTA per SM, allowing up to 255 registers per thread; the explicit kernel uses 26 [M, G.3].

**Launch-linear cluster id** - The id `CY x 32 + CX` of the cluster at launch-grid cluster coordinate `(CX, CY) = (blockIdx.x / 2, blockIdx.y / 2)` (grid (64, 64) = 32 x 32 clusters), i.e. `(y0 / 2) x 32 + x0 / 2` for a CLC response's first-CTA id `(x0, y0)`. (Sections 7.5.4 and 12.6.3)

**`mapa`** - PTX instruction mapping a `shared::cta` address to the corresponding `shared::cluster` address in another CTA of the cluster (W10/W13); lowered by ptxas to a byte-3 insert of the rank (`PRMT ..., 0x654`) [M, D.2].

**mbarrier** - An 8-byte shared-memory synchronisation object with a phase, a pending arrival count and a transaction count; a phase completes when the arrival count reaches zero and the tx-count is balanced. Operations used: `init`, `arrive`, `arrive.expect_tx`, `try_wait.parity` (blocking, with suspend hint), `try_wait.parity` (single peek), `test_wait.parity` (W5-W13).

**Multicast (TMA / commit)** - `.multicast::cluster` with a 16-bit CTA mask: a TMA load writes the same box to the same CTA-relative offset in every masked CTA and signals each destination's barrier; a `tcgen05.commit` arrives on the barrier at the same offset in every masked CTA. Masks: A 0x5 << x, release 0xF, accumulator 0x3 << 2y (Sections 4.4.1-4.4.3).

**Occupancy / residency** - How many CTAs (clusters) are simultaneously resident: one CTA per SM here (smem 230400 B), 33 clusters of 4 = 132 SMs [M, D.3], not 148 / 4 = 37, because 2 x 2 clusters need two whole TPCs in one GPC and each GPC with an odd number of TPCs in this B200's skyline (NVIDIA internal) idles one TPC [A, arithmetic in Section 2.1.1].

**Pair leader / peer** - The even rank of an MMA pair {2y, 2y+1} issues the TMEM allocation atomic (SASS `UTCATOMSWS`, the even CTA's elected lane only, note D.2; the pair-collective PTX `tcgen05.alloc` behind it is executed by warp 0 of both CTAs), all `tcgen05.mma` and both commits, and owns the `full[]` and `acc_empty[]` barriers the pair uses; the odd rank (peer, `r ^ 1`) loads its halves, runs its epilogue, and arrives on the leader's barriers.

**Parameter space / constant bank 0** - Where `__grid_constant__` kernel parameters live; the device reads `k`, `alpha`, `beta` and the four tensor maps from there (`ld.param`, SASS `LDCU` in the explicit kernel, `LDC`/`LDCU` in the CUTLASS baseline).

**Peer-bit mask (`0xFEFFFFFF`)** - Clears bit 24 of a `shared::cta` address, turning an odd CTA's barrier address into its pair leader's (Section 2.9.3).

**Persistent kernel** - A kernel whose CTAs loop over many output tiles instead of exiting after one; here each CTA computes about 31-32 tiles (1024 cluster tiles over 33 resident clusters; the trace run measured 32 or 31 per cluster, 19 for the probe-slowed cluster (0,0), note D.3), the loop being driven by CLC responses.

**Phase / parity** - An mbarrier's phase is a counter of completions; `try_wait.parity P` succeeds once the phase of parity P is complete (the barrier's current phase has the other parity). Each pipeline state (producer or consumer) tracks one phase bit next to its stage index; the bit flips each time the index wraps (Section 4.2.3).

**Pipeline (producer / consumer)** - A ring of `Stages` buffers with a full and an empty barrier per stage; producers wait empty, fill, and signal full (or let TMA bytes complete it); consumers wait full, read, and signal empty. Four mbarrier-guarded pipelines here: mainloop (8), accumulator (4), CLC (2), throttle (2); the epilogue C/D ring (4) is guarded by bulk groups instead (Section 4.1).

**`producer_tail`** - The `Stages` extra waits a producer performs after its last fill so that the CTA does not exit while consumers may still arrive on its empty barriers (Section 4.8; exercise D7 in Section 14.2.2).

**Raster order** - see AlongN.

**`scale_c` / `ScaleOut::Zero` vs `One`** - The `tcgen05.mma` predicate operand that selects `D = A x B` (0, `ScaleOut::Zero`) or `D = D + A x B` (1, `ScaleOut::One`). (Sections 9.5.2, 9.5.3 and 12.2.1)

**Scoreboard** - The SASS-level dependency tracking (per-warp scoreboards encoded in the instruction control words; that `sm_100a` keeps a scheme of this kind, tokens a producer sets (`&wr=x` in a decorated disassembly) and a consumer requires (`&req={x}`), is NVIDIA internal information; the exact control-code fields are implementation details, and the listings here print only hex control words, so the encoding stays an inference, Section 12.1.3 [H]) that ptxas uses to stall a consumer until an asynchronous producer (`LDTM`, `STS` read, `UTMASTG` read) completes. (Sections 12.1.3 and 12.2)

**`shared::cta` / `shared::cluster`** - PTX state spaces for shared memory addressed within the executing CTA (32-bit window address, `__cvta_generic_to_shared`) or within the cluster (a CTA's own `shared::cta` address is also a valid `shared::cluster` address of that CTA, with the rank in bits [24,32) on this compiler/hardware [M, D5 for ranks 0..3 in bits [24,26); D.2 for the byte-3 `PRMT` lowering]).

**SM / TPC / GPC** - Streaming multiprocessor; a Texture Processing Cluster = a group of SMs sharing some resources ("one or more SM", Nsight Compute Profiling Guide); 2 per TPC on the B200, 148 SMs = 74 TPCs (NVIDIA internal, Section 2.1.1; the consumer RTX Blackwell whitepaper publishes the same count), and every MMA pair was placed on an SM pair (2j, 2j+1) [M, D.3] (reading that pair as a TPC is the note's inference); a GPU Processing Cluster = a group of TPCs within which a thread-block cluster must be placed; its skyline = the list of enabled-TPC counts, one per GPC; of the two B200 skylines (8 or 11 GPCs, both 74 TPCs), this B200's is 10/10/10/9/9/9/9/5/1/1/1 (both NVIDIA internal), which fits the measured 33 clusters on 132 SMs (arithmetic in Section 2.1.1).

**Speed of light (SOL)** - The runtime a kernel would have if its single binding resource ran at full rate with zero overhead; Chapter 3 builds the model, G3 applies it.

**Stage (`s`)** - One slot of the mainloop smem ring: 16384 B of A (128 x 64 fp16) at `OFF_SMEM_A + 16384 s` and 8192 B of B (64 x 64 fp16) at `OFF_SMEM_B + 8192 s`, guarded by `full[s]` / `empty[s]`.

**Subtile (`e`)** - One 128 x 16 column slice of the CTA tile the epilogue processes per iteration: one `tcgen05.ld.32x32b.x16` per warp, one 8192-byte C/D smem stage (`e % 4`), four TMA store boxes.

**SW128 / `Swizzle<B,M,S>`** - CuTe's XOR swizzle on byte offsets: keep the low M bits, XOR B bits at position M with B bits S positions higher. `Swizzle<3,4,3>` (bits [4,7) ^= bits [7,10)) is the SWIZZLE_128B pattern the TMA unit applies on write and the UMMA unit on read for A/B; `Swizzle<2,5,2>` (bits [5,7) ^= bits [7,9)) is SWIZZLE_128B_ATOM_32B for D, which the epilogue computes in `st_off` (`cute/swizzle.hpp:42-96`: doc comment from 42, `struct Swizzle` at 55, `apply` at 76, `operator()` at 84).

**`tcgen05`** - The PTX instruction family of the 5th-generation tensor core: `alloc/dealloc/relinquish_alloc_permit` (TMEM management), `mma` (UMMA), `commit` (completion to an mbarrier), `ld`/`wait::ld` (TMEM to registers). Requires an architecture-specific target such as `sm_100a` (this build's) or a family-specific one such as `sm_100f`; the plain `sm_100` target is not in the supported list (PTX ISA 9.4, 9.7.18.7.1 and 9.7.18.10.10.1 Target ISA Notes).

**Tensor map (`CUtensorMap`)** - The 128-byte opaque descriptor produced by `cuTensorMapEncodeTiled` that tells the TMA unit a tensor's base, shape, strides, box, element type and swizzle; passed in the parameter block, prefetched with `prefetch.tensormap` (W20).

**Throttle** - The 2-stage CTA-local pipeline on rank 0 (counts 32/32) that lets the scheduler issue query t only after warp 2 has begun loading tile t, so at most one CLC query is outstanding per cluster beyond the tile being loaded (note 7.4; [M] never more than one outstanding).

**TMA (Tensor Memory Accelerator)** - The asynchronous copy engine for multi-dimensional tiles between global and shared memory (`cp.async.bulk.tensor`), completing loads through mbarrier tx bytes and stores through bulk groups; it applies swizzles and multicast in hardware.

**TMEM (Tensor Memory)** - Blackwell's 256 KB per-SM on-chip accumulator memory: 128 lanes x 512 columns of 32-bit cells, addressed as `(lane << 16) | column`; allocated in columns (power of two, at least 32) by one warp; a warp may read lanes `[32 (warp % 4), +32)` only (Colfax TMEM tutorial; note B.6). The kernel allocates all 512 columns per pair and holds 4 accumulator stages. The launch/scheduling resource associated with TMEM allocation is the Virtual Resource Counter (VRC): a CTA holds it from launch and `relinquish_alloc_permit` releases it so another CTA can proceed (NVIDIA internal, Section 9.6.2).

**Token (`WaitDone` / `WaitAgain`)** - The result of a single `try_wait.parity` peek (W7) carried into the next iteration so that the blocking wait (W6) is entered only when the peek failed; the kernel peeks the next stage right after advancing.

**tx-count (transaction count)** - The byte counter of a transaction mbarrier: `arrive.expect_tx` adds the expected bytes, each async copy's `complete_tx` subtracts what it delivered; the phase completes when arrivals and bytes both balance (49152 per mainloop stage, 16 per CLC response).

**UMMA** - CUTLASS's name for the `tcgen05.mma` family and its descriptors (`cute/arch/mma_sm100_desc.hpp`, `mma_sm100_umma.hpp`).

**Uniform datapath / UR** - The per-warp scalar execution path of the SM with uniform registers `URn` and predicates `UPn`; TMA, MMA, commit and CLC issues are uniform instructions (`UTMALDG`, `UTCHMMA`, `UTCBAR`, `UGETNEXTWORKID`) that execute once per warp regardless of how many lanes reach them [M, D.2].

**Warpgroup** - Four consecutive warps (128 threads) with warp ids 4k..4k+3, the unit that Hopper's `wgmma` addresses and that the Blackwell epilogue inherits for its 128-thread named barrier. Here warps 0-3 (MMA, scheduler, producer, idle C loader) form warpgroup 0 and warps 4-7 (epilogue) warpgroup 1; the `tcgen05.ld` lane rule `[32 (warp % 4), +32)` is what maps epilogue warp `w = warp_idx - 4` to TMEM lanes `32 w` (Section 3.7).

**Warp specialisation** - Assigning different roles to different warps of one CTA (producer, scheduler, MMA, epilogue) so that each runs a simple loop and communicates through barriers; the structure of `explicit.cu` sections 6-9.

**Wave quantisation** - The efficiency loss when the number of work units is not a multiple of the number of workers: 1024 tiles / 33 clusters = 31.03 (loss about 3%), 256 / 33 = 7.76 (G3).

**SASS mnemonics used in the lecture** - `UTCHMMA.2CTA` (`tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2`), `UTCBAR.2CTA.MULTICAST` (`tcgen05.commit` multicast), `UTCATOMSWS` (TMEM alloc/dealloc atomics), `LDTM.x16` (`tcgen05.ld`), `UTMALDG.3D[.MULTICAST].2CTA` (TMA load), `UTMASTG.3D` (TMA store), `UTMACMDFLUSH` (`commit_group`), `DEPBAR.LE SB0, N` (`wait_group.read N`), `UTMACCTL.PF` (`prefetch.tensormap`), `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64[.TRYWAIT]` (`mbarrier.test_wait/try_wait`), `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64[.RED]` (`mbarrier.arrive`; `.RED` on the remote arrives, required for a remote target and also legal locally, NVIDIA internal), `SYNCS.EXCH.64` (`mbarrier.init`), `UGETNEXTWORKID.BROADCAST` (`try_cancel`), `ACQBULK` (`griddepcontrol.wait`), `PREEXIT` (`launch_dependents`), `UCGABAR_ARV/WAIT` (`barrier.cluster`), `FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC.S` + `MEMBAR.ALL.CTA` (`fence.proxy.async`) [M, note D.2 dictionary].
